papers.abstract: Speaker representation learning is fundamental to speech processing tasks such as speaker verification and diarization. Although long-context speaker encoders can produce stable and discriminative embeddings, short-duration verification and diarization require finer-grained temporal representations. Short temporal contexts limit the available speaker evidence and make speaker identity difficult to disentangle from phonetic and acoustic variability. This creates a temporal resolution-representation reliability trade-off: speaker representations should maintain local within-speaker consistency, between-speaker discriminability and remain sensitive to speaker changes at fine temporal resolution. Accordingly, we propose a framework for reliable speaker representation learning at fine temporal resolution. FineSpeaker first constructs resolution-controllable frame-wise speaker representations through mean pooling over an adjustable n-frame window, enabling flexible control of representation granularity. It then introduces a speaker encoder with local temporal modeling that exploits short-range speaker context to improve the stability and discriminability of short-duration and frame-wise representations. Furthermore, we develop a generative disentanglement strategy for optimizing frame-level speaker representations, combining VAE-based probabilistic modeling with flow matching to characterize speaker-related variation and suppress non-speaker interference. Experiments demonstrate competitive full-utterance performance, improved fine-grained speaker verification on VoxCeleb and CN-Celeb, and strong zero-shot diarization results, highlighting the benefits of balancing temporal resolution and representation reliability.

papers.title: Single Spin Hall Conversion in the Hall Response of Magnetic-Insulator/Heavy-Metal Bilayers Identified by Odd Spin-Hall-Angle Dependence
papers.abstract: The Hall response of magnetic-insulator/heavy-metal bilayers is usually ascribed to two successive spin Hall conversions and is therefore expected to be even in the spin Hall angle. Using distinct magnetic-field windows, we separate the Hall voltage of yttrium iron garnet bilayers with Ta and Pt of opposite spin Hall angle into contributions from magnetization- and magnetic-field-driven precession as well as from ordinary Hall effect. The field-driven component reverses sign between Ta and Pt, revealing a Hall response odd-in-spin-Hall-angle. The magnetization-driven component also has opposite signs for Ta and Pt, except for the thinnest heavy-metal layers. A drift-diffusion model with interface-generated spin currents describes this behavior: the field-driven component is predominantly carried by a single spin Hall conversion, and the magnetization-driven component is consistent with one as well. Other potential explanations, based on a description with a finite imaginary spin-mixing conductance rather than interface-generated spin currents, require unusually large values of this conductance, making this mechanism unlikely. Our findings advance the understanding of Hall responses in magnetic-insulator/heavy-metal bilayers toward a more general description.

papers.title: When Chekhov's Gun Fires Anyway: Over-Realization in Text-to-Image Models
papers.abstract: In text-to-image generation, a target that the prompt mentions often appears in the generated image in a way the prompt does not call for. We call this failure over-realization. Mental-spaces theory points to the situations where it can happen: under a negation, inside what a character believes or imagines, as the vehicle of a figurative comparison, or behind a viewpoint that hides the target. Prior work has studied only negation in depth, and the conventional alignment and preference metrics do not penalize the failure. We build OverReal to measure it: OverReal-Gen, 698 prompts covering the four situations, on which we measure each generator's over-realization rate; and OverReal-Det, 2,841 generated images human-labeled for whether and how the target is over-realized, on which we verify the automatic judge that produces this rate. Our evaluation of eight text-to-image systems reveals that all of them over-realize, and that conventional metrics such as CLIPScore reward the failure rather than penalize it. Prompt expansion only partly mitigates the failure. Inside the generator, the diffusion backbone attends to a mentioned target almost as much as to a requested one. The cue words that should hold the target back receive less attention than ordinary words.

authors.name: Akiko Aizawa
authors.institution: Nara Institute of Science and Technology

papers.title: Atomistic simulations of electrochemical systems with machine learning potentials
papers.abstract: Modern machine learning potentials (MLPs) enable large-scale atomistic simulations at unprecedented accuracy. The incorporation of explicit physical interactions such as long-range electrostatics has continuously broadened their applicability to increasingly complex systems in chemistry and materials science. Extending MLPs to electrochemistry and electrocatalysis, however, is still challenging as it requires the consideration of electrode potentials and electric fields in the atomic interactions. Such approaches have emerged only recently, and although the field is evolving rapidly, further conceptual advances are still needed for carrying out reliable simulations at finite temperature under applied potential. In this review, we provide a comprehensive overview about recent progress in the atomistic simulation of electrified interfaces using MLPs. Current developments fall into three different categories. The first comprises linear response models that describe polarisation, polarisability, and Born effective charges, extending conventional MLPs to finite electric fields. The second includes methods that directly learn a field-dependent potential energy surface. The third consists of a series of hybrid approaches combining classical models with machine learning. Although still under active development, these methods represent a major step toward more realistic simulations approaching the quality of electronic structure calculations. Finally, we discuss open challenges and possible future directions for advancing MLP-based simulations aiming for a bottom-up understanding of atomistic processes at electrified interfaces.

authors.name: Marialore Sulpizi
authors.institution: Max Planck Institute for Polymer Research

papers.title: UAV-Flow++: A Unified Suite for Benchmarking and Learning Language-Guided UAV Flight
papers.abstract: Language-guided UAV navigation has largely focused on long-horizon route planning, leaving short-range, object-relative flight maneuvers underexplored. To address this gap, we formulate Flying-on-a-Word (Flow), a task requiring a UAV to convert concise natural-language instruction, egocentric visual observation, and current state dynamics into continuous flight actions. Flow encompasses both primitive motion commands and complex object-interactive behaviors, assessing motion intent comprehension and spatial context grounding. To enable policy learning and closed-loop evaluation, we introduce UAV-Flow, a comprehensive dataset comprising 30,692 expert-piloted real-world trajectories across eight distinct motion categories, alongside 10,109 simulation trajectories in the UAV-Flow-Sim environment equipped with task-specific completion criteria. Furthermore, we develop FlowVLA, which undergoes imitation pretraining on mixed real-sim demonstrations and online post-training via Tail-Aware GRPO (TGRPO). By leveraging group reward distributions, TGRPO effectively reinforces high-reward action sequences. Evaluated on 273 held-out UAV-Flow-Sim episodes, pretrained FlowVLA achieves a mean success rate of 75.58%, outperforming the strongest baseline by 6.72 percentage points, which TGRPO post-training further elevates to 93.16% with superior sample efficiency. Physical UAV experiments demonstrate robust execution of object-relative commands in both indoor and outdoor real-world scenes. Together, Flow establishes a novel benchmark and learning framework for language-conditioned flight maneuvers.

authors.name: Donglin Yang
authors.institution: Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences & Peking Union Medical College

authors.name: Wenhao Zheng
authors.institution: Max Planck Institute for Polymer Research

authors.name: Ke Xu
authors.institution: Beijing National Research Center for Information Science and Technology

papers.title: Random Exploration is Random
papers.abstract: Decision making often requires balancing exploitation of familiar options with exploration of uncertain alternatives. One strategy for exploration is random exploration, in which choices become more variable and less tied to the option that currently appears best. However, it remains unclear whether this variability reflects genuine stochasticity or instead a deterministic structure that traditional cognitive models fail to capture. We examined this question using the Horizon Task in an aggregated dataset of 1,392 participants completing over 1,270,695 trials. In this task, exploration becomes more valuable when participants have more future choices, and choice variability increases under longer horizons. We tested whether more expressive neural network models could recover deterministic structure from this additional variability. Although neural networks provided better overall fits to behavior than the traditional model, long-horizon choices remained consistently less predictable than short-horizon choices. These findings show that limited model expressiveness cannot fully account for the increased variability associated with random exploration, suggesting random exploration truly is substantially random.

papers.title: Shared Item-Level Error Limits the Aggregation of Small Language Models in Fermi Estimation
papers.abstract: Multi-agent systems of language models are often motivated by an averaging argument: if the agents' errors are unbiased and independent, the error of an aggregate of N answers falls as 1/sqrt(N). Fermi estimation, whose continuous answers are aggregated on the logarithmic scale, permits a direct test. We decompose the log10 error of each answer into the mean error of its model on the item, common to all its draws on the item, and a residual, and estimate both from 2.51M answers given before any communication by 15 open-weight models (3B-72B) on realFP, with replication under a single prompt pair on realFP, Science Olympiad Fermi questions and a guesstimation set. Given the item, teammates' errors are uncorrelated and teams behave as independent draws, but the item-level component accounts for a median 0.906 of the error variance over items. Teams of thirty therefore reduce a single agent's error by a median 1.7% (at most 5.4%), whereas draws that were also unbiased on each item would reduce it by 74-79%. All models compress their estimates toward about 10^6; this trend explains a median 17% of the item-level component, and a cross-validated linear recalibration on labelled items removes the overall bias but not that component. Three rounds of debate reduce within-team dispersion by 93% and leave the item-level component unchanged; revision without peers attains the same small gain. Mixing five models of similar accuracy reduces error by 6.6% relative to their own homogeneous teams, but no mixture improves on the most accurate model. Higher sampling temperature changes team error by about 1% at most, and contrastive activation steering not detectably; per-agent scaffold prompts (not significant after multiplicity correction) and skipping one layer in a single-model screen improve it. The results are conditional on the models, benchmarks, prompts and settings tested.

papers.title: Asymptotic Dimension of Persistence Modules of Bounded Presentation
papers.abstract: We compute the asymptotic dimension of spaces of multiparameter persistence modules of bounded presentation under the interleaving distance. The $d$-parameter modules with at most $n$ generators and $m$ relations have asymptotic dimension, and Assouad-Nagata dimension, exactly $d(n+m)$, the number of coordinates of their generator and relation grades, over every field; for two parameters this is $2(n+m)$. The space has continuous moduli, already for two parameters and $n,m\ge2$: over an infinite field it contains, at every scale, infinite uniformly separated families of pairwise non-isomorphic modules with one fibered barcode, so it is not doubling even at a fixed fibered barcode; already for $m\ge1$ it is not coarsely equivalent to a proper metric space. The proof is an induction on the number of distinct grade coordinates: an interleaving small compared with the gaps between these coordinates moves each of them by at most twice its size and preserves the induced grid representation, so the continuous moduli are invisible at large scale. Each class of modules at finite distance therefore embeds coarsely into Hilbert space; for $n,m\ge2$ over an uncountable field, the classes that contain these families admit no such embedding into a separable Hilbert space. Under the two-parameter matching distance $2(n+m)$ is a lower bound, attained for one generator and for two generators with at most one relation; on a finite net of $S$ slices the asymptotic dimension is at most $2nS$.

papers.title: Mathematical foundations for symmetric programming and reasoning
papers.abstract:
We develop a mathematical abstraction for uniformly exploiting symmetries in programming and reasoning based on the mathematical proof principle `without-loss-of-generality' (w.l.o.g.). Given: group actions that describe symmetries of the input and the output; and a canoniser, which captures how arbitrary inputs get sent to canonical ones, our construction extends any function from the canonical inputs to the whole domain.
  We characterise the conditions on the canonisers which guarantee that the construction gives the unique equivariant (i.e. symmetry-preserving) extension. Furthermore, we adapt the construction to a dependently-typed setting, where it captures traditional symmetric w.l.o.g. arguments via the Curry-Howard correspondence. Finally, we extend the construction to algebraic data types, where the symmetries of the constructors both uniquely determine the symmetries of the data type and pave the way for efficient execution.

papers.title: Tokenization: Hardness and Bicriteria Approximation Algorithms
papers.abstract: We study Binary Tokenization: given a corpus of binary strings over $\{0,1\}$ and a vocabulary budget $K$, select at most $K$ substrings (called vocabulary) to minimize the total number of tokens needed to represent the corpus. The primitive symbols $0$ and $1$ are always available, and each document must be segmented separately. Letting $n$ denote the total corpus length and $M$ for the maximum document length, we prove that, for every fixed $\varepsilon\in(0,1)$, Binary Tokenization problem does not have polynomial-time $n^{1-\varepsilon}$-approximation algorithms unless $\mathsf{P}=\mathsf{NP}$. To complement the hardness result, we give a polynomial-time $(\gamma,\gamma)$-bicriteria algorithm, with $\gamma = \sqrt{M}\log n$: The algorithm outputs a vocabulary of size at most $\gamma K$ with number of tokens at most $\gamma {\rm OPT}_K$, where ${\rm OPT}_K$ is the optimal number of tokens under the original budget $K$. We also study a storage-budget variant, in which the sum of the selected substrings' lengths is bounded by $B$. For $2\le B<n$, we obtain an $(O(\log n\log B),O(\log n\log B))$-bicriteria approximation algorithm.

authors.name: Xiaoling He
authors.institution: Nanjing University of Posts and Telecommunications

papers.title: Silscore: modelling siRNA potency with positional thermodynamics and data-selected nucleotide-identity terms
papers.abstract: Small interfering RNAs (siRNAs) enable programmable gene silencing, but candidates targeting the same transcript can differ markedly in potency. Existing predictors range from interpretable empirical rules with limited accuracy to high-capacity models that can lose performance when datasets or targets change. We present Silscore, a guide-only model that combines a quadratic preference for overall duplex stability, a position-resolved profile of nearest-neighbour stacking energies and sparse nucleotide-identity terms selected from residuals left unexplained by thermodynamics. Its main fit uses 26 parameters, fewer than half as many as any trainable comparator evaluated here. We evaluate Silscore on the canonical split of the Huesken dataset, two external datasets (Mixset and Katoh-Suzuki), and an evaluation in which the same guides are tested after training on dissimilar targets. Silscore attains the highest observed Pearson correlation in all three transfer evaluations, and the data support an advantage over every applicable comparator on Katoh-Suzuki. For a fixed evaluation set, we compare two equally sized training sets with higher or lower sequence similarity to the evaluation sequences. After training on the less similar sequences, Silscore has the highest observed correlation, and the data do not establish a change in its performance. The fitted parameters can also be interpreted directly: identity terms locate sequence effects that base-pairing energies cannot express, global stability has a data-estimated intermediate optimum, and local energy profiles recover terminal asymmetry and a preference for weaker seed and stronger central pairing. Silscore thus provides a compact, data-driven model that combines strong predictive performance with robustness when tested in new settings and expresses previously reported empirical preferences as quantities estimated from data.

authors.name: Giovanni Bussi
authors.institution: Scuola Internazionale Superiore di Studi Avanzati

papers.title: Spectroscopy of ultracold molecules in the mid-infrared
papers.abstract: Unlike the microwave and optical domains, frequency metrology in the mid-infrared has not yet benefited from the long coherence times and exquisite control provided by ultracold particles. We use a quantum cascade laser operating at 17.5 THz to drive ro-vibrational transitions in ultracold calcium monofluoride molecules. The laser linewidth is narrowed to 15 kHz by locking it to a custom mid-infrared ring cavity, which is in turn locked to an ultrastable laser. We study the spectrum for molecules confined in red-detuned and blue-detuned magneto-optical traps, and in an optical dipole trap. In the dipole trap, the spectroscopic linewidth is close to that of the laser. We consider the stability and accuracy that can be reached using these methods in the context of a broader programme for improving frequency metrology in the mid-infrared.

authors.name: B. Darquie
authors.institution: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique

papers.title: Detecting non-Hermitian topology from long-time dynamics
papers.abstract: We propose a protocol to measure the non-Hermitian topological invariant associated with the Lindbladian spectrum of chiral-symmetric open Gaussian systems from the relaxation of the covariance matrix. Importantly, the method works in the long-time regime and does not rely on isolating edge modes, so it remains applicable even when the Liouvillian skin effect may obscure them. We illustrate the technique on a Kitaev chain with reservoir-induced nonreciprocity, for which we first obtain a fully analytical and previously unknown description of its topological phase diagram. We then show that our protocol reliably distinguishes all the different phases.

authors.name: Rosario Fazio
authors.institution: The Abdus Salam International Centre for Theoretical Physics (ICTP)

papers.title: Anonymous in Name Only: A Critical Review and a Reidentification Exercise on the European Commission's Anonymization Measures for Google Search Data under Article 6(11) of the DMA
papers.abstract: In July 2026, the European Commission (EC) set out the anonymization measures Alphabet must implement to share Google Search data with competing search engines under Article 6(11) of the Digital Markets Act. As the first concrete illustration of how the EC operationalizes anonymization under the EU digital rulebook, this methodology could become a regulatory benchmark. In this paper, we show why it should not. We critically review the anonymization measures proposed by the EC, from the characterization of residual risk to the suppression thresholds and the reliance on contractual safeguards. For each of those issues, we highlight significant conceptual flaws, and, where applicable, we illustrate these flaws with empirical observations from real Google Search data provided by Alphabet and protected under the EC's measures. Importantly, we present examples of low-effort reidentification, record linkage, and confidential attribute inference achieved through straightforward and automatable attack patterns. Our findings show that the approach of the EC relies on unjustified heuristics rather than formal privacy guarantees, underestimates the risks inherent in free-text search queries, and sacrifices data utility without achieving meaningful protection. We also demonstrate that the proposed measures do not meet any of the three anonymization criteria established by the European Data Protection Board (EDPB): no record isolation, no linkage, and no inference. Practitioners and regulators are therefore cautioned against treating these measures as a sound anonymization practice.

authors.name: Josep Domingo-Ferrer
authors.institution: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique

papers.title: The 21 cm-Lyman-$\alpha$ forest cross-power spectrum with a minimal effective field theory
papers.abstract: Intensity maps of the 21 cm line and the Lyman-$\alpha$ (Ly$\alpha$) forest trace the same cosmic volume at $2\lesssim z\lesssim 4$. Their cross-power spectrum is insensitive to foregrounds that do not correlate between the two probes and, together with the Ly$\alpha$ auto-spectrum, separates the mean 21 cm brightness temperature from the neutral hydrogen (HI) bias. Effective field theory models of each tracer exist, but at one loop they carry tens of nuisance parameters. We test whether a minimal effective field theory (mEFT), consisting of the tree-level Kaiser model with leading-order counterterms and stochastic terms, previously validated for the Ly$\alpha$ auto-spectrum, describes the 21 cm auto-, Ly$\alpha$ auto- and cross-power spectra jointly. We use the Sherwood 80 $h^{-1}$Mpc hydrodynamical simulation with HI painted onto halos at $z=2.4$-$4.2$, and reduce sample variance with Zel'dovich control variates. Each spectrum is validated separately and then in a joint fit with shared parameters. With scale cuts $k_{\rm max}=0.5$, $1.2$ and $2.0\,h\,{\rm Mpc}^{-1}$ for the 21 cm auto-, cross- and Ly$\alpha$ auto-spectra, the mEFT fits all three spectra at all five redshifts. In the joint fit the mEFT determines the HI bias to 2.0-2.5% and the Ly$\alpha$ density bias to 2.1-2.3%. The scale cuts follow the HI velocity dispersion and the Ly$\alpha$ pressure-smoothing scale. When the brightness temperature is left free, the fits that include the cross-spectrum prefer values 20-30% above the true one, at 1-2$\sigma$, while the two auto-spectra together do not constrain it. A prior on the HI bias recovers the true value of the brightness temperature.

authors.name: V. Irsic
authors.institution: Scuola Internazionale Superiore di Studi Avanzati

papers.title: Emergent Anyons in a Weakly Interacting Gauged Chern Insulator
papers.abstract: We derive a microscopic relation between the many-body Chern number $C$ of the fermionic ground state and the braiding of fluxes in $\mathbb{Z}_{2}$ gauge theory coupled to matter: under a spectral gap condition, dressed flux loops obey $W_2W_1=e^{i\frac{\pi}{2}C}W_1W_2$ on the ground-state sector. We realize $C=1$ by gauging charge parity in a weakly interacting Qi-Wu-Zhang insulator. Reflection positivity and chessboard estimates show that flux defects are massive, which yields a gapped, topologically ordered phase with four locally indistinguishable ground states.

authors.name: Leonardo Goller
authors.institution: Scuola Internazionale Superiore di Studi Avanzati

authors.name: Marcello Porta
authors.institution: Scuola Internazionale Superiore di Studi Avanzati

papers.title: Optimal higher order convergence rates for the MUON optimizer
papers.abstract: Gradient descent optimization methods are the key tools to train deep neural networks in artificial intelligence systems. In practice, one typically employs suitable accelerated gradient descent optimization methods such as the momentum optimizer, the Adam optimizer, or the MUON optimizer proposed by Jordan et al. in 2024. In 1964 Polyak showed that, in a neighborhood of a local minimizer, the momentum optimizer converges with the rate $(\sqrt{\chi}+1)^{-1}(\sqrt{\chi}-1)$, which is strictly faster than the rate $(\chi+1)^{-1}(\chi-1)$ of the standard gradient descent optimizer, where $\chi\in(1,\infty)$ is the condition number (the ratio of the largest to the smallest eigenvalue) of the Hessian of the objective function at the local minimizer. Recently, the same faster rate has been established for the Adam optimizer. In this work we show that the MUON optimizer achieves the same higher speed of convergence and we establish the optimality of the obtained convergence rates. More specifically, we propose a precise concept for measuring the speed of convergence of gradient descent optimization methods, and we establish optimal convergence rates for the standard gradient descent, the momentum, the RMSprop, the Adam, and the MUON optimizers.

authors.name: Thomas Beretti
authors.institution: Scuola Internazionale Superiore di Studi Avanzati

papers.title: Dynamical mean-field theory of latching Potts networks
papers.abstract: Spontaneous transitions between memories, as observed in internally generated cognition such as mind-wandering and free association, require neural dynamics capable of destabilizing one attractive memory state and moving towards another. We ask what minimal representational structure is required for such transitions to emerge in random associative networks. To address this question, we study Potts associative networks with $S$ active states per unit and slow adaptive thresholds. The $S=1$ case can model a standard Hopfield-like network of binary units. We employ dynamical mean-field theory in the extensive-load regime, where the number of stored patterns scales linearly with network size and connectivity, and we focus on transitions between two condensed memories, which are singled out in the connectivity matrix. In the finite-load regime, we show that transitions are governed by an effective drive term, whose sign and temporal evolution distinguish high-latching (structured), low-latching (random), and non-latching regimes. The resulting phase diagram shows that adaptation alone is not sufficient: transitions only occur within certain ranges of the overlap between the two memories. In the binary case $S=1$, in particular, no unit can be active in both memories but in different Potts states, thus strongly supressing the high-latching, structured transitions that exist for $S>1$. In the extensive-load regime, non-condensed memories generate colored fluctuations and retarded self-interactions through an effective memory kernel. We find that latching trajectories change the effective timescale of this kernel, a dynamical signature of transitions in the extensive-load regime. These results indicate that multi-state Potts-like representations are essential for structured memory-to-memory transitions, a hallmark of spontaneous thought.

authors.name: Carlo Orientale Caputo
authors.institution: Scuola Internazionale Superiore di Studi Avanzati

authors.name: Fernando Lucas Metz
authors.institution: Universidade Federal do Rio Grande do Sul

authors.name: Alessandro Treves
authors.institution: Scuola Internazionale Superiore di Studi Avanzati

papers.title: Unequal-probability distributional balance and the Horvitz-Thompson estimator
papers.abstract: Auxiliary information can improve estimation precision under probability sampling, but the relationship between the study and auxiliary variables may not be known well enough to specify suitable balancing variables. Distributionally balanced designs address this by targeting agreement between sample and population auxiliary distributions. We extend energy-based distributional balance to prescribed unequal inclusion probabilities by comparing the empirical sample distribution with an inclusion-probability-weighted population distribution. Under a regularity condition relating the study values divided by their inclusion probabilities to the auxiliaries, we establish an upper bound on the design variance of the Horvitz-Thompson estimator in terms of the expected energy distance. This bound motivates an algorithm that exchanges units between randomly paired candidate samples without increasing their average energy distance. Combined with random initialization and uniform selection of a final candidate, the procedure preserves the prescribed first-order inclusion probabilities. We evaluate its auxiliary-space properties and estimation performance using generated populations and the Meuse data.

authors.name: Marco Reale
authors.institution: National Institute of Oceanography and Applied Geophysics

papers.title: Competing Octahedral Tilting and $B$-Site Off-Centering Govern the Phase Diagram of CsGe$_{1-x}$Sn$_x$Br$_3$ Perovskite Alloys
papers.abstract: Lead-free halide perovskites based on Ge and Sn avoid the toxicity of Pb, but the two cations favor different structural distortions. The stereochemically active Ge $4s^2$ lone pair drives polar $B$-site off-centering, whereas the larger Sn$^{2+}$ cation favors octahedral tilting. Here, we map how these two instabilities compete across the full composition range of CsGe$_{1-x}$Sn$_x$Br$_3$ using large-scale molecular dynamics simulations with a charge-aware machine-learned interatomic potential trained on hybrid-functional data. At low temperature the alloy exhibits a morphotropic phase boundary between $x=0.60$ and $0.65$ that separates a ferroelectric monoclinic $Cc$ phase from a monoclinic $P2_1$ phase with mixed antipolar and polar off-centering, with both the tilt pattern and the off-centering order changing discontinuously. The composition-temperature phase diagram reproduces the known transition sequences and temperatures of both end members and reveals an intermediate tetragonal $I4/mcm$ phase near the boundary that has no counterpart in either parent compound. Above the transition temperatures the $B$ cations remain locally off-centered but orientationally disordered. The structural transition at the boundary causes a jump in the band gap at low temperature, whereas at $350$ K the gap decreases smoothly with Sn content. These results establish $B$-site mixing as a means to tune polar and rotational order in lead-free halide perovskites.

papers.title: Counterexample to Flow-Transfer Conjectures
papers.abstract: An edge map $f:E(G)\to E(H)$ between graphs is called an $FT_M$ map if the pullback of every $M$-tension on $H$ is an $M$-flow on $G$; equivalently, the pullback of every $M$-valued 1-coboundary is an $M$-valued 1-cycle. The correspondence between restricted tensions and homomorphisms to Cayley graphs motivates two flow analogues. An $(M,B)$-flow (or tension), is an $M$-flow (resp. $M$-tension) taking values in $B$. For subsets $B=-B\subseteq M$ with $M$ an abelian group, \v{S}\'amal conjectured that a graph admits an $(M,B)$-flow if and only if it admits an $FT_M$ map to the Cayley graph $\operatorname{Cay}(M,B)$. DeVos conjectured that, whenever there is a graph homomorphism $\operatorname{Cay}(M,B)\to\operatorname{Cay}(M',B')$, every graph admitting an $(M,B)$-flow also admits an $(M',B')$-flow. We prove that these conjectures are equivalent and give a counterexample using the Petersen graph.

papers.title: Solovay's Construction via Proof Search
papers.abstract: Solovay's celebrated result establishes the arithmetical completeness of GL by embedding Kripke models into arithmetic. We provide an alternative proof of the arithmetical completeness of GL, in which we instead embed failed proof searches into arithmetic. Our methodology requires only a well-behaved sequent calculus and does not rely on completeness with respect to Kripke semantics or any of its variants. This approach is particularly interesting for logics that do not behave well semantically, such as ER, for which we also provide a new proof of arithmetical completeness.

papers.title: Self-Organizing Maps for the Exploration and Classification of X-Ray Sources in the Chandra Source Catalog
papers.abstract: In this work, we apply Self-Organizing Maps (SOMs) to the Chandra Source Catalog (CSC) to investigate the distribution of observation-level detections in the feature space defined by their spectral and variability properties. SOMs are neural-network-based models that project points in high-dimensional space onto a two-dimensional latent space while preserving their local topological structure. From CSC 2.1.1 we extract a sample of 36,904 ACIS-only, observation-level, high statistical significance detections, belonging to 17,927 unique sources. Among these detections, 25,192 (10,078 sources) are associated with a label from SIMBAD via a 1" cross-match that provides information about their astrophysical nature. Training a 40x40 hexagonal SOM reveals structured regions in the U-Matrix and activation response map, and feature-projection maps trace coherent patterns in spectral shape and variability. Overlaying SIMBAD classes shows that labeled populations occupy distinct, partially adjacent regions of the map and that generic categories can be interpreted via their SOM locations. We then retrain the SOM for classification using a source-grouped train/validation/test split and introduce SOMClassifier. When applied to 11,712 detections without SIMBAD labels, it assigns valid (non-abstained) labels to 6,225 detections (coverage ~53%). Furthermore, we release the trained models and visualization/classification workflows through a public web application built on the most up-to-date CSC release.

papers.title: Universal Invariants for $\gcd(n^k-1,n!-1)>1$
papers.abstract: For integers $k\geq2$ and $\lambda_1,\lambda_2\in\{-1,+1\}$, let $S_k^{\lambda_1,\lambda_2}:=\{n\in\mathbb{N}\setminus\{0,1\}:\gcd(n^k+\lambda_1,n!+\lambda_2)>1\}$. This family arose from a MathOverflow problem concerning the existence of integers $n$ satisfying $\gcd(n^2+1,n!+1)>1$ and from the subsequent question of whether arbitrarily many, but finitely many, solutions can be obtained by varying the exponent and the signs. We concentrate on the case $\lambda_1=\lambda_2=-1$ and introduce the notion of a universal invariant for an odd prime $p$, namely an integer $n\geq2$ such that $\gcd(n^{p\cdot m}-1,n!-1)>1$ for every integer $m\geq1$. We prove that this condition is equivalent to $\gcd(n^p-1,n!-1)>1$, characterize the possible prime divisors in terms of roots of unity over finite fields, and recall an explicit construction due to Jonathan Love that yields a universal invariant for every odd prime $p\geq5$, with the cubic case treated separately. As an application, we prove that $|S_k^{-1,-1}|\geq\omega_{\mathrm{odd}}(k)$ for every integer $k\geq2$, where $\omega_{\mathrm{odd}}(k)$ denotes the number of distinct odd prime divisors of $k$. Hence, the cardinalities of these sets are unbounded as $k$ varies. This lower bound is deliberately coarse and constructive, as it is obtained by considering only universal invariants; stronger general lower bounds are obtained by different constructions. We also discuss minimal universal invariants, their persistent common divisors, the special structure of the cubic case, and a heuristic due to Will Sawin suggesting that there may be infinitely many cubic universal invariants, although the known examples are exceptionally sparse. Whether $S_k^{-1,-1}$ is finite or infinite for any fixed exponent $k\geq3$ remains an open problem.

papers.title: Leaderboard Hacking: Preference-Based Model Evaluations are Vulnerable to Manipulation
papers.abstract: Arena-style rankings of language models are a widely used evaluation framework in online leaderboards, research papers, and model evaluation in production. These rankings aim to realistically assess model performance using pairwise comparisons of anonymous models on user prompts, aggregating votes via the Bradley-Terry model to produce the final ranking. However, we find that these leaderboards are highly vulnerable to several manipulation strategies that unscrupulous providers could use to boost a model's rank: strategic voting (individual votes that boost a model's rank, including votes on irrelevant models), strategic prompting (choosing prompts that favor a model), and strategic nomination (boosting the rank of a model by inserting irrelevant models). We demonstrate these effects on public leaderboard data, analyze the circumstances that cause these vulnerabilities, and describe approaches to safeguard against each attack. Notably, these issues hold for any preference-based evaluation using the Bradley-Terry model that allows open prompting, voting, or model submission. These manipulations boost the rank of nearly every tested model; each attack can boost a model by up to 15-20 places in a ranking and, combined, they can boost a model by up to 45 places.

authors.name: Dylan Hadfield-Menell
authors.institution: MIT Computer Science and Artificial Intelligence Laboratory

papers.title: The optimization landscape of robust high-dimensional mean estimation: stability, moment adaptation, and mirror descent reweighting
papers.abstract: We study efficient robust estimation of a high-dimensional mean under strong contamination when the clean distribution has only $p\ge2$ moments, bounded by $\nu_p$. We give a unified proof of stability for every $p\ge2$ with the optimal dimension-free sub-Gaussian rate, linking the reweighting, trimming and truncation techniques of the outlier and heavy-tailed robust literatures through concentration of counting and truncation processes. Building on stability and spectral signatures, we quantify the optimization landscape over sample weights that remove at most a fraction $\varepsilon_{n,k}=k/n$ of the mass, where the trimming parameter $k$ slightly exceeds the number of outliers. An unobserved convex spectral loss has inexact quadratic growth, with curvature $\frac{1-\varepsilon_{n,k}}{\varepsilon_{n,k}}$, relative to a mean-induced Bregman divergence, and the observable spectral loss supplies a dimension-free, inexact, relatively weakly star-convex subgradient oracle for it. This yields a Lyapunov analysis of mirror descent reweighting for $\varepsilon_{n,k}<\frac13$ that covers Hedge, the projected subgradient method, a new mean-induced mirror descent, and a centered multiplicative weights update. Each method uses one top-eigenvector computation per step and attains the optimal sub-Gaussian rate without knowledge of $(p,\nu_p)$. Mean-induced mirror descent further achieves faster optimization rates and last-iterate guarantees, at the cost of a more expensive projection step in higher dimensions.

authors.name: Roberto I. Oliveira
authors.institution: Instituto Nacional de Matemática Pura e Aplicada

papers.title: Affine Combiners for Reed-Solomon Proximity Gaps
papers.abstract:
Reed-Solomon proximity gaps establish soundness guarantees for protocols that test received words through random combinations. For length-$n$ codes over $\mathbb{F}_q$, classical scalar combiners achieve error $O(n/q)$ in the unique-decoding regime, with larger known bounds near the Johnson radius.
  We prove smaller error bounds using affine combiners, which combine two received words $f,g$ as $f(x)+(\alpha+\beta x)g(x)$, where $\alpha,\beta$ are independent uniform elements of $\mathbb{F}_q$. For output degree bound $d=\rho n$, fixed $\rho\in(0,1)$ and $0<\eta<1-\sqrt{\rho}$, and sufficiently large block length $n$, we prove mutual correlated agreement (MCA) with one coordinate of agreement loss at threshold $A=\lceil(\sqrt{\rho}+\eta)n\rceil$, with error $O_{\rho,\eta}\left(\frac{1}{q}+\frac{n^2}{q^2}\right)$. The result holds over arbitrary evaluation domains in every finite field, including prime and binary extension fields. The agreement threshold can approach the Johnson threshold, beyond unique decoding.
  For $q\ge n^2$, our error is $O_{\rho,\eta}(1/q)$, an asymptotic factor-$n$ separation from scalar combiners: we prove that their worst-case MCA error is $\Omega_{\rho,\eta}(n/q)$ at the same agreement threshold and with the same one-coordinate loss. We also prove that affine combiners incur worst-case error $\Omega_{\rho,\eta}(n/q)$ when no agreement loss is allowed. Thus one coordinate of agreement loss is necessary for our guarantee; this relaxation of standard MCA reduces the guaranteed common agreement fraction by at most $1/n$. We also extend the result to $k$-variate Reed-Muller codes on subfield grids, obtaining MCA error $O_{\rho,\eta,k}(q^{-k})$ for fixed $\rho,\eta,k$, sufficiently large $n$, and $q\ge n^{k+1}$, with agreement loss $n^{1-1/k}$.

authors.name: Alessandro Chiesa
authors.institution: Istituto Nazionale di Fisica Nucleare, Sezione di Milano Bicocca

authors.name: Kai Zhe Zheng
authors.institution: University of Electronic Science and Technology of China

papers.title: Decentralised model predictive control of recurrent neural network models
papers.abstract: This work proposes a decentralised nonlinear model predictive control algorithm for systems described by input-coupled recurrent neural network models. The proposed approach exploits closed-loop incremental input-to-state stability to design the local controllers and provide robustness to subsystem couplings. The resulting control scheme guarantees asymptotic convergence to a desired equilibrium while satisfying input and output constraints. Simulation results illustrate the performance of the proposed approach.

authors.name: Andrea Ballarino
authors.institution: Institute of Intelligent Industrial Systems and Technologies for Advanced Manufacturing

papers.title: PDO Drug Screening Data for Evaluating and Training AI Drug Response Prediction Models
papers.abstract: Anti-cancer drug response prediction (DRP) is critically important for precision oncology and therapeutic development. Currently, most DRP models are developed using drug screening data from immortalized cancer cell lines, which can differ substantially from patient tumors at the genomic and molecular levels, even though patient tumor response is the ultimate prediction target. To help bridge this gap and bring DRP models closer to their intended clinical application, we conducted four drug screening studies using patient-derived organoids (PDOs), which more faithfully recapitulate patient tumors than immortalized cell lines. These studies generated data for improving and evaluating DRP models, including multi-omics profiles of PDO lines, drug feature data, and treatment response measurements. Using these data, we retrained and evaluated multiple publicly available DRP models under three model-building scenarios: training models using cell line data only, training models using combined cell line and PDO data, and pretraining models on cell line data followed by fine-tuning on PDO data. We then evaluated and compared model prediction performance on PDOs across these analysis scenarios. In addition, we also assessed the consistency of drug screening viability data generated by different laboratories using different assay technologies and/or experimental protocols.

authors.name: M. Sacco
authors.institution: Institute of Intelligent Industrial Systems and Technologies for Advanced Manufacturing

papers.title: Posterior contraction rates for banded approximations of Gaussian processes
papers.abstract:
Gaussian process regression models are widely used in modern statistics and machine learning due to their flexibility, interpretability, built-in uncertainty quantification, and strong theoretical foundations. However, training Gaussian processes (GPs) has a computational cost of $O(n^3)$, while the memory and prediction costs are also $O(n^2)$.
  For large datasets commonly encountered in practice, this becomes infeasible and necessitates the use of approximate posterior methods.
  In this work, we propose a class of approximations based on sparse covariance matrices, where the kernel matrix is sparsified according to the spatial proximity of the design points.
  We analyze the accuracy of the resulting approximate posterior distribution and show that the proposed approach preserves optimal statistical inference properties, provided that the dependencies among a sufficient number of neighboring points for each feature are retained.
  We derive explicit sufficient and necessary conditions on the number of neighbors required in a general setting and apply these results to standard kernels, including the squared exponential and Mat\'ern kernels. Our theoretical findings are supported by numerical experiments.

papers.title: Global Fit Inference for LISA with samsara++
papers.abstract: The Laser Interferometer Space Antenna (LISA) will observe a superposition of gravitational-wave signals, requiring joint inference of an unknown number of sources, parameters, and instrumental noise. To disentangle these contributions, that overlap in both time and frequency, a Global Fit (GF) analysis is needed. We present samsara++, a C++/CUDA sampler designed to address this trans-dimensional GF problem. Building on the continuous-time MCMC framework of samsara, the algorithm combines birth-death processes for adding and removing sources, with mutation moves for parameter estimation. Birth and death are selected through posterior-dependent rates. Shared-memory parallelism, incremental likelihood updates, and indexed storage reduce the computational and memory costs, while parallel tempering improves the exploration of multimodal posteriors. We assess the performance using simulated one-year LISA datasets containing Galactic double white dwarf binaries and stationary Gaussian instrumental noise. Analyses of populations containing 143 and 866 binaries start from empty source models, without preliminary searches or proposals tailored to the injected population. These tests demonstrate source reconstruction and catalog generation, highlighting, at the same time, the importance of source-count, overlapping signals, and incomplete mixing on joint source and noise inference. Then we perform a separate stress test, initialized at the injected parameters, exploring a population of 16,435 binaries, corresponding to 131,480 source parameters. This run completes 15 million iterations in approximately 16 hours using about 3 GB of RAM. All together, these benchmarks show the computational feasibility of birth-death sampling for large Galactic-binary populations, and provide a foundation for extending samsara++ toward a comprehensive LISA global fit.

authors.name: Riccardo Buscicchio
authors.institution: Istituto Nazionale di Fisica Nucleare, Sezione di Milano Bicocca

papers.title: Martingale posteriors for flexible regression via recursive least squares
papers.abstract: Predictive Bayes quantifies uncertainty by specifying a sequence of one-step-ahead predictive distributions, inducing a martingale posterior without an explicit prior. Existing parametric constructions rely on stochastic-gradient updates and have seen limited development for flexible regression. We propose a predictive Bayes framework based on recursive least squares, whose martingale posterior has an explicit representation: given future covariates, it is the law of the posterior mean plus a weighted series of independent draws from the standardized predictive distribution. The posterior mean is a penalized least squares estimator, available in closed form and invariant to data ordering, whereas the predictive distribution, for example heavy tailed, is chosen separately without changing the estimator or algorithm. We derive the exact posterior variance under a known design and an asymptotically Gaussian approximation, and obtain the martingale posterior in closed form for Gaussian predictive distributions. Posterior draws are independent by construction, with a known truncation error, and require no Markov chain Monte Carlo. The construction extends to additive, mixed and Gaussian process models. In simulations and an analysis of NHANES triglyceride data, the method attains accuracy comparable to that of a fully Bayesian model with the same response distribution at a fraction of its computational cost.

papers.title: Alignment De-Identifies Without Aligning: A Congruence-Invariant Relational Gap in Cross-Subject Neural Representations
papers.abstract: In brain-computer interfaces, inter-subject variability remains a major challenge that limits decoding performance across users. Subject-wise alignment is widely used to improve cross-subject transfer of neural decoders, yet it is typically evaluated only through decoding accuracy, which cannot determine whether aligned representations share greater task-related structure. We therefore distinguish two questions that accuracy conflates: whether alignment removes subject-specific information and whether it makes the relational organization of task conditions more similar across individuals. Using three motor imagery-EEG cohorts, trials are represented as covariance matrices and aligned by recentering each subject's mean covariance to a common reference. Subject-specific information is quantified with a subject-identification probe, whereas relational structure is assessed using representational dissimilarity matrices (RDMs) computed from condition means with the affine-invariant Riemannian distance. We show that recentering leaves this distance, and therefore the resulting RDMs, unchanged. Consistent with this result, recentering reduces subject identification accuracy from 0.96 to chance level across all cohorts, while altering RDMs only at numerical precision. Cross-subject agreement in relational structure is significantly above zero but below the estimator's lower noise ceiling. Introducing an explicit similarity regularizer during training also fails to increase held-out agreement: the apparent reduction in between-subject differences is explained by a decline in the reliability ceiling rather than improved alignment. These findings show that eliminating subject identity is not equivalent to aligning relational geometry. More broadly, alignment claims must be interpreted relative to the invariances of both the distance and the statistic used to evaluate them.

papers.title: Brute-force molecular dynamics simulation of aging in amorphous Ge$_2$Sb$_2$Te$_5$
papers.abstract: Chalcogenide alloys such as the prototypical Ge$_2$Sb$_2$Te$_5$ compound are used in phase change electronic memories due to their ability to undergo a fast and reversible transition between the amorphous and crystalline phases upon heating. The amorphous phase is subject to aging that leads to an increase in the electrical resistance, which is detrimental to the operation of the devices. Using a machine learning interatomic potential, we have investigated the structural relaxations responsible for aging in amorphous Ge$_2$Sb$_2$Te$_5$ in molecular dynamics simulations at temperatures slightly below the glass transition. The aging simulation, lasting about 100 ns, follows an equilibration of 24 ns at 400 K. During aging we observed an enhancement of the Peierls distortion in axial bonds which is a typical feature of these alloys that we relate to the widening of the electronic band gap computed within Density Functional Theory in smaller aged amorphous models. We also observed a marked reduction of the atomic mobility with an increase of the bond lifetimes during aging. However, we do not see a reduction in homopolar bonds, which are expected to be absent in the ideal aged glass and which should be removed on a much longer time scale.

papers.title: Prediction-Error-Tightened MPC for Socially Compliant Crowd Navigation
papers.abstract: Autonomous navigation of mobile robots in crowded environments, while preserving pedestrians' psychological comfort, requires distinguishing pedestrians from other obstacles, predicting their future motion, and accounting for uncertainty in the predicted trajectories of both pedestrians and the robot. This work extends a previous MPC framework by integrating obstacle and pedestrian detection, Koopman-based motion prediction, and online prediction-error estimation directly within the collision-avoidance mechanism. To reduce collision-avoidance complexity in crowded scenarios, nearby obstacles are aggregated, thereby reducing the number of collision-avoidance constraints. Simulation studies evaluate the prediction-error margins and the computational benefits of semantics-aware aggregation. In a paired 300-seed closed-loop comparison with a moving generic obstacle, Markov residual tightening reduces the fraction of runs with physical contact from $10.0\%$ to $1.33\%$, at a mean travel-time cost of $0.68$ s. In a separate crowd-navigation semantic ablation, the offline robot-footprint/personal-space overlap occupies $2.11\%$ of observed time with pedestrian-aware handling versus $22.84\%$ with generic-obstacle handling.

papers.title: Poisson and Jacobi structures on quadratic Lie algebras
papers.abstract: We study Poisson and Jacobi structures compatible with quadratic structures on finite-dimensional Lie algebras, mostly over fields of characteristic zero. Building on the theory of generalized double extensions, we give necessary and sufficient reconstruction criteria for the skew operators preserving a marked isotropic ideal, allowing degenerate operators, a nonabelian quadratic quotient, and the full generalized extension data. Recalling the characterization of quadratic Poisson structures in terms of skew-symmetric solutions of the classical Yang--Baxter equation, we combine the ambient bracket reconstruction of Kostant and Meyer with prescribed symplectic leaf data to reconstruct Poisson structures whose characteristic subalgebra is nondegenerate for the quadratic form. We express the standard algebraic Jacobi equations through the invariant form and obtain analogous reconstruction results for nondegenerate characteristic subalgebras. Particular attention is given to the contact and locally conformally symplectic cases. A common cochain framework identifies the remaining scalar obstruction in third cohomology in the Poisson case and in the Jacobi branch whose Euler element belongs to the marked ideal, with coefficients in a one dimensional module in the latter case. Our reconstruction results yield systematic procedures for constructing quadratic Poisson structures in dimension $n+2k$ from those in dimension $n$, and recover the earlier quadratic symplectic extension formulas when the Poisson operator is invertible. Explicit examples illustrate the applicability of the theory, including oscillator algebras, the five-dimensional Lie algebra $A_{5,3}$, and Poisson structures associated with the curvature tensor of a bi-invariant metric.

papers.title: Some families of birational cubic and Verra fourfolds
papers.abstract: We study the birational relationship between cubic fourfolds and Verra fourfolds, which are double covers of the product of two projective planes. We show that in?nitely many divisors in the moduli space of cubic fourfolds containing a plane parametrize cubic fourfolds birational to Verra fourfolds. Our approach relies on the geometry of quadric surface bundles and their associated K3 surfaces, together with the study of Brauer classes. We also investigate two particularly interesting families, providing explicit geometric descriptions and equations for the associated varieties. In one case, the cubic fourfolds have two planes and the two projections from these planes directly show the existence of birational isomorphisms with Verra fourfolds.

papers.title: Climate Temporal Temperature Prediction via an Adaptive Stacked Bidirectional Residual Mamba Network
papers.abstract: Accurate temperatures forecasting relies on traditional meteorological parameters that are essential for monitoring weather informatics and guiding forecasting efforts. This study presents Deep DualMamba, a novel deep learning framework for temporal temperature prediction, built upon an enhanced variant of the recently proposed Mamba network. Unlike conventional Transformer-based architectures, which dominate foundation models but suffer from computational inefficiencies on long sequences, Deep DualMamba leverages selective structured state space models (SSMs) to achieve both scalability and performance. We identify a core limitation of prior subquadratic-time models-namely, their inability to perform long-term and robust forecasting and introduce two key innovations. First, we propose an adaptive bidirectional Mamba as encoders to learn complex and efficient features. Second, we develop a hardware-aware, parallel recurrent algorithm to compensate for the loss of convolutional efficiency, ensuring practical viability at scale. Last, the Deep DualMamba's approximation ability and convergence is theoretical analyzed. These design choices culminate in a simplified, attention- and MLP-free neural architecture that exhibits linear complexity with sequence length and significantly improved inference throughput. To demonstrate its applicability in climate informatics, we implement a full forecasting pipeline using historical meteorological data from UK monitoring stations.

papers.title: Large Language Models as Digital Twins: a Distribution-Aware Questionnaire-Based Evaluation
papers.abstract: This paper investigates whether Large Language Models can answer a personality questionnaire as a specific individual would. Given a user's social-media posts, the model completes the BFI-2-60 Big Five questionnaire as that user. The predicted responses are converted into trait scores and compared with the user's actual scores. We evaluate GPT-4, Gemma, Llama 3.1, and Mistral on the MyPersonality dataset. To determine whether predictions reflect information from the user's writing, we compare them with answers produced without user text and with values derived from general population tendencies. We measure prediction error across all users and separately for individuals with low, intermediate, and high trait scores. We also test whether an LLM can express an explicit personality profile when given only the target Big Five scores, without user text, and examine how predictions change as more text is provided. The results show that user text does not consistently improve performance. Models perform better near the middle of the trait distribution, while at the lower and upper ends they often remain close to central values or perform well at one end but poorly at the other. When given an explicit profile, GPT-4 most clearly translates trait information into consistent questionnaire responses, particularly for Extraversion and Neuroticism. Increasing context does not systematically reduce error: open-source models fluctuate more, whereas GPT-4 remains comparatively stable. Overall, the evaluated models do not consistently reproduce the questionnaire behavior of specific individuals.

papers.title: A locally complete family of Kummer type hyperk\"ahler fourfolds
papers.abstract: We construct a 4-dimensional family of projective hyperk\"ahler fourfolds of Kummer type. A general member of this family can be described as an irreducible component of a complete intersection of Heisenberg-invariant cubics in an 8-dimensional projective space. Several properties of the corresponding moduli space are also obtained. Our arguments rely on specializing to the case of generalized Kummer fourfolds of genus-two Jacobians, and make use of classical results dating back to Burkhardt and Coble.

authors.name: Franco Giovenzana
authors.institution: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique

papers.title: Complete critical metrics for the quadratic scalar curvature functional: examples and rigidity
papers.abstract: We study complete critical metrics for the quadratic scalar curvature functional \[ g\mapsto\int_M S_g^2\,\dv_g, \] with criticality understood under compactly supported variations, focusing on rigidity phenomena and nontrivial examples. In dimension three, we prove that every complete critical metric is scalar-flat, without any additional assumption. In dimension four, we construct complete non-Einstein critical metrics with bounded, nonconstant negative scalar curvature. In every dimension $n\geq5$, we show that either $S_g\equiv 0$ or $S_g<0$ everywhere, and a new argument proves scalar-flatness whenever $S_g \in L^p$ for some $0<p\leq P_n$, where $P_n>2$ is an explicit threshold. Moreover, we construct complete critical metrics with bounded, negative scalar curvature, decaying to zero at infinity. These examples establish the optimality of our rigidity threshold $P_n$ in dimension six and in every dimension $n\geq10$. To the best of our knowledge, these are the first complete critical metrics for this functional that are neither scalar-flat nor Einstein.

papers.title: Topological Entropy of Group Cellular Automata is Effectively Computable
papers.abstract:
Topological entropy is a fundamental invariant of dynamical systems, quantifying their complexity. For cellular automata, however, determining topological entropy is generally algorithmically intractable. We study group cellular automata, namely cellular automata over a finite group alphabet whose global map is a group endomorphism.
  In dimension one, we decompose topological entropy into two one-sided components describing information propagating from the left and from the right in space--time. We introduce finite families of left and right traces and prove that the entropy is the sum of their growth rates. Hence, the entropy is completely determined by the growth rate of a fixed-width family of space--time patterns. This reduction from arbitrarily large windows to uniformly bounded width yields an effective procedure for computing the entropy. In particular, the entropy of every one-dimensional group cellular automaton is the logarithm of a positive integer.
  Using Pontryagin duality and the Bridge Theorem between topological and algebraic entropy, we also derive an explicit formula for linear cellular automata over $(\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z})^n$ in terms of their characteristic polynomial. Moreover, in every dimension $D\geq 2$, a group cellular automaton is either equicontinuous with zero entropy or sensitive to initial conditions with infinite entropy. Combined with decidability of equicontinuity, this implies that topological entropy is effectively computable from the local rule in every dimension.
  Thus, group cellular automata form a natural nontrivial class in which algebraic structure restores computability of topological entropy.

papers.title: Evaluating Pretrained Language Semantics for Structured EHR Prediction Tasks
papers.abstract: Structured Electronic Health Records (EHR) models typically treat each clinical concept as a dataset-specific token, discarding the natural-language semantics associated with the event. As a result, relationships between concepts must largely be learned from EHR co-occurrence, without directly exploiting any prior semantic knowledge. We investigate how pretrained causal language models can be adapted for longitudinal EHR prediction by developing tEHR. Here, we represent events with their natural language description and use this text stream to apply EHR-adaptive continued pretraining, followed by task-specific discriminative fine-tuning using LoRA, utilising the LLM as a longitudinal patient-encoder. We evaluate this approach across four prediction tasks on the MIMIC-IV dataset and pancreatic cancer prediction on the CPRD dataset at 1 to 12 month horizons, with tEHR using the Mistral-7B-v0.3 backbone achieving the strongest overall performance. Ablations show that performance declines when clinical descriptions are removed or misaligned, when numerical values are omitted, and when either stage of adaptation is removed, while explicit elapsed-time descriptions provide little additional benefit. Analysis of the learned patient representations further reveals clinically coherent structure associated with distinct patterns of disease risk and clinical history.

authors.name: Alessandra Russo
authors.institution: Fondazione IRCCS Istituto Nazionale dei Tumori

papers.title: An Invariant Neural-Network Eddy-Viscosity Closure with Iterative Solver Coupling for Molten Salt Fast Reactor Thermal-Hydraulics
papers.abstract: System thermal-hydraulics codes such as the System Analysis Module (SAM) close turbulence on coarse meshes with algebraic zero-equation mixing-length models. These models cannot represent the non-equilibrium turbulence, flow separation, and large-scale recirculation of open-cavity advanced reactors. We develop an invariant neural-network eddy-viscosity closure for SAM and apply it to the Molten Salt Fast Reactor (MSFR). The closure predicts the turbulent kinetic energy and timescale of each element from the flow and geometry of its neighbors, without solving turbulence transport equations. The resulting non-negative eddy viscosity enters the implicit diffusive operator, which keeps the momentum equations well conditioned. We prove that the closure is exactly invariant to translation, Galilean boost, rotation, reflection, and neighbor ordering. A network trained on high-order Nek5000 fields sees a different feature distribution on the coarse SAM mesh. We remove this covariate shift by iteratively retraining the network on SAM flow states against fixed Nek5000 targets. For a held-out steady state, the coupled closure reproduces the single recirculation cell and eddy-viscosity plume of the Nek5000 reference. In a 120 s pump-coastdown transient, it halves the velocity error of the mixing-length model, from 37.6% to 17.7%, and matches the Nek5000 eddy viscosity with a time-averaged relative error of 12%. The remaining velocity error comes from the coarse mesh. The coupled transient takes about 0.2 core-hours, compared with about 330 core-hours for Nek5000. The results show that the closure can recover two-equation RANS turbulence behavior in a coarse-mesh system code at a small fraction of the CFD cost.

papers.title: Spatiotemporal learning improves quantification of pore-space evolution and fluid displacement
papers.abstract: Pore-space evolution and fluid displacement influence how rocks transmit and store fluids, affecting geological carbon storage, underground hydrogen storage and groundwater contaminant transport. A single time-resolved micro-CT experiment may produce tens to hundreds of three-dimensional images, and segmentation is required to quantify physical properties and run image-based simulations. Traditional methods such as thresholding perform poorly on noisy, low-contrast images and need manual adjustment per image; 3D deep learning networks segment each image without temporal information, so their errors vary between images and could be mistaken for physical change. Here we introduce a transformer-based 4D segmentation framework combining spatial and temporal information. It uses sequential images to resolve ambiguous phase assignments and separate physical change from segmentation error. The method is tested on images of mineral dissolution: it measures pore-volume growth and rock boundaries more accurately than an equivalent 3D model that ignores temporal information. It also captures the increase in permeability verified against reference segmentations and flow simulations. The advantage transfers to another dissolution sample without retraining. On two other datasets of fluid displacement, it reduces spurious changes in predicted rock and porosity fluctuations and accurately identifies filling events. Spatiotemporal segmentation turns sequences of hundreds of three-dimensional images into more reliable quantitative measurements of pore-space evolution and fluid displacement without per-image parameter adjustment to support the analysis of time-resolved CT imaging.

papers.title: FORGE: Force-Aware Multi-Granularity Control for Efficient Humanoid Loco-Manipulation
papers.abstract: Humanoid loco-manipulation requires coordinated locomotion, balance regulation, and manipulation under frequent contacts, making teleoperated demonstration collection difficult: a practical controller must simultaneously provide precision, stability, and contact awareness. We propose FORGE, a force-aware multi-granularity control system with a coarse-to-fine command space spanning velocity navigation, planar foot placement, wrist-pose tracking, and optional force-conditioning inputs. Policy training requires no full-body human motion trajectories or joint-angle references; deployment consumes only sparse bilateral wrist poses relative to the pelvis, coarse motion commands, and optional desired wrist-load inputs. For sustained contact, FORGE combines a momentum observer with a learned correction trained using simulator contact-force supervision. At deployment, it estimates low-frequency, wrist-equivalent interaction forces from proprioception and reconstructed low-level arm PD torques, without wrist force/torque sensors. A quasi-static virtual-target loop uses this estimate and an optional desired applied-force input to adapt the wrist target. A frozen locomotion prior and asymmetric residual actions stabilize manipulation-induced whole-body corrections. Experiments evaluate unified-control stability, task-space tracking, quasi-static wrist-equivalent force estimation, squeezing forces during sustained contact with a rigid box, and downstream diffusion-policy execution of a squat-and-lift task across payload conditions. Website: https://bb0928.github.io/forge/.

authors.institution: Nanjing University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Diversification under Global Competition: A Cutoff-Induced Localization Mechanism
papers.abstract: Niche differentiation promotes biological diversity but does not necessarily eliminate competition for shared limiting resources. What determines the extent of diversity when evolutionary diversification takes place under such constraints? We investigate this question using a simple, analytically tractable model combining mutations in continuous trait space, local competition, and global competition for shared resources. We show that, without an establishment threshold, the population spreads indefinitely in trait space even as its total abundance approaches a finite limit. In contrast, an arbitrarily small establishment threshold allows a stable localized distribution. Together with mortality induced by global competition, the threshold creates bistability, and global feedback drives the system exponentially close to the Maxwell point, where an isolated invasion front is stationary. The resulting soliton has height $H\propto\varepsilon^{2/3}$ and width $W\propto\varepsilon^{-2/3}$. Simulations with discrete individuals reveal an archipelago of fluctuating clusters whose spatial extent eventually reaches statistical saturation, unlike the continuous deterministic soliton. Nevertheless, an effective cutoff $\varepsilon_{\mathrm{eff}}\simeq0.8/(N\sqrt{\mu})$ reproduces the observed scaling of the population mass deficit. Remarkably, both occupied trait-site richness and effective species richness exhibit approximately the same scaling as the deterministic soliton width. Thus, deterministic cutoff theory captures global diversity scaling despite failing to reproduce the community's spatial organization.

papers.title: Influence of Alfven wave turbulence dissipation in stellar winds of the Sun and M dwarfs
papers.abstract: The physics of M-dwarf stellar winds is increasingly being investigated within the framework of wave-driven models. In the case of the solar wind, Alfven-wave turbulence (AWT) is believed to play a crucial role in heating and accelerating the plasma. In this study, we perform one-dimensional magnetohydrodynamic simulations of the solar and M-dwarf winds using a model that incorporates shock heating generated by mode conversion and treats AWT as an optional component. For the solar wind, we confirm that including AWT reproduces the observed predominance of outwardly propagating Alfven waves, supporting the role of turbulent dissipation in driving the wind. We further validate this AWT-driven solar wind directly against Parker Solar Probe observations, finding good agreement in both the location of the Alfven point and the level of the normalized cross helicity in the fast solar wind. In M-dwarf simulations, we find that AWT dominates the overall heating budget within the investigated parameter range. A parameter survey of coronal magnetic field strength reveals that the dependence of the mass-loss rate on Bcor differs qualitatively between cases with and without AWT, highlighting the importance of chromospheric dissipation. In the absence of AWT, the resulting mass-loss rates are broadly consistent with previous studies and observations. In contrast, when AWT is included, the mass-loss rate is significantly reduced because turbulent dissipation decreases the Alfven-wave (Poynting) flux entering the corona. These results suggest that the effects of chromospheric turbulence play a crucial role in modeling M-dwarf winds.

papers.title: Moving Beyond the DRW Model: Learning Quasar Variability with Generative Models
papers.abstract: The optical continuum variability of quasars is often described by a damped random walk (DRW) model, with characteristic damping timescales $\tau_{\rm DRW}$ of hundreds of days and amplitudes $\sigma_{\rm DRW}$ of $\mathcal{O}(0.1)$ magnitudes. This model has been widely used as a null hypothesis to assess the significance of periodic signals in quasar light curves in the search for supermassive black hole binaries, the significance of extreme quasar variability like tidal disruption events (TDEs) and changing-look (CL) quasars, or to model time lags in reverberation mapping. However, the DRW model is known to be incomplete, and an incorrect null hypothesis can lead to biased significance estimates. We investigate the impact of such null-hypothesis mis-specification on the detection of periodic signals in synthetic quasar light curves and introduce the generative model Nullasar, capable of learning quasar variability directly from time-series data. We demonstrate that Nullasar, trained with flow matching, can learn delicate statistical properties of stochastic light-curve variability without explicitly assuming any noise model. We further demonstrate that Nullasar can learn correlated distributions of noise parameters and generate new light-curve realizations from a range of deviations from the Gaussian DRW noise model, approximating parametric descriptions of stochastic processes. When used as a null hypothesis for detecting periodic signals in synthetic light curves, Nullasar performs comparably to fitting the correct DRW model to each light curve, and outperforms parametric fitting when the variability follows a more flexible AR(2) model. Finally, we identify practical limitations, including sensitivity to contamination of the training set by non-null signals, and show that projecting the conditioning vector of the model onto its leading principal components largely mitigates it.

papers.title: Steering Skyrmion Diffusion with Chiral Molecules
papers.abstract: Chiral molecules adsorbed on a magnetic film interact with its magnetization and can thereby alter the thermal motion of magnetic skyrmions. Here we develop a theoretical model in which an aligned layer of tilted molecules modifies the interfacial magnetic interactions according to its handedness. Within this model a skyrmion responds only to spatial variations of the coupling, so a uniform layer leaves its position unaffected, whereas boundaries and coverage gradients exert forces on it. Near a chiral region, these forces deflect the skyrmion transversely in a direction that reverses between enantiomers, which provides a direct signature of the chiral interaction. In extended periodic patterns, the same forces reshape the long-time diffusion, suppressing it in the direction in which the potential varies and enhancing it in the perpendicular direction. The net effect on the mean diffusion is set by the balance between the gyrotropic and dissipative responses of the skyrmion, as we show exactly for one-dimensional landscapes. Stochastic micromagnetic simulations and collective-coordinate calculations confirm these predictions and show how molecular orientation, spatial patterning, and skyrmion properties together determine the motion.

authors.institution: Institute of Science and Technology Austria

papers.title: The ZTF Variability Archive (ZVAR): Initial Data Release (DR1)
papers.abstract: The Zwicky Transient Facility (ZTF) has observed the northern sky observable from Palomar Observatory since March 2018, accumulating a median of a thousand photometric measurements across $gri$ for each of more than a billion sources. Among these billions of objects are millions of periodically variable stars, active galactic nuclei, stellar remnants, and substellar objects. We describe the initial data release (DR1) of the ZTF Variability Archive (ZVAR) which provides image difference forced photometry, candidate periods, and variability metrics for approximately 1.3 billion sources in ZTF having an identification in Pan-STARRS1 DR1 (PS1). The data cover the 5.37 year interval between March 2018 and July 2023. ZVAR is sensitive to periods between 5 minutes and 2.7 years. We also describe tools for accessing the ZVAR data.
