authors.institution: Institute of Science and Technology Austria

authors.name: Jan van Roestel
authors.institution: Institute of Science and Technology Austria

papers.title: Omakase: Execution Congestion Control through Conflict-Graph Integration in Multi-Proposer Blockchain
papers.abstract:
As multi-proposer protocols push consensus throughput, transaction execution has become the dominant bottleneck in blockchains. Layer-1 blockchains parallelize execution either pessimistically (Solana, Sui), requiring upfront state-access declarations and serializing contended transactions, or optimistically (Aptos, Sei, Monad), resolving dependencies at run time but suffering cascading aborts under contention. Both treat blocks in isolation, leaving inter-block parallelism unexploited and most cores idle.
  We introduce Omakase, a parallel execution framework that combines pre-execution, inter-block conflict-graph integration, and graph-aware Optimistic Concurrency Control (OCC). Replicas use idle cores to pre-execute only the blocks they propose, spreading prediction work across concurrent proposers. After building per-block conflict graphs and identifying their hot resources, a greedy scheduler integrates graphs across the blocks committed in a round, keeping an integration only when a lightweight balance heuristic predicts a parallelism gain. A graph-aware OCC executor then runs the integrated graph, admitting transactions in dependency order, which eliminates aborts when the predicted graph is exact and reduces re-executions when it is not.
  On 15,000 Ethereum mainnet blocks (~2.4M transactions) and synthetic workloads with configurable contention, Omakase reaches a 2.47x speedup over sequential execution, well above single-block OCC and graph-aware baselines. Against the strongest alternative, which runs the whole round as one optimistic window, Omakase matches mean throughput but is markedly more stable under high contention, because integration bounds how much optimistic work is in flight: this is the congestion control of our title. Integration is not free, but overlapping it with execution across rounds hides 94% of its measured cost in the validator pipeline.

authors.name: Ray Neiheiser
authors.institution: Institute of Science and Technology Austria

papers.title: Influence of Assortativity on the SICP Spreading Process in Hypergraphs
papers.abstract: Many real-world systems involve group interactions that cannot be captured by pairwise graphs. They can be better represented by hypergraphs where each hyperedge could connect an arbitrary number of nodes. The Susceptible-Infected Contact Process (SICP) has been proposed to model the spreading of information and epidemics on hypergraphs. However, how higher-order topological properties of a hypergraph influence the SICP spreading process remains understudied. In this paper, we examine the impact of hypergraph assortativity based on the Neighborhood Coefficient (NC)-the average size of hyperedges incident to a node-on the SICP spreading process. By introducing a low-complexity measure of hypergraph assortativity grounded in analysis of variance, we apply hyperdegree-preserving rewirings to real-world networks and synthetic hypergraph models to tune their assortativity. We find and explain why lower NC assortativity yields higher average epidemic prevalence and lower prevalence variance across different seed selections. This phenomenon is evident when hyperdegree-preserving rewirings are applied to real-world networks with heterogeneous topological structures, but it is largely absent when comparing synthetic random hypergraphs to their rewired counterparts.

papers.title: Inheritance of Connectivity: Modeling Higher-Order Dynamic Networks with the Birth-Death Process
papers.abstract: Higher-order networks extend pairwise interactions to represent group relationships and provide a useful framework for modeling complex systems. Understanding their dynamic evolution is important for explaining emergent structural and functional properties. However, constructing dynamic higher-order network models with stable topology remains challenging. In this paper, we propose a higher-order dynamic network model based on an inheritance-based deletion (IBAD) mechanism, which probabilistically redistributes connections when nodes or hyperedges are removed. The model combines birth-death dynamics with preferential attachment, enabling the analysis of evolving higher-order systems. Inheritance is guided by a Gaussian similarity measure based on the distance between degree histories. We derive stationary population distributions and conditional relations for connection retention and degree evolution. Simulation results show that the model generates networks with statistically stable node and hyperedge populations and heterogeneous degree distributions. The degree distributions and local clustering can be adjusted through the node and hyperedge attachment parameters. Comparisons with alternative mechanisms show that inheritance enhances connectivity relative to direct deletion, while the similarity measure influences degree heterogeneity. Comparisons with empirical networks from ecological and communication systems quantify distributional differences using Jensen-Shannon and Kullback-Leibler divergences and reveal discrepancies in clustering and within-hyperedge node-pair counts. These results provide a framework for studying population stability and structural evolution in dynamic higher-order networks.

papers.title: Integer Programming with Polyhedral Constraints on the Image
papers.abstract:
We generalize integer programming to the setting in which the image $A \mathbf{x}$ is restricted to an explicitly given rational polyhedron $P$. That is, we solve $\min\{\mathbf{c}^{\mathsf T}\mathbf{x}:A\mathbf{x}\in P, \mathbf{x}\in\mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}^n\}$, where $A\in\mathbb{Z}^{d\times n}$ and $P$ is an explicitly given rational polyhedron. We present a randomized algorithm running in time $(d\Delta)^{O(d)}\operatorname{poly}(L)$ in this regime, where $\Delta := \|A\|_\infty$ and $L$ is the binary input length. This running time matches that of the best-known parameterized algorithms for integer programming, due to Eisenbrand and Weismantel and to Jansen and Rohwedder, and improves on the $O(d^2)$ exponent achieved by Dadush, L\'eonard, Rohwedder, and Verschae in a more general setting.
  This result enables several applications, including exact algorithms for integer programming and unbounded knapsack in which the consumed resources $A\mathbf{x}$ must satisfy arbitrary additional linear constraints. We also obtain a randomized fixed-parameter algorithm for Unbounded Subset Sum parameterized by the doubling constant, resolving an open problem of Randolph and W\k{e}grzycki. For integer programs with $m$ constraints and bounded row doubling, we obtain an $f(C,m)n^{O(m)}\operatorname{poly}(L)$-time algorithm and show that the dependence on $m$ in the exponent of $n$ is necessary under $\mathsf{W[1]}\ne\mathsf{FPT}$.

papers.title: RGB-D SLAM on the Edge: Benchmarking and Profiling RTAB-Map and ORB-SLAM3 on the Raspberry Pi 5
papers.abstract: Micro aerial vehicles that operate without GPS often run SLAM on ARM-based edge boards, yet there is little published data on how standard RGB-D SLAM systems behave on such hardware. We benchmark RTAB-Map and ORB-SLAM3 on the Raspberry Pi 5 using six TUM RGB-D sequences at three image resolutions, recording tracking coverage, trajectory error, time per frame, memory, CPU load and temperature for every run, and we profile both systems at the stage and function level. RTAB-Map was configured to process and keep every frame, so its back end runs on every frame rather than at its default rate of 1 Hz. On the sequences that every configuration tracked, its front end takes 38-74 ms per frame and its full pipeline 150-462 ms, compared with 13-45 ms and 26-62 ms for ORB-SLAM3. RTAB-Map's main cost is optimizing a pose graph that keeps growing, because its working memory is unbounded by default; ORB-SLAM3's local bundle adjustment costs about as much as its tracking but runs in a parallel thread. At quarter resolution, both systems lose tracking on most sequences, and runs that lose tracking finish sooner and report lower error on the poses they keep, so time and accuracy must be read alongside coverage. Timing is repeatable to within 1-5%, but trajectory error varies by up to 27% between identical runs, so the accuracy differences between the two systems are inconclusive. No thermal throttling occurred.

authors.institution: All India Shri Shivaji Memorial Society College of Engineering

authors.name: Jaideep Joshi
authors.institution: International Institute for Applied Systems Analysis

authors.name: Rohit Saluja
authors.institution: All India Institute of Medical Sciences

papers.title: Piecewise Interpretations in Many-Sorted Logic
papers.abstract: Piecewise interpretations, introduced by Visser, generalize ordinary interpretations between first-order theories by allowing formulae to be interpreted using disjoint unions of definable sets. This makes it possible to capture natural constructions, such as the projective completion of an affine plane, but also leads to a notion of equivalence of theories, namely piecewise bi-interpretability. We develop the theory of piecewise interpretations systematically in the many-sorted setting. Each piecewise interpretation induces a semantic dual, a functor between categories of models. In addition, we introduce a syntactic notion of morphism between piecewise interpretations, which likewise has a semantic dual. Using these semantic duals, we collect theories, piecewise interpretations, and morphisms between them into a bicategory, in particular defining a well-behaved notion of composition of interpretations, associative up to coherent isomorphism. As an application, we consider a familiar idea, championed by Quine, namely that one can replace any many-sorted theory with a corresponding single-sorted one by replacing sorts with sortal predicates. We show that this leads to a biequivalence between the developed bicategories of theories with finitely many sorts and single-sorted theories, thereby providing an argument for the dispensability of sorts.

papers.title: Face rings and the cohomology of unions of Schubert varieties
papers.abstract: The cohomology ring of a union of Schubert varieties $X_{W}=\bigcup_{w\in W}X_w,$ for $W\subseteq S_n$, in the complete flag variety is well known to be a quotient of the coinvariant ring $R_n$. We determine exactly when the ideal defining this quotient is generated by squarefree monomials, i.e. when it can be identified with the image of a Stanley-Reisner ideal $I_\Delta$ in $R_n$. We prove that a single Schubert variety $X_w$ has this property exactly when $w\in S_n$ avoids a set of seven patterns, and in this case we describe the corresponding doubly-pruned simplicial complex $\Delta$. We then show this is equivalent to $X_w$ being cut out of the complete flag variety by particular inclusion conditions on the pieces of the flag. We prove these complexes are vertex decomposable, and are Cohen-Macaulay precisely when $X_w$ is smooth. We then give a closed formula for the Poincar\'e polynomial of $X_w$. For unions $X_W$, pattern avoidance is necessary but no longer sufficient, and we prove a necessary and sufficient condition we call prunable that describes how the individual complexes associated to each $w\in W$ may be glued in the union. Quotients of $R_n$ by squarefree monomial ideals appear naturally in the Adams-Reiner conjecture on resolutions of Stanley-Reisner rings over certain parameter rings. We prove their conjecture for a family of simplicial complexes that includes the doubly-pruned complexes.

papers.title: Higher order convergence rate in probability for approximations of the stochastic Burgers and Cahn-Hilliard equation
papers.abstract: We consider temporal approximations of stochastic PDEs driven by additive space-time white noise, with nonlinearities that may lose both integrability and regularity. Our key examples are the stochastic Burgers equation in dimension 1 and the stochastic Cahn-Hilliard equation in dimensions $\leq 3$. We show that the accelerated exponential Euler scheme achieves a rate of convergence in probability that is well beyond the state of the art: arbitrarily close to $3/4$ in the case of Burgers and $1-d/8$ in the case of Cahn-Hilliard.

authors.name: Ana Djurdjevac
authors.institution: Mathematical Institute of the Slovak Academy of Sciences

papers.title: Towards Better Legal Reasoning LLMs: Signal Balancing and Reward Scheduling
papers.abstract: In the legal domain, LLMs can improve reliability and interpretability by generating explicit reasoning traces. However, training LLMs to produce high-quality reasoning traces remains challenging. Existing supervised fine-tuning methods struggle when reasoning traces are significantly longer than final answers, as the learning signal for the answer becomes diluted. Meanwhile, reinforcement learning methods such as Group Relative Policy Optimization also have several limitations, including costly reward design, performance plateaus, and reward hacking. We therefore propose a two-stage training framework. In Stage I, JurisCoT-SFT employs a length-normalized dual objective to balance learning signals between reasoning traces and final answers. In Stage II, Lifecycle-Aware Backtrackable Policy Optimization dynamically evaluates and retires auxiliary reward signals based on their impact on final evaluation objectives, enabling efficient reward utilization. Our framework substantially improves legal reasoning performance on relevant tasks selected from multiple legal benchmarks, including ChJGBench, LawBench, and LegalBench. Experimental results demonstrate consistent improvements in both reasoning trace quality and final answer accuracy, while our models remain competitive with larger models.

papers.title: The periodic Short-Pulse equation by the Riemann-Hilbert problem approach
papers.abstract: In this paper, we formulate a Riemann--Hilbert problem framework -- based on the Unified Transform Method (Fokas method) -- for the Short Pulse equation posed on a periodic domain. Under the stated spectral and reconstruction regularity assumptions, we show that a local solution of the periodic initial-value problem can be reconstructed from the solution of a suitably defined Riemann--Hilbert problem, whose jump data are explicitly characterized by spectral functions associated with the initial condition.

authors.name: Dmitry Shepelsky
authors.institution: B. Verkin Institute for Low Temperature Physics and Engineering of the National Academy of Sciences of Ukraine

papers.title: Splitting Number at Singular Cardinals
papers.abstract: We study the splitting number at singular cardinals with emphasis on what we call the reduction to the cofinality problem: whether $\mathfrak{s}_{\kappa} = \mathfrak{s}_{\mathrm{cf}(\kappa)}$ holds for a singular cardinal $\kappa$. Our main tool is the transfinite logarithm function $\mathrm{log}_{2}(\mu) := \min \{ \lambda \in \mathrm{card} \colon \mu \leq 2^{\lambda} \}$ defined for every infinite cardinal $\mu$. We prove that the reduction holds, and in fact $\mathfrak{s}_{\kappa} = \mathrm{log}_{2}(\mathrm{cf}(\kappa))$, whenever $\mathrm{cf}(\kappa)$ is uncountable and not weakly compact. When $\mathrm{cf}(\kappa) = \aleph_{0}$, we show that $\mathfrak{s}_{\kappa} = \mathfrak{s}$ provided that $\mathfrak{s} \leq \log_{2}(\kappa)$, while the failure of the reduction is consistent with $\mathrm{ZFC}$. When $\mathrm{cf}(\kappa)$ is weakly compact, we use a model constructed by Ben-Neria and Gitik to prove that, under suitable large cardinals hypothesis, $\mathfrak{s}_{\kappa} < \mathfrak{s}_{\mathrm{cf}(\kappa)}$ is consistent. Furthermore, we show that the consistency strength of $\mathrm{ZFC} \, +$"$\exists \kappa \in \mathrm{card} [\mathrm{cf}(\kappa) > \aleph_{0} \wedge \mathfrak{s}_{\kappa} < \mathfrak{s}_{\mathrm{cf}(\kappa)}]$'' is at least that of the negation of the singular cardinal hypothesis. Finally, we study the cofinality of $\mathfrak{s}_{\kappa}$, extending several results about the cofinality of $\mathfrak{s}$ to the uncountable setting. In particular, we show in $\mathrm{ZFC}$ that there are regular cardinals $\kappa$ such that $\mathfrak{s}_{\kappa}$ is singular, partially answering an open question posed by Fischer and Soukup.

papers.title: Where to Generate Touch: Do Image Latents Preserve Material Recognition?
papers.abstract: Generated touch could extend robot learning beyond recorded contacts. A tactile generator needs a latent space, and we choose one by testing whether a material classifier trained on real GelSight presses still works on encode-decode reconstructions from pretrained image models. On ObjectFolder Real, the classifier loses 6.5 to 9.7 points on reconstructions from three 16x discrete tokenizers and 0.3 points on those from the Stable Diffusion VAE (SD-VAE). The 16x tokenizers again lose far more on Touch and Go and on DIGIT object recognition (YCB-Slide). Retraining the classifier on reconstructions, with no new labels, narrows the discrete gap. SD-VAE reconstructions also keep object identity, with 76.7% object-matching accuracy against 78.9% for real touch and 67.0% for MAGVIT-v2. We therefore select SD-VAE latents and show a photo-to-touch generator trained in them. Code will be released upon acceptance.

authors.name: Wanghao Ye
authors.institution: Zhejiang University of Science and Technology

authors.name: Meng Liu
authors.institution: Xi'an University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Rigid Theories
papers.abstract: A structure is rigid if it admits no non-trivial automorphisms. We investigate an analogous invariance property for first-order theories, with relative interpretations playing the role of morphisms. A theory $T$ is called rigid if and only if every self-interpretation of $T$ is definably isomorphic to the identity interpretation. Extending work of Pakhomov and Zapryagaev (2020) on Presburger Arithmetic, we establish rigidity for Successor Arithmetic and Skolem Arithmetic (with respect to one-dimensional interpretations), True Arithmetic, and the theories of fields $\mathrm{RCF}$ and $\mathrm{ACF}$. By contrast, $\mathrm{PA}$ and $\mathrm{ZF}$ admit infinitely many self-interpretations, though both remain rigid with respect to (co-)retractions. Our main negative result is that $\mathrm{ZFC}$ has no consistent rigid extension in its own language. We compare rigidity with categoricity, model rigidity, completeness, and solidity, showing it to be independent of the first three, and indicate the relevance of rigidity to questions about semantic determinacy.

papers.title: Many more odd zeta values are irrational
papers.abstract: We prove that for any sufficiently large odd integer $s$, there exist at least \[ 2.78 \, \sqrt{\frac{s \log\log s}{\log s}} \] irrational values among $\zeta(3), \zeta(5), \dots, \zeta(s)$, where $\zeta$ is the Riemann zeta function. This improves on the best known estimate by a constant factor times $\sqrt{ \log\log s}$. The proof combines the elimination technique and an arithmetic lemma of Fischler--Sprang--Zudilin, the hypergeometric constructions of Lai--Yu, and the Hankel determinant method that appeared in the proof that $\zeta(5)$ is irrational posted by Fauzan on September 17, 2026.

authors.name: Stephane Fischler
authors.institution: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique

papers.title: Proliferating against the current: how multistep branching nucleation can sort microtubule polarity in the spindle
papers.abstract: The spindle, which segregates chromosomes during cell division, is a paradigm of cytoskeletal self-organization: a highly ordered structure that persists for hours is assembled from dynamic microtubules that branch, grow, slide, and turn over within tens of seconds. Its microtubules point inward, with minus ends clustered at the poles and plus ends extending toward the chromosomes at the center of the structure. In large meiotic spindles this arrangement is puzzling, since microtubules nucleate near the chromosomes and grow at their plus ends much faster than motors slide them backward. One would therefore expect the plus ends, rather than the minus ends, to radiate outward. Here, we propose a resolution to this seeming paradox through a kinetic model that integrates the core filament-level processes. When branching complexes assemble with a sufficient delay, for instance through several sequential rate-limiting steps, they accumulate on old microtubule lattice sites near the backward-sliding minus ends of mother microtubules. Each generation is then born farther back than the last, so the self-renewing population drifts toward the minus ends even though each filament's center advances toward its plus end. For the sliding and growth velocities measured in Xenopus egg extract spindles, a multistep mechanism requires at least four rate-limiting steps. The kinetic theory has a surprisingly amenable structure: the filament length configuration variable can be eliminated exactly, yielding a finite space-time hierarchy, and the direction of population drift follows from a general criterion comparing the mean lattice age at branching sites with the ratio of plus-end advance to sliding speed.

papers.title: Strong Lyndon Interpolation for Multi-Modal Logics with Converses: A Constructive Approach with Tree Sequents
papers.abstract: Grammar logics with converses are multi-modal logics that generalize tense logics and whose frame conditions are determined by context-free production rules. We study the strong Lyndon interpolation property (strong LIP) for these logics, which requires interpolants to respect both the polarities of propositional atoms and the indices of modalities. We show that the strong LIP properly strengthens the Lyndon interpolation property over grammar logics, since it fails for certain grammar logics with bridge axioms, i.e., path axioms relating modalities with distinct indices. We then prove that every bridge-free grammar logic, possibly extended with seriality axioms, has the strong LIP. This class includes the multi-modal tense logics obtained by imposing any combination of seriality, reflexivity, transitivity, symmetry, and Euclideanity on each pair of converse modalities. Our proof is constructive and purely syntactic, and is based on tree sequent calculi. Because standard methods for computing interpolants with tree and nested sequents may introduce modalities whose indices are not common to both sides of an implication, we introduce a novel tripartite partition method. It sorts the labels of a proof into common labels and labels private to the left or right component, and only lets relational atoms pointing to common labels contribute modalities to interpolants. Given a proof of an implication, our method computes a strong Lyndon interpolant together with proofs of its correctness.

papers.title: The Regular Cover Problem is NP-complete
papers.abstract: The regular cover problem is the following question: given a finite language $L$ and a $k\geq 0$, is there an acyclic regular grammar $G$ with at most $k$ productions that covers $L$, i.e., that satisfies $L(G) \supseteq L$. The study of this problem is motivated by applications in proof theory and automated deduction. The regular cover problem is known to be in NP. In this paper we show that it is NP-complete by reducing the vertex cover problem for graphs with maximum degree three to it.

papers.title: Scaling limits of Chebyshev polynomials at a hard edge
papers.abstract: Let $\mathsf{E}\subset\mathbb{R}$ be compact. We derive local scaling limits of the Chebyshev polynomials associated to $\mathsf{E}$ at a gap edge. We describe the scaling limits by a one parameter family of functions explicitly given by elliptic integrals. We show that for the union of two generic intervals all functions in this family are in fact attained as limits. As a consequence, we describe the local scaling behavior of the zeros of the Chebyshev polynomials at the gap edge.

papers.title: A binomial-adjusted $\theta$-trapezoidal tau-leaping method for chemical kinetic systems
papers.abstract: In Hu, Li and Min (2011), the authors propose a weak second order accurate $\theta$-trapezoidal method as an improvement to the classical tau-leaping method. However, for complex chemical kinetic systems their model's underlying analytical assumptions can fail to hold in practice, leading to a significant reduction in its computational effectiveness. Here we introduce a modification to the method which allows it to regain desirable convergence characteristics, both given the original and a relaxed version of the underlying assumptions. We confirm this improvement through a local error analysis and present numerical examples showing it consistently performs either better or comparable to the $\theta$-trapezoidal method.

authors.name: Sam McCallum
authors.institution: AITHYRA GmbH- Research Institute for Biomedical Artificial Intelligence (Austria)

papers.title: Dwarfs of Fire and Ice: UV-Irradiation-Driven Thermal Inversion, Disequilibrium Chemistry, and a Cloud-Free Atmosphere in a Strongly Irradiated Brown Dwarf Probed by JWST/NIRSpec Phase-Resolved Spectroscopy
papers.abstract: We present time-resolved JWST/NIRSpec PRISM spectrophotometry of the white dwarf (WD)-brown dwarf (BD) binary SDSS J141126.20+200911.1 (SDSS1411). Close WD-BD binaries provide powerful laboratories for studying the effects of stellar irradiation on substellar atmospheres because of their high companion-to-host flux ratios, short orbital periods, and intense UV irradiation from the WD. We measure strong wavelength-dependent variability, with day-night relative flux variations reaching ~280%. The SDSS1411B phase curves are well described by a second-order Fourier model, and correlations among the Fourier amplitudes suggest larger flux and temperature variations in the upper atmosphere. Non-irradiated forward models under chemical equilibrium do not reproduce the observed phase-resolved SDSS1411B spectra, indicating substantial departures from isolated-BD atmospheric structures. In contrast, atmospheric retrievals successfully reproduce both the dayside and nightside spectra. The retrievals reveal a prominent dayside temperature inversion, favor cloud-free atmospheres, and provide evidence for CO2 disequilibrium chemistry. An energy-budget analysis indicates low day-to-night heat redistribution efficiency and constrains the BD cooling age to ~3 Gyr, while the inferred BD radius is significantly more compact than predicted by BD evolutionary models. These results reveal the rich atmospheric dynamics and disequilibrium chemistry of a UV-irradiated BD and demonstrate the power of full-orbit JWST phase-resolved spectroscopy for constraining the atmospheric physics of strongly irradiated substellar objects.

papers.title: Complete enumeration of maximal T-curves in degrees eight and nine
papers.abstract: We use a highly parallelized backtracking algorithm implemented in CUDA to enumerate every compatible collection of Harnack splits in degrees eight and nine. By a theorem of Haas (1997) this yields every maximal T-curve. In this way, we find that exactly 38 real schemes of real plane algebraic curves of degree eight with 22 real components and 225 of degree nine with 29 real components are realized by combinatorial patchworking.

authors.name: Michael Joswig
authors.institution: Max Planck Institute for Mathematics in the Sciences

papers.title: Tight Algorithms for Conservative Finite-Valued CSPs Parameterized by Treewidth
papers.abstract:
We consider valued constraint satisfaction problems (VCSPs) with a fixed finite domain $D$ and a fixed finite constraint language $\Gamma$, in the setting where $\Gamma$ contains all crisp unary constraints (called hard lists) and the remaining cost functions are finite-valued. We call such a language a finite-valued hard-list language. Let $c_\Gamma$ be the size of the largest set $S\subseteq D$ such that $\Gamma$ can express (using the usual VCSP closure operations) a binary disequality function on elements of $S$. Our main result tightly connects the complexity of the problem parameterized by treewidth to this value $c_\Gamma$.
  (1) The problem can be solved in time $(c_\Gamma)^{\mathsf{tw}} \cdot (|I| + |\mathcal{T}|)^{O(1)}$ when given an instance $I$ with a tree decomposition $\mathcal{T}$ of width $\mathsf{tw}$ of the primal graph of $I$.
  (2) If $c_\Gamma \geq 2$, there is no such algorithm solving the problem in time $(c_\Gamma - \varepsilon)^{\mathsf{tw}} \cdot (|I| + |\mathcal{T}|)^{O(1)}$ for any $\varepsilon > 0$, unless the Primal Treewidth SETH (and hence CNF-SETH) fails.
  In particular, this gives a far-reaching generalization of a similar result of Esmer et al. [ESA 2024] on the optimization version of list homomorphism for graphs.

authors.name: George Osipov
authors.institution: N.D. Zelinsky Institute of Organic Chemistry

papers.title: Differential properties of Drinfeld modular forms
papers.abstract: We study the action of vector fields on the Drinfeld symmetric spaces on de Rham classes of the generic Drinfeld module. The resulting Kodaira-Spencer map is an isomorphism, and is described by the Jacobian matrix \(J := (\frac{\partial g_{j}}{\partial \omega_{i}})_{1 \leq i,j \leq r}\), where the \(g_{j}\) are the basic coefficient modular forms of rank \(r\). We show that \(J\) is the matrix inverse of the period matrix \(P\) that results from the de Rham theory of Drinfeld modules. We define the notion of Drinfeld modular differential form, which generalizes the transformation behavior of Drinfeld modular forms from functions to differential \(n\)-forms on the Drinfeld symmetric space \(\Omega^{r}\). The algebra \(\mathbf{M}^{(*)} = \bigoplus_{0 \leq n < r} \mathbf{M}^{(n)}\) of all such is provided with a Serre derivation \(D \colon \mathbf{M}^{(n)} \to \mathbf{M}^{(n+1)}\) from \(n\)-forms to \((n+1)\)-forms, where \(\mathbf{M}^{(0)} = \mathbf{M}\) is the algebra of customary modular forms for \(\mathrm{GL}(r, \mathbb{F}_{q}[T])\). We determine the structure of \(\mathbf{M}^{(*)}\), which turns out to be the exterior algebra \(\bigwedge (\mathbf{M}^{(1)})\) of the \(\mathbf{M}\)-module \(\mathbf{M}^{(1)}\).

papers.title: Goal Encoding in LLMs
papers.abstract: We investigate whether and how LLMs encode goals: internal neural representations that precede and guide action, and that are flexible enough to be realized through many different execution paths. We construct a coding setting with multiple sub-tasks that allows us to evaluate goal-seeking behavior and the selection of sub-goals. In this setting, we localize an encoding of the next sub-goal in the outputs of a sparse set of attention heads. The same heads can be used to decode the LM's future actions in natural language (e.g., "I'm checking if a word is a palindrome"). We verify that this encoding is causal for next action and is plastic: transplanting it into a different environment, e.g., another programming language, triggers the same operation realized with a different sequence of tokens. The LM also sustains the encoding throughout the action's execution, which is puzzling because a transformer LM without recurrence cannot carry a state forward for more tokens than it has layers left. We propose that it does not need to. Under a non-recurrent goal-seeking (NRGS) account, the LM frequently re-reads the goal from the task specification, compares it with the progress visible in the growing context, and pursues what remains. We test the predictions of this account with targeted causal interventions.

papers.title: Agentic Orchestration for SLA-Constrained Network Slicing in Programmable Mobile Data Planes
papers.abstract: The Third Generation Partnership Project (3GPP) Technical Specification 23.501 (Release 17) defines Maximum Bit Rate (MBR) enforcement at the User Plane Function (UPF) in fifth-generation (5G) networks. Supporting differentiated service-level agreements across the radio access and core networks requires the UPF to enforce MBR limits according to configured slice priorities. During overload, the challenge is to adapt these limits while preserving that differentiation and avoiding oscillations. Building on programmable enforcement and intelligent orchestration, we propose an agentic control loop combining UPF telemetry with locally hosted Large Language Model (LLM) selection from a finite set of admissible rate candidates. Deterministic logic validates each selection and derives Packet Forwarding Control Protocol (PFCP) updates. The evaluated runs show no oscillations or fallbacks and unchanged highest-priority rate limits. These observations establish configuration preservation; delivered per-class QoS protection remains unmeasured.

authors.name: Joberto S. B. Martins
authors.institution: Hochschule für Technik und Wirtschaft des Saarlandes

papers.title: Sustainable Federated Fine-Tuning with LoRA: Environmental Impact and Performance Footprint
papers.abstract: Federated Learning (FL) with Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning (PEFT) enables efficient adaptation of Large Language Models (LLMs), yet its energy and carbon costs across hardware remain poorly understood. We evaluated federated Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) fine-tuning on NVIDIA A40, RTX 6000 Ada, and A100 GPUs using a $2^2$ full factorial design with 135M/360M models and 10/100 local steps. CodeCarbon tracked energy and estimated CO$_2$-equivalent emissions. Descriptive allocation of variation assigned 84.8-91.2% of energy and emissions variation to local steps within these ranges. On A40 and RTX 6000 Ada, configurations with fewer steps achieved comparable accuracy with roughly 6-8-fold lower energy consumption and higher accuracy per kWh. These findings support smaller local budgets for energy-efficient federated fine-tuning within the evaluated setting.

authors.name: Joberto S. B. Martins
authors.institution: Hochschule für Technik und Wirtschaft des Saarlandes

papers.title: Steady-state of L\'evy process with general resetting: unreflected and reflected cases
papers.abstract: We study (unreflected and reflected) L\'evy processes that are modified at independent Poisson review epochs by a random state-dependent reset map. The first model is unreflected: between resettings the level evolves as a L\'evy process, and at a resetting epoch the new level is $F$ of the level seen just before the resetting. The second model is the reflected L\'evy process at $0$, but with reset maps chosen from a wider transform-solvable class. In this work, we give contraction-type ergodicity criteria for the existence of the steady-state. We identify this steady-state of the system as the solution of certain stochastic fixed-point equation. This allows to find the Laplace-transform, moments recursions, and regularly-varying-tail formulae. For non-reflected case, the examples include affine deterministic resets $F(x)=cx+b$, random-coefficient resets $F(x)=Cx+b$ with two-point $C$ for the finite-activity L\'evy process, spectrally positive L\'evy flight, reflected Brownian process. For the reflected cased we analyse affine resetting mechanism $F(x)=cx$, the alternating resetting $F(x)=(B-x)^+$, and uniform proportional resetting $F(x)=Cx$ with $C$ having uniform distribution.

papers.title: Binding Mode Matters: Hotspot-Aware Drug Discovery via Explorative Preferences
papers.abstract: Discovering hit molecules requires not just high binding affinity, but also the identification of diverse binding modes, which are critical for experimental assays. Existing generative approaches have predominantly relied on optimizing a scalar docking score, obscuring the distinct contributions of key binding determinants. To this end, we introduce a paradigm shift by formulating target-based drug design as a multi-objective exploration task, where each objective explicitly corresponds to enhancing interactions with a specific hotspot. Here, we introduce BindMol, a novel generative framework driven by a customized multi-objective reinforcement learning algorithm. By incorporating explorative preferences during training, our approach efficiently uncovers molecules with diverse and desirable binding profiles. Empirical results demonstrate that BindMol facilitates the discovery of high-affinity compounds characterized by both structural novelty and diverse binding modes. Validated across target-based drug discovery and multi-property optimization tasks, our approach provides a versatile paradigm for goal-oriented drug discovery.

papers.title: A Tutorial on Infrastructure Self-Calibration for Radio-Based Indoor Positioning
papers.abstract: Radio positioning needs the positions of its anchors, access points, base stations, or reconfigurable intelligent surfaces, and manual surveying is costly and error-prone. Calibrating this infrastructure from its own measurements is one estimation problem, studied in at least four communities as self-calibration, auto-positioning, anchor self-localization, network localization, or radio simultaneous localization and mapping. This tutorial teaches the problem through one factor graph. The measurement topology sets its factors, the reference information enters as priors, and other measurement models add nuisance states. The tutorial shows what ranges can identify, from rigidity to the motion a mobile device must contribute, and presents multidimensional scaling, nonlinear least squares, recursive filters, and convex relaxations as inference engines over this graph. One session of a ten-anchor ultra-wideband deployment is carried through every step, and recordings from a second, harsher deployment and a public partial mesh serve as contrasts. The examples illustrate three lessons. On a full mesh, choose a robust loss and set its scale first, and calibrate with the engine of the positioning system, since the engines then reach similar errors. On thinned or partial meshes, test the result at surveyed check points, because the start decides which minimum a solver reaches. On a line-of-sight deployment, estimate range offsets, which lower the error floor that a systematic ranging bias sets and a robust loss cannot remove. A decision tree and a table of their effects turn them into deployment guidance. Code and result tables are openly released, and the data are published separately.

papers.title: How to Defeat a Mafia (of Size 1)
papers.abstract: The game "Mafia'' is a social deduction game where $n$ players attempt to uncover a covert coalition of $m$ players among the $n$. Typically, $d=1$ of the non-coalition players are labelled ``Detective'' and have special abilities. Most game-theoretic analysis considers, however, only the variant without a Detective. Once the Detective role is introduced, extremely complex strategies can be employed, for which reason only upper and lower bounds for winning have been established, namely by considering specific strategies. We analyse the case $m=d=1$, providing a first example where an explicit, provably-optimal strategy can be described beyond $d=0$.

papers.title: Optimal Polyomino Fences
papers.abstract: The $n$-omino fence problem asks how many cells can be surrounded by placing every $n$-omino exactly once in the grid. We present a new dynamic programming approach for this problem, allowing us to prove optimality for the pentomino and hexomino fence and to classify all possible pentomino orders by optimal area. For the first time we also provide strong heuristic solutions and upper bounds for all fences up to $n = 15$, after which we even approximate the $500$-omino fence with computational experiments. Finally, we generalize the problem to 3D, where we prove optimality for pentacubes and derive heuristic solutions for hexacubes and heptacubes.

authors.name: Erika Roldan
authors.institution: Center for Scalable Data Analytics and Artificial Intelligence

papers.title: Monolayer MoSe2 as an Attenuator of Spintronic Terahertz Emission
papers.abstract: Understanding ultrafast spin-to-charge conversion at ferromagnetic/2D interfaces is critical for developing THz-frequency spintronic devices such as ultrafast memories, sensors, and compact THz sources. We investigate this by studying spintronic THz emission (STE) from Py/Au heterostructures capped with transition metal dichalcogenide (TMD) monolayer MoSe2 using time-domain THz spectroscopy. We observe a pronounced reduction in emitted THz amplitude when a monolayer MoSe2 flake covers Py/Au or Py/Pt emitters compared with uncovered regions. A consistent, approximately fourfold attenuation occurs for both systems, despite an order-of-magnitude larger THz radiation from the bare Py/Pt emitter. These results indicate that the suppression is independent of emitter strength. We attribute the attenuation to THz absorption by free charge carriers and trions that are either present due to charge transfer from the metallic layer or photoexcited by the laser pulse, which can significantly diminish the detectable STE signal. This finding provides an explanation for the discrepancy between weak STE signals from FM/TMD heterostructures and magnetotransport reports of sizable spin-orbit torques in similar systems, and highlights the need to account for photoinduced THz attenuation when interpreting ultrafast spin-to-charge conversion measurements in 2D TMD heterostructures.

papers.title: Compiling Known Rules into Compact Neural Agents: Weight-Space Programming on Unseen Games
papers.abstract: Weight-space programming (WSP) uses language models to construct neural network weights without training. We test whether known game mechanics can be compiled into compact agents that generalise to held-out levels, renderings and start states within a game family. Writers receive simulator source with held-out level data removed for 20 privately authored, unpublished ARC-AGI-3-style game families. With a fixed 57k-parameter recurrent architecture, the strongest writer reaches 56% held-out-level success with feedback, while the four main writers' Python players reach 97-100%. An exploratory free-architecture condition reaches 68-90%. Learning from support-level examples transfers much less well, but these learners lack the source information given to writers. Written networks have a program-like structure: 93% of parameters are zero, and 90% of the rest are small integers or powers of two. NumPy players under comparable computation caps reach 91%, versus the networks' 79%. Training the strongest writer's architectures from scratch yields about 1% success within our budget. Written fixed-network weights are fragile, and standard PPO removes most of their success. Prompts for noise robustness increase tolerance by about four orders of magnitude for two of three writers, but PPO makes larger updates and still removes most success. These results demonstrate rule-to-network compilation in this setting, while showing limited benefits over Python programs and no successful combination with the tested PPO fine-tuning.

authors.name: Jens Lehmann
authors.institution: Center for Scalable Data Analytics and Artificial Intelligence

papers.title: Sedimentation of flexible fibers through an ordered array of pillars
papers.abstract: In this study, we extend our previous work [Makanga \textit{et al.}, Physical Review Fluids 8, 044303 (2023)] to investigate the effects of a periodic array of pillars on the settling dynamics of a flexible fiber in a viscous fluid. By means of numerical simulations, we show that the fiber trajectory falls at long times into one of two migration modes, ``zigzag" and ``displacement", which are determined by the short-time scattering dynamics induced by fiber-pillar interactions. In the zigzag mode, there is no average displacement relative to the direction of gravity; the center of mass of the fiber follows a quasi-straight line. Conversely, in the displacement mode, there is a net displacement relative to the direction of gravity; the fiber center of mass follows a cyclical skew-bumping path. We show how this long-time behavior can be predicted using a theoretical model with minimal ingredients. These findings, together with the long-time transport properties of the fiber, provide insights into future experiments, as well as the design of gravity-based deterministic lateral displacement (DLD) devices to sort elongated particles based on their geometric and/or mechanical properties.

authors.name: Ursy Makanga
authors.institution: Max Planck Institute for the Physics of Complex Systems

authors.name: Camille Duprat
authors.institution: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique

authors.name: Blaise Delmotte
authors.institution: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique

papers.title: Coset Geometries and Tameness of Certain Classes of Shephard Groups
papers.abstract: For the class of Shepard groups (which contain Coxeter groups, Artin-Tits groups, and many finite complex reflection groups), we investigate the structure of the coset incidence systems defined using the standard parabolic subgroups. For the class of tame Shephard groups, which is when all the standard parabolic subgroups are equal to the corresponding Shephard groups, then the intersection of standard parabolic subgroups is also a standard parabolic subgroup. We show that when the Shephard group is either finite, right-angled, or rank two, then it is tame; this is further evidence that all Shephard groups are tame. Finally, we mix the Burau and the geometric representations to produce a representation for all Shephard groups, but we show it is not faithful in rank two unless the Shephard group is finite or an Artin-Tits group.

authors.name: Philippe Tranchida
authors.institution: Max Planck Institute for Mathematics in the Sciences

papers.title: Intersections, Equations, and Singularities of Lissajous Varieties
papers.abstract: Lissajous varieties are affine algebraic varieties parametrized by sine and cosine functions. They generalize algebraic Lissajous curves in the plane to higher dimensions by applying a component-wise trigonometric map to a rational affine subspace and are motivated by applications in dynamical systems (Kuramoto model) and semidefinite optimization (graph elliptopes). We establish several algebraic and geometric properties of Lissajous varieties. In particular, we show that intersections of Lissajous varieties are finite unions of such varieties and describe them explicitly. We investigate algebraic properties of the defining polynomials of Lissajous hypersurfaces and describe the singular locus of Lissajous varieties.

authors.name: Francesco Maria Mascarin
authors.institution: Max Planck Institute for Mathematics in the Sciences

papers.title: Fragility of Aeolian Ripples
papers.abstract: Sand surfaces exposed to the wind are covered by aeolian sand waves of diverse wavelengths, from centimetres for small ripples to decameters for dunes. Sand dunes can be said to be antifragile, since their growth is not prohibited by storms, whereas ripples and megaripples are fragile since they get flattened. The fluid-entrainment hypothesis attributes their fragility to a common cause: the spontaneous aerodynamic entrainment of grains. Here, we challenge this conventional view by revealing its major shortcomings and inconsistencies. An alternative framework, routed in the granular bed rheology, posits that impact ripples are erased when the two-phase flow of ballistically hopping grains on a solid sand surface gives way to a three-phase flow, featuring an intermediate, collision-dominated, fluid-like transport layer. Notably, both martian wind-drag ripples and terrestrial aerodynamic ripples, which emerge via a hydrodynamic instability, are insensitive to such "surface-melting". Their destruction is predicated on the transition from aerodynamically smooth to rough conditions, instead. Our theoretical arguments are well supported by a stability diagram in terms of Shields number and grain diameter, assembled from a carefully reassessed large body of literature, and backed up by dedicated control measurements.

papers.title: Band geometry, Anderson's theorem, and vortex nucleation in unconventional 2D superconductors
papers.abstract: Motivated by the recent discovery of chiral superconductors in 2d materials, we study the effects of disorder on superconductivity in materials with non-trivial band geometry. First, we show how Anderson's theorem and the conventional Abrikosov-Gorkov description of disorder-induced pair breaking are modified by the structure of the normal-state Bloch functions. We apply these results to twisted MoTe2 and show that a BCS pairing mechanism for the observed superconductor is in tension with the measured normal state residual resistivity. Second, we study whether random potential disorder can nucleate superconducting vortices in a chiral time- reversal-breaking superconductor. We show that, for a superconductor stabilized by the usual BCS mechanism, weak disorder does not induce a vortex glass phase, in contrast to superconductivity formed from an anyon fluid.

papers.title: From Isolated Protocols to Integrated Pipelines: Benchmarking IoT Communication in the MASA Living Lab
papers.abstract: The performance of real-time IoT communication systems depends not only on individual transport protocols, serialization formats, and data-processing stages, but also on how these components interact within the complete communication pipeline. Selecting an appropriate communication stack is therefore application-dependent and requires considering processing capabilities, network characteristics, communication patterns, and reliability requirements. This paper provides an experimental, evidence-based analysis of these interactions through a controlled benchmark of integrated communication pipelines deployed in the MASA living lab. We jointly evaluate local processing overhead, end-to-end latency, jitter, throughput, and delivery reliability across different combinations of transport, messaging, serialization, and compression mechanisms. Results show that component-level processing costs do not directly predict end-to-end performance. In particular, differences of only tens of microseconds in serialization or compression costs can coexist with several-millisecond differences in end-to-end latency, while middleware buffering and transport behavior substantially affect timing performance. The results demonstrate that communication-stack components should be evaluated as integrated pipelines and under representative operating loads rather than ranked independently.

authors.name: Enrico Rossini
authors.institution: University of Modena and Reggio Emilia

authors.name: Marcello Pietri
authors.institution: University of Modena and Reggio Emilia

authors.name: Marco Picone
authors.institution: University of Modena and Reggio Emilia

authors.name: Carlo Augusto Grazia
authors.institution: University of Modena and Reggio Emilia

papers.title: Realizability-Based Kinetic-Fluid Domain Decomposition for Multitemperature Gas Mixtures on Unstructured Meshes
papers.abstract: We present a dynamic domain decomposition method for gas mixtures described by a multi-species BGK model in the regime where collisions between particles of the same species are dominant. In this regime the hydrodynamic limit is a system of Euler equations in which every species keeps its own velocity and temperature, the species being coupled through momentum and energy exchange terms. To decide locally whether this multi-velocity, multi-temperature Euler description is accurate, we extend the moment realizability criterion of Levermore, Morokoff and Nadiga: for each species, a realizability matrix is derived from the Chapman--Enskog expansion of the kinetic model, and its zeroth- and first-order approximations are compared. The indicator involves only macroscopic quantities and is evaluated species by species, so that in the same cell one species may be described by the Euler equations and another one by the kinetic equation. The kinetic solver is therefore used only where, and for the species for which, the indicator detects non-equilibrium effects, such as across shocks or near obstacles in rarefied flows. Both solvers are discretized on unstructured triangular meshes with second-order accuracy in space and time. The kinetic equation is integrated by an asymptotic-preserving IMEX Runge--Kutta scheme, whose limit for vanishing Knudsen number is a consistent discretization of the multi-velocity, multi-temperature Euler system. In the numerical tests the hybrid solution stays close to the kinetic one, while the computational time is reduced by a factor between about three and almost five.

papers.title: "It's still 100% on me": Designing AI Tools for the Intersection of Physicians' Care and Legal Infrastructures
papers.abstract: Laws and regulations deeply shape physicians' workflows and impact how they incorporate AI-based decision support tools to care for patients. Despite calls to comply with legal standards, many AI-based decision support tools have not transitioned well to clinical settings. The medical community remains concerned about their legal liability, risks to patients, and limited clinical value of such tools. To better understand how to address these concerns in the design of AI tools for clinical decision-making, we conducted 19 interviews with physicians in the U.S. We used scenario-based design to investigate physicians' legal concerns in the context of an AI-based drug recommendation tool. Drawing on the ethics of care, we surface connections between physicians' care and the healthcare laws and regulations that deeply shape their information needs. We describe how physicians wanted to use the tool in individual and collective practices to care for themselves, their patients, their colleagues, work institution, and even the broader medical profession. We discuss how the design of AI-based decision support tools can present legal ambiguities that would prevent their caring actions and lead to non-use of the AI tool. Through our work, we contribute to responsible AI development in healthcare. Our analysis illuminates why and how certain kinds of information reduce legal ambiguity and support physicians' care when using AI-based decision support tools. We contribute an understanding of how to help physicians navigate legal liability and draw implications for grounding AI tools' designs in their care.

papers.title: Freezing transition and shock-like transients in ballistic random walks under threshold resetting
papers.abstract: We investigate the transient dynamics of a one-dimensional ballistic random walker under threshold resetting (TR). The walker starts at $x_0>0$, moves towards a threshold at the origin with a velocity drawn from a distribution $\phi(v)$, and on reaching the threshold is reset to $x_0$ with a new sampled velocity. Whenever the mean first-passage time to the threshold is finite, the walker reaches a steady state that is uniform on $[0,x_0]$ and independent of $\phi(v)$. The relaxation towards it, in contrast, is highly sensitive to the behavior of $\phi(v)$. For a large class of $\phi(v)$-s, we find, rather remarkably, that the relaxation rate depends explicitly on the spatial coordinate, in contrast to conventional relaxation phenomena, where the rate is typically position-independent. Furthermore, this space-dependent relaxation rate eventually freezes to a constant, position-independent value beyond a critical position, a phenomenon we identify as \textit{freezing transition}. Additionally, for a power-law velocity distribution, the system exhibits an anomalously slow, algebraic relaxation towards the steady state. We also showed that a sharp cutoff in $\phi(v)$ generates a shock-like discontinuity in the particle propagator that travels towards the threshold, with a jump height that decays with time. These results demonstrate how velocity fluctuations, despite leaving the steady state unchanged, can profoundly influence the transient spatial structures and showcase rich non-equilibrium behavior. Our analytical results are corroborated by Monte Carlo simulations, showing an excellent agreement.

papers.title: Tailored magnetic domain-wall ratchet effects through density gradients in triangular-hole arrays
papers.abstract: We investigate domain wall (DW) dynamics and morphology in amorphous Co$_{0.86}$Zr$_{0.14}$ thin films patterned with engineered, density-graded triangular-hole arrays. Using Kerr microscopy and high-resolution XMCD-PEEM imaging, we demonstrate that DW propagation is governed by the interplay between hole orientation, density gradients, and local magnetostatic interactions. In cooperative configurations, the density gradient reinforces the geometric ratchet effect, whereas in competing configurations, the two mechanisms oppose each other, leading to an inverse ratchet and enabling experimental access to backward DW propagation. Remarkably, density-graded arrays substantially reduce the stochastic variability of depinning fields observed in periodic arrays, resulting in highly reproducible DW motion. The depinning fields are described by a rigid DW model and an empirical scaling law incorporating both inter-hole spacing and array periodicity. These results demonstrate that engineered density gradients provide an effective route to deterministic control of DW propagation, with potential applications in spintronic and neuromorphic devices.

papers.title: "We Are the Dirty Hands": Reimagining an Ambient Intelligence Care System with Professional Caregivers
papers.abstract: While ambient assisted living (AAL) sensing systems offer promise for aging in place, their impacts on professional caregivers are overlooked. We conducted two collective speculation workshops (N=24) with personal health aides (PHAs, n=18) and certified nursing assistants (CNAs, n=6) to examine the ethical implications and value tensions of a care system with ambient intelligence (CSAI), our conceptualization of an AAL. Participants anticipated different implications across care roles and settings. PHAs anticipated additional responsibilities from CSAI, including learning how it operates and supporting older adults in its use. CNAs, who had greater access to workplace resources and protections, similarly noted that CSAI could create additional work. Participants also identified tensions around visibility, as sensing could support caregivers by documenting difficult working conditions while simultaneously making their behavior more vulnerable to misinterpretation. Through their modifications and surfaced discussions, we propose design guidelines for AAL systems, such as integrating context-aware sensing.

papers.title: ComBO: Community Bayesian Optimization for Carrier Shutdown in HAPS-Hypercell Networks
papers.abstract: In this paper, we investigate carrier shutdown (CS) in high-altitude platform station (HAPS)-Hypercell-assisted networks, leveraging network-wide information to optimize both coverage macro cells and capacity cells CS. To address the high dimensionality of this problem, we propose ComBO, a community-aware Bayesian optimization framework that exploits user equipment (UE) reference signal received power (RSRP) reports to construct a fallback graph representing the underlying network and identify groups of strongly coupled cells. The resulting communities decompose the original optimization problem into lower-dimensional subproblems, which are sequentially optimized using trust region Bayesian optimization (TuRBO) and refined through a final joint search. Evaluation in a high-fidelity 3GPP-based system-level environment shows that ComBO consistently outperforms legacy CS strategies and overcomes the scalability limitations of global Bayesian optimization (BO). Considering normalized terrestrial power ComBO achieves nearly 84% savings while preserving quality of service. These results demonstrate the potential of community-aware decomposition as a scalable approach to large-scale network optimization.

papers.title: Quantum loop symmetric pairs and meromorphic abelian K-matrices
papers.abstract:
Let $\mathfrak{g}$ be a symmetrizable Kac--Moody algebra, let $q\in\mathbb{C}^\times$ not be a root of unity, and let $\mathbf{U}=U_q(L\mathfrak{g})$ be the corresponding quantum loop algebra, equipped with Hernandez' deformed Drinfeld coproduct. For every diagram involution $\tau$ of $\mathfrak{g}$, we introduce a coideal subalgebra $\mathbf{B}$ in a topological completion of $\mathbf{U}$, obtained by adapting the Letzter-Kolb construction of quantum symmetric pairs to the Drinfeld generators of $\mathbf{U}$. We derive necessary constraints on the parameters defining $\mathbf{B}$ from a minimality condition on its intersection with the quantum loop Cartan subalgebra $\mathbf{U}^0\subset\mathbf{U}$. We show that $\mathbf{B}$ yields a topological realization of the quasi-split $\imath$quantum loop group $\mathbf{U}^\imath$ associated with $\tau$, in the presentation recently obtained by Lu-Pan, building on work of Chen-Lu-Pan-Ruan-Wang on $\imath$Hopf algebras. By pullback, this gives rise to a rational restriction functor on category O representations. For modules with rational weights and generic values of the spectral parameter, every $\mathbf{U}^\imath$-submodule of a restricted module is stable under the derived quantum loop algebra $\mathbf{U}'$. In particular, irreducibility is generically preserved under restriction for such modules.
  For $|q|\neq1$ and under explicit assumptions on the quantum Cartan matrix, we construct meromorphic abelian K-matrices whose tensor counterparts yield boundary $q$-characters for both $\mathbf{U}$-modules and $\mathbf{U}^\imath$-modules.
  Finally, we extend the coideal construction and Drinfeld coaction to shifted $\imath$quantum loop algebras with arbitrary coweight shifts, providing a new approach to $\imath$GKLO representations by restriction from ordinary shifted quantum loop algebras.

papers.title: PRELUDE: Separating Common Components from Target-Specific Dependencies for Multivariate Time Series Forecasting
papers.abstract: Multivariate time series forecasting often improves the prediction of a target by modeling the interactions among variables, and cross-variable modules such as cross-sectional pooling, inter-variable attention, and graph structures are used to construct such interactions. However, by intervening on the cross-variable reading of existing models at inference time, we find that although these models substantially reduce forecasting error through cross-variable interaction, their reading is nearly identical for all targets: the gain appears to come from dependencies among variables but mainly comes from the common component. We term this phenomenon spurious dependency and attribute it to common-component confounding: present in every variable, the common component affects how reading distinguishes sources, so that reading tends to be shared across targets and concentrates on a few similar averages; dependencies thus make up a small share of the read-in content, and a common component composed of several drivers is only partly captured. Theoretical analysis further shows that the common component and dependencies place different requirements on reading and should therefore be handled in different ways. Accordingly, we propose PRELUDE, a separated-reading framework that estimates the common component holistically through cross-sectional pooling and multiple common factors, and reads dependencies for each target via lead-lag relations in the innovation space obtained by prewhitening. Extensive experiments on 16 real-world datasets from four domains show that PRELUDE effectively mitigates spurious dependency and achieves the best overall performance: it attains the best MSE on 23 of the 24 short-horizon and air-quality settings and reduces the average MSE by 6.1% relative to the strongest baseline.

papers.title: A Modular Framework for ESG Prediction through Domain-Specific Language Modeling and Graph Learning
papers.abstract: Environmental, Social and Governance (ESG) scores are increasingly used to evaluate corporate sustainability, supporting investment decisions, ensuring regulatory compliance and assessing risk. However, current ESG evaluations largely rely on proprietary methodologies that often produce inconsistent ratings. This motivates the development of data-driven prediction frameworks. In this paper, we present ESGPred, a modular framework for predicting ESG scores by combining domain-specific language modeling with graph-based learning over a network that models the relationships among the companies being evaluated. In addition to presenting the rationale behind ESGPred and detailing its ESG score prediction process, we show that ESGPred can effectively predict both overall ESG ratings and their individual Environmental, Social, and Governance components. We evaluated ESGPred using a dataset of 5,266 sustainability reports published by 2,134 publicly listed companies between 2020 and 2023. In this evaluation, we used ESG ratings provided by LSEG Data & Analytics as ground truth. Our experimental results demonstrated that integrating graph-based relational learning improves prediction performance over purely text-based baselines.

papers.title: Inertial modes in a turbulent rotating magneto-convection simulation with the solar-like differential rotation
papers.abstract: Recent observations have revealed a variety of solar inertial modes, but their nonlinear properties remain largely unexplored. We aim to identify and characterize inertial modes in a state-of-the-art simulation of rotating magnetoconvection, in which solar-like differential rotation was self-consistently reproduced. We analyzed nine years of high-cadence data from the Hotta (2025) simulation. The spatial eigenfunctions of various low-frequency inertial modes were extracted using singular value decomposition. We identified major classes of retrograde inertial modes, including equatorial Rossby modes, high-latitude modes, and high-frequency retrograde modes, with frequencies and near-surface amplitudes roughly consistent with the solar observations. In particular, thanks to the strongly baroclinic background in the simulation, the observed large amplitude ($\sim 10$ m/s) and the characteristic polar spiral pattern of the high-latitude mode at azimuthal order $m=1$ are successfully reproduced. This indicates that high-latitude modes are excited by baroclinic instability, which can occur even amid turbulent convection. We further show that the prograde columnar modes undergo a qualitative transition at $m \sim 6$, separating the fast-propagating convective modes at $m \gtrsim 6$ from thermally diffusive slow modes at $m \lesssim 6$ whose frequencies closely match recent observational inferences of thermal Rossby modes. Finally, we find that turbulent magnetic fields primarily influence the inertial modes indirectly through modifications of the background state. Our results suggest that the observed properties of solar inertial modes are broadly consistent with a simulation in which solar-like differential rotation is maintained in a magnetically dominated regime, although the simulation still overproduces prograde columnar modes at large $m$.

papers.title: Bayesian determination of structural ensembles from single-particle X-ray scattering images
papers.abstract: Single-particle X-ray scattering with free electron lasers records snapshots of individual molecules with femtosecond time resolution and is therefore ideally suited to study structural heterogeneity or molecular motions. Current approaches to determine structural ensembles rely on prior classification of the scattering images, which is error-prone and becomes infeasible for single macromolecules, whose images contain too few coherently scattered photons. Here, we present a Bayesian approach that samples weighted ensembles of electron densities directly from the posterior probability distribution given all scattering images, thereby avoiding classification altogether. We demonstrate our approach in the low signal-to-noise high heterogeneity regime using synthetic scattering data of a small and flexible protein, as well as on published experimental scattering images for the coliphage PR772 virus.

papers.title: On $L^p$ density of self-similar measures and Bernoulli convolutions
papers.abstract: We prove that an absolutely continuous self-similar measure has an $L^p$ density for some $p>1$. Moreover, explicit examples of Bernoulli convolutions with a continuous density are established.

papers.title: GHA-SmellFix: Taking Action with Agentic LLMs for Detecting and Refactoring GitHub Actions Workflow Smells
papers.abstract: Continuous integration and continuous delivery workflows are key artifacts in software projects. In GitHub Actions, they encode build, test, release, deployment, and security automation in YAML. These workflows contain configuration smells affecting security, reliability, maintainability, or operational stability. Existing approaches are mostly rule-based, with rules hard to create and evolve, and typically report findings without fixes. Agentic LLM pipelines can combine contextual detection, transformation selection, and patch generation. Specialized agents can gate refactoring on positive detection verdicts, potentially avoiding unnecessary changes, but it is unclear whether decomposition improves effectiveness or mainly changes overhead. We present GHA-SmellFix, an agentic LLM pipeline for detecting and refactoring GitHub Actions workflow smells. We compare two designs: Joint, where one agent detects and refactors, and Decomposed, where separate agents detect and then refactor. We operationalize 19 smells from an existing catalog with explicit detection criteria, refactoring expectations, exclusion rules, and safety checks, and curate a ground truth of 1,710 (workflow, smell) pairs. We evaluate the designs with four LLMs (GPT-5.4-nano, Gemini 3.5 Flash, Claude Haiku 4.5, and DeepSeek V4 Flash) on 570 sampled pairs. Results show that decomposition does not universally improve patch quality; its main benefit is controlling when patch generation is attempted. It helps models prone to missing smells and can reduce overhead by gating patches. Once a smell is correctly detected, clean refactoring is generally effective, making detection the main end-to-end bottleneck. However, false positives can trigger unnecessary edits to execution-relevant constructs. Practical CI/CD agents thus need reliable abstention and construct-aware validation alongside patch generation.

papers.title: GNN-Enhanced TCN Algorithms for ECG Anomaly Detection
papers.abstract: To a time series can be also given the structure of directed graph, opening the doors to the usage of graph neural networks (GNNs) in this context. In this paper we develop a new pipeline involving novel geometric deep learning models that merge the capabilities of ordinary TCNs with the ones of GNNs to solve an anomaly detection problem on electrocardiogram signals.

papers.title: Damped wave equation with a dynamic boundary condition: sharp resolvent estimate
papers.abstract: This work investigates the stabilization of a wave equation with a localized damping and dynamic boundary conditions. This model traces back to the classical treatment of torsion and impact problems. Consider a second-order hyperbolic equation posed with a dynamic boundary condition on a smooth compact Riemannian manifold $(\M,g)$ with boundary, in which the damping acts either in the interior or on $\d \M$. Under the assumption that the damping is positive on an open subset of its domain of action, a resolvent estimate is established. A logarithmic decay rate is then deduced for the energy of strong solutions. We provide examples that establish the sharpness of the resolvent estimate.

papers.title: Training Calibrated Conditional Generative Models with a Sample-Only Coverage Loss
papers.abstract: Conditional generative models have become the tool of choice for sampling posteriors in scientific inverse problems, where we seek to sample images or signals conditioned on a set of indirect and noisy measurements. Yet they are often overconfident, which is a critical failure in scientific applications where accurate uncertainty quantification is essential. Existing regularizers fall short in complementary ways: differentiable coverage objectives require the model's density and do not identify the posterior, while strictly proper scoring rules such as the energy score need only samples but do not directly enforce coverage. We close this gap by introducing a differentiable loss function based on the expected coverage probability, estimated from samples alone. It applies to any conditional generative model, with no need for tractable densities or architectural changes. We prove that it is a strict divergence, vanishing if and only if the model equals the true posterior. On simulation-based inference benchmarks, it matches a density-based coverage loss without evaluating the density. On high-dimensional imaging inverse problems, it yields better-calibrated posteriors than scoring-rule regularizers, with little change in the reconstruction quality of point estimates.

papers.title: On the algebraic Mackey deformation
papers.abstract: This paper provides a conceptual understanding of the Mackey bijection from the admissible dual of a real reductive group $G$ into the admissible dual of its Cartan motion group $G_0$, by studying the primitive spectrum of a Hecke algebra over $\mathbb{C}[t]$ arising from the contraction of $G$ to $G_0$. If $K$ denotes a maximal compact subgroup of $G$, our approach leads to the following two results: the admissible Mackey bijection is a piecewise homeomorphism, each piece being defined by the length of the lowest $K$-types; the Hecke algebras of $G$ and $G_0$ have, up to $K$-types not exceeding a certain length, the same periodic cyclic homology.
