In particular, the Mackey bijection can be seen as a bijection Prim⁡(U)→Prim⁡(U0)\mathrm{Prim}(U)\to\mathrm{Prim}(U^{0}). For each S∈{U,U0,𝑼,U⁡[t]}S\in\{U,U^{0},\bm{U},U[t]\} and n∈ℕn\in\mathbb{N}, let Prim​(S)n\mathrm{Prim}(S)_{n} be the set of annihilators of simple SS-modules having lowest KK-types of length lnl_{n}. As a consequence of Theorem I, we obtain the following for every n∈ℕn\in\mathbb{N}.

papers.title: Niche construction as an emerging phenomenon from fast ecological and slow evolutionary-environmental timescales in individual-based models
papers.abstract: We consider an individual-based model of niche construction built upon birth-death processes of d interacting biological entities (e.g., species, subpopulations or mutant strains in the same species) immersed in a slowly-varying environment which is influenced by the population state. In this setting, extinction and/or emergence of entities with negligible size or rarity, on long time scales can be observed. We prove that the joint dynamics of the environment and the species sizes on a logarithmic scale undergo a piecewise deterministic Markov process in a large time regime, which can be approximated by an explicit dynamical system in the limit of large populations. This convergence result holds true under the assumption that no "bad event" occurs during the population dynamics, corresponding to situations where several species become dominant or go extinct simultaneously. We also prove that no such bad event occurs for Baire-almost all initial conditions of the population sizes and the environmental resources. We apply this framework to study the long term coexistence of two specialist species consuming two resources, with a "joint" niche construction where each species constructs the niche of the other while depleting its resources. We also study an example of immune escape in cancer, where the environmental variable is associated with the state of the immune system and the species are associated with three types of tumor cells.

authors.name: Pablo A. Marquet
authors.institution: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique

authors.name: Nicolas Zalduendo
authors.institution: Institut National de Recherche pour l'Agriculture, l'Alimentation et l'Environnement

papers.title: Evaluating AI Musical Creativity: Towards a Quantitative Multi-Dimensional Framework Based on Value, Novelty, and Surprise
papers.abstract: Despite the increasing sophistication of generative Artificial Intelligence (AI), research on the evaluation of AI-generated musical creativity remains limited. To address this gap, this paper proposes a quantitative framework for the formalization and evaluation of AI musical creativity. Building on Margaret Boden's theory, which conceptualizes creativity in terms of value, novelty, and surprise, the framework adapts and operationalizes these three dimensions for the musical domain. On the hypothesis that certain aspects of musical creativity can be assessed with a degree of objectivity, a domain-specific set of quantitative metrics for evaluating the creativity of AI-generated music is introduced. Rather than reducing musical creativity to a single unifying measure, this article proposes an ensemble of complementary metrics that capture its different dimensions, recognizing the complexity of musical artifacts and the difficulty of defining meaningful multi-objective compositional criteria. The framework has two implications. First, it gives researchers and developers a principled methodology and quantitative tools for empirically evaluating creative outputs, enabling more informed model development and reducing unnecessary computational costs. Second, it lays the groundwork for future generative models to optimize directly for creativity by adopting these metrics as learning objectives.

papers.title: Robust Decoupled Input Filtering for Internal Model Principle-Based Output Regulation of Polynomial Exogenous Signals
papers.abstract: Internal model principle-based controllers regulate polynomial references and disturbances exactly, but only asymptotically, and their transient input can peak and oscillate, increasingly so as the degree of the exogenous signals grows. A filter placed in series with the plant smooths the command but alters the closed-loop spectrum and can destroy stability. We propose an architecture that keeps the filter outside the loop the regulator stabilizes: the internal model is driven by the error of an ideal, unfiltered copy of the plant, the physical plant receives the filtered command, and an auxiliary plant copy absorbs the mismatch between the two inputs. If the filter satisfies blocking conditions at the origin, any gains that stabilize the unfiltered loop can be combined with any such filter without losing regulation of the true error. Under additive plant uncertainty, we derive a small-gain condition that guarantees robust stability and regulation. On a scalar plant, the proposed controller produces a smoother input and a larger input-delay margin than the unfiltered one, and it maintains regulation under a large loss of actuator effectiveness. On a three-mass chain, its tolerance to unmodeled actuator dynamics and delay stays essentially constant as the regulator is made more aggressive.

papers.title: Benchmarking Multilingual Document Understanding in Vision-Language Models
papers.abstract: Recent Vision-Language Models (VLMs) perform strongly on multimodal tasks, Document Understanding (DU) among them, but the benchmarks that measure them mostly cover English documents and narrow problems. How well current VLMs generalize across languages, tasks, styles and layouts therefore remains unclear. We introduce MDU, a multilingual DU benchmark of 23146 examples spanning 13 tasks and five languages: English, French, German, Italian, and Spanish. The tasks isolate complementary capabilities, from surface-level text and Markdown extraction through summarization, classification and named-entity recognition to layout-sensitive passage and layout extraction. We evaluate 45 state-of-the-art open-weight VLMs from 1.7B to 235B parameters, plus one commercial system under the same protocol. The benchmark is far from saturated: the best average is 69.0, only eight of the 45 evaluated systems reach 65, and the two best results come from 27B models rather than from the largest systems we evaluate. Performance is uneven in ways that scale does not fix. The gap between the strongest and weakest language does not close as models grow, and it survives controlling for the domain composition of each language. Capabilities also do not improve together: once we partial out overall model quality, per-task scores are largely uncorrelated, and transcription ability in particular trades off against semantic extraction.

papers.title: K-stable Fano varieties can have obstructed deformations
papers.abstract: We exhibit examples of K-stable Fano varieties with obstructed qG-deformations; more precisely, their miniversal qG-deformation spaces can be non-reduced. As a consequence, we show that both the K-moduli stack and the K-moduli space can be non-reduced, and hence non-smooth, at points corresponding to K-stable Fano varieties.

papers.title: Regularized trimmed Factorial and Reduced K-means for contaminated high-dimensional data: separating geometry, search and selection
papers.abstract: Factorial and Reduced K-means estimate a partition and a low-dimensional clustering subspace jointly, which makes them attractive when the variables that separate groups are not those that dominate total variance. On contaminated high-dimensional data they face three linked problems: trimming can make the scatter matrices singular, the criterion has many local optima, and the rank, number of groups and trimming proportion are unknown and interact. We propose REG-HD-TFKM and REG-HD-TRKM, regularized trimmed versions of the two methods, together with a selection procedure that handles these problems as separate decisions. A ridge-stabilized spectral step keeps every fit well defined; heterogeneous multistart search explores alternative solutions; method-specific agreement and reproducibility scores choose among them; and trimming is applied only when a radial diagnostic or the path over trimming levels supports it. A simulation study with 41 design cells shows why the separation matters. Two representations of euro-area bank balance sheets show that similar partitions can rest on nearly orthogonal subspaces, and that the same selected structure can describe different retained samples.

papers.title: Digitally Supported Transitional Care Pathways for Older Adults: A Multi-Site Co-Design Study
papers.abstract: During transitions from hospital to home, older adults are frequently affected by fragmented communication, limited coordination between levels of care, and insufficient post-discharge follow-up. Digital technologies, including remote patient monitoring (RPM), digital communication, and artificial intelligence (AI), offer opportunities to improve continuity of care. However, their integration needs to reflect the organizational and clinical contexts of different healthcare systems. This study presents the development and early implementation of digitally supported transitional care pathways within the TransCare project. Care pathways were analyzed and redesigned across three pilot sites in Italy, Romania, and Norway. Existing clinical and organizational processes were mapped to identify challenges and opportunities for improvement. Technology-augmented pathway matrices were developed to integrate RPM, digital communication tools, and AI-supported analytics across the stages of assessment, hospitalization, discharge, and post-discharge follow-up. The pathways were iteratively refined through a co-design process involving healthcare professionals, patients, caregivers, and technical partners. Early implementation experiences were subsequently analyzed across the three sites. Common challenges included fragmented communication and poor care coordination, particularly during discharge and post-discharge follow-up. However, the underlying cause and required solutions differed across the pilot sites, reflecting variations in patient profiles, healthcare organizations, available resources, and digital maturity.

authors.name: Roberta Bevilacqua
authors.institution: Istituto Nazionale di Riposo e Cura per Anziani

authors.name: Lorena Rossi
authors.institution: Istituto Nazionale di Riposo e Cura per Anziani

papers.title: Graded Intersection Types
papers.abstract: We introduce graded intersection types, in which arrow domains are multisets of types with coefficients in a semiring. Boolean and natural number grades recover idempotent and non-idempotent intersection types. We give algebraic conditions on the semiring for subject reduction and expansion in finite systems and in locally finite systems with guarded infinite types. We construct a lifting to multisets of grades corresponding, in this general setting, to lifting the idempotent system to the non-idempotent one. We recall the main existing operational characterisations from the literature, and show some general extensions.

papers.title: Qualitative properties of solutions to anisotropic parabolic equations: Part III- H\"{o}lder continuity
papers.abstract: In this work, we study the local H\"older continuity of non-negative solutions to a class of doubly nonlinear anisotropic partial differential equations, with prototype \[ u_t-\sum_{i=1}^N D_i\Big(|D_i u^{m_i}|^{p_i-2}D_i u^{m_i}\Big)=0, \quad m_i>0,\quad p_i>1,\quad i=1,\ldots,N. \] The main result shows that, when the exponents describing the diffusion in different spatial directions are sufficiently close to one another, the solutions enjoy local H\"older continuity. A key feature of the analysis is the distinction between two diffusion regimes: the degenerate and the singular cases; the local regularity results are established in both regimes, under suitable conditions on the exponents.

authors.name: Eurica Henriques
authors.institution: University of Trás-os-Montes and Alto Douro

papers.title: MRxD: A Usage-Pattern Framework for Mixed-Reality Cross-Device Interaction
papers.abstract: Mixed reality (MR) cross-device experiences often combine MR headsets with non-immersive devices such as laptops, tablets, and phones. Yet such cross-device design remains challenging because users must coordinate workflows across heterogeneous devices with different roles. This motivates our focus on usage patterns: recurrent ways in which people distribute and coordinate work across devices. Through a systematic analysis of 238 MR cross-device papers, we developed MRxD, a usage-pattern framework organized around three dimensions: user attention, task relatedness, and cognitive symmetry. Using these dimensions, we identified six usage patterns and synthesized the design strategies commonly used within each pattern. We further investigated the framework's application in design practice through a workshop (n=6) and the results suggest that MRxD can guide pattern-based design exploration and identify blind spots. We further discuss how usage patterns may shift or combine, and outline research gaps and design implications for future MR cross-device systems.

authors.name: Yuchen Cai
authors.institution: Istituto Nazionale di Fisica Nucleare, Sezione di Bologna

papers.title: The exact region of the Average Rectangular Volume and Spearman's rho, with an application to arachnitude
papers.abstract: The average rectangular volume ($\ARV$) of a bivariate aggregation function is the average of its volumes over all axis-parallel rectangles of the unit square; for a copula, it is the expected copula volume of the rectangle spanned by two independent uniform points. We determine the exact region of the pairs $(\ARV(C),\rho(C))$, where $C$ ranges over all bivariate copulas and $\rho$ is Spearman's rho. The region is compact, convex and symmetric, and its upper boundary consists of three analytically parametrized arcs. A previously proposed family of shuffles of Min generates one arc, but only on part of its range; the other two arcs are generated by singular copulas whose supports contain hyperbolic branches. The boundary is continuously differentiable away from its left endpoint $\ARV=\frac{11}{120}$, where it has a vertical tangent. The proof uses a folding transformation and explicit Kantorovich potentials for a family of optimal transport problems. Finally, we show that the arachnitude, a rank correlation used in actuarial practice, is an affine transformation of $\ARV$, so that the result also describes the joint region of Spearman's rho and arachnitude.

authors.name: Fabrizio Durante
authors.institution: Fondazione ICSC Centro Nazionale di Ricerca in High Performance Computing, Big Data e Quantum Computing

papers.title: Cosmic Ray Heating of the Early IGM: Realistic Galaxy Populations, Reduced Efficiency, and 21-cm Signatures
papers.abstract: Cosmic rays (CRs) accelerated by the first supernovae could heat the intergalactic medium (IGM) before reionization. Previous 21-cm simulations, assuming a kinetic-energy power-law spectrum and simplified galaxy populations, found that CR heating can rival X-ray heating from high-mass X-ray binaries, imprint a distinct signature on the 21-cm power spectrum, and flatten the absorption trough of the global 21-cm signal. Here we model CR heating in 21cmFAST with: (i) the momentum power-law spectrum predicted by diffusive shock acceleration; (ii) Coulomb losses off free electrons; and (iii) injection from data-informed populations of atomic-cooling and molecularly cooled galaxies. We find that CR heating is about an order of magnitude weaker than previously estimated because a momentum power law places little energy in the sub-relativistic protons ($\lesssim 40$ MeV) that supply 99% of the heat. For our fiducial spectral slope, at the hard end of those inferred for Galactic supernova remnants, and for matched efficiency, this reduces the heating by a factor of $\approx 12$, and together with a more realistic galaxy model, by a factor of $\approx 28$ at $z = 15$. At the efficiencies that supernovae can supply, CR heating is weaker than standard X-ray heating, and the global signal alone cannot tell the two apart. Distinguishing CR from X-ray heating with the 21-cm power spectrum requires CR efficiencies a few times higher than those expected from local observations. At such efficiencies, CR heating yields up to $\approx 55\%$ more power than X-ray heating at matched global signal (median over scales), compared with only 3-6% at a locally motivated efficiency. A flattened absorption trough, like the one claimed by EDGES, requires efficiencies over two orders of magnitude above the local ones, beyond plausible Population III supernova budgets.

authors.name: Andrei Mesinger
authors.institution: Fondazione ICSC Centro Nazionale di Ricerca in High Performance Computing, Big Data e Quantum Computing

papers.title: Time-Domain and Spectral Decomposition of Dynamic Coupling with Instantaneous and Time-Lagged Causality: Methodological Evaluation and Application to Cardiovascular Variability
papers.abstract: The quantification of dynamic interactions in coupled physiological time series is a central question in biomedical signal processing. A critical issue is the presence of instantaneous dependencies, often neglected in conventional Granger causality (GC) analyses despite potentially reflecting physiologically meaningful effects. We investigate time- and frequency-domain measures of causality within the linear autoregressive (AR) framework, treating instantaneous dependencies according to three formulations: (i) the classical strictly causal AR model, providing spectral measures of time-lagged GC and instantaneous interaction; (ii) the Geweke approach, assigning instantaneous dependencies to the direction opposite to that under investigation; (iii) a single extended AR model incorporating causally-oriented instantaneous dependencies, yielding spectral GC measures accounting for both instantaneous and time-lagged causality. The three approaches are evaluated in simulated Gaussian systems, where dynamic measures can be derived analytically and compared with the expected coupling structure. The single extended AR model emerges as the most consistent formulation when instantaneous dependencies have a physiologically meaningful causal direction and is then applied to cardiovascular interactions between heart period (HP) and systolic (SAP) or diastolic arterial pressure (DAP) in healthy subjects during postural and mental stress. Accounting for instantaneous dependencies substantially affects HP-SAP and HP-DAP interactions, enabling better quantification of baroreflex and cardiac run-off mechanisms and characterization of their responses to stress and of low- and high-frequency dynamics. Overall, the framework provides consistent representation of causal interactions across time and frequency and highlights the importance of accounting for instantaneous dependencies in physiological coupling.

papers.title: Speed-to-Power Dominates Energy Costs for AI Data Centers: Technoeconomic Analysis of Powering AI in the Continental United States
papers.abstract: The rapid growth of artificial intelligence is driving demand for new data centers at large scale and on short deployment timelines. To power them, firms connect to the commercial grid or contract generation directly, but interconnection and gas-turbine delays now incentivize on-site generation. We compare grid-connected and off-grid data center energy infrastructure (AC- and DC-coupled solar-plus-storage, islanded natural gas, and grid interconnection) across the continental U.S. Using an open-source technoeconomic framework built on empirically calibrated AI training loads, climate-driven cooling, stage-by-stage power conversion, and physics-based battery degradation, we model designs providing equivalent energy services. Our central contribution is a speed-adjusted cost of energy that values the compute unlocked by faster construction, making options with different deployment timelines directly comparable on one physically consistent basis. We find DC coupling reduces lifetime energy costs by 18% ($0.09/ kWh) on average versus AC counterparts by eliminating inverters and improving efficiency. Though rarely cheapest on unadjusted energy cost, DC-coupled microgrids' faster deployment makes them the lowest-cost modeled option in 85% of U.S. locations once foregone compute is valued, or 55% under accelerated natural gas timelines. For AI infrastructure, deployment speed rather than unit energy cost determines the economically preferred path to power.

papers.title: Directed Wada cascade in systems with discrete scale invariance
papers.abstract: Dissipative systems whose equations are unchanged by a dilation can host an infinite ladder of attractors, each shell an exact magnified copy of the one before. Since such dynamics cannot tell a magnification from its inverse, the natural expectation is that these basins are maximally entangled, with every boundary point lying on the boundary of all of them, following the Wada property. We find that this expectation fails, and fails in a precise way. Dilation covariance and a single trapping region together bound which basin boundaries a point can lie on, and the bound depends only on its distance to the origin. No point lies on the boundary of all of them. The basins on whose boundary a point does lie are the deeper ones, as we prove for the stable manifolds of the boundary saddles and support numerically for the rest of the boundary, so the boundaries nest in one direction only. We call this structure a directed Wada cascade, and the standard Wada tests, as usually applied, do not detect it. It arises in maps whose nonlinearity is a log-periodic modulation of a homogeneous function, because the same periodicity builds the ladder through mode locking and confines the orbits. We show the cascade in maps that differ in invertibility, nonlinearity, scaling exponent and dimension, and in a flow.

authors.name: I. L. Caldas
authors.institution: Institute of Physics of the Slovak Academy of Sciences

papers.title: Convergence rates for smoothed particle hydrodynamics (SPH) with nonlinear pressure
papers.abstract: We establish quantitative convergence results for the smoothed particle hydrodynamics (SPH) method approximating the compressible Euler equations with nonlinear pressure laws $\rho^\gamma$, $\gamma\geq 2$. Our approach is based on a nonlocal approximation of the pressure force that preserves the energy structure of the original system, including an exact energy balance. Using the relative entropy method, we prove convergence towards smooth solutions of the compressible Euler equations as the nonlocality parameter $\varepsilon\to0$, with algebraic convergence rates and an explicit algebraic relationship between $\varepsilon$ and the number of particles $N$. In particular, we obtain quantitative convergence rates for the density in the Wasserstein distance and negative Sobolev norms, and for the momentum in the flat metric. A key feature of our analysis is that it applies to measure-valued densities in the nonlocal system, providing a unified framework for both continuum and particle solutions. Our results extend the existing rigorous convergence theory for SPH beyond quadratic pressure ($\gamma=2$) to general nonlinear pressure laws with $\gamma\geq 2$ on the periodic domain.

authors.name: Jakub Skrzeczkowski
authors.institution: Mathematical Institute of the Slovak Academy of Sciences

papers.title: Particle systems and the supercooled Stefan problem: Long time behaviour and fluctuations
papers.abstract: We consider an infinite system of particles on the positive real line, initiated from a Poisson point process, which move according to Brownian motion up until the hitting time of a barrier. The barrier increases when it is hit, allowing for the possibility of sequences of successive jumps to occur instantaneously. The scaling limit gives a representation for the supercooled Stefan problem and its free boundary, from which we can determine the asymptotic limit for the barrier movement. We establish also a functional central limit theorem describing the fluctuations about this limit, from which we can determine the rate of convergence for particle system approximations to the supercooled Stefan problem under ``weak feedback" assumptions introduced in arXiv:1811.12356. We finally show that these fluctuations are identical to the fluctuations of a continuous analogue to 1D-MDLA.

authors.name: Ben Hambly
authors.institution: Mathematical Institute of the Slovak Academy of Sciences

papers.title: Gaussian processes for real-time urban traffic estimation using a fleet of drones
papers.abstract: Real-time urban traffic monitoring is essential for modern city management, yet conventional static sensors provide only limited spatial coverage. Autonomous drone fleets can complement this infrastructure by offering flexible, high-resolution mobile sensing across different parts of the network. This paper introduces a spatio-temporal Gaussian process (GP) framework for reconstructing network-wide traffic states from partial aerial observations. The model accounts for the physical structure of the road network through a graph Mat\'ern kernel, which embeds network topology into the spatial covariance structure, and captures temporal dependencies through an exponential temporal kernel. Within this framework, historical loop detector data provide an informative prior mean that is updated in real time using incoming drone observations, yielding network-wide point estimates together with predictive uncertainty. We validate our framework in two distinct case studies: a microscopic simulation of Barcelona and real-world drone data from Athens. The results demonstrate that our approach outperforms historical baselines in estimating and predicting Vehicle Hours Traveled (VHT), notably reducing the required fleet size. Furthermore, leveraging the model's predictive uncertainty to guide drone movements yields additional performance gains, highlighting the potential for future uncertainty-aware fleet routing algorithms.

papers.title: MAHA-z: A Mahalanobis distance kNN estimator for photometric redshifts
papers.abstract: We present \texttt{MAHA-z}, a photometric-redshift (photo-$z$) estimator that combines $k$-nearest neighbour ($k$NN) regression with a Mahalanobis distance metric learned from the covariance of a spectroscopic reference sample. For each target galaxy, \texttt{MAHA-z} performs a neighbour search in a colour-magnitude feature space with optional morphological parameters, and returns both a point estimate and a redshift posterior $p(z\mid\mathbf{f})$ obtained by kernel density estimation over the neighbour redshifts. The Mahalanobis metric accounts for correlated features and heterogeneous units, eliminating ad hoc normalisation, and its subspace restriction allows \texttt{MAHA-z} to handle missing bands on a per-galaxy basis without imputation. We validate the method on four datasets spanning simulations and survey photometry: the Euclid Flagship~2 mock, the Legacy-KiDZ calibration sample, VIPERS, and the DES Year~3 BAO sample. On Euclid Flagship~2 (LSST+NISP) we achieve $\sigma_{\rm NMAD}=0.0148$ with a $0.27\%$ outlier fraction, and on DES Y3 we obtain $\sigma_{\rm NMAD}\approx0.023$ with $<1\%$ outliers and posterior calibration comparable to the \texttt{ANNz2} catalogue. \texttt{MAHA-z} processes millions of galaxies in minutes and provides competitive PDFs at substantially lower computational cost than trained machine-learning models, making it a practical option for iterative photo-$z$ production and validation in Stage-IV surveys.

authors.name: Ribamar R. R. Reis
authors.institution: Universidade Federal do Rio de Janeiro

papers.title: Mind-wandering preserves word-level coupling while disrupting comprehension
papers.abstract: Readers can move their eyes through a page but retain little of its meaning when their minds wander. We tested whether word properties still guide their eyes during these lapses. We analyzed public eye-tracking and electroencephalography (EEG) data from 44 adults who read articles. They marked the text read during each lapse they noticed. We linked these spans to the sentences needed for later comprehension questions. Word frequency, length and surprisal still predicted which words readers skipped and how long they looked at them. Compared with on-task reading, these effects met equivalence bounds of $\pm$10% for skipping and $\pm$20% for gaze duration. Readers spent 14.6% longer on words during lapses. Yet readers answered less accurately when lapses covered sentences needed for a later question. The adjusted difference was 25.7 percentage points for lapses covering all versus none of these sentences. The fixation-related EEG response was 42.7% smaller during lapses. At left posterior-lateral sensor P7, the median increase in alpha power was 10.0%. Occipital sensor Oz showed no reliable increase. These results suggest that word properties can guide the eyes while readers fail to form or retain a useful representation of the text.

papers.title: TQIR: Trellis Quantization with Integer Reconstruction for Bandwidth-Efficient Edge LLM Acceleration
papers.abstract: Autoregressive large language model (LLM) inference is often limited by external-memory bandwidth, while existing ultra-low-bit trellis quantization reconstructs floating-point weights and leaves runtime Hadamard-transform and decoder costs unresolved. This paper presents TQIR, an algorithm--hardware co-design that decouples storage precision ($S$) from decoded-weight ($W$) and activation ($A$) compute precisions, enabling a better accuracy--hardware trade-off. TQIR performs trellis matching with floating-point candidates offline while constraining each candidate to an INT8 or INT4 codeword that can be reproduced exactly for integer GEMM at runtime. To reduce transform cost while preserving the integer weight path, TQIR relocates the reverse Hadamard transform to the activation side and employs an $H_{128}$ Subspace Hadamard Transform, together with a subspace-aligned $128\times2$ trellis tile that preserves the original 256-weight sequence length. The configurable decoder, synthesized in a TSMC 16-nm process, delivers 307.2~Gweights/s in 0.0509~mm$^2$ and achieves 13.93$\times$ and 1.52$\times$ the normalized decoder-area efficiency of Ecco and Codeword Decomposition, respectively. These results show that fixed-rate trellis compression can reduce weight traffic while sustaining an integer-GEMM datapath matched to the evaluated memory and PE rates.

authors.name: Tian-Sheuan Chang
authors.institution: National Yang Ming Chiao Tung University

papers.title: DETER: Suppression During Pretraining for Tamper Resistance
papers.abstract: Open-weight language models can acquire knowledge that could enable biological, chemical, or cyber misuse. Any attempt to limit such knowledge must remain effective after the model weights are released and can be fine-tuned. Unlearning applied after pretraining can be rapidly undone, whereas filtering the pretraining corpus offers greater resistance. We ask whether actively suppressing knowledge during pretraining can further increase the fine-tuning required to acquire it. Even simple gradient ascent interleaved with standard pretraining on the filtered corpus makes medical knowledge harder to acquire through adversarial fine-tuning than filtering alone or post-hoc unlearning. At 1B parameters, reaching the held-out PubMed loss of an unfiltered model requires over 20$\times$ as many PubMed fine-tuning tokens as after filtering alone. Retained knowledge is evaluated using both held-out data and downstream tasks. Across model sizes, varying suppression strength reveals an increasingly favorable trade-off between fine-tuning difficulty and held-out loss on retained pretraining data. These results point to pretraining as an effective stage for making unwanted capabilities harder to acquire through subsequent fine-tuning. Code is available at \href{https://github.com/MEGlr/DETER}{\texttt{github.com/MEGlr/DETER}}.

papers.title: MAGIC: Modality-Aware Gini Inspection for Clinical Hallucination Detection in LMMs
papers.abstract: Recent advances in medical large multimodal models (LMMs) have brought promising progress to clinical decision support, yet hallucination, the generation of confident but clinically unverifiable outputs, poses a critical threat to the reliability demanded in high-stakes medical settings. Existing hallucination detection methods, predominantly designed for unimodal settings, fail to capture the visual-linguistic dynamics inherent to medical imaging. We formulate the problem of hallucination detection in LMMs as disproportionate distribution of attention weights across the modalities during answer token generation. We quantify modality-specific attention concentration across layers and heads using the Gini coefficient and demonstrate statistically significant redistribution of attention mass between visual and textual tokens in hallucinated responses. We leverage these features to train a logistic regression-based classifier and evaluate it on two medical LMMs across three medical imaging modalities, demonstrating that our method achieves competitive or superior performance against contemporary hallucination detection baselines.

authors.name: Sachin Acharya
authors.institution: Institute for Social and Environmental Research-Nepal

authors.name: Niyoj Oli
authors.institution: Institute for Social and Environmental Research-Nepal

papers.title: Faithful in Steps: Improving Generalization and Citation in RAG via Query Decomposition
papers.abstract: Retrieval-augment generation is a prevalent strategy to mitigate hallucinations of LLMs. The attributable RAG (RAGQ) generates quotes for its answers. The quotes indicate which input contexts support the RAG to derive the answers, enhancing the answer's verifiability and trustworthiness. However, existing RAGQs exhibit significant degradation when dealing with questions that require multi-hop reasoning and multi-modal understanding, suffering from over-citation, implicit entity identification failure, and poor generalization. In this paper, we propose a novel RAGQ framework, namely QDRAG. QDRAG breaks down the input question into atomic subquestions to identify the implicit entities. Then, the reranker prunes context distractors to eliminate the downstream over-citation. To facilitate query decomposition, we propose two zero-shot approaches: QD-C and QD-R, which guide the QD MLLM to decompose the question based on context knowledge and retrieval rewards, respectively. One interesting finding is that finetuning on the QD task shows better generalizability compared to directly finetuning on the downstream RAGQ task. Experiments on four multi-modal QA benchmarks demonstrate QDRAG's efficacy in grounding answers and generating faithful citations. The framework significantly outperforms all the baselines on both in-domain and out-of-domain tests, even surpassing Gemini-Pro.

authors.name: Xiaofang Zhou
authors.institution: Henan University of Science and Technology

papers.title: WorldDraft: If Code Builds the World, Can Video Models Just Render It?
papers.abstract: Multimodal coding agents decouple 4D world construction from visual generation, repurposing video models from world generators toward generative renderers. This division of labor raises a fundamental question: if code builds the world, can video models just render it? A reliable generative renderer hinges on two complementary criteria: (i) world preservation, retaining prescribed 4D kinematics and camera paths; and (ii) visual realization, persistently binding text-specified target attributes over time. To evaluate this capability, we introduce WorldDraft, a benchmark of $432$ strictly paired test cases across $48$ executable 4D world families spanning six dynamic challenge categories. Under a $3 \times 3$ factorial design, WorldDraft orthogonally crosses draft granularity (abstract proxy to previs) and appearance alignment (neutral to conflicting) under identical dynamics. Extensive evaluations across $12$ representative models reveal that: (I) world preservation and visual realization remain in stark operational tension; (II) richer draft scaffolding anchors structure but paradoxically impairs appearance fidelity; and (III) conflicting source cues trigger severe source leakage (up to $64\%$), exposing fragile cross-modal disentanglement. To mitigate these bottlenecks, we propose WorldDraft-Primer, a plug-and-play visual prompting strategy that consistently improves both objectives across frozen video renderers. Together, WorldDraft and WorldDraft-Primer lay a foundation for bridging programmatic 4D simulation with video generation, advancing physically grounded generative rendering.

authors.name: Harold Haodong Chen
authors.institution: The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology (Guangzhou)

authors.name: Weilin Ruan
authors.institution: The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology (Guangzhou)

papers.title: Dynamics and Statistical Mechanics of Born-Oppenheimer Auxiliary Velocities
papers.abstract: In Born-Oppenheimer (BO) dynamics, auxiliary variables such as electron densities, induced polarization and electrode charges follow stationarity conditions, yet their time derivatives, such as currents, are physical observables. Using Mass-Zero constrained dynamics, we interpret these derivatives as explicit dynamical variables and derive the invariant measure giving their equilibrium statistical properties. We illustrate the framework in constant-potential molecular dynamics, where the electrode-charge velocities reproduce BO current fluctuations and the frequency-dependent admittance.

papers.title: Data Center Governance Under AI Expansion Pressures
papers.abstract: The promised benefits of data centers are global, but their negative impacts are very much local, affecting the energy bills, aquifers and living environments of citizens across the United States. While governments and authorities have historically provided data centers with incentives such as tax credits and exemptions, AI's aggressive growth in scale has changed this dynamic, and recent months have seen them issue bills and file lawsuits in order to ensure that data centers remain a net positive influence on their legislatures. Existing pieces of federal legislation -- such as the Public Trust Doctrine, the Pollution Prevention, Clean Air and Safe Drinking Water Acts -- exist to manage natural resources, but their scope remains contested, and the current federal government's stance on competitiveness and growth of AI has put the onus on regional governments to endeavor to protect local resources. There are also state- and regional laws and regulations that are relevant for building and operating data centers since, in practice, they require substantial land, electricity, water, and infrastructure at a local level. Given this situation, communities are currently provided with the opportunity to raise their concerns regarding the potential negative impacts of how data centers are built and operated, and have existing regulations that can be used to put pressure on data center operators.

papers.title: List Update with Time Windows and Delays without Batch-Serving
papers.abstract: We study list update with time windows and delays when every request requires a separate access. Unlike batch-serving models, serving several requests to one element still incurs one access per request, and each access may change the list for subsequent requests. For time windows of overlap at most $k\ge2$, our deterministic First-Element Removal algorithm is $(3-2/k)$-competitive, hence $3$-competitive in general. Against an oblivious adversary, a randomized adaptation of BIT is $7/4$-competitive on arbitrary $2$-overlap inputs. More generally, on inputs without self-overlap, it is $\left(13/4-9/[2(k+1)]\right)$-competitive for every $k\ge2$. For delays, we give a deterministic $5$-competitive algorithm and a lower bound of $2+\sqrt3$ for deterministic delay-unaware algorithms. Our analyses extend inversion potentials with per-request credits that reconcile different service times and orders.

papers.title: High-pressure behavior of the low-frequency mode of water
papers.abstract: The low-frequency (LF) mode observed in the THz spectrum of liquid water near 10 meV has been known for decades, yet its microscopic origin remains debated. Leading interpretations assign it to a transverse acoustic-like excitation, a transverse optic-like mode, or a mode-mode coupling mechanism. We address this question by probing the collective dynamics of H$_2$O and D$_2$O at room temperature and pressures from 0.1 to 1 GPa using high-resolution (1.6 meV) inelastic X-ray scattering (IXS). The LF mode remains heavily damped, close to critical damping, throughout the explored range, while its frequency hardens markedly with pressure, much more than expected for a transverse acoustic mode. Comparison with IXS measurements and \textit{ab initio} simulations of crystalline Ice VI reveals a cluster of weakly dispersive modes in the same energy range, suggesting that the low-frequency mode in liquid water reflects a mixed character arising from the superposition of several branches rather than a single well-defined excitation, providing a coherent microscopic picture of water's anomalous THz dynamics under compression.

papers.title: Mass gap for the fractional $\Phi^4_2$ model
papers.abstract: We present a new, simple and self-contained technique for proving a mass gap for Euclidean quantum field theories in the high-temperature regime using the stochastic quantisation approach. As an application, we establish exponential decay of spatial correlations for the fractional $\Phi^4$ model on the plane in the Wick-ordering regime. The key idea is to analyse the propagation of perturbations using the linearised stochastic quantisation equation. Spatial propagation is controlled by an auxiliary random walk, while the potentially destabilising effect of the renormalised nonlinearity is controlled by combining dissipative energy estimates for the nonlinear dynamic with the Bou\'e-Dupuis variational formula.

papers.title: Consensus Capture in Reference-Based UAV Video Stabilization: A Benchmark on Dynamic Urban Scenes
papers.abstract: Reference-frame stabilization registers every frame of a hovering-drone video onto one reference frame, keeping object positions comparable. The registration pipelines it relies on are selected on feature-matching benchmarks in which only the camera moves. Over a busy intersection, vehicles moving together supply mutually consistent correspondences that can draw the robust homography estimate toward their motion: consensus capture, which inlier statistics cannot flag. A two-part benchmark measures it and the object masking meant to prevent it. A static protocol scores ten pipelines under exactly known homographies on 4K aerial frames, tuned on a site-disjoint split at a matched resolution and feature budget. A dynamic protocol scores them at an offline and a real-time budget on hovers selected from the video alone to span the amount and coherence of moving foreground, plus a stationary control. It measures background alignment, object position error and the share of a moving group's displacement an estimate follows, against a pseudo-ground-truth reference audited with manually annotated ground control points, which also score every candidate. On static scenes, tuned AKAZE, RootSIFT, SIFT and BRISK lead, retuning the matcher thresholds raises the mean average accuracy (mAA) by at most 0.0062, and masking costs less than 0.005. Unmasked ORB is captured on 28 of 304 real-time dynamic pairs and on 6 offline; its real-time captured estimates have a median corner error of 18.8 px yet typical inlier counts and ratios. Masking removes capture for every pipeline and leaves the leading pipelines unchanged. Code, data and results are released.

papers.title: Better Boundary Prediction Does Not Guarantee Better Structural Representation
papers.abstract: Punctuation marks often mark phrase boundaries, carrying linguistic information. Therefore, punctuation marks' abundance and feasibility as proxies of linguistic structure has led to suggestions that using punctuation marks to optimise on phrasal structure may help language models (LMs) improve their representations of argument, semantic, and syntactic structures. In this paper, we test the above claim in English across three primary LM architectures: decoder-only, encoder-only, and encoder-decoder LMs, by complementing traditional token prediction with punctuation restoration (PR). Our evidence, collected at the <1B parameter scale, suggests that optimising for boundary prediction does not necessarily guarantee higher-quality structural representation in decoder-only, encoder-decoder, and encoder-only LMs, failing to improve performance on downstream tasks that require understanding structure in linguistic input.

papers.title: DySR-GNN: Dynamic Sensor-Relationship Graph Neural Network for Root Cause Analysis in Automotive HiL Multivariate Time Series
papers.abstract: Root-cause analysis in automotive Hardware-in-the-Loop (HiL) systems is challenging because faults can propagate across multiple interacting signals, making the most abnormal sensor different from the actual fault origin. This work proposes DySR-GNN, a Dynamic Sensor-Relationship Graph Neural Network for supervised multi-label root-cause identification in multivariate HiL time series. The approach jointly extracts temporal patterns within individual sensor signals and structural relationships across sensors. Each sensor is processed by a shared temporal encoder and combined with a trainable sensor-identity representation, from which a sparse relationship graph is reconstructed independently for every input window. This window-specific structure provides an explicit representation of the sensor relationships used for graph message passing and direct root-location prediction. Under a recording-disjoint evaluation protocol, the proposed model outperforms CNN--LSTM, Static GCN, Static GAT, and context-based variants, achieving a recording-level Macro-F1 of 0.9524, MCC of 0.9302, and strict exact-match accuracy of 0.8519. Analysis of the learned graphs reveals both persistent and state-dependent relationships among sensor variables. The results demonstrate that extracting adaptive relational structure alongside temporal representations can improve multi-label root-cause identification in complex automotive cyber--physical systems.

papers.title: Discrete total variation under the multinomial, Part 5: cyclic total variation
papers.abstract: We study the cyclic discrete total variation obtained by adding the wrap-around edge to the usual open-chain statistic. Under the uniform multinomial law the cyclic symmetry recombines the same per-edge, adjacent, and disjoint covariance blocks used for the linear statistic, but with different multiplicities, and this simplifies the variance: the bin-independent leading coefficient \(2A+4B\) carries over, the constant-order correction collapses \emph{exactly} to \(\beta_c(n)=\beta_1 n\) (no \(n^0\) or \(1/n\) tail; obtained directly here, and already reached in Part~2 through the transfer identity), and a conditional second-order coefficient \(\gamma_c(n)\) is given. The exact finite-\(N\) cyclic--linear transfer identity of Part~2, read order by order, both delivers these and, as its main consequence for the \emph{linear} statistic, explains the traveling mode of the linear variance: comparison with the (first-order) mode-free symmetric cyclic profile shows that deleting one edge introduces a rising contribution whose balance against the falling cyclic bulk creates a ridge at \(n\asymp\sqrt{K_0N}\) with local optimizer \(K_0=C_1/\beta_1\). Uniform control of three ridge blocks proves this optimizer on every compact ridge window, upgrading the previously heuristic \(\sqrt N\) mode law to a theorem; the global localization of the exact maximizer remains open. We also record the corresponding cyclic reference-centered statistic under a fixed alternative and the leading Nabeya variance formula for the matched non-uniform cyclic statistic. Throughout, ``exact'' refers to the asymptotic coefficient in \(N\); the operative symmetry is cyclic stationarity (rotation invariance), not exchangeability.

papers.title: Variational approximation by complex Gaussians for the nonlinear logarithmic equation
papers.abstract: We consider the semiclassical logarithmic Schr{\"o}dinger equation, with an at most quadratic potential and with Gaussian initial states. For a critical nonlinear term in the semiclassical regime, we analyze an approximation based on the variational evolution of Gaussian wave packets. We also prove a nonlinear superposition principle for solutions issued from the sum of two Gaussian wave packets initially localized at distinct points in phase space. For both a single Gaussian wave packet and a superposition of two Gaussian wave packets, we compare the variational approximation with the standard coherent-state approximation and highlight their respective features. The required assumptions are weakened in this setting without becoming technically involved.

authors.name: Marianne Curely
authors.institution: Laboratoire Angevin de Recherche en Mathématiques

papers.title: Lara Mini Base: Language Diversity as a Resource, Not a Trade-off
papers.abstract: General-purpose language models are trained mostly on English: over open models we review, at most, non-English pretraining data makes up only a 12% share. Models built for European languages give them far more, but score well below general-purpose models of the same size. A common concern is that, in small models, languages compete for capacity. We present Lara Mini base, a model trained from scratch on 6T tokens in English and 44 other languages, which together cover all 24 official languages of the European Union. As training progresses, the 44 other languages together come to outweigh English. To give these languages enough capacity at low cost, Lara Mini base uses a mixture of experts architecture with 7.2B total and 0.6B active parameters. Among open base models with up to 2B active parameters, it achieves the highest average score across standard English, multilingual, math, and code benchmarks, ahead of models trained on 4 to 6 times as many tokens. Its margin is largest on multilingual benchmarks in the languages it supports and on math benchmarks. It supports contexts of up to 128k tokens. We find that our MoE architecture reduces capacity competition between languages. For a single user on one GPU, without quantization, it generates text at least 1.8 times faster than any model with a higher average score. We release the weights of Lara Mini base under the CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 license. In addition, we will release T-HellaSwag, a higher-quality machine translation of the commonsense reasoning benchmark HellaSwag into 110 language variants.

authors.name: Andrea Fernandez Tostado Ro. Diego Andrea

papers.title: IoTPwnBench: A Synthetic Benchmark for IoT Firmware Security Analysis
papers.abstract: Building and evaluating security tools for IoT firmware requires targets whose weaknesses are known in ad- vance and can be reproduced in a running device. Two problems remain: (1) firmware collected from real-world products provides realistic software, but hardware dependencies and undocumented defects make it difficult to establish what a security tool should be expected to find; and (2) existing benchmarks typically collect sets of vulnerable or misconfigured firmware images without providing purpose-built vulnerable services with explicit weaknesses that a security analysis tool can target. We present IoTPwnBench, a synthetic, modular benchmark that brings these requirements together. IoTPwnBench contains 716 vulnerable firmware images covering 86 weakness scenarios and 28 CWE classes across 11 device profiles, including industrial controllers, health monitors, and household devices. Each vulnerable image runs a plausible device application with simulated sensors and actuators that generate live readings over its native interfaces while exposing one target weakness mapped to a primary CWE. A documented exploitation payload and observable signal establish the expected behavior independently of the evaluated tool. Every vulnerable image is paired with a corrected twin that preserves the device and service while removing that weakness. Researchers can therefore compare the same target before and after correction to assess detection and false positives for the target weakness. The benchmark produces kernel and filesystem binaries for static inspection and dynamic testing under QEMU. Device profiles and weakness modules remain separate, allowing the same scenario to be reused across device contexts. Vulnerable targets were validated manually, and the open source build workflow regenerates the firmware bit-for-bit.

papers.title: Ideal polyhedral surfaces with prescribed cusped hyperbolic metric and their degeneration
papers.abstract: Rivin showed that every cusped hyperbolic metric on a punctured sphere is uniquely realized by a convex ideal polyhedron in hyperbolic space with possible degeneration. We consider the analogous problem for cusped hyperbolic metrics on a punctured surface of positive genus: locally convex ideal polyhedral surfaces in hyperbolic space. Each such surface determines a complex projective structure on the underlying closed surface. With a cusped hyperbolic metric $h$ prescribed, we investigate the space $\mathcal{P}(h)$ of such ideal polyhedral realizations and their possible degeneration. Particularly in the case of tori, we show that the space $\mathcal{P}(h)$ is homeomorphic to $\mathbb{R}^2$, and that the induced map to Teichm\"uller space of the closed torus is a $C^1$-embedding. This map extends to a bijection from the closure of $\mathcal{P}(h)$ onto the whole Teichm\"uller space, where the added points are degenerate surfaces. This is dual to the Kojima-Mizushima-Tan conjecture about circle patterns on closed surfaces with complex projective structures.

papers.title: Simple Length Multiplicity on X(n)
papers.abstract:
We study multiplicity among lengths of simple closed geodesics on the principal congruence surfaces $X(n)=\Gamma(n)\backslash\mathbb{H}$. We show that for every $\varepsilon>0$ there are positive constants $n_\varepsilon,C_{\varepsilon}$ so that, for $n\ge n_\varepsilon$, there are at least $\exp((\frac{\pi^2}{12}-\varepsilon)n)$ simple closed geodesics on $X(n)$ of the same length $\ell<C_\varepsilon n$. We produce the same multiplicity for $\lambda$-length of simple arcs with distinct endpoints via the McShane identity, which is immediately relevant as the size of a McShane gap around such an arc is roughly the reciprocal square of its $\lambda$-length. Our method of proof relies on an independently interesting theorem about the McShane identity for $X(n)$: the total mass of the gaps of pants with two cusps tends to 1 as $n\to \infty$. We present a proof of this latter fact that relies on estimates for the speed of mixing provided by Selberg's 3/16-Theorem (discovered with the help of ChatGPT).
  We indicate several avenues for further investigation.

papers.title: The Tiglath Pileser principle and models of persuasion
papers.abstract: This paper develops a formal framework for analysing how agents extract reliable information from narratives and communicative interactions involving strategic deception. Building on Rubinstein and Glazer's models of persuasion, we introduce Tiglath-Pileser relations, a generalization of codex-based guidance relations, to formalize Baruch Halpern's Tiglath-Pileser principle: despite systematic bias, reported claims must retain a connection to the truth. We analyse these relations set-theoretically and axiomatically, identifying conditions for their successful application in persuasion. Our dynamic approach examines how such relations are formed, revised, and strategically manipulated, extending existing models beyond one-shot interactions. Two case studies, including a formal reconstruction of Halpern's interpretation of the biblical account of King David, illustrate the framework's application to historiographical reasoning. Combining logic, epistemic reasoning, and game theory, the paper provides an account of belief formation and truth approximation under partial information and strategic manipulation.

papers.title: Isotonic least squares is robust to heteroscedasticity, unimodal least squares is not
papers.abstract: We compare the least squares estimator (LSE) with the $\ell_{1}$-estimator recently introduced by Baraud and Maillard~\citeyearpar{BM-2026} for estimating a regression function under a fixed design, when the errors are independent but possibly heteroscedastic and heavy-tailed. We show that the two estimators coincide on the class of nondecreasing (or nonincreasing) functions on an interval. As a consequence, the isotonic LSE inherits the non-asymptotic $\ell_{1}$-risk bounds of the $\ell_{1}$-estimator, which only require a moment of order $p\in[1,2]$ on the errors and depend on the average of their $p$-th absolute moments rather than on their maximum. This coincidence no longer holds on the nonconvex class of unimodal functions: we exhibit a heteroscedastic Gaussian example in which the LSE is inconsistent while the $\ell_{1}$-estimator converges at the parametric rate. Finally, we show on a one-dimensional linear model that neither estimator dominates the other: depending on the way the noise is distributed among the design points, the LSE may converge at rate $1/n$ while the $\ell_{1}$-estimator is inconsistent.

papers.title: Decide Before You Move: Diffusion-Generated Search Reference for Zero-Shot Open-Vocabulary Object Navigation in Semi-Static Environments
papers.abstract: Open-world navigation requires a robot to locate a user-specified target in an indoor scene under open-vocabulary queries. Realistic indoor environments are semi-static: walls and furniture largely persist while smaller objects move, relocate, or vanish between visits. Prior-map systems answer queries from object poses recorded at reconstruction time, which expire as soon as objects move, whereas online methods re-derive where to look from current observations every few steps, often through expensive calls to a vision--language model. Assuming that walls and large furniture do not move, we keep their map to plan paths, but use a target--furniture co-occurrence prior to decide where to search. We present PreNav, an ObjectNav framework on semi-static environments. Rather than invoking a vision-language model at each step, PreNav generates a single global search reference before the robot moves: an LLM converts target--furniture co-occurrence into a spatial prior, a conditional diffusion model turns that prior and the persistent structure into an ordered centerline with a band around it, and the robot approaches the target once it is detected online. Experiments on a Gibson ObjectNav benchmark show that PreNav outperforms a strong online baseline under matched structural priors, using a generator trained only on room-level ScanNet++ scenes and applied to floor-level Gibson without fine-tuning. Real-world experiments under object relocation and open-vocabulary queries further validate the approach.

authors.name: Hermann Blum
authors.institution: Lamarr Institute for Machine Learning and Artificial Intelligence

papers.title: HeriKGQA: Grounded Knowledge-Graph Question Answering over Cultural Heritage Sensor Data
papers.abstract: Cultural heritage sites are increasingly monitored by sensor networks, but querying their data requires database expertise. Large Language Models (LLMs) offer a natural-language interface, yet over raw sensor records they lose track of which sensor, site, and time each value belongs to, and silently miscompute. We present HeriKGQA, a knowledge-graph question-answering method that confines the LLM to interpreting questions and phrasing answers, leaving computation to SPARQL and deterministic code. Questions are parsed into intents constrained by a heritage ontology aligning W3C SOSA/SSN with CIDOC-CRM, compiled into SPARQL, and answered from query results and temporal, spatial, and anomaly facts derived by a grounding layer, with error correction guarding each LLM step. On 500 questions over real data from five heritage sites, HeriKGQA reaches 99.0% accuracy, 18.2 points above the strongest of three baselines using the same LLM and receiving the same anomaly rules and answer conventions, with comparable answer quality while running almost four times faster. Without grounding, accuracy drops by 12.2 points and on anomaly questions from 99% to 66%. We report lessons from development and live deployment.

papers.title: Generic unipotent representations of finite reductive groups
papers.abstract: Let $\mathbb{G}$ be a generic reductive group in the sense of Brou\'e--Malle--Michel. We construct a category over $\mathbb{Z}[t,t^{-1}]$ which interpolates between the various categories of unipotent representations of $\mathbb{G}(q)$ as we specialize $t$ to $q$. We use this category to show two properties of the unipotent decomposition matrix of $\mathbb{G}(q)$ mod $\ell$ (not dividing $q$): that, uniformly in $(q,\ell)$, there are finitely many such matrices and that for $\ell$ large enough, depending only on $\mathbb{G}$, this decomposition matrix depends only on the root of unity corresponding to $q$ mod $\ell$. We also prove that for $q$ and $q'$ two prime powers that are $\ell$-adically close enough, the categories of unipotent mod $\ell$ representations of $\mathbb{G}(q)$ and $\mathbb{G}(q')$ are equivalent.

papers.title: On the Brou\'e--Digne--Michel conjectures: disjointness of the cohomology groups
papers.abstract: The goal of this paper is to start proving the Brou\'e--Digne--Michel conjectures concerning the cohomology of Deligne--Lusztig varieties attached to roots of the full twist. The main result establishes that the $\mathrm{Ext}$-algebras of the cohomology complexes attached to roots of the full twist are concentrated in degree $0$. The main idea is to reduce the problem to a calculation in the Hecke category. The resulting argument is essentially topological and applies to all realizations of the Hecke category.

papers.title: Maximal nilpotence for higher Verlinde categories
papers.abstract: We show that all higher Verlinde categories are maximally nilpotent, as conjectured by Coulembier (2023). By previous results, it suffices to show that non-trivial simple objects have only finitely many non-zero symmetric powers in odd characteristic. We compute the maximal degrees of these non-zero symmetric and exterior powers explicitly, hence confirming their finiteness. We discuss some of the far-reaching consequences.

papers.title: Advancing global water cycle science with the upcoming MAGIC satellite mission through data assimilation
papers.abstract: The GRACE and GRACE-FO missions provide unique global measurements of terrestrial water storage anomalies (TWSA) from space since 2003. However, in order to spatially downscale the GRACE/-FO resolution of 300 km further, and to vertically disaggregate TWSA into soil moisture, groundwater and other contributions, the TWSA observations were assimilated into hydrological and land surface models in the past while improving the realism of the models. With the upcoming MAGIC (Mass Change and Geosciences International Constellation) constellation consisting of two satellite pairs (NASA/DLR GRACE-C and ESA NGGM), significant advancements are expected for the monitoring of water mass changes, with improved temporal and spatial resolution, reduced latency, and with lower noise levels. In this study, we reviewed the capabilities and limitations of existing GRACE/-FO data assimilation systems. We then investigated the benefit of including data from the upcoming MAGIC constellation into existing assimilation frameworks to improve not only data sets for water and carbon cycle science but also in view of operational applications, within a closed-loop simulation. For example, we extended a global 17 years GRACE/-FO assimilation era to a long time series of 33 years with synthetic MAGIC data assimilated and show reductions in groundwater trends errors and errors in identifying hydrological extreme events. We further showed for Europe that both storage and river runoff simulations benefit from more frequent assimilation, which the integration of MAGIC data will enable due to the foreseen 5-daily (instead of monthly) TWSA product. Finally, we demonstrated for the Iberian Peninsula and for Eastern Europe that MAGIC TWSA data assimilation also improved simulated carbon cycle variables via coupling in the land surface model, especially in water-limited regions.

papers.title: Minimizing Monotone Norms in Fractional Load Balancing
papers.abstract:
We devise a fully polynomial time approximation scheme for minimizing a monotone norm $\left\lVert\cdot\right\rVert$ over a convex set $X\subseteq \mathbb{R}^d_{\geq 0}$. We study the multi-customer setting, where $X=\sum_{i=1}^n X_i$ and the solution set $X_i\subseteq \mathbb{R}^d_{\geq 0}$ is given by a linear minimization oracle for each customer $i$. Our algorithm computes, for any given $\varepsilon>0$, a $(1+\varepsilon)$-approximate solution. With high probability, it uses $\tilde{\mathcal{O}}\left( \varepsilon^{-2}(n+d) \right)$ single-customer linear minimization oracle calls and the same number of generalized KL projections to the dual space $Y=\{y\in \mathbb{R}^d_{\geq 0}: \left\lVert y \right\rVert^* \le 1\}$. We assume no prior knowledge on $X$, and our running time depends only on $n$, $d$, and $\varepsilon$. Our result is robust in the sense that it allows for approximate linear minimization oracles and approximate KL projections. We show that the (approximate) KL projection can be performed efficiently for large classes of monotone norms, demonstrating the applicability of our approach.
  While such a result (with exact projection) is well-known for the $\ell_{\infty}$ norm via multiplicative weight updates and was recently obtained for ordered norms via a smooth norm approximation and a novel randomization, existing techniques do not extend to general monotone norms. In particular, a key feature used in previous proofs was dual price stability, which was derived from a global contraction property of the KL projection to the dual space $Y$. We show that this property does not extend to general monotone norms. Therefore, we use a different price mechanism, based on the well-known mirror descent paradigm, for which a local contraction property holds and guarantees stability.

papers.title: PSR J1807-2459B in NGC 6544: A Unique Relativistic Binary in a Dense Cluster
papers.abstract: The globular cluster NGC 6544 is a high-density, dynamically evolved system located in the direction of the Galactic Center, known for hosting the eccentric binary millisecond pulsar PSR J1807-2459B. We present a new timing solution for this pulsar, based on more than 26 years of observations with the Parkes, Green Bank and MeerKAT radio telescopes. We measure for the first time the variation of the orbital period, which is dominated by the acceleration of the binary in the cluster potential: this places the pulsar in front of the cluster center and reveals its intrinsic spin-down, typical of a fully recycled millisecond pulsar. We also improve the measurements of the rate of advance of periastron and of the Einstein delay, the latter by a factor of four, and include the previously neglected contributions of the proper motion, which makes these parameters and the derived masses of the pulsar and its companion, $1.3636^{+0.0017}_{-0.0021}\,M_\odot$ and $1.2071^{+0.0021}_{-0.0017}\,M_\odot$, more realistic. Together with the Shapiro delay, these measurements allow two independent tests of general relativity, both passed. Our results show that precise post-Keplerian parameters of a binary pulsar in a dense cluster can probe both the cluster gravitational field and general relativity, provided that kinematic effects are carefully taken into account.

papers.title: On the Adams spectral sequence of $eo_2(C_4)$
papers.abstract: We calculate the mod $2$-homology of the fixed points of the $C_4$-equivariant Hill--Hopkins--Ravenel theory $BP^{((C_4))}\langle 1\rangle$, as an $\mathcal{A}_*$-comodule algebra. $2$-locally these fixed points are $tmf_0(5)$ by a theorem of Quinn. We deduce that $tmf_0(5)$ is an indecomposable $tmf$-module that is an extension of two $tmf$-modules of the form $tmf\otimes K$ for a finite spectrum $K$. The $K(2)$-localization of $tmf_0(5)$ is $32$-periodic, and we compute the Adams spectral sequence of $tmf_0(5)$ through the $32$-stem.

papers.title: Over-the-Air Computation for Imperfectly Synchronized Multi-View Semantic Communication
papers.abstract: Compared to classical task-agnostic communication systems, which focus on reliable transmission of a message, semantic communication (SemCom) focuses on transmitting the task-relevant meaning behind the message. In this paper, we design a SemCom system for a distributed multi-view scenario, where multiple semantic devices observe a scene and collaborate through a single semantic receiver to execute a task. We propose adopting an Over-the-Air Computation (AirComp) channel for efficient use of resources, as AirComp uses a superposition of signals to directly compute a function, which in SemCom is decoding the semantic variable. However, AirComp relies heavily on perfect time and phase synchronization, which is not practical in real-world communication. We show that timing offsets of standards like 5G cause negligible degradation, and that larger timing offsets can be compensated by training. Nevertheless, the system cannot deal with the encountered levels of phase synchronization errors, even when trained with those levels of synchronization errors. Therefore, we propose integrating existing phase synchronization algorithms into the AirComp SemCom system training. Simulation results show that the proposed system can approach the task execution performance of a perfectly synchronized SemCom system.

papers.title: A posteriori error estimates for the bulk--surface Cahn--Hilliard system with dynamic boundary conditions
papers.abstract: This paper develops reliable residual-based a posteriori error estimators for the full discretization of a bulk--surface Cahn--Hilliard system with a two-parameter family of dynamic boundary conditions on a curved domain. The main novelty are theoretically justified computable temporal, coarsening and geometric error estimators. The numerical method combines a linear bulk--surface finite element method in space and a linearly implicit backward Euler method in time. Based on the derived error indicators, a space--time adaptive algorithm is proposed and numerical experiments illustrate and complement the theoretical result.

papers.title: A Joint Study of Epoch Astrometry and Radial Velocities of Gaia-4b
papers.abstract: Gaia-4b is the first confirmed exoplanet discovered with Gaia astrometry, based on its identification as a possible exoplanet in the solution in Gaia Data Release 3 and subsequent confirmation with radial velocity. In this work we present a \texttt{python} framework called \texttt{pyGaiafits} that can jointly analyze astrometric time series and radial velocities. We use this to combine the precise along-scan astrometric time series for Gaia-4 from the Gaia DR4 pre-release with 44 radial velocities (RVs) obtained over three years from four independent spectrographs (HPF, HARPS-N, NEID, and FIES). By jointly fitting these two complementary datasets that collectively span a 12-year baseline ($\sim$7 orbital periods of Gaia-4b), we refine the system parameters and determine the true mass of Gaia-4b to be $10.70\pm0.32$~$M_J$. Critically, we do not find significant evidence for the long-term quadratic RV trend previously reported in the literature, recovering $\ddot{\gamma} = 5.5^{+8.3}_{-6.7}\;\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}\,yr^{-2}}$ consistent with zero. We discuss how this discrepancy likely arises from a degeneracy between orbital period and long-term trends when RVs span only $\sim$1.5 orbital cycles --- a degeneracy that is broken by anchoring the ephemeris with early Gaia astrometry.

papers.title: The Black Hole Mass of the Sunflower Galaxy NGC 5055: Direct Measurement via Stellar Kinematics with Keck/OSIRIS Laser Guide Star Adaptive Optics
papers.abstract: We present the first stellar-dynamical supermassive black hole mass measurement in the nearby spiral galaxy NGC 5055 (M63) using near-infrared integral-field spectroscopy with Keck/OSIRIS assisted by the laser guide star adaptive optics system. The observations deliver two-dimensional stellar kinematics extracted from the CO bandhead absorption features via pPXF at an angular resolution of $0.045''$. The stellar velocity dispersion rises steeply from $\sim90~{\rm km~s^{-1}}$ at $r\sim1''$ to a central peak of $\sim135~{\rm km~s^{-1}}$, kinematically tracing the gravitational influence of a central mass concentration. Modeling these kinematics with an ensemble of four JAM models, spanning cylindrical and spherical velocity-ellipsoid alignments and two independent MGE decompositions of archival HST imaging, yields a black hole mass of $M_{\rm BH}=4.56^{+1.73}_{-1.82}\times10^6~{\rm M_\odot}$. The stellar orbits are consistent with near-isotropy ($\beta\approx0$), typical of rotating late-type galaxies. NGC 5055 emerges as a remarkable local analogue to the Milky Way in terms of its black hole, nuclear star cluster, and total stellar mass. The surface brightness profile of NGC 5055 shows no evidence for a classical bulge; if confirmed bulgeless, NGC 5055 would join the rare class of spirals with a direct dynamical $M_{\rm BH}$ determination in the absence of a bulge, a regime currently populated by only a handful of galaxies including NGC 2748 and NGC 4395. This measurement provides a new anchor for black hole scaling relations in late-type galaxies at the low-mass end of the black hole mass spectrum.

authors.institution: Centre de Recherche Astrophysique de Lyon

authors.institution: Astronomical Institute of the Slovak Academy of Sciences
