papers.title: Extension of the Renard-Deck Drag Decomposition to Compressible Rough-Wall Turbulent Boundary Layers
papers.abstract: A generalized Renard-Deck (RD) drag decomposition is developed for spatially developing compressible turbulent boundary layers over rough surfaces. Derived from the locally resolved, time-averaged momentum equations, the formulation accounts for both viscous friction and pressure drag without requiring spatial averaging at the roughness-element scale. Eight direct numerical simulations are considered at freestream Mach numbers of 2.5 and 5.86, comparing smooth walls and two-dimensional transverse square ribs ($\lambda_x/k=8$) under adiabatic and cold-wall conditions. The decomposition reconstructs the total drag with errors below 5%. Mean-flow viscous dissipation and turbulent kinetic-energy production together account for approximately 90% of the drag work. While their contributions are comparable over smooth walls, turbulent production dominates over rough walls, contributing approximately 80%. More importantly, roughness substantially alters the wall-normal distributions of both contributions. Viscous dissipation becomes concentrated near the roughness crest, whereas turbulent production peaks above the crest, with both contributions decaying more gradually into the outer layer than over smooth walls. The resulting differences in their cumulative contributions persist across a substantial fraction of the boundary layer, demonstrating that the energetic influence of surface roughness extends well beyond the roughness sublayer.

papers.title: A parametrized simulation code to simulate the response of ground detector arrays to Extensive Air Showers above 100 TeV
papers.abstract: Surface arrays detecting the secondary particles of Extensive Air Showers (EAS) are one of the techniques used to detect gamma-rays from high-energy sources. To evaluate the reconstruction performance, gamma/hadron separation, and sensitivity of such experiments, many simulations of gamma rays and protons are required. The usual approach is divided into two steps. First, the CORSIKA software is used to generate EAS at the observation level. Then, a GEANT4-based full simulation code is used to simulate the array response. For very large fill factors, above 30-100 TeV, the computational resources required become too demanding. In this work, the authors present an alternative way to evaluate the performance-related quantities of a simulated array configuration through the parametrization of the detector response. We will present the implementation of such software, the validation checks we performed, and the application of this tool to a representative future ground-based water-Cherenkov detector array.

authors.name: Andrea Chiavassa
authors.institution: Istituto Nazionale di Fisica Nucleare, Sezione di Torino

papers.title: SPADE: Soft Prompts for Ai-text DEtection
papers.abstract: The easy access to Large Language Models (LLMs) has made AI-generated texts on the web increasingly ubiquitous, making AI-text detection a crucial task. Prompts greatly influence the generation process, but existing detectors focus solely on the generated texts --- supervised methods learn from labeled texts only, and zero-shot methods rely on the text's probability distributions --- ignoring the underlying generation process, which limits their robustness in open-world scenarios. We introduce SPADE: Soft Prompts for Ai-text DEtection, a novel framework for detecting AI-generated text that transfers better across datasets. Specifically, we measure the prompt's influence and use it as a discriminative signal. We characterize the prompt's influence by introducing a Pointwise Mutual Information (PMI) term that captures how much a prompt explains a text. Based on this quantity, SPADE trains one soft prompt per class to amplify the separation, and predicts the class whose prompt best explains the candidate text. Extensive experiments on several benchmarks against various detectors demonstrate the robustness and effectiveness of our method, achieving state-of-the-art (SOTA) performance on out-of-distribution (OOD) datasets.

papers.title: AGB Atmospheres in Binary Environments: A First Step with CO5BOLB
papers.abstract: Asymptotic Giant Branch (AGB) stars are characterized by complex atmospheric dynamics driven by convection and pulsations. In binary systems, the presence of a companion can further influence these dynamics, potentially affecting mass-loss processes and the morphology of the circumstellar environment, yet this influence on the atmosphere itself remains poorly quantified. This study aims to fill this gap by employing CO5BOLD simulations with a modified gravitational potential to explore how companion mass affects the atmospheric structure of AGB stars. We used radiative hydrodynamics (RHD) simulations with CO5BOLD to model the convective interior and atmosphere of AGB stars. We modified the gravitational potential to include a secondary mass and a centrifugal term, representing the companion as a point-mass potential on a steady, tidally locked circular orbit outside the computational domain, with the Coriolis force neglected. We performed simulations with different companion masses and using singular value decomposition (SVD), we identified the spatial distribution of pulsation energy and quantified its properties. We also examined the density structure to identify anisotropies induced by the companion. We isolate two dynamically distinct regimes, a pulsation-dominated layer and an outer, low-frequency outflow region, whose pulsation properties remain largely unaffected by the companion: their frequency, amplitude, and coherence stay consistent across all models. The density structure, by contrast, responds clearly to the companion, forming a pronounced anisotropy along the binary axis that strengthens with companion mass. This indicates that the intrinsic pulsational dynamics of the AGB star dominate over the tidal influence of the companion within the explored parameter space, while the density structure remains the most sensitive tracer of binarity.

authors.name: Andrea Chiavassa
authors.institution: Istituto Nazionale di Fisica Nucleare, Sezione di Torino

papers.title: Spinorial geometry of Bismut--Hermitian--Einstein manifolds
papers.abstract: We present a pair of spinorial equations, generalizing the internal Killing spinor equations of Type I supergravity, and show that they characterize several classes of Bismut-Hermitian-Einstein structures on six-dimensional Riemannian spin manifolds. We show that in this framework the local reduction to a four-dimensional transverse Hermitian geometry is provided by two canonical, commuting, Bismut-parallel Killing vector fields arising as bilinears in the Killing spinors, without assuming compactness. In one class, the transverse geometry is conformally Kahler and both compact and non-compact solutions exist. We also discuss variants that do not admit compact solutions, one of which has hyper-Hermitian transverse geometry. We discuss the relation of these structures to the Hull-Strominger system with closed three-form and to five-dimensional Gauntlett-Kim geometries and provide explicit embeddings in Type I, Type IIB and massive Type IIA supergravity, as well as in generalized supergravity. We illustrate our results with a number of examples, both compact and non-compact.

authors.name: Matteo Kevin Crisafio
authors.institution: Istituto Nazionale di Fisica Nucleare, Sezione di Torino

authors.name: Dario Martelli
authors.institution: Istituto Nazionale di Fisica Nucleare, Sezione di Torino

papers.title: Beyond weak convergence of signed spectral measures: Eigenvector overlaps and high-dimensional prediction risk
papers.abstract: Many results in random matrix theory and high-dimensional statistics depend on weak convergence of spectral measures, which is usually established via pointwise convergence of Stieltjes transforms. This approach has recently been applied to signed measures. However, for signed measures, pointwise convergence of Stieltjes transforms alone no longer characterizes weak convergence. While this is unproblematic in many cases, in the high-dimensional regression setting, recently considered by Green and Romanov (2025), the underlying signed eigenvector-overlap measures can fail to converge weakly, despite pointwise convergence of their Stieltjes transforms. Using a novel approach to risk analysis, we show that weak convergence can be replaced by a simple convergence result for bilinear forms. This allows us to establish convergence of the prediction risk for estimators based on arbitrary continuous spectral filters, including (regularized) gradient descent and ridge regression, even when the underlying signed measures fail to converge weakly. Under additional regularity conditions, we construct an explicit finite signed measure yielding an integral representation of the asymptotic prediction risk. This representation provides necessary and sufficient conditions for minimum-norm interpolation and optimally tuned ridge regression to attain the smallest asymptotic prediction risk among estimators with continuous spectral filters. Moreover, we provide characterizations of weak and vague convergence of finite signed measures in terms of pointwise convergence of their Stieltjes transforms.

authors.name: Thomas Stark
authors.institution: Deutsches Zentrum für Luft- und Raumfahrt e. V. (DLR)

papers.title: Huge If True: Learning from the Size of the Surprise
papers.abstract: Responses to earnings surprises depend on an unknown multiplier mapping earnings to value. Investors, however, learn about the news and the multiplier from the same number. Large surprises may indicate small multipliers and tiny surprises large ones. We model how greater uncertainty about the multiplier attenuates responses on average but makes them steeper near zero surprises. In an incentivized experiment, we find that greater processing constraints lower average sensitivity but raise it near zero. We confirm this with real-world earnings announcements: stocks with higher valuation uncertainty, our proxy for multiplier uncertainty, respond less on average but more steeply near zero.

papers.title: Canonical Truncation for Mixed-Integer and Combinatorial n-Fold Optimization
papers.abstract:
We consider a special block-structured integer program with $n$ blocks. Every block has a prescribed number of vectors that need to be selected while minimizing the objective $c^{\intercal}x + g(Ax)$, where $c$ is a rational cost vector, $A$ is an integral matrix with $d$ rows, and $g \colon \mathbb{Z}^d \to \mathbb{Q}\cup \{+\infty\}$ is an arbitrary function. We access $g$ via an oracle that minimizes $c^{\intercal}x + g(Ax)$ when all but $O(d)$ variables are fixed. Our algorithm runs in time $(nd\Delta)^{O(d)}(Q + \text{poly}(|I|))$ where $\Delta$ is the largest absolute value of an entry in $A$, $Q$ is the necessary time to evaluate the oracle for $g$ and $|I|$ is the size of the input. This model is a variation of the model studied by Dadush et al.~[IPCO 23]. Their model has only a single block but individual upper and lower bounds on the variables instead of prescribed block sums. For their model they present an algorithm with running time $t^d(d\Delta)^{O(d^2)}Q$ where $t$ is the number of variables.
  We use our algorithm to solve mixed-integer linear programs with no upper bounds on the variables, a linear objective, and arbitrarily many constraints involving only fractional variables in time $(m\Delta)^{O(m)}\text{poly}(|I|)$, where $m$ is the number of constraints involving integral variables and $\Delta$ is the largest absolute value of coefficients of integral variables. This improves the dependence on $m$ in the exponent to asymptotically match the dependency in the integer setting. Further, we use our algorithm to generalize the parameterized algorithm for scheduling on uniformly related machines by Rohwedder~[ICALP 25] to obtain an algorithm for multiple knapsack with running time $w_{\max}^{O(d)}\text{poly}(|I|)$ where $w_{\max}$ is the maximum weight of an item and $d$ the number of different weights.

papers.title: Interfacial Structure and Dynamics of Active-Passive Fluid Mixtures
papers.abstract: We investigate the interface between an active and a passive fluid using molecular dynamics simulations of active Brownian particles in contact with a passive Lennard-Jones fluid. We compute the surface tension via two independent routes, pressure anisotropy and capillary-wave analysis, and find that they disagree systematically once activity is switched on. Static density and orientation profiles reveal three distinct activity regimes, with particles preferentially oriented toward the interface. Going beyond these static properties, we characterize the interface dynamics: a threshold activity above which mixing becomes irreversible, coinciding with the onset of the mixing regime, and a transient overshoot in interfacial width before relaxation to steady state.

authors.name: Linnea Heitmeier
authors.institution: Deutsches Zentrum für Luft- und Raumfahrt e. V. (DLR)

papers.title: Typed Knowledge over Constructive Institutions: A Proof-Relevant Type Theory for Verified Science
papers.abstract:
Mathematical proof assistants such as Coq, Agda, and Lean 4 build proof irrelevance into definitional conversion ($p \equiv q$ for $p, q : P$ with $P : Prop$), erasing which derivation established a theorem. While natural for mathematics over fixed axioms, judgmental proof irrelevance is incompatible with verified scientific stores, which must inspect and compare independent derivations of the same claim to assess consilience and compute counterfactual retractions when an assay, reagent, or model is invalidated. Moreover, combining definitional proof irrelevance with subsingleton elimination breaks strong normalization and renders algorithmic conversion non-transitive.
  We present the type-theoretic and institutional foundations of Eigenius, a verified knowledge substrate for science. First, we formulate a dependent kernel with cumulative universes ($Prop, Set, Type_k$), impredicative $Prop$, inductive families with index-forced subsingleton elimination, and intensional identity types, where definitional equality $\equiv$ is untyped joinability under an orthogonal CRS and proof irrelevance is a witnessed propositional axiom ($irrel : \Pi P{:}Prop.\,\Pi p,q{:}P.\,Id\,P\,p\,q$). Second, we unify universe cumulativity, codomain-covariant $\Pi$-subtyping, and ontology class inclusions in a coercion-free subsumption judgment whose bidirectional fragments ($\mathcal{K}_0, \mathcal{K}_1$) satisfy subject reduction and are sound and complete for declarative typing. Third, we organize external verifiers into a three-level institutional hierarchy with explicit axiom policies (Adopt, Discharge, Relativize), internalize a justification logic with Why-provenance semiring support $supp(j,P)$, and embed Cooper's Type Theory with Records (TTR) to type open-world knowledge graphs. Finally, we prove consistency in Grothendieck universes and mechanize the metatheory in Lean 4 with zero sorry axioms.

papers.title: Learning to Calibrate Jet Energies
papers.abstract: Hadronic jets are produced copiously at the Large Hadron Collider, and are a vital element of its physics program. Accurate reconstruction of their energies is therefore crucial, including correction for pile-up, detector response and data-simulation differences. Currently, each correction is performed by fitting parametric functional forms, an approach which is effective but can be fragile and challenging to extend. We present a prototype machine-learning pipeline which performs pile-up dependency removal, absolute corrections and data-mc corrections. No functional form is imposed on the correction, additional features can be easily added, and the pipeline matches or exceeds the performance of the functional approach at nearly every stage.

authors.name: Benjamin Nachman
authors.institution: Centre de physique des particules de Marseille

papers.title: MemCredit: From Relevance to Utility for Decision-Time Memory in Long-Horizon Web Agents
papers.abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents increasingly operate over long Web interaction histories, making memory management critical for reliable and efficient decision making. Existing methods primarily optimize storage, retrieval, or compression, but the memories most semantically relevant to the current state are not necessarily those that most improve the agent's action. We introduce MemCredit, a decision-centric memory framework that shifts memory selection from semantic relevance to decision utility. MemCredit estimates the state-, reference-context-, and policy-conditional marginal contribution of individual memories through controlled counterfactual interventions, and distills these intervention-derived credits into a lightweight utility estimator. At inference time, semantic relevance is used only for high-recall candidate generation, while predicted utility arbitrates which memories are retained under a fixed token budget, without modifying the underlying agent policy or requiring additional environment interaction. We evaluate MemCredit on ALFWorld and WebShop against representative memory baselines. On ALFWorld, MemCredit achieves 86.57 SR@50 under a 500-token historical-memory budget, compared with 65.67% for BM25 retrieval. Counterfactual analysis further shows that memory utility is sparse, strongly state dependent, and poorly captured by semantic relevance. These results suggest that decision utility provides a more effective principle than relevance alone for long-horizon agent memory management.

authors.name: Quanjiang Guo
authors.institution: University of Electronic Science and Technology of China

authors.name: Qianyang Zhu
authors.institution: University of Electronic Science and Technology of China

papers.title: Zugwise: Domain-Aware Game Reconstruction for Digitizing Handwritten Chess Scoresheets
papers.abstract: Digitizing handwritten chess scoresheets has been studied as a handwriting-recognition problem: read the move in each box and check that it is legal. This framing misses the errors that matter most. A misread that yields an illegal move is loud. One that yields a legal-but-wrong move is silent, because a legality-only pipeline accepts it and reads every later move against a wrong position. We therefore treat the task as game reconstruction and present Zugwise, which repurposes computer-chess machinery (quiescence search, static exchange evaluation, pin detection) to ask not "what should be played?" but "could a human plausibly have written this?" An absurdity detector makes silent errors loud at or near where they occur, and a backward search traces late symptoms to their cause. Candidate ranking excludes chess-quality signals. A Needleman-Wunsch merge adds the second player's sheet as evidence, and review stops send every disagreement between the sheets' legal readings to a human. In oracle replay of two tournament sections, a release adding them cuts silent errors from 16 to 1 and from 50 to 13. Two learned signals, CTC re-scoring against the recognizer's raw output and a Maia-style human-move prior, raise the correct fix's top-rank rate from 58.8% to 78.0% of the replacement decisions where it is a candidate, and hold without refitting on a later section. On the first section, the human-verified output matches an independent expert transcription move for move on 34 of 45 games, and adjudication against the sheets found errors in both records, on different plies. We do not establish that either workflow is faster or more accurate. The system runs entirely in the browser and is free, private, and offline-capable; alongside it we offer a three-way adjudication protocol for a domain where no single record is ground truth.

papers.title: Small Maximum Likelihood on Fixed Cavender-Farris-Neyman Trees: An Approximation Scheme and Limits to Fully Polynomial Approximation
papers.abstract: Small Maximum Likelihood fits the edge substitution probabilities of a given phylogenetic tree to an observed alignment, summing over the unobserved ancestral states. For the binary Cavender--Farris--Neyman model, we assume a uniform root and an edge-specific substitution probability $p_e\in[0,\tfrac12]$ for each edge $e$, shared across all alignment sites. We give a deterministic polynomial-time approximation scheme. The algorithm achieves a factor of $1+\varepsilon$ for both the negative log likelihood and the loss after subtracting the uniform-root contribution. Its main step fixes ancestral sequences at one periodically spaced class of depths while summing over all remaining ancestors. A posterior entropy bound controls the cost of this restriction, and dynamic programming optimizes the resulting components over a finite parameter grid. We also give a randomized reduction from Clique showing that an FPTAS returning feasible rational edge probabilities would imply $RP=NP$. These results separate fixed-accuracy approximation from fully polynomial approximation for the same fixed-tree model.

papers.title: Testing Conversation Preservation Across LLM APIs: A Rule-Based Oracle for Detecting Silent Information Loss
papers.abstract: LLM applications increasingly rely on translators and compatibility layers to move conversations across APIs. Yet a translated request can be accepted by the target API while silently losing information about instruction roles, tool interactions, error states, or generation controls. We introduce isloss, a deterministic oracle for testing conversation-information preservation across LLM API translations. It maps source and translated requests and replies to a shared intermediate representation, ConvIR, and applies explicit rules to distinguish legitimate representation changes from information loss. Unlike schema validation or reference-based differential testing, isloss requires neither a reference translation nor additional model calls. It also distinguishes avoidable loss from degradation caused by target API limitations. We evaluate isloss using specification-based fault injection, human review, and experiments on translators, gateways, and client libraries. On held-out tests, it detects 95/125 planted faults (76.0%) with 2/100 false alarms (2.0%). Across a synthetic request suite spanning six configurations of five translator codebases, 127/685 completed translations (18.5%) pass static target checks while silently changing prompt, role, or tool information in ways the target API could have preserved. In translated replies, 203/558 streams (36.4%) cause exceptions or silent corruption in at least one tested official OpenAI SDK. Targeted experiments across six models show that translation-induced changes can alter model behaviour when tasks depend on the affected information. These results establish conversation preservation as a distinct correctness requirement for reliable LLM interoperability, agent execution, and model evaluation.

authors.name: Xu Han
authors.institution: Heilongjiang University of Science and Technology

authors.name: Haoran Song
authors.institution: Leibniz Institute for Analytical Sciences - ISAS

papers.title: A Modified Glicko Model for Rating Soccer Clubs and National Teams Worldwide
papers.abstract: Comparing soccer teams that rarely or never meet is a fundamental challenge in sports analytics: clubs play mostly within their national leagues, and national teams within their confederations. We propose a rating framework that places clubs and national teams worldwide on a common probabilistic scale. Building on a recent extension of Glicko with order effects and strength-dependent draw probabilities, we adapt the model to soccer with goal-scoring adjustments, a decomposition of home advantage, extra time, league-aware rating initialization and rules of promotion and relegation that do not inflate the levels of leagues; national teams start from the levels of their confederations. The models are evaluated on about 1.2 million club matches of 252 leagues from 166 countries (2000-2026) and 12.6 thousand national team matches (1998-2026). On held-out seasons, the modified Glicko model is clearly more accurate than Elo and as accurate as score-matrix models built on the goal expectations of a gradient boosting model, including the Dixon-Coles and Markov chain models, while it is substantially more accurate in international club matches. Averaging the predictions of the rating model and the Markov chain model is more accurate than either model alone. For national teams, the model is significantly more accurate than all baselines, especially in the final tournaments, where teams of different confederations meet. The resulting ratings are interpretable and can be used for player evaluation, transfer analysis and match forecasting. The match data, the ratings and the code are publicly available at https://github.com/andreyshelopugin/SportsRatings

authors.name: Alexander Sirotkin
authors.institution: Constantine the Philosopher University in Nitra

papers.title: Latroids on Young's Lattice
papers.abstract: Latroids are a generalization of matroids and polymatroids, given by a submodular rank function on a modular lattice. We study integer-valued latroids whose length function is the height of a finite modular lattice, without assuming that the lattice is complemented. We show that their cyclic flats form a lattice and, together with their ranks, determine the rank function. We also characterize which families of lattice elements, together with prescribed rank values, occur as the cyclic flats of such latroids. We then focus on principal intervals of Young's lattice, where we classify the latroids with modular rank functions and characterize the sparse paving ones. Finally, we attach a latroid to every Ferrers diagram rank-metric code and show that its cyclic flats, together with their ranks, determine the dimensions of all shortenings to Young subdiagrams.

authors.name: Gianira N. Alfarano
authors.institution: Institut de recherche mathématique de Rennes

papers.title: In-orbit demonstration of object-based change detection applied to the maritime domain
papers.abstract: This article presents the successful in-orbit validation of an object-based change detection pipeline for low latency maritime monitoring onboard the CogniSAT-6 mission. We propose and validate a lightweight, three-phase operational sequence: optimized ground-based dual-acquisition scheduling, real-time onboard AI-based vessel segmentation, and multi-temporal matching. Upon acquiring consecutive images over a targeted Area of Interest (AoI), the onboard system correlates vessel detections using a hybrid matching approach that integrates the Hungarian algorithm for optimal assignment with RANSAC-driven spatial and size filters for outlier rejection. A series of in-orbit validations demonstrated robust performance across 11 diverse maritime scenarios, achieving valid recall and precision values (considering only vessel size and location) exceeding 0.8. The validation demonstrated the ability of the system to track both cooperative targets and uncooperative "dark" vessels strictly through geometric consistency. This capacity to autonomously generate and act upon real-time intelligence establishes a foundation for next-generation Insight-as-a-Service (IaaS) and tipping-and-cueing architectures.

authors.name: Nicolas Longepe
authors.institution: Istituto Nazionale di Fisica Nucleare, Galileo Galilei Institute for Theoretical Physics

authors.name: Gabriele Meoni
authors.institution: European Space Research and Technology Centre

papers.title: On the quasi-static growth of cavities in incompressible elastomers
papers.abstract: For a variational model of incompressible elastomers exhibiting cavitation, we establish the existence of irreversible quasi-static evolutions driven by time-dependent boundary conditions. Our result extends previous work by Mora-Corral (2014) to incompressible materials under weaker regularity assumptions on the boundary datum. The proof employs the multiplicative splitting introduced by Francfort and Mielke (2006) to reduce the problem to time-independent boundary conditions and then invokes abstract results on the existence of energetic solutions to rate-independent systems. Specifically, the construction of mutual recovery sequences requires particular attention to accommodate the incompressibility constraint: to this end we employ the method by Moser (1965) to exhibit incompressible diffeomorphisms interpolating between localized translations and the identity.

papers.title: Cross-channel amplification of frequency-distinct scattered waves in multibeam stimulated Brillouin scattering
papers.abstract: Multibeam stimulated Brillouin scattering (SBS) can be amplified when one side-scattered wave draws energy from several pumps, each through a separate ion-acoustic-wave (IAW) branch. This is not common-daughter-wave coupling: scattered waves from different parent pumps may occupy nearly the same wave-vector region yet remain distinct optical modes because their frequencies differ. We examine this process with local-growth and finite-width-gain models, three-dimensional coupled-mode calculations and two-dimensional particle-in-cell (PIC) simulations. Adding the extra branches increases temporal growth and spatial gain across the tested crossing angles. In three dimensions, direct branches alone give weak, localized side scatter; with the cross branches present, a strong field fills much of the interaction region even though the incident beams, direct channels and initial seed are unchanged. The distinction persists at fixed total power. The coupled response remains strong as the power per beam falls, whereas the direct-only response drops rapidly. PIC spectra contain nearby scattered-light features accompanied by several pump-specific IAW branches, and the fixed-power scans yield a strong, non-monotonic response. These results support cross-channel feedback through separate IAWs as a multibeam SBS amplification mechanism that may help predict and control SBS losses in laser-fusion plasmas.

authors.name: Y. Chen
authors.institution: Hunan Institute of Science and Technology

authors.name: H. Wen
authors.institution: First Affiliated Hospital of Xinjiang Medical University

papers.title: Satellite pairs in the Local Group: from spatial clustering to dynamical associations in observations and $\Lambda$CDM simulations
papers.abstract: We investigate the incidence and physical nature of satellite galaxy pairs in the Local Group using updated observational data for the Milky Way (MW) and Andromeda (M31), together with analogues from the HESTIA constrained cosmological simulations. Our comparison uses three distinct simulated Local Group analogues drawn from the HESTIA suite, allowing us to assess the observed pair statistics against multiple cosmological realisations of the Local Group environment. We identify close nearest-neighbour associations by comparing the observed satellite distributions with isotropic populations that reproduce the radial distributions of each host, and investigate their physical nature using line-of-sight velocities, proper motions, and gravitational binding estimates. We find that the MW exhibits a significant excess of close satellite associations relative to isotropic expectations, with a pairing efficiency of $\sim53\%$, nearly twice that found in the simulated analogues ($\sim17$-$27\%$). This excess persists after applying a stellar mass cut ($M_\star > 10^4\,\mathrm{M}_\odot$) to match the resolution limits of the simulations. In contrast, the M31 satellite system is broadly consistent with isotropy, with a pairing efficiency of $\sim28\%$. However, only a minority of pair candidates exhibit coherent kinematics or are likely to be gravitationally bound, indicating that most represent transient alignments or remnants of common group infall rather than long-lived binary satellites. These results suggest that the MW hosts an unusually rich population of phase-space-correlated satellites, likely reflecting its recent accretion history, whereas M31 is more consistent with typical $\Lambda$CDM expectations.

papers.title: Competing lattice instabilities in epitaxially strained BaSnO3
papers.abstract: We use density functional theory to map the lattice-dynamical landscape of BaSnO3 under biaxial compressive strain and uncover the hierarchy of structural instabilities. Our results demonstrate that the phase stability of strained BaSnO3 cannot be inferred from the softening of the polar mode alone. Instead it is governed by the competition among lattice instabilities and their anharmonic coupling to structural relaxation. Two-mode energy-surface analyses show that the polar and rotational order parameters interact predominantly competitively. While A- and M-point octahedral rotations become unstable before the zone-center polar mode and dominate the harmonic response for moderate values of strain, they are related to a continuous transition without anharmonic lattice coupling and a moderate gain of energy with strain. Large strain may induce a first order transition to a supertetragonal polar state. Once this state is stabilized, the magnitude of polarization and ferroelectric energy well depth are comparable to BaTiO3 under compressive strain. Furthermore, we discuss how an electric field or electron doping may tip the balance between the different modes and favor of the supertetragonal structure over antipolar and rotational alternatives at a reduced critical strain.

papers.title: Lost in Delegation: Studying the Effectiveness of Task Orchestration in Generative Search
papers.abstract: LLMs have quickly evolved from models used in isolation to agentic systems that delegate tasks to external tools and other LLMs to solve complex assignments. This agentic augmentation has led to impressive capability gains. However, when and how delegation improves performance remains poorly understood. For example, it is unclear whether delegation helps when tasks involve post-cutoff information that the orchestrating LLM cannot reliably resolve from its own knowledge. In this work, we use purpose-built datasets with pre- and post-cutoff splits to compare various delegation modes. We find that delegation provides no consistent accuracy improvement over non-delegated setups, with effects varying across models and tasks. When tasks involve knowledge unavailable to the orchestrator, delegation can substantially degrade accuracy, while direct tool use with the same LLM performs much better. Our analysis identifies distorted delegated queries, inefficient tool use, and failures to preserve and use information between agents as recurring failure modes. These findings suggest that effective orchestration requires both well-calibrated delegation decisions and effective exchange of information between agents.

papers.title: Robust Control Design for LTI Systems with Sampling-Time Jitter
papers.abstract: Sampling-time jitter makes a sampled-data control loop time-varying, so standard LTI robust-control synthesis does not apply directly. This paper reformulates dynamic output feedback design under bounded, unmeasured sample-to-sample jitter as a robust-control problem. The exact zero-order-hold model is decomposed into a nominal time-invariant plant and a memoryless, time-varying uncertainty block with a norm bound representing the sampling-time jitter. As the block is memoryless, the operator small-gain condition for the time varying loop reduces to a standard robustness test with a matrix norm bound. It is shown that the same test also guarantees uniform exponential stability for every admissible jitter sequence. Embedding the decomposition into a generalized plant with performance channels serves two synthesis objectives with standard robust-control tools: Robust stability with optimized nominal performance through structured H-inf synthesis, and robust performance through mu synthesis with constant scalings. A numerical example shows that jitter can destabilize a control loop with a nominal H-inf controller, whereas both robust designs remain stable and the robust-performance design is less sensitive to jitter at the cost of nominal performance.

papers.title: JOINTS: Classification and analytical evaluation of detachable dry connections for reusable concrete elements
papers.abstract: This paper presents a systematic classification for detachable dry joints suitable for the structural reuse of reinforced concrete elements, together with an analytical evaluation of representative configurations. The classification, named JOINTS and applicable to concrete connections beyond the reuse context, organizes the design space along five categories whose initials spell JOINT: the Juxtaposition (spatial arrangement of the paired elements), the Origin (their prior structural function), the Interface geometry, the Newly introduced materials at the joint, and the force-Transfer mechanism. A sixth category, the Score, completes the acronym and evaluates each configuration for sustainability, cost-efficiency, and mechanical performance. From this design space, three representative configurations are evaluated analytically under active post-tensioning, differing in both their joint geometry (planar, stepped, and angled) and their tendon inclination. The evaluation covers failure of the anchorage of the post-tensioning member, the contact limit of the interface, and the material limit of the concrete adjacent to the interface. Although complex joint geometries theoretically enhance interlocking, their benefit is limited by the compressive-shear strength of the concrete. The reinforcement of the reused elements may be damaged near the cut, and the splitting reinforcement that a conventional design would require is not guaranteed to exist. The present analysis therefore conservatively assumes that the concrete at the joint face alone resists the combined compression and shear, neglecting any residual contribution from the existing reinforcement. This analytical evaluation represents a first step toward quantifying the score over a parametric range of connections, here focusing on the mechanical criterion.

papers.title: Pre-QED: Environment Specifications for Agentic Verification
papers.abstract:
LLM agents are making formal verification practical at scale. Recently, many attempts have raised this as an enticing possibility. However, formal verification at scale is only meaningful if deep formal specifications capturing functionality are available for checking. Unfortunately, recent works seek to bypass this issue by using shallow specifications devised for purposes other than verification. OSS-Verify from Anthropic and Theorem, for example, reuses the fuzz harnesses of open-source libraries as specifications and has an agent prove that each harness never crashes. However, a fuzz harness follows a single sequence of API calls under a single calling context, so the resulting proof covers one usage scenario rather than the library.
  We argue that the bottleneck of agentic verification has shifted from how to prove to what to prove. Before zooming into verification at scale, we need deep environment specifications to prove, which is why we call our effort Pre-QED. We propose verification harnesses, executable harnesses that model all legal usages of an API, so that a proof about the harness is a proof about every well-behaved client. To construct them, we use an agentic workflow that extracts the API's usage contract from code / documentation, and uses Linear-time Temporal Logic (LTL) to rule out illegal call orders. We identify the challenges in proving verification harnesses and release our harnesses open-source as challenges for the community. The overarching vision is that verifying an open-source library should become as routine as fuzzing it, with a guarantee that covers every well-behaved client rather than a single scenario like a fuzzing harness.

papers.title: Data-center growth impacts household electricity costs more through wholesale prices than through grid reinforcement
papers.abstract: Rapid data-center expansion is raising concerns about electricity affordability, yet how the costs of serving these large new loads reach residential customers remains poorly understood. Here, we quantify the potential impact of 371 announced Texas data-center projects, totaling 38.9 GW by 2030, on residential electricity costs by linking power system expansion, wholesale electricity markets, transmission reinforcement, and retail cost allocation. We find that accommodating this demand increases modeled residential electricity costs in one representative case by 1.64 cents/kWh, with 68% arising from higher wholesale electricity prices and 32% from regulated transmission charges. Allowing new gas generation near data centers reduces the 2023 residential cost increase to 0.92 cents/kWh, whereas excluding data centers from the transmission cost-sharing base raises it to 1.87 cents/kWh. These findings reveal that the residential cost burden of data-center growth is driven primarily by wholesale electricity price increases, rather than direct transmission investment costs, and depends critically on generation siting, infrastructure planning, and cost allocation.

papers.title: A sharp bound for the $a$-number of a cyclic cover of $\mathbb{P}^1$
papers.abstract: Let $X$ be a smooth projective curve of genus $g$ over an algebraically closed field $k$ of characteristic $p>2$. We give upper bounds for the $a$-number $a(X)$ when $X$ is hyperelliptic or, more generally, a tame cyclic cover of the projective line. For hyperelliptic curves, writing $g=pm+r$ with $0\le r<p$ and $n=(p-1)/2$, we prove the sharp bound $a(X)\le nm+\min\{n,r\}$. For tame cyclic covers, we refine previously known upper bounds and give curves attaining the resulting bound in infinitely many genera in characteristics $3$ and $5$. The proofs combine an alternating pairing on the bundle of locally exact differentials, originally due to Raynaud, with an explicit polynomial description of the Cartier operator. We also produce an explicit locus of hyperelliptic curves $X$ with $a(X)\ge a_g$, where $\frac{a_g}{g}$ converges to $\frac{p-1}{2p}$ as $g$ goes to $\infty$, whose dimension grows linearly with the genus $g$. These families exhibit excess intersections of the Torelli locus with loci of large $a$-number in the moduli space of principally polarized abelian varieties.

papers.title: Structure-Preserving Learning for Nonlinear Nonholonomic Dynamics
papers.abstract: Learning the dynamics of mechanical systems subject to nonlinear nonholonomic constraints is challenging, as data-driven models may violate the underlying physical constraints, leading to inconsistent predictions. To address this problem, we develop a constraint-preserving learning framework based on the Lagrange-d'Alembert-Chetaev equations and tangency to the constraint submanifold, which together define an affine space of admissible accelerations. Using the kinetic-energy metric and the Moore-Penrose pseudoinverse, we construct a metric projector and the corresponding Chetaev correction. Embedding this geometric structure directly into a Gaussian process prior ensures that both prior and posterior dynamics satisfy the acceleration constraints exactly. We characterize the resulting reproducing kernel Hilbert space (RKHS), derive an adapted-coordinate representation, and establish nonexpansiveness and consistency transfer. Numerical experiments on a three-dimensional directional flocking system with up to 50 agents demonstrate exact constraint preservation and robustness to constraint-incompatible observations.

papers.title: Al-Ghasali: A Computational Framework for Simulating Islamic Jurisprudential Rulings via Finite State Automata and Large Language Models
papers.abstract: This paper presents Al Ghasali, a computational framework designed to formalize and simulate Islamic jurisprudential (Fiqh) rulings. Building upon recent set theoretic formalizations of al sabr wa al Taqsim that extract minimal operational rules as simple Horn clause logical programs, this work proves that the semantics of closed Fiqh chapters collapse completely to deterministic Finite State Automata (FSA). We establish a formal computational hierarchy, demonstrating that restricting formalization to finite propositional Horn theories guarantees decidability and constant time (O(1)) verdict extraction after offline compilation. The framework formally proves that hierarchical compositions of sub-chapter FSAs preserve this O(1) complexity, and that temporal juristic requirements, such as Tartib (order), are deterministically flattened into static ontological states, preserving the memoryless property of the automaton. To generate human-readable juristic summaries, Al Ghasali incorporates Large Language Models (LLMs) via an architecture where the deterministic FSA strictly controls the probabilistic LLM. Crucially, the paper formulates sufficient design safety conditions for this FSA LLM integration, ensuring strict adherence to the epistemological boundaries of Usul al Fiqh. To neutralize the risk of LLM hallucination, the system employs a Grammar Guided Constrained Decoding mechanism. We formally define the mapping function that dynamically constructs unambiguous right linear grammars from the FSA execution history. The paper mathematically proves that this architecture, augmented by a Bounded Neutral Lexicon and Valence Locking, guarantees the absolute absence of Decisional Hallucination, Juristic Factual Hallucination, and Semantic Inversion reducing the LLM to a pure linguistic transformer of deterministic juristic facts

papers.title: Low-Cost Mobile Bimanual Manipulation for Long-Horizon Toilet Cleaning
papers.abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models have shown promising capabilities for robot manipulation, but their performance on accessible mobile bimanual platforms remains underexplored. We present a low-cost and reproducible mobile bimanual platform integrating two LeRobot SO-101 manipulators with a TurtleBot 4 and a LeRobot-ROS 2 software stack. Using long-horizon toilet cleaning as a case study, we collect 250 real-world demonstrations and evaluate $\pi_0$, $\pi_{0.5}$, SmolVLA, and GR00T under the same embodiment and task conditions. We further evaluate variants using SARM-derived task-progress signals and short-term MEM observation history. Among the evaluated models, $\pi_0$ performs best, achieving 60% strict and 70% relaxed autonomous success, increasing to 90% with limited human intervention. In contrast, the evaluated progress- and memory-augmented variants do not improve their corresponding baselines. Our results demonstrate the feasibility of long-horizon mobile bimanual manipulation on accessible hardware while highlighting remaining challenges in reliable VLA deployment. Project website: https://so101-turtlebot4.github.io/mobile-bimanual-cleaning/

papers.title: Fast Subproblem Solving in Benders Decomposition for Affine Potential-Based Flow Problems with Topology Switching and Scenarios
papers.abstract: Potential-based flow problems arise for a range of practical problems, like the operation of lossless power networks. The distribution of flows through the network is governed by the potential equation, which relates arc flows and node potentials following arc potential functions. We consider a general variant with affine potential functions, topology switching, and scenarios. It can be solved using a Benders decomposition algorithm, with each scenario corresponding to a subproblem. Subproblem solving time can then significantly contribute to overall running time. We present a fast algorithm to obtain Benders optimality and feasibility cuts from fixed master solutions. Problems with affine potential functions are reduced to equivalent problems where every potential function is the identity function. Optimal primal and dual solutions as well as unbounded dual rays are determined by systems of linear equations (SLE), resulting in a constant number of SLEs solved per subproblem. SLEs are solved using LU-factorizations, with the similarity between primal and dual, scenarios, and master solutions exploited by reusing factorizations via low-rank updates to significantly reduce theoretical complexity. We demonstrate the method on security-constrained optimal transmission switching instances, where subproblem solve time reductions of 97.98 percent compared to a standard LP solver are observed.

papers.title: Efficient Knowledge Transfer in Federated Bayesian Optimization through Neural Network Surrogates
papers.abstract: Federated Bayesian Optimization (FedBO) has emerged as a powerful paradigm for enhancing Bayesian Optimization (BO) in distributed, privacy-sensitive settings, enabling agents to accelerate the optimization of their local objectives by sharing knowledge about their similarities without exposing raw data. However, existing methods rely on restrictive assumptions, such as near-identical objective functions or shared Gaussian process hyperparameters that are often violated in heterogeneous real-world applications. We present GLOBAFED, a novel framework that enables efficient knowledge transfer across different but related objectives without compromising privacy. At its core is a probabilistic neural network surrogate with a shared feature-extracting backbone and agent-specific heads equipped with varia- tional Bayesian last layers to provide uncertainty estimates. During optimization, agents use federated learning on the shared backbone to collaboratively build a common latent feature representation, while agent-specific heads adapt to their individual objectives. Our empirical results demonstrate that GLOBAFED significantly accelerates convergence and reaches better final performance compared to state-of-the-art FedBO baselines, and enables agents to warm-start their optimization from previously learned global features.

papers.title: Intense and stable second-harmonic generation in robust MePEA-based quasi-2D halide perovskite crystals
papers.abstract: Quasi-2D halide perovskites offer a unique platform for nonlinear optics applications, where structural and optical properties are tuned by the variation of organic spacer cations. Notably, quasi-2D perovskite single crystals can demonstrate intense and stable second-harmonic generation signals when a proper composition is selected. Here, the influence of phenethylammonium and 4-methyl-2-phenylethylammonium spacers on the crystal symmetry and second-harmonic signal response of quasi-2D perovskite phases with a varying number of single-octahedron [PbX$_6$]$^{4-}$ layers ($n$) is investigated. High-quality perovskite crystals with lateral dimensions of several hundred micrometers are fabricated using a cavity-confined crystallization synthesis method. Optical characterization of the crystals shows strong and temporally stable second-harmonic generation. Power-dependent and polarization-resolved measurements confirm the second-order nonlinear origin of the observed response and reveal anisotropic emission patterns. Our results demonstrate a direct correlation between spacer-induced center-symmetry breaking and nonlinear optical activity. These results establish quasi-2D halide perovskites as a promising class of symmetry-engineered materials for efficient frequency conversion and integrated nonlinear photonics.

papers.title: Adaptive Constraint Sampling for Stochastic Gradient Methods in Constrained Optimization
papers.abstract: This paper proposes an adaptive constraint-sampling technique for stochastic gradient-based methods to efficiently solve constrained optimization problems with a large number of inequality constraints. The proposed constraint-sampling technique maintains a set of recently violated constraints and draws the constraint used in each iteration uniformly either from this set or from the set of all constraints. This keeps its per-iteration arithmetic overhead independent of the number of constraints. In simulations on synthetic convex optimization problems and in the synthesis of a control barrier function for the Dubins Car, the constraint-sampling technique is shown to significantly outperform uniform constraint sampling.

papers.title: A Dual-Branch Graph and Convolutional Network for Interpretable Movement EEG Classification
papers.abstract: Decoding upper-limb movements from scalp electroencephalography (EEG) is an important problem for brain-computer interfaces (BCIs), but many deep learning models provide limited insight into the brain regions underlying their predictions. We propose a two-branch architecture that combines an LGGNet-inspired local-global graph branch with an EEGNet-style convolutional branch for movement-versus-rest classification. The graph branch groups 61 EEG electrodes into anatomically informed regions and learns their spatial relationships, providing a direct representation of the regions emphasized by the model. We evaluate the proposed architecture using leave-one-subject-out cross-validation on the Ofner upper-limb movement dataset. The model achieves a mean F1-score of 0.74 +/- 0.06 across subjects. Beyond classification performance, we analyze the learned graph structure to identify the regions with the strongest connectivity. Across all held-out subjects, the highest connectivity is consistently observed in the Parietal Left Low region, corresponding to electrodes P1 and P3. This region is opposite to the performed right-arm movements and lies within the posterior parietal area previously associated with upper-limb movement processing. These results show that incorporating a region-based graph into the decoder can provide an anatomically interpretable representation while maintaining effective movement classification, offering a practical approach toward more transparent EEG-based BCIs.

papers.title: Quantum unique ergodicity and the critical crossover for 1-d Gaussian band matrices
papers.abstract: We consider an $N\times N$ complex Gaussian random band matrix in one dimension with band width of order $W$, in the periodic block form of Yau and Yin. The $N$ sites are split into $n=N/W$ blocks of size $W$ on a ring, and the entries are nonzero only within a block and between adjacent blocks. The conjectured localization--delocalization transition occurs at $W\sim\sqrt N$. We prove quantum unique ergodicity for bulk eigenvectors at every deterministic rank whenever $W^2/N\to\infty$, with no power or logarithmic separation between $W^2$ and $N$. At the threshold $N/W^2\to\tau\in(0,\infty)$, we show that the rescaled bulk eigenvalues and the block-mass profiles of their eigenvectors (the probability measures on the circle placing at $k/n$ the squared norm of the eigenvector on block $k$) converge jointly to a unique law. This law is encoded by a random entire function whose zeros give the limiting eigenvalues, and its derivatives there give the limiting profile integrals. The law of this function is determined by the Dorokhov--Mello--Pereyra--Kumar (DMPK) diffusion of the unitary class. In the critical law, the profiles have strictly positive variance against every nonconstant smooth test function, so they are not concentrated on the uniform profile. As $\tau\to0$ this variance vanishes and the local spectrum tends to the sine process. As $\tau\to\infty$ it tends to a Poisson process where both limits taken after the critical one. The critical family thus interpolates between the delocalized and localized regimes, confirming for this model the prediction of Fyodorov and Mirlin that at $W^2\asymp N$ the joint law of eigenvalues and eigenvectors depends only on $N/W^2$. The full content of this work has been autoformalized in Lean4 by AxiomProver.

papers.title: Boundary-layer detachment and infinite-Reynolds limit of two-dimensional wall-bounded flows
papers.abstract: Understanding boundary-layer detachment and its consequences for the infinite-Reynolds-number limit remains a major challenge in fluid mechanics. Here, direct numerical simulations of incompressible flow in a two-dimensional periodic channel with no-slip walls are used to investigate this problem. Reynolds-number-dependent initial conditions are constructed with a boundary layer of Prandtl thickness that converge in the energy norm to an analytic, stationary Euler flow, while the associated Prandtl system develops a finite-time singularity. Highly resolved simulations show boundary-layer detachment and departures from Prandtl scaling, yet provide numerical evidence that the Navier--Stokes solutions continue to converge to the Euler flow over the simulated time interval. In particular, the squared energy norm of the velocity difference and the time-averaged energy dissipation both scale approximately as $Re^{-1/2}$, consistently with established convergence criteria. Although the detached vortices become more numerous and intense as the Reynolds number increases, their characteristic size and occupied area appear to decrease. These observations suggest how boundary-layer detachment and the breakdown of the Prandtl description can coexist with convergence to a smooth Euler flow.

papers.title: Going beyond the standard quasiparticle picture: Entanglement spreading after quenching from highly entangled states
papers.abstract: The quasiparticle picture provides a quantitative description of entanglement spreading after quantum quenches in integrable systems. In interacting models, however, it relies on the assumption that the quench creates entangled pairs of quasiparticles, which is justified only for the so-called integrable initial states. Here we go beyond this setting by studying quenches in the XXZ spin chain from the $n$-rainbow states, a family of macroscopically homogeneous states formed by increasingly long-range Bell pairs, which are not integrable for $n>1$. The local stationary state after the quench approaches the infinite-temperature state as $n\to\infty$, with corrections of order $1/n$, as we show analytically. Nevertheless, in the noninteracting XX chain the quench produces entangled multiplets of $2n$ species of quasiparticles. Although interspecies correlations vanish as $1/n$, they strongly suppress the growth of the entanglement entropy, whose rate vanishes as $n\to\infty$. We capture this behaviour within a generalized quasiparticle picture. In the interacting XXZ chain, instead, time-dependent density matrix renormalization group (tDMRG) simulations show that the entanglement entropy grows at the rate at which thermodynamic entropy is exchanged across the cut. Within the time scales accessible to tDMRG, the data show no trace of the multiplet suppression. This holds both after homogeneous quenches and after joining the $n$-rainbow state with an infinite-temperature state, for which we conjecture a formula for the von Neumann entropy.

papers.title: Geometric structure of Green currents for holomorphic correspondences on projective surfaces
papers.abstract: Let $f$ be a holomorphic correspondence on a complex projective surface $X$ such that $f^{-1}$ is also holomorphic. Assume that the action of $f^*$ on cohomology is simple and that the dynamical degrees of $f$ satisfy $d_1>\max\{d_0,d_2\}$. We prove that the Green currents $T^\pm$ associated with $f$ are woven. We also provide a large family of examples of holomorphic correspondences satisfying our assumptions, obtained as generic complete intersections in $X\times X$.

papers.title: A new indirect approach for oxygen abundance determinations across a wide range of physical conditions
papers.abstract: In this work we present a new approach to derive HII region metal abundances based on sulfur emission lines. We select M101 as benchmark galaxy to test our new methodology along the wide metallicity gradient of this huge face-on star-forming spiral. Based on previous studies, we compile a sample of 151 HII regions and compare their properties base on the galaxy radial profile. The new methodology is based on the derivation of the electron temperature of the double ionised sulfur, either by the direct measurement of the [SIII] auroral line or, at supersolar metalicities, from the $SO_{23}$ parameter. This new indirect method is able to extend the abundance gradient up to the very centre of the M101 galaxy (0.04 $R_e$). This new methodology mitigates systematic biases in direct abundance determinations based on auroral lines, while opening up new opportunities to improve commonly used strong line abundance calibrations in the intermediate to high metallicity regime.

papers.title: Autonomous Neural Adaptive Control as a Self-Consistent Transfer Operator
papers.abstract:
We study autonomous neural adaptive control, where the controller modifies the physical dynamics while the data generated by the physical dynamics itself drive subsequent parameter updates. We formulate the coupled evolution of the physical state distribution and controller parameters through a self-consistent transfer operator.
  Assuming that the physical dynamics under each fixed controller admits a unique invariant distribution, we characterize adaptive equilibria through a finite-dimensional self-consistency equation for the stationary mean learning update. We establish existence using Brouwer degree, without requiring global convexity, and reduce uniqueness to uniqueness of the corresponding zero.
  Under suitable differentiability and spectral-gap assumptions, we derive a finite-dimensional criterion for local exponential convergence of both the physical distribution and controller parameters at sufficiently small positive learning rates. The criterion involves the Jacobian of the reduced equation, computed using linear response to include the effect of controller-induced changes in the invariant distribution. The asymptotic slow relaxation time scales inversely with the learning rate.
  We rigorously verify the assumptions and apply the theory to a noisy Duffing-type system with a neural residual compensator, providing a nontrivial example of adaptive control with provable existence, uniqueness, and local stability of an adaptive equilibrium. Numerical experiments illustrate statistical feedback and the role of time-scale separation.

papers.title: Semi-log canonical minimal model program for projective morphisms between complex analytic spaces
papers.abstract:
We prove the existence of certain steps of the minimal model program for projective morphisms between complex analytic spaces in the semi-log canonical case, generalizing results of Ambro and Koll\'ar. This is obtained by providing a sufficient criterion for the finite generation of the relative log canonical algebra. As a consequence, we prove demi-normal analogues of results of Hacon--Xu and Birkar. As a further application, we derive the existence of crepant semi-dlt modifications of analytic slc pairs whose irreducible components are normal in codimension 1, extending a result of Hashizume.
  The methods are new even in the algebraic case, providing streamlined proofs of the algebraic counterparts to the statements proved in this work, without relying on Koll\'ar's gluing techniques.

papers.title: Universal Realization of Milnor Attractors in Low Dimensions
papers.abstract: We study the realization problem for Milnor attractors on compact metric spaces and establish a general sufficient criterion for universal realization. In particular, we prove that every smooth compact one-dimensional manifold, with or without boundary, and every smooth closed two-dimensional manifold has the property that each nonempty closed subset is the Milnor global attractor of a continuous self-map. If the manifold is connected, the realizing map may be chosen to be a homeomorphism. We also investigate the realization problem on selected one-dimensional continua and exhibit spaces for which universal realization fails.

papers.title: A Sublogarithmic Competitive Algorithm for Online Graph Exploration
papers.abstract: In online graph exploration, an agent must visit every vertex of an unknown weighted graph and return to its start, learning the incident edges at each vertex it visits. On $n$-vertex graphs, the best known competitive ratio has been $O(\log n)$, achieved by several algorithms, among them the hierarchical depth-first search of Megow, Mehlhorn, and Schweitzer. We give an algorithm with competitive ratio ${(2+o(1))}\ln n/\ln\ln n$ for known~$n$. Like hierarchical depth-first search, it groups the edges into geometric weight classes and searches depth-first between components of lighter edges. Unlike it, the agent tours each component along a minimum spanning tree for the original weights, so only crossings between components pay for rounding, and the base $b$ of the weight class can grow with~$n$. The leading constant $2$ is tight for our choice of base. Without knowing $n$, restarts with increasing size guesses give upper bounds with leading constant $4$ for a fixed schedule and $2$ in expectation for a randomly shifted schedule. If the weights lie in a known range $[1,2^k]$ with $k\ge4$, choosing $b=k/\log_2 k$ gives a competitive ratio of $O(k/\log k)$ without knowing $n$.

papers.title: Set-Theoretic PAPR Reduction in Multi-Antenna Systems
papers.abstract: In this study, we propose an optimization framework for PAPR reduction in multi-antenna systems with beamforming. Unlike previous techniques, the proposed approach permits full control over the distorted symbol constellation via arbitrary (convex) constraints on the frequency domain symbols, while minimizing the PAPR at each individual transmit antenna. We propose an iterative algorithm based on an extrapolated alternating projection method, which relies on an iterative soft-thresholding subroutine to compute projections onto sublevel sets of the objective function, and we compare its performance to optimal solutions obtained with general-purpose convex solvers.

papers.title: Open Quantum System Embedded in an Optimized Reservoir of Molecules
papers.abstract: Open-boundary Quantum Mechanics/Molecular Mechanics (QM/MM) simulation provides a direct way to test whether a quantum subsystem and its surrounding classical reservoir are physically consistent. Here we use this framework to replace a standard flexible TIP3P reservoir by a dipole-renormalized (DR) Amber-compatible three-site water model optimized against a full \textit{ab initio} trajectory of liquid water. The renormalization targets the molecular dipole distribution and adjusts the atomic charges, bonded, and Lennard-Jones interaction parameters through a stochastic optimization procedure. In the case of a large QM region ($\langle N\rangle\approx 440$), where the surface-to-volume ratio is small, the DR reservoir induces, as expected, Grand Canonical statistics for the quantum subsystem. In smaller subsystems ($\langle N\rangle\approx 190$), where the surface-to-volume condition is deliberately less favorable, the same reservoir shows substantially improved molecular consistency with the QM region relative to the non-renormalized flexible TIP3P model. These results show that quantum information at molecular dipole level is crucial for the microscopic physics of liquid water. When this concept is transferred into a classical reservoir, it can be used to extend the reliable regime of adaptive open-QM/MM water simulations even beyond the physically dictated Grand Canonical conditions. \end{abstract

papers.title: Thermal convection and jets produced by human exhalation dominate the indoor spreading of emitted CO$_2$ and aerosols
papers.abstract: For understanding airborne viral infection pathways, the prediction of the spreading and effective diffusivity of saliva droplets emitted from a person while speaking and breathing is crucial. In non-ventilated indoor spaces, the spreading of tracer particles or molecules emitted by a person is governed by the complex interplay of molecular diffusion, convection due to body heat and temperature boundary conditions as well as propulsion due to breathing in and out. By comparison of grid-based simulations of the compressible Navier-Stokes equation with experiments measuring the spreading of CO$_2$ emitted from a person, we demonstrate that molecular diffusion of CO$_2$ is present, but that the long-distance CO$_2$ spreading is completely dominated by the combination of convection due to body heat and temperature gradients at walls and windows and the periodic breathing pattern of a person. Breathing out induces long-range advection by a mid-Reynolds number flow pattern akin to the Landau-Squire jet, while breathing in creates only short-range flow. In conjunction with thermal convection, this symmetry breaking between breathing in and out produces fast long-distance transport of CO$_2$ and small aerosols.

papers.title: Strong Well-Posedness and Path-by-Path Uniqueness for Fractional SDEs with Integrable Drifts
papers.abstract: In dimension $d$, we consider stochastic differential equations driven by additive fractional Brownian motion with Hurst parameter $H<1/2$ and with a time-dependent drift that is $p$-integrable in space and $q$-integrable in time. Under the subcriticality condition $\frac{Hd}{p}+\frac1q<1-H$, complemented by two integrability conditions needed for Girsanov's theorem, we prove strong existence and path-by-path uniqueness of solutions. We also establish stability with respect to the initial data and the drift, both pathwise and in moment norms, and construct a H\"older continuous semiflow. When $H$ approaches $1/2$, our conditions reduce, up to an endpoint case, to the condition of Krylov and R\"ockner (2005) for Brownian motion, and in dimension one they complement the results of Nualart and Ouknine (2003), which rely on comparison arguments. Our methods combine the stochastic sewing lemma, Lyons' rough path theory, and the quantitative John--Nirenberg inequality for stochastic processes of vanishing mean oscillation.

authors.name: Toyomu Matsuda
authors.institution: Weierstrass Institute for Applied Analysis and Stochastics

papers.title: Access to the quasi-geostrophic model from within the BK19 compressible flow solver
papers.abstract: We extend BK19 the semi-implicit finite-volume solver, to provide access to the quasi-geostrophic (QG) regime within the same compressible framework that already admits soundproof and hydrostatic limits. In order to achieve this goal, we incorporate the asymptotic framework from the continuous theory into the numerical scheme. Adopting the usual asymptotic setting for the quasi-geostrophic regime and using it directly in the numerical model, we perform a scale analysis of the compressible Euler equations in the synoptic length and time scales in the limit of small Rossby number. In this limit, the discrete implicit step recovers geostrophic balance, together with the pseudo-incompressible divergence constraint. We construct a staggered-grid curl operator consistent with the discrete derivatives and use it to define the vorticity in the numerical framework. An asymptotic analysis of the fully discrete scheme then yields a Poisson-type equation for the leading-order Exner-pressure perturbation that coincides with the QG pressure Poisson equation in the continuous theory. As a result of this analysis, we introduce two additional blending switches that (i) convert the elliptic pressure problem from the full Helmholtz to its QG Poisson-type equation and (ii) control whether the horizontal momenta are updated prognostically or diagnosed from geostrophic balance. In combination with the existing soundproof and hydrostatic switches, the resulting algorithm can be operated in fully compressible, pseudo-incompressible, hydrostatic, and QG modes without changing the underlying discretization. The functionality of the numerical scheme in the QG regime is then tested by two idealized vortex test cases to show how stable the vortices remain in the QG run and that, as the Rossby number is reduced, the full compressible scheme converges to slow, balanced QG dynamics.

papers.title: Optimal control for an anisotropic Stokes-Nernst-Planck-Poisson system
papers.abstract: We study an optimal control problem aimed at enhancing mixing in anisotropic electrolytes described by an instationary Stokes-Nernst-Planck-Poisson system in three space dimensions, where the anisotropy is encoded by a given director field in the diffusion and permittivity matrices. The control is the external electric potential entering through the Robin boundary condition of the Poisson equation. The cost functional combines tracking-type terms for the charge concentrations and an $L^2$-regularization of the control with a negative vorticity term that favors rotational flow. Assuming that the diffusion and permittivity matrices coincide, we first prove existence and uniqueness of weak solutions with nonnegative, essentially bounded concentrations, together with Lipschitz continuous dependence on the control. Since, through the negative vorticity term, the cost functional is no longer weakly lower semicontinuous, existence of an optimal control relies on strong convergence of the velocity gradients. Finally, we prove Fr\'echet differentiability of the control-to-state operator, introduce the adjoint system, and derive first-order necessary optimality conditions in the form of a variational inequality.

papers.title: Systematic Evaluation of Training Data Generation Strategies for Machine Learning-Based Molecular and Materials Property Prediction
papers.abstract: Machine-learning (ML) models for molecular and materials property prediction are often trained on large datasets curated through arbitrary or generic sampling strategies. Such approaches can lead to the over- or under-representation of regions of chemical and materials space that are most relevant to the prediction task. An important challenge is therefore how to efficiently curate training data to maximize predictive performance while minimising the number of labelled examples required. Here, we systematically compare training data acquisition strategies for molecular and materials property prediction, ranging from random sampling to various active learning approaches. We evaluate their performance across different model classes, representations, datasets, and target properties. Our results show that the effectiveness of data acquisition strategies depend strongly on the interplay between the model, dataset, and prediction task, although uncertainty-based sampling generally outperforms alternative strategies. Based on these findings, we derive guidelines for selecting data acquisition strategies under a given labelling budget.

papers.title: A constructive computer-assisted existence proof for a Calabi--Yau metric
papers.abstract: We give a rigorous, constructive proof that there exists a Ricci-flat K\"ahler metric on the Fermat quartic hypersurface, independently of Yau's famous theorem, along with an explicit and accurate analytic approximation to the metric. The proof combines numerical techniques to obtain the approximately Ricci flat metric, a fixed point theorem to prove existence, and verified numerics to get the bounds used by the fixed point theorem. The method is general and we discuss the computational issues in applying it to other manifolds.

papers.title: Determinant Identities and Branch Selection in the Stationary Multi-Horizon Balance Problem
papers.abstract: We study the Hennig-Neugebauer family of stationary and axisymmetric vacuum multi-horizon candidates. The regularity conditions on the symmetry axis lead to quadratic determinant relations which leave an apparent ambiguity between two sign branches. Under explicit non-degeneracy assumptions, we prove that one of these branches is impossible. This branch selection yields a system of explicit determinant equations characterizing equilibrium within the family.

papers.title: A new proof of nonamenability for free Burnside groups of odd exponent
papers.abstract: We prove that the free Burnside group $B(m,n)$ is nonamenable for every $m\ge 2$ and every odd exponent $n\ge 557$. This improves Adian's bound $n\ge 665$ and matches the infiniteness bound of Atkarskaya, Rips and Tent. Our proof combines their canonical form construction with a counting argument to obtain an explicit isoperimetric inequality.

papers.title: Weak stability of Ricci flow with almost WPIC1 curvature
papers.abstract: We prove weak $L^\infty$ stability for complete, non-collapsed Ricci flows with almost WPIC1 curvature and scaling-invariant curvature bounds. Small $L^\infty$ perturbations of the initial metric admit Ricci-DeTurck flows which remain uniformly close to the background flow and depend Lipschitz continuously on the initial data. This extends an earlier stability theorem of the first and third authors with Lai.

papers.title: Asymptotic transportation cost of the optimal matching subject to different boundary conditions
papers.abstract:
We establish equality between several asymptotic limits of the transportation cost between stationary random measures, with respect to the Euclidean distance cost raised to the $p$-th power, with different boundary conditions.
  Our approach relies on a comparison with the optimizer of the mean transportation cost between the two random measures, which is defined on the whole space. In particular we do not use any PDE techniques related to the regularity theory for optimal transport maps.

papers.title: $C^*$-selflessness for free Burnside groups
papers.abstract: The free Burnside group $B(m,n)$ is obtained from the free group of rank $m$ by imposing the relations $w^n=1$ for all words $w$. We prove that $B(m,n)$ is completely $C^*$-selfless for every $m\geq2$ and every odd exponent $n\geq557$. Consequently, its reduced group $C^*$-algebra has stable rank one and strict comparison of positive elements by its canonical trace. This answers the question of whether $C^*$-selfless groups can satisfy a nontrivial group law. The proof establishes Ozawa's property $P_{PHP}$ by combining a combinatorial construction with a relative power-avoidance argument based on the canonical forms of Atkarskaya-Rips-Tent.

It expresses the possibility of adjoining a freely independent copy of an algebra inside a norm ultrapower while keeping the diagonal copy fixed. In the presence of a faithful tracial state, selflessness implies strict comparison and other structural properties. Nonabelian free groups provide basic examples in the setting of reduced group C∗C^{*}-algebras [17, 3]. Ozawa [15] developed dynamical and combinatorial criteria for the stronger property of complete selflessness.
