papers.title: Free G\"odel algebras over G\"odel hoops
papers.abstract: We give an explicit description of the left adjoint $F$ of the forgetful functor $U\colon\mathsf{GAlg}\to\mathsf{GHoops}$ from G\"odel algebras to G\"odel hoops. If $H$ is a G\"odel hoop with a least element $m$, then $F(H)$ is the direct product of the G\"odel algebra obtained by adjoining a new bottom element to $H$ and of $H$ itself, regarded as a G\"odel algebra with bottom element $m$. For an arbitrary G\"odel hoop $H$, we glue these products along the principal filters of $H$, and we describe the operations of $F(H)$, the action of $F$ on homomorphisms and the unit of the adjunction. As an application, we show that the unit of the adjunction $F\dashv U$ is not cartesian, and that the same holds for BL-algebras and basic hoops. Moreover, the semi-abelian categories of G\"odel hoops and of basic hoops are not equivalent to the slice categories of G\"odel algebras and of BL-algebras over their initial object. Thus, in contrast with the cases of Wajsberg hoops and of product hoops, the free-forgetful adjunctions between G\"odel algebras and G\"odel hoops, and between BL-algebras and basic hoops, do not give rise to ideally exact contexts.

papers.title: Rebrightening in the Radio: Secondary Flares from Tidal Disruption Events AT2019ehz and AT2019eve
papers.abstract: We present the discovery of new secondary delayed radio flares from two tidal disruption events (TDEs), AT2019ehz and AT2019eve from observations ranging 1-18 GHz using the Karl G. Jansky Very Large Array. For AT2019ehz, we find a secondary flare in radio emission began at 1545 days post-disruption, 770 days after the first radio flare detected at 775 days post-disruption, and for AT2019eve the secondary flare was detected at 1594 days post-disruption, 825 days after its initial radio detection at 769 days post-disruption. Through spectral modeling of the multi-frequency observations, we extract physical parameters of the new flares to constrain the origin of the rebrightening. We find the secondary flare of AT2019ehz is likely produced by a second outflow launched at roughly 1000 days. For AT2019eve, the secondary flare reveals unexpected spectral evolution with a self-absorbed peak increasing from 1325 to 2173 days post-disruption, which is not well explained with most models of expanding outflows and instead suggests a more complex physical geometry. This inconclusive origin of AT2019eve highlights the need for more complex models to explain observed TDE radio evolution.

authors.name: Adelle J. Goodwin
authors.institution: International Centre for Radio Astronomy Research

papers.title: Modelling the occurrence and reporting dynamics of weather-related home insurance claims
papers.abstract: We study the occurrence and reporting dynamics of weather-related claims in private home insurance, combining detailed portfolio and claim information with publicly available high-resolution weather data. Existing approaches typically start from an identified severe weather event, such as a hailstorm, and model the dynamics of the claims caused by that event. In practice, however, claims arise under moderate as well as severe conditions, and the claims handling process runs continuously. An insurer therefore requires insight into the occurrence and reporting of claims on every calendar day. Modelling all calendar days jointly poses two challenges: recently occurred claims are only partially reported, and days with severe weather are rare while accounting for a large share of the claims. We propose a multi-regime EM-XGBoost framework that addresses both: an expectation-maximisation setup accounts for the incurred-but-not-reported (IBNR) claims, while a data-driven regime structure lets the occurrence and reporting dynamics differ across weather conditions. In a case study on a Dutch home insurance portfolio, we compare single- and two-regime specifications for two spatial resolutions: the country as a whole, and its individual regions. We find that the regional two-regime model outperforms the regional single-regime model as well as both national models, indicating that the benefit of a multi-regime setting depends on a sufficiently granular spatial resolution. We also show that daily covariates constructed from hourly weather observations, capturing the duration and the intra-day timing of severe weather, improve both the occurrence and the reporting model.

papers.title: Fr\'echet structure over AF algebras I: The compact case
papers.abstract: This is the first of two papers devoted to spatial Fr\'echet structures on AF algebras and their derivations. Here, we study the simplest example of such a structure: the Fr\'echet algebra of almost-local compact operators associated with a fixed orthonormal basis. We revisit the characterization of its continuous derivations in terms of infinite matrices and their operator-theoretic implementation on rapidly decreasing vectors. Reformulating this description in the language of 0-chains, borrowed from the theory of quantum many-body systems, we establish a sufficient condition for continuity in terms of spatial growth. Finally, we construct a Fr\'echet-continuous symmetric derivation that does not generate a one-parameter group of automorphisms of this algebra that is strongly continuous with respect to its Fr\'echet topology.

authors.name: Julian Gomez
authors.institution: Consejo Nacional de Investigaciones Científicas y Técnicas

papers.title: Integrated optical isolators enabled by 2D semiconductors via spin-momentum locking
papers.abstract: Integrated optical isolators based on spin-momentum locking hold great potential for protecting photonic integrated circuits from unwanted reflections. Currently, the most common implementations are magneto-optical isolators that require an externally applied magnetic field. Nevertheless, a wide range of nonreciprocal effects remains to be exploited in alternative material platforms. Although the majority of these effects induce changes to the propagation of light as a function of its polarization, they can be directly connected to the propagation direction through spin-momentum locking. We employ a computational approach to investigate various designs of integrated isolators based on nonreciprocal 2D semiconductors, studying the influence of their geometry and optical properties on the device performance. Additionally, we propose a novel concept for an all-optical isolator based on spin-valley polarization and optically tunable magnetism in transition metal dichalcogenide monolayers. Our results establish 2D semiconductors as an advanced platform for integrated nonreciprocal devices, enabling functionalities that are difficult to achieve with conventional magneto-optical materials like all-optical operation.

papers.title: On Energy-Based Modelling for Fluidic Excitable Neurons
papers.abstract: Motivated by the potential of pneumatic excitable devices in soft robotics, this paper develops an energy-based, domain-agnostic equivalent of the Hodgkin-Huxley modelling framework using bond graph theory. The proposed model is used to guide the design of a pneumatic excitable neuron. The potential of this approach is illustrated through the design of a pneumatic half-center oscillator, an essential building block for rhythmic neuromorphic behaviours.

papers.title: Lense-Thirring induced repeating blast trains in continuous gravitational waves
papers.abstract: We characterise gravitational lensing induced by the Lense-Thirring effect in a continuous gravitational-wave source orbiting a spinning supermassive black hole. This scenario is very likely to generate lensing events, as long as the source's orbital inclination is not aligned with the black hole's spin axis and the Lense-Thirring timescale is shorter than the observational window. The signal appears as short-duration ($T_{\rm blast}$) gravitational-wave "blasts" that repeat after every orbit ($T_{\rm orb}$) within a limited time window ($T_{\rm train}$). The blasts' signal strength depends on the system's geometry and not on the black hole mass. The signal will go silent and renew twice in a full Lense-Thirring precession period.

papers.title: On the minimum energy required to trigger a spike
papers.abstract: We formulate and numerically study the problem of finding the minimum energy required to trigger a spike in a three-dimensional conductance-based excitable model. The variational formulation seeks a state trajectory that reaches the boundary of the spiking region with the least \textit{peak} cumulative work supplied through the membrane port. We approximate voltage histories by sums of real exponentials, reducing the problem to a finite-dimensional optimization. The best-found voltage waveform consists of a hyperpolarization phase followed by a depolarization phase, which seems to match the experimentally determined optimal stimulus in squid giant axons.

papers.title: FanCyqlone: A Parallelized Solver for Multi-Horizon Optimal Control
papers.abstract: Multi-horizon optimal control aims to select optimal control sequences simultaneously for several possible future scenarios, ensuring consistency at the first stage. While this enables advanced model predictive control schemes that explicitly handle prediction uncertainty, solving these problems tends to be costly. We introduce FanCyqlone, a linear solver that exploits parallelism across both time steps and scenario branches. The method builds on Cyqlone to compute the contribution of each branch and combines these results through a shared root problem. We integrate FanCyqlone into QPALM to develop FanCyQPALM, a solver for multi-horizon optimal control problems with general linear stage-wise constraints. We compare its performance with state-of-the-art solvers on spring-mass and quadruped control benchmarks.

papers.title: The Distant Milky Way Halo from the Southern Hemisphere: Spatially broad and closer stellar debris associated to the Magellanic Stream
papers.abstract: The Magellanic Stream (MS) is a gaseous structure extending over $150^\circ$ across the sky, likely formed through interactions between the Large and Small Magellanic Clouds (LMC and SMC) as they fell into the Milky Way (MW). Its predicted stellar counterpart would provide a collisionless record of these interactions, but few candidate members have been identified. To expand this sample, we constructed a catalog of 87,763 distant K-giant candidates using DELVE DR2 and VHS DR5 photometry and Gaia DR3 astrometry, and analyzed VLT and Magellan spectra of 51 targets along the trailing MS. Combining radial velocities, spectrophotometric distances, and proper motions, we identify five new MS candidates at 58--95 kpc. Their metallicities are consistent with the outskirts of the SMC, while orbit integrations in a time-dependent MW--LMC--SMC potential support a possible Magellanic origin. Combined with previously identified candidates, these stars span a substantially broader range of Magellanic latitude than predicted by existing models, suggesting an extended debris field rather than a narrow stream. The candidates also lie predominantly closer than the simulated debris. More recent, less eccentric SMC orbits may help explain this distance discrepancy, although new simulations are required to test their implications for the stellar debris, along with larger spectroscopic samples.

papers.title: Nonabelian Hodge theory in positive characteristic for rank-2 vector bundles over curves
papers.abstract: We describe the Nonabelian Hodge Theory correspondence in positive characteristic between nilpotent Higgs bundles and flat bundles with nilpotent p-curvature, as constructed in the seminal paper by Ogus-Vologodsky, in the special case of rank-2 vector bundles over a smooth projective curve. In this set-up we can rephrase this correspondence as a shift of the extension class of a rank-2 vector bundle by a cohomology class encoding a W_2-lift of the curve. As an application, we obtain that a general rank-2 vector bundle of degree 0 admits a connection with non-zero nilpotent p-curvature.

papers.title: Plurality Consensus for $h$-Majority via First-Repetition Rules
papers.abstract: In the h-Majority dynamics, each of n agents holds one of k opinions and, in every synchronous round, observes the opinions of h agents chosen independently and uniformly at random and adopts a most frequent one among them, breaking ties uniformly at random. Let M_0 be the initial number of agents holding the most frequent opinion, and Delta_0 its bias, its lead over the second most frequent opinion. We show that, for every sample size h >= 3, if Delta_0 >= L sqrt(M_0 log n) max{1, n/(h^2 M_0)} for a sufficiently large constant L, then h-Majority reaches consensus on the initially most frequent opinion within O((1 + n/(h^2 M_0)) log n) rounds with high probability. This is the time bound proved for the DejaVu dynamics with h samples (arXiv:2604.03648); our bias condition is that of DejaVu when h >= sqrt(n/M_0), and larger by a factor sqrt(n/(h^2 M_0)) otherwise. Our main contribution, the analysis of one round, rests on a comparison principle: among all rules that read the same observations and treat opinions symmetrically, plurality maximizes the difference between the probability of outputting the most frequent opinion and that of outputting any fixed competitor. We apply it to the rule that adopts the first opinion repeated among h-1 observations, and otherwise the h-th observation: its output law is the law of the new opinion of a random agent after one round of DejaVu with h-1 samples. Hence, in expectation, one round of h-Majority widens the gap between the most frequent opinion and each competitor at least as much as that round of DejaVu, whose analysis we use as a black box. Independently and concurrently, d'Amore, Rybicki, Shimizu, Shiraga and Vacus (arXiv:2610.40562) obtained, among other results, the same time bound under the weaker bias condition of DejaVu, with a different analysis of one round and a martingale analysis over many rounds.

authors.name: George Giakkoupis
authors.institution: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique

papers.title: Non-evolutionary effects on period change in Magellanic Cepheids. III. Empirical connection with additional low-amplitude variability
papers.abstract: The O-C method in classical Cepheids traces both evolutionary and shorter-timescale (non-evolutionary) period changes. In our previous works, we found irregular period changes in $\sim$33% of Magellanic classical Cepheids, but excluded Cepheids showing additional low-amplitude variability. Here, we establish whether first-overtone Cepheids hosting such variability differ in their period-change behaviour from the general first-overtone population. We analyse 544 Magellanic Cepheids with period ratios $P_{\rm x}/P_{\rm 1O} \sim 0.60-0.65$ or $P_{\rm 1O}/P_{\rm x} \sim 0.68$, using OGLE photometry, and classify and characterise their O-C diagrams following our previous studies. We find irregular period changes in 339 first-overtone Cepheids (195 in the LMC and 144 in the SMC), an incidence rate of $\sim$75.5%, a statistically significant increase over the $\sim$68.1% of our previous single-mode first-overtone sample. The combined first-overtone incidence becomes $\sim$69.7%. This provides the first empirical connection between additional low-amplitude variability and irregular period changes in first-overtone Cepheids. At a fixed pulsation period, the irregularity strength anticorrelates with the dominant pulsation amplitude but not with the additional-signal amplitude, suggesting that the additional periodicity marks a weakly saturated pulsation state rather than driving the irregularity. We further detect cycle-to-cycle (C2C) period variation in 37% of the class 3 sample, with jitter roughly seven times larger than in non-Blazhko RRc stars and a shallower scaling with pulsation period.

authors.name: Radosław Smolec
authors.institution: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique

papers.title: Magnetically Deformed Neutron Stars and Gravitational Waves
papers.abstract: We study the geometric figures of neutron stars and magnetars with spin periods from milliseconds to seconds and magnetic fields from $10^{12}$-$10^{15}$ G to hypothetical values near the Chandrasekhar-Fermi virial scale, $10^{18}$ G. In Newtonian theory, we find the equilibrium figure of a rotating incompressible fluid with a current-free uniform interior magnetic field matched to an exterior dipole field by surface currents. For aligned axes, an oblate spheroid is obtained by minimizing the total gravitational, rotational and magnetic energy at fixed mass, volume, angular momentum and frozen magnetic flux. Its ellipticity is the sum of rotational and magnetic contributions, recovers the Ferraro limit for a weak magnetic field, and has a magnetic weight that depends on the eccentricity for large deformation. For misaligned magnetic and spin axes, we introduce a quadrupolar shape tensor and diagonalize it to find a triaxial ellipsoid whose principal axes are tilted by magnetic pressure. The tilt angle and eccentricities are computed analytically as functions of the rotational and magnetic eccentricities and the misalignment angle. The magnetic energy of the misaligned configuration is obtained in closed form in oblate spheroidal harmonics for arbitrary eccentricity and obliquity. Its weak-field deformation, up to $10^{15}$ G, is proportional to $P_2(\cos\alpha)$, which fixes the magnetic forcing tensor, and its finite-eccentricity form gives a generalized Ferraro-Maclaurin relation for rotation-dominated misaligned stars. In the weak-field regime, the triaxial eccentricity is determined by the Ferraro eccentricity and the harmonic mean of order 2 of the rotational and magnetic eccentricities. The deformation parameters give the quadrupole moments and hence the continuous gravitational-wave amplitudes, luminosity and spin-down torque of the triaxial configuration.

papers.title: Winter wheat improves soil carbon sequestration with reduced gains in warmer climates
papers.abstract: Sustainable agricultural intensification requires a precise understanding of how land use decisions influence soil organic carbon (SOC) sequestration under varying environmental conditions. We apply causal machine learning to evaluate the heterogeneous impact of winter wheat-based rotations on SOC at the field-level across Lithuania. Using a nationwide dataset collected over five years (2018-2022), including crop types, management practices, soil properties, and environmental conditions, we estimate how the effects of winter wheat-based rotation vary across space and climate. Our results indicate that winter wheat generally enhances SOC levels, but its effectiveness is modulated by climate. Cooler regions experience higher SOC gains, whereas warmer regions show diminished or even negative effects. Future climate projections suggest that the potential for winter wheat carbon sequestration may decline under high-emission scenarios. These findings highlight the importance of localized agricultural strategies that account for climate variability to maximize SOC sequestration and ensure long-term soil sustainability.

papers.title: Beyond Curiosity: Habit and Organizational Learning Capability as Predictors of Shadow AI
papers.abstract: Generative AI has entered the workplace faster than organizations can govern it. A large share of employees now use AI tools their employer has not sanctioned, and many actively conceal that use, but the psychology of this covert technology behavior remains poorly understood. A common assumption, in popular accounts and early commentary, treats unauthorized (shadow) AI use as curiosity-driven exploration by adventurous individuals. We test this against a competing account grounded in the psychology of habitual technology use, in which automaticity rather than exploratory disposition sustains the behavior. Using survey data from 510 employed generative AI users across multiple countries, we adjudicated among individual and contextual predictors (workplace curiosity, habit, technology-acceptance beliefs, and organizational learning capability) with hierarchical regression, relative weights analysis with bootstrap confidence intervals, and full-subset dominance analysis. Habit was the strongest predictor, accounting for 28.3% of explained variance, and completely dominated joyous exploration, the curiosity dimension most aligned with the exploration account, across all 512 possible predictor subsets. Joyous exploration contributed 3.4% (95% CI [1.6, 7.4]) and fell to nonsignificance once use behavior and habit were modeled. Learning-supportive organizational conditions accounted for a further 24.1% and operated additively rather than by moderating dispositions. Parallel models decomposing the outcome showed the same dominance pattern for unauthorized use and concealment, and perceived social support for AI use was protective specifically against concealment. These findings reframe shadow AI as a habit-and-environment phenomenon rather than an individual-exploration phenomenon. The cross-sectional design means causal claims are exploratory.

papers.title: K2V: Generative Keyframing For Physically Plausible Video Generation
papers.abstract: Video diffusion models are able to generate samples with high-quality appearance and textural qualities. However, content produced by these methods is known to exhibit significant physical errors. This is because, in a classical video generation setting, all physical reasoning must take place simultaneously and exclusively within the diffusion process.We propose to resolve these issues by redistributing the task of physical reasoning onto a language model-backed keyframe generation module, which allows for explicit reasoning in language, and fine-grained control over the appearance of the video at important moments in the video. We then condition a video generation model with these keyframes, reducing the role of the diffusion model to the simpler task of interpolating between physically-correct intermediate states, rather than inferring an entire sequence with diffusion. Results demonstrate that our approach significantly outperforms existing approaches, achieving state-of-the-art performance on the Physics-IQ Verified benchmark and PhyGenBench.

papers.title: CAFIN: CUDA-accelerated Adaptive Fisher Information Matrix Network Optimization via GPU-Native Kernel Fusion
papers.abstract: Second-order optimizers improve deep neural network training using curvature information, but their practical efficiency is limited by GPU execution overhead. AdaFisher reduces Fisher Information Matrix (FIM) approximation costs through diagonal Kronecker structures and exponential moving averages, yet its PyTorch implementation requires sequential CUDA kernel launches, intermediate tensor allocations, and repeated memory accesses. We introduce CAFIN, a GPU-native CUDA kernel fusion framework that improves AdaFisher execution efficiency without changing its optimization formulation. The proposed approach progressively integrates FIM preconditioner construction, exponential moving average updates, gradient preconditioning, momentum accumulation, weight decay, and parameter updates into fused CUDA kernels. Shared-memory reuse, register-resident computation, and in-place operations further reduce memory traffic and intermediate allocations. Experiments using ResNet-18 on CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, and Tiny ImageNet across NVIDIA GTX 1660 Ti and RTX 3060 Laptop GPUs demonstrate up to 78.4% lower isolated FIM construction latency and 2.1-26.9% lower optimizer-step latency. The implementation also eliminates approximately 18.91 MB of intermediate GPU memory allocations per optimizer step. Numerical validation confirms consistency within the predefined FP32 tolerance, while convergence accuracy remains comparable across evaluated datasets and random seeds. These findings demonstrate that CUDA kernel fusion can substantially accelerate second-order optimization while preserving AdaFisher's underlying mathematical formulation and learning behavior.

papers.title: Large diameter for $(\Delta+2)$-colouring reconfiguration
papers.abstract: Given a graph $G$ and an integer $k$, the reconfiguration graph $\mathcal{R}_{k}(G)$ has the proper $k$-colourings of $G$ for vertices, two of which are adjacent if and only if they differ on precisely one vertex of $G$. In $2022$, Cambie, Cranston and the author proved that the diameter of $\mathcal{R}_{\Delta+2}(G)$ is at most $n+2\mu$, and put forth a collection of conjectures that in its strongest and most beautiful form would imply that the diameter of $\mathcal{R}_{\Delta+2}(G)$ is precisely equal to $n + \mu$, for every graph $G$ with $n$ vertices, matching number $\mu$ and maximum degree $\Delta$. Here we disprove most of those conjectures. Our constructions have reconfiguration diameter at least $n+\frac{3}{2}\mu-2$. We also provide counterexamples that are $\Delta$-regular, we show that every graph has reconfiguration diameter at least $n+\frac{1}{2} \mu$, and we advertise an extension to hypergraphs. It is now much more mysterious how the diameter behaves, so we propose a number of open problems.

papers.title: ZTF J2229+1928: A 23 Minute Eclipsing Double White Dwarf Binary
papers.abstract: We report the discovery of ZTF J2229+1928, a detached and eclipsing DA double white dwarf binary in a 23-minute orbit. The system was identified in a GPU-accelerated search of ZTF photometry and confirmed through follow-up observations with the high speed imager proto-Lightspeed on the 6.5-meter Magellan Clay telescope. Combining the proto-Lightspeed eclipse model with mass-radius relations gives component radii and masses of $R_1 = 0.0146^{+0.0009}_{-0.0008} \, R_\odot$, $R_2 = 0.0186^{+0.0010}_{-0.0008} \, R_\odot$, and $M_1 = 0.49^{+0.08}_{-0.07} \, M_\odot$, $M_2 = 0.37^{+0.06}_{-0.05} \, M_\odot$. Fitting the Keck/LRIS spectra gives component temperatures of approximately $11,100$ K and $8,200$ K, and scaling this model to the broadband spectral energy distribution gives a distance of $\sim965$ pc. Its short orbital period places it firmly in the millihertz gravitational-wave regime, and we estimate an expected signal-to-noise ratio $\mathrm{SNR} \approx 5.3$ with the upcoming LISA mission over its nominal four-year duration. ZTF J2229+1928 thus adds to the small but growing sample of eclipsing ultracompact binaries that will serve as important sources for future space-based gravitational-wave observatories.

authors.name: Jack Dinsmore

papers.title: The Unseen Threat: How Complementary Combinations of Acoustic Features Compromise Speech Privacy
papers.abstract: The interaction of acoustic features in leaking private information remains underexplored. This work focuses on time-domain features, i.e., broadband RMS level and pitch, alone and combined with temporally smoothed and subsampled Mel spectrograms. Privacy is assessed using informed automatic speech recognition and speaker-verification attacks, while utility for conversational analysis is evaluated using voice activity detection and speaker diarisation. RMS level and pitch alone exposed limited information, but fusion with 500 ms-smoothed Mel spectrograms enhanced utility while substantially increasing speech-content leakage. Specifically, the combination with RMS level showed that fine-grained temporal dynamics can amplify leakage from coarsely sampled spectral features. Speaker-identity protection remained limited for all tested features. Overall, these findings indicate that privacy assessments performed on individual acoustic features may underestimate leakage after feature fusion.

papers.title: Diffusion phenomena for evolution equations
papers.abstract:
We study the diffusion phenomenon for the abstract damped wave equation $u''+Bu'+Au=0$ on a Banach space and its possibly degenerate parabolic counterpart $Bv'+Av=0$. We assume that $B$ is bounded and the wave equation is well-posed, without requiring symmetry, injectivity, or commutativity of $A$ and $B$. Our aim is to identify initial data for which the parabolic solution is a genuine diffusive profile: $\|u(t)-v(t)\|=o(\|v(t)\|)$ as $t\to\infty$.
  Using Fourier analysis of resolvent expressions for the associated quadratic and linear operator pencils, we establish decay estimates for the difference of hyperbolic and parabolic solutions and their time derivatives. In particular, we characterize broad classes of initial data yielding the classical upper bounds of orders $t^{-1}$ and $t^{-2}$. We also prove lower bounds for both solutions, of the form $\|u(t)\|,\|v(t)\|\gtrsim r(t)$, for large sets of initial data and arbitrary prescribed functions $r(t)\to0$ that decay sufficiently slowly. Combining these results with high- and low-frequency resolvent estimates and a condition on the ranges of $A$ and $B$, we obtain genuine diffusive profiles. The analysis uses spectral properties of a sectorially holomorphic parabolic solution semigroup, which need not be strongly continuous.
  We apply the theory to damped wave equations on $L^2(\Omega)$ with the Dirichlet Laplacian and bounded nonnegative damping that may vanish on large sets. We establish criteria for the required resolvent and range conditions, treat the whole space and exterior domains, and construct diffusive initial data using Weyl sequences.

papers.title: On piecewise-regular and quasirational functions
papers.abstract: We fully characterize piecewise-regular functions on nonsingular real algebraic varieties in terms of continuous quasirational functions. We also obtain extension theorem for piecewise-regular functions defined on closed semialgebraic subsets of $\mathbb{R}^n.$

papers.title: Learning Rate Transfer and Feature Learning Across Depth for Constrained Spectral Optimizers: Complete Scion
papers.abstract: Hyperparameter transfer across model depth is instrumental in training deep models, as it enables learning rates calibrated on shallow networks to be effectively applied to deeper architectures. The recent CompleteP framework establishes a $1/L$ residual scaling rule that demonstrates this for Adam-family optimizers. We study whether similar transfer extends to constrained optimization methods, specifically Frank-Wolfe and projected non-Euclidean normalized steepest descent, where updates are determined by linear minimization oracles. We derive scaling rules for these methods which confirm that the $1/L$ residual scaling applies, although the arguments differ from the Adam-family optimizers. Our analysis supports depth-wise transfer and width-wise transfer of the learning rate for the Scion algorithm while ensuring feature learning and avoiding the kernel-regime. In experiments on NLP transformers (nanoGPT on FineWeb), vision transformers (DeiT on ImageNet), and vision MLPs (MLP-Mixer on CIFAR-10), we observe learning rate transfer across depth and feature learning for appropriately chosen residual scaling.

papers.title: Beyond the Diff - VulSpot: A Vulnerability Dataset Where No Vulnerability Goes Unlocalized
papers.abstract: A vulnerability detector is only as trustworthy as the benchmark that scores it, and today's real-world datasets tend to flatter detectors. They are often built once and never refreshed, so they quickly miss new vulnerabilities, their labels are either noisy or heavily filtered, and their random splits let models train on near-copies of test code and on future vulnerabilities. Above all, when a fix only adds code, such as a missing NULL check, they do not point at where the vulnerability was, preventing detectors from learning to localize some of the most common C/C++ weaknesses. We present VulSpot, a living benchmark for detecting, classifying, and localizing vulnerabilities, with over 500k functions in 21 languages from 24k registered CVEs, including over 15k vulnerable C/C++ functions. By linking the code added by a patch to the existing statement it protects, VulSpot locates the vulnerability in 99.3\% of the functions that previous diff-based datasets used to leave without a location. Rather than discarding uncertain labels, it tells users how reliable each one is, and it comes with leak-free splits, complementary code context, and hierarchical CWE labels. An automated pipeline refreshes VulSpot every month, so that each release brings vulnerabilities no model has seen yet.

papers.title: StructRL: Model-Free Reinforcement Learning with Replay Graphs
papers.abstract: StructRL turns the experience collected during reinforcement learning into an explicit replay graph. Once the graph contains a path to the task goal, dynamic programming selects actions on the observed part of the state space; these actions form a graph policy that is defined only where the required transitions have been observed. StructRL transfers these actions to model-free learners: as action preferences for a DQN Q-model and as target directions along shortest observed paths for a SAC actor. For DQN on three sparse-reward MiniGrid tasks, final success rises from 0.10 to 0.90 (DoorKey), 0.10 to 0.80 (KeyCorridor) and 0 to 0.50 (ObstructedMaze); plain DQN does not catch up with three times the budget. For SAC on continuous PointMaze, graph-derived direction labels raise final success from 0.17 to 1.0 on seven matched runs that reached the goal. Distilling the graph policy into a fresh Q-model gives a DoorKey 6x6 controller that reaches the goal from 91% of reachable states, against 38% for plain DQN. Scaling experiments identify three bottlenecks: incomplete graph support, structural aliasing, and loss of graph information in high-dimensional inputs.

papers.title: BiPOP: Partial-Order Planning for Long-Horizon Bimanual Robotic Manipulation
papers.abstract: Bimanual robotic manipulation is versatile, yet its central challenge lies not only in executing dexterous motion with each hand, but also in coordinating the two arms for long-horizon manipulation under coupled spatial and temporal constraints. Prior work has largely focused on endowing robots with human-level manipulation skills, paying less attention to the structure of bimanual behaviour itself: many practical tasks are a coordinated composition of reusable unimanual skills and a small set of synchronous bimanual skills. This makes high-level spatio-temporal coordination, rather than skill acquisition alone, a key bottleneck for efficient bimanual execution. We propose BiPOP, a framework that couples Large Language Models (LLMs) with Temporal Partial-Order Planning for long-horizon bimanual manipulation. At its core is an explicit spatio-temporal model that partitions the workspace by arm reachability and captures inter-arm dependencies, arm assignment, synchronization requirements, and opportunities for safe concurrent execution. Building on this model, an LLM translates natural-language instructions into a formal PDDL specification, while a temporal planner enforces the constraints and schedules actions, yielding plans that are logically consistent at the symbolic level and efficient through parallel execution. On simulated long-horizon tasks of varying complexity, BiPOP outperforms open-loop planning with strong reasoning models and closed-loop ReAct-style planning in success rate, planning time, and plan efficiency, and the full pipeline runs end to end on the real bimanual robot NICOL. A failure analysis further shows that LLM-only planners mainly violate spatial and temporal coordination constraints, which motivates delegating these constraints to a symbolic planner. Code: https://github.com/Kchu/BiPOP

papers.title: Reading the Table: Sim-to-Real Game State Detection for the Chef's Hat Card Game
papers.abstract: Tabletop games offer a compelling scenario to study the interaction between artificial and human agents, combining social interaction with game state tracking and physical manipulation. To assess the game state, a robot needs to precisely detect closely related game objects, such as different card designs, requiring dedicated training data that is costly to annotate in the real world. Instead, we develop a fully automated synthetic data collection pipeline, using re-projection of known 3D coordinates to generate labels automatically and domain randomization to bridge the reality gap. This approach is used to collect a dataset of 25413 samples to finetune an object detection and a segmentation model, which are combined to assign detected cards to game-relevant zones and infer the game state. When evaluated on a real NICO humanoid robot, our pipeline achieves an F1-score of 0.906 for card-to-zone assignment, thus providing the perceptual foundation for a robot that can autonomously play Chef's Hat against human players.

papers.title: Stable irrationality of quartic hypersurfaces
papers.abstract: We prove that a very general quartic hypersurface of any positive dimension over an uncountable algebraically closed field of characteristic different from 2 does not admit an integral decomposition of the diagonal, and in particular it is not stably rational.

papers.title: NIBench: benchmarking autonomous AI agents for execution, skill evolution and scientific judgment in neuroimaging
papers.abstract: Autonomous AI agents are increasingly used to automate biomedical research, creating a growing need to benchmark their capabilities on real scientific data and workflows. Their reliability in neuroimaging remains insufficiently characterized, where plausible analytical outputs can conceal errors that affect scientific conclusions. Existing studies have advanced scientific question answering and tool-based automation, but provide limited evidence on workflow reconstruction, acquisition of procedural expertise and evidence-based scientific judgment. Here we present NIBench, a neuroimaging benchmark comprising three complementary evaluations of autonomous agents. First, we benchmark execution and workflow reconstruction using 56 tasks across seven tool ecosystems, covering structural, diffusion and functional magnetic resonance imaging, positron emission tomography and multimodal analyses. Second, we examine whether agents can evolve their procedural skills through distillation of execution trajectories, evaluating the resulting skills on previously encountered tasks, unseen tasks and other models. Third, we assess scientific judgment using 36 claims from published Alzheimer's disease studies, requiring agents to analyse raw cohort data and provide reproducible evidence. We evaluate 19 language models within a shared agent framework, with selected models undergoing skill distillation and claim evaluation. Leading agents execute supplied analysis protocols nearly perfectly, whereas withholding procedural guidance widens performance differences. Distilled skills improve performance on acquisition tasks and transfer between models, but benefits on unseen tasks are inconsistent. Agents reproduce their reported results yet sometimes reach conclusions inconsistent with expert-derived answers, and access to data does not always improve judgment.

papers.title: Measuring Preferred Representation in AI-generated Images with Community Scorers
papers.abstract: AI-generated images often misrepresent historically marginalised communities, with real-world consequences beyond the images themselves. However, conventional metrics fail to measure how communities want to be represented in AI-generated images. To address this, we introduce the concept of preferred representation. Building on previous work, we propose a measurement instrument that operationalises this concept through a Community Scorer - a model that evaluates a specific community's preferred representation in AI-generated images. We interrogate the validity of Community Scorers on three diverse disability communities that span the Global North and South. The results show that Community Scorers align significantly better with community ratings compared to other widely used text-to-image metrics. We then demonstrate the usefulness of these scorers in a downstream content filtering task. We release the Community Preference Dataset to enable others to optimise how Community Scorers can be scaled for culturally specific evaluation of AI-generated visual media.

papers.title: A Serious Game for Training Civil Participation in Flood Crisis Management
papers.abstract: Floods are among the most frequent and destructive natural disasters, requiring citizens to make critical decisions under rapidly changing conditions. Most serious games related to flooding emphasize awareness, preparedness, and education in flood management, but there is still a research gap on how to train citizens to act under pressure, uncertainty, and stress. In this paper, we position Virtual Reality (VR) serious games as a promising approach to addressing this gap by providing experiential and immersive training opportunities for citizens. We propose a conceptual VR serious game that enables participants to experience realistic flood scenarios, practice decision-making, rehearse appropriate response behaviors, and develop response-related skills in a safe and controlled environment. In addition, we suggest a research agenda and an evaluation framework focused on flood risk awareness, response capabilities, and stress-related outcomes. The framework thoughtfully integrates subjective, objective, and physiological measures to assess the effectiveness of immersive flood-response training. Finally, we present design, methodological, ethical, and user-experience considerations in VR-based disaster training, and outline future research directions for the development and evaluation of immersive serious games for flood emergency response. The present study aims to contribute to the growing intersection of serious games, extended reality, and disaster risk reduction by establishing citizen-centered response training as a significant yet under-researched field.

authors.name: David Maruscsak

papers.title: Language Learning through Immersive Multi-User Gamification
papers.abstract: We propose an immersive virtual-reality game designed to enable multi-user, multi-language learning during co-play. We hypothesize that our method will be more engaging, leading to better rhythm, pronunciation, memorization, and speaking confidence. We implement the experience as a fantasy role-playing game by introducing vocabulary and phrases to the user as spells to learn. Players then cast more efficient spells depending on their language skills. For evaluation, we compare the game to a single-user baseline that replicates traditional language learning in a non-immersive setting. We measure short- and long-term retention of vocabulary and phrases, as well as scoring rhythm and pronunciation. Furthermore, we collect user data on engagement and mental workload.

papers.title: PhysLoop: Harnessing LLMs' Physics Awareness for Self-Improving Video Generation Models
papers.abstract: Video generation models produce visually realistic videos but still struggle with physical dynamics and causal consistency. Learning from generated videos requires fine-grained physical supervision, yet reliable quality judgments, correction pairs, and controlled variations are difficult to obtain. Large language models (LLMs) possess physical knowledge, but struggle to reliably guide video generation models in producing their training videos. We present PhysLoop, a unified harness designed to support physically grounded self-improvement in video generation models. The harness guides and constrains LLMs throughout video generation, selection, and correction, distilling their physical knowledge into physically consistent videos. The framework supports controllable training-data construction and inference-time video repair. By identifying and correcting failures, PhysLoop marks a key milestone toward recursive self-improvement (RSI) in video generation models with limited human intervention. We release 100K videos spanning diverse, realistic indoor and outdoor scenes, along with generation tools and two evaluation datasets: PhysLoop-Gen and PhysLoop-Repair. We evaluate controllable generation and localized repair on these datasets, respectively, and assess physical behavior on the external Physics-IQ Verified benchmark.

papers.title: Braided module categories from small braidings
papers.abstract: We introduce small braidings on inclusions of monoidal categories $\mathcal{C}\hookrightarrow\mathcal{D}$, which allow one to braid objects in $\mathcal{C}$ with objects in $\mathcal{D}$. A small braiding makes $\mathcal{C}$ a braided monoidal category, and turns $\mathcal{D}$, as well as certain subcategories of $\mathcal{D}$, into braided module categories over $\mathcal{C}$. We prove versions of previously known reconstruction results for braided module categories which do not rely on finiteness assumptions. We construct a number of new examples coming from quantum groups, as well as the associated quantum moment maps.

papers.title: Upscale energy transfer from mesoscale convective systems to African easterly waves
papers.abstract: African easterly waves (AEWs) drive the synoptic variability of West African monsoon rainfall via intricate two-way interactions with mesoscale convective systems (MCSs). The composite MCS-AEW system is a canonical example of multiscale interactions in the tropical atmosphere, with upscale feedbacks from deep convection driving the evolution of a larger-scale circulation. Here we support this perspective through application of techniques from turbulence theory, calculating for the first time patterns of interscale kinetic energy transfer, $\mathcal{D}_L$, across different spatial scales $L$ around MCSs and AEW lifecycle phases. We study AEW and MCS dynamics in two pan-tropical 40 day Met Office Unified Model simulations with $\sim$5km grid spacings, for which $\mathcal{D}_L$ is calculated with the LoSSETT software package. We find explicitly-simulated MCSs show a distinctive vertical dipole structure of $\mathcal{D}_L$ at scales below 1000km, with strong upscale energy transfer located in the upper troposphere within storm anvils. Regionally, upscale energy transfer occurs most strongly where organised convection is active. We find 200hPa upscale transfer consistently leads AEW troughs, and that growing continental AEWs in the explicit simulation are characterised by strengthened upscale transfer of energy from MCS to AEW scales. Case-study analysis shows this transfer can contribute to the eddy kinetic energy growth of strengthening AEW troughs. These signals are weak in a simulation with parameterised convection: here, zonal mean energetics show enhanced barotropic conversion, caused by a stronger African Easterly Jet, provides a stronger AEW population. Our analysis of upscale energy transfers complements previous analysis of AEW potential vorticity dynamics, providing a route towards building new theoretical understanding of tropical dynamics from km-scale models.

papers.title: Rule-Sensitive Sensor Participation in Distributed Detection with Prescribed Boolean Fusion Rules
papers.abstract: We study distributed binary detection when the fusion node must implement a prescribed Boolean decision rule. Under conditionally independent Bernoulli observations, we derive a signed-influence path identity valid for arbitrary Boolean rules; for monotone rules, it reduces to an exact Russo--Margulis representation in terms of coordinate influences. The identity yields rule-sensitive necessary conditions for a target Bayes error and an influence-weighted Kullback--Leibler feasibility bound. We then connect Boolean relevance to exact rule implementation and derive lower bounds on the number of sensors that must participate, including a heterogeneous bound based on the ordered per-sensor hypothesis separations. Numerical and Monte Carlo results illustrate both the tightening provided by the heterogeneous participation bound and the performance penalty that can arise when a prescribed fusion rule is retained instead of optimal likelihood-ratio fusion.

papers.title: Mechanical behaviour of the intact brain-skull interface under tension, compression and shear
papers.abstract: The brain-skull interface governs the boundary/contact conditions of the brain in computational head models, yet its mechanical behaviour remains poorly characterised experimentally. We characterised the brain-skull interface by testing brain-skull complex samples (skull bone, meninges and brain tissue in their native arrangement) excised from 19 sheep cadaver heads under uniaxial tension and compression at strain rates of 0.002, 0.02 and 0.2 s$^{-1}$ and simple shear at 0.02 s$^{-1}$. Histology confirmed that the meningeal layers remained intact and attached to the brain and skull after excision. We acquired magnetic resonance images of every sample, reconstructed their geometry and developed a sample-specific finite element model of each experiment. We represented the brain tissue using a second-order Ogden hyperelastic model and the brain-skull interface using a cohesive zone model. Using inverse finite element analysis, we first calibrated the brain tissue parameters for each subject. Keeping these parameters fixed, we then identified the interface parameters from the corresponding brain-skull complex specimen. The brain tissue shear modulus increased with strain rate from 0.94 $\pm$ 0.16 kPa at 0.002 s$^{-1}$ to 1.60 $\pm$ 0.30 kPa at 0.2 s$^{-1}$. In contrast, the interface properties (maximum normal traction 2.35 $\pm$ 0.81 kPa, maximum tangential traction 4.14 $\pm$ 0.97 kPa, and fracture energy 0.35 $\pm$ 0.14 N m$^{-1}$) showed no significant dependence on strain rate or loading mode. In all samples, failure occurred within the subarachnoid space. Neither a rigid brain-skull connection nor frictionless sliding contact with separation reproduced the measured mechanical response or failure mode of the brain-skull interface. Our experimentally derived cohesive zone model provides a realistic representation of the brain-skull interface for computational head models.

papers.title: Computing extensions of flag-jump t-modules
papers.abstract:
We study Anderson t-modules whose positive-degree coefficient matrices admit a flag-jump basis and extend the t-reduction algorithm to this setting. We prove that these t-modules are abelian, with motive rank equal to the sum of their jump degrees. If $\Phi$ has jump degrees $j_1,\ldots,j_d$ and $deg_\tau\Psi<\min_s j_s$, we compute the t-module structure on ${\mathbf{Ext}}^1_\tau(\Phi,\Psi)$, its subgroup ${\mathbf{Ext}}_{0,\tau}(\Phi,\Psi)$, and the associated exact sequence.
  The construction allows nonzero nilpotent constant terms and includes the strictly pure case. When $\Psi$ is the Carlitz module, $N_\Phi=0$, and all jump degrees are at least two, the construction yields a dual t-module. We give complexity bounds for the algorithms and implementations in SymPy and Mathematica.

papers.title: Pl@ntNet machine-to-machine identification service with Pl@ntNet API: enabling automated biodiversity monitoring through large-scale plant identification
papers.abstract: 1. Monitoring plant biodiversity requires identifying large numbers of plants across space and time. Although artificial intelligence (AI) can now identify plant species from images with high accuracy, most existing systems rely on users manually submitting images. As ecological monitoring increasingly generates large image collections from cameras, drones, robots and online platforms, there is a growing need for plant identification services that can be directly integrated into automated data-processing workflows. 2. Here, we present Pl@ntNet's machine-to-machine AI plant identification service. This service uses an application programming interface (API) to provide programmatic access to Pl@ntNet's plant recognition models and the associated taxonomic processing. This service enables the implementation of automated identification workflows without human intervention and can thus directly link large image collections and automated observation systems to an AI-based plant identification system. 3. We establish that this service, which covers 85,000 species from around the world, (1) has a species prediction accuracy of 0.89, (2) process images up to 666 times faster than workflows requiring human intervention, (3) and has processed over 84 million identification requests since its launch, including more than 40 million in 2025 alone. We demonstrate how it has already enabled the implementation of a new generation of ecological workflows: identifying plants from images of insects to reconstruct the plant-pollinator interactions, analysing geolocated images from social media to study plant distribution, detecting invasive plants using images taken at the roadside, and identifying weeds using agricultural robots. Finally, we illustrate its application using a reproducible example: identifying plants from insect photos on iNaturalist. In approximately 30 min on a standard laptop, 2,424 images were processed to generate a dataset of 708 plant-pollinator interactions, with a weighted precision of 0.98 for flower detection and an accuracy of 0.88 for genus plant identification. 4. In conclusion, this machine-to-machine species identification is already operating on a considerable scale and meets a genuine need. All of this paves the way for a new paradigm in biodiversity monitoring, in which automated sensors and image collections can be directly connected to AI-based identification services.

papers.title: Beyond Curvature Bias: Higher-Order Manifold Fitting via Multiscale Cancellation
papers.abstract:
Local manifold-fitting procedures smooth noisy observations
  over neighborhoods of scale $h$, inducing a systematic normal bias of order $h^2+\sigma^2$ that persists at the population level. We develop geometric bias cancellation (GBC), a multiscale framework for higher-order manifold recovery under ambient Gaussian noise. For procedures admitting a normal-bias expansion $c(h,\sigma)b(x)+O(h^4)$, we construct cross-scale correspondence using estimated normal fibers and show that second-order normal accuracy suffices for fourth-order correspondence accuracy. Canceling the leading geometric bias yields $O(h^4)$ population Hausdorff accuracy while preserving an embedded manifold diffeomorphic to the underlying manifold. We establish the required expansions and finite-sample recovery guarantees for successive tangent-space projection and Gaussian density ridges. For STSP, geometric bias cancellation also achieves an asymptotically vanishing Hausdorff error ratio relative to oracle bandwidth-tuned single-scale fitting. For the local contraction estimator of \citet{yao2023manifold}, we identify an obstruction to scalar bias cancellation and develop a directional cancellation achieving $O(\sigma^4)$ population Hausdorff accuracy with uniform positive reach, as well as fourth-order finite-sample accuracy when $n\gtrsim\sigma^{-(d+6)}\log(1/\sigma)$. Simulations confirm the predicted improvement from second- to fourth-order population bias.

papers.title: The Sprague--Grundy Function of Slow Exact $k$-Nim with $k+1$ Piles
papers.abstract: We give an explicit formula for the normal-play Sprague--Grundy (SG) function of slow exact $k$-Nim with $k+1$ piles. A move removes one stone from each of exactly $k$ nonempty piles. A truncation preserves every legal move sequence. The SG value depends only on the total of the truncated coordinates modulo $2k$, their number of odd entries, and the parities of the two smallest piles. For every $k\geq2$, the set of the SG values is $\{0,1,2,3\}$. We prove the formula by the mex characterization, including the reductions needed after boundary moves. We also prove a unit-shift identity and use it with a known optimal-move theorem to explain the four-value bound independently of the explicit formula.

papers.title: Crystal Nucleation Driven by Microjets from Hydrodynamically Interacting Thermocavitation Bubbles
papers.abstract: Primary nucleation predominantly dictates the physicochemical, optical and mechanical properties of crystals emerging from solution. Here, we reveal a previously unrecognized nucleation mechanism arising from bubble-bubble hydrodynamic interactions using laser-induced thermocavitation bubble pairs. Under confinement, antiphase generation of two bubbles produces a micron-scale, high-speed liquid jet. Upon impact with the surrounding supersaturated liquid, this microjet generates intense localized shear, thereby inducing crystallization of the model inorganic salt, potassium permanganate. Under identical laser energies and supersaturation levels, crystallization was not observed in single-bubble experiments, in which no microjet was present. We show that the crystallization probability increases with microjet velocity. Boundary integral simulations reveal how experimental parameters such as confinement, bubble spacing, and laser energy govern microjet formation and velocity. We quantify the relationship between jet velocity and the observed enhancement in crystal nucleation kinetics by incorporating shear into the kinetic prefactor in classical nucleation theory. By combining experiments, theory, and simulations, we establish how microjets emerging from bubble-bubble hydrodynamic interactions may influence crystallization kinetics, opening new opportunities for the manufacture of crystalline materials.

papers.title: Towards Green Text Generation: Memory-Based Speculative Decoding
papers.abstract: Speculative decoding accelerates text generation with large language models by letting a cheap draft model propose tokens that a large verifier checks in a single forward pass. We introduce Olifant, a draft model built on a memory-based classifier. It predicts the next token from a four-token window in under 0.3 ms on CPU, requiring no GPU, no backpropagation, and no accelerator memory. We measure throughput and energy under two verifier regimes on consumer hardware. Without a KV cache, drafting is nearly free: a domain-matched Olifant model reaches 38.1% acceptance on EU legal text, delivering 2.43x throughput and 2.51x lower energy per token than the neural verifier model alone. With a KV-cached verifier, itself a ~10x energy saver, drafting costs matter: a TinyLlama draft model halves throughput and triples energy despite high acceptance, whereas Olifant still yields 1.25x throughput and the lowest energy in the study (93 J per 100 tokens, 14x below the uncached baseline). We further show that KV caching decouples time from energy: verification of longer drafts raises power draw, shifting the energy-optimal draft length below the speed-optimal one. Speculative decoding is not dead in the age of fast verifiers, provided drafting is nearly free.

papers.title: Localization of gravitational-wave source behind galaxy clusters by gravitational-wave lensing
papers.abstract: Gravitational-wave observations have opened new opportunities to study massive object events like merging binary black holes. When combined with electromagnetic counterparts, accurate localization of gravitational-wave sources could allow us to identify their host galaxies and carry out follow-up studies, such as study the environment of merging black holes and determine the Hubble constant. One of the possible methods for precise localization is strong gravitational-wave lensing. Previous studies have considered strong gravitational-wave lensing with galaxy lenses. However, galaxy clusters have yet to be investigated due to the complexity of their mass structures. Here we take the list of known cluster lenses from the Hubble Frontier Fields, simulate lensing properties of gravitational waves from their reconstructions as they would be observed by the ground-based gravitational-wave detectors. When same model family is used in simulation and localization, we find that the correct lens is identified for around 90\% of the simulated events. We also show that the source positions within the cluster can be pinpointed at sub-arcsecond precision with an estimate on source redshift. When we marginalize over all possible lens models for the clusters, the lens identification and localizations remain valid as long as the correct lens model is contained in the available cluster lens models. However, most localization attempts fail at initialization if the correct cluster model is excluded. These tests establish a proof of concept of localization under idealized conditions, while more work is needed to understand the cluster lens modeling discrepancies and reconstruction bias to validate the approach further.

papers.title: Compactness-uniqueness method for null controllability
papers.abstract: We develop the compactness--uniqueness method for the null controllability of abstract linear control systems on Banach spaces. Our first main result characterizes the null controllable states for systems that are null controllable up to finite dimensional spaces, and shows that null controllability is then equivalent to the Fattorini--Hautus test. Our second main result gives a dual counterpart of this assumption, an observability inequality with a suitable compact remainder. These results unify and extend several known results, such as those on heat equations with nonlocal terms and on the simultaneous controllability of systems. Finally, for a transport equation with nonlocal terms from population dynamics, we characterize the null controllable states after a sharp time, including in the non-reflexive space $L^1$.

papers.title: Lempert and pluricomplex Green functions near non-semipositive boundary points
papers.abstract: We study the two-step Lempert function and the pluricomplex Green function near a non-semipositive boundary point of a bounded domain $D\subset\mathbb{C}^n$. We prove a sharp upper estimate for the two-step Lempert function in terms of the local boundary scale $H_D$, and obtain matching estimates for the pluricomplex Green function. As a consequence, these quantities have the same boundary behaviour as the Kobayashi distance. For the usual Lempert function, we prove an upper estimate of order $\sqrt{H_D}$, which implies the optimal local $1/4$-H\"older estimate, and determine its precise boundary behaviour along the real normal.

papers.title: A projective Calabi--Yau threefold in characteristic 5 non-liftable to characteristic 0
papers.abstract: We construct a smooth projective Calabi--Yau threefold $X_5$ over $\mathbb F_5$ with $b_3(X_5)=0$ and $b_2(X_5)=31$. Consequently, $X_5$ has no smooth proper lifting to characteristic zero, including over ramified bases. To our knowledge, this is the first smooth projective Calabi--Yau threefold with this property in characteristic $p>3$. The threefold is a crepant resolution of the Kummer quotient of the self-fiber product of a rational elliptic surface. We prove the vanishing of its third Betti number by semistable reduction and point counts. A birational double-octic model gives a direct obstruction to lifting to the ring of Witt vectors of length two, through an explicit inconsistent system of linear equations for the branch data. We also determine the Hodge and crystalline cohomology: the threefold is infinitesimally rigid, its crystalline cohomology is torsion-free, and its third de Rham cohomology vanishes. Its Hodge-de Rham spectral sequence has exactly two nonzero differentials, both of rank one on the second page.

papers.title: Almost sure behaviour of empirical measures for intermittent maps whose return time distribution is 1-regularly varying
papers.abstract: In this article we study sets of limit points $\mathcal{L}$ for the sequence of empirical measures of intermittent maps with several equally sticky neutral fixed points. Such intermittent maps come with a parameter $\alpha > 0$ which determines the "stickiness" of the neutral fixed points. When $\alpha \neq 1$, it is known that two different behaviours can occur: either $\mathcal{L}$ is almost surely the singleton $\{\mu\}$ where $\mu$ is an absolutely continuous invariant probability measure; or $\mathcal{L}$ is almost surely given by the entire simplex $\pi\mathcal{S}$ of invariant measures supported at the neutral fixed points. We study the case that $\alpha = 1$ and show that neither of these two behaviours occur and that $\mathcal{L}$ is almost surely equal to a star-shaped subset of the simplex $\pi \mathcal{S}$. Moreover, we show that when slowly varying functions are introduced one can obtain a large range of different behaviours, including both the possible outcomes when $\alpha \neq 1$. Our results apply to a large class of intermittent interval maps as well as parabolic rational maps of the Riemann sphere.

authors.name: Douglas Coates
authors.institution: Universidade Federal do Rio de Janeiro

papers.title: Kac lemma on noncommutative probability spaces
papers.abstract: We prove non-commutative Kac's formula for actions of countable groups. We replace the return time functions by suitable projections in von Neumann algebras. Moreover, we prove a generalised Kac's formula in the non-commutative setting which extends the allocation construction of Meyerovitch and Weiss and is motivated by the random Kac inequality of Aaronson.

papers.title: Connected regular $\Gamma$-distance magic graphs with magic constant zero
papers.abstract: Let $(\Gamma,+)$ be a finite Abelian group. A $\Gamma$-distance magic labeling of a graph is a bijection from its vertex set to $\Gamma$ such that the sum of the labels of the neighbours of each vertex is a fixed element of $\Gamma$, called the magic constant. The constructions of Kov\'a\v{r} and collaborators provide regular distance magic graphs of odd order with consecutive integer labels for every even degree from $4$ to $14$. We adapt these constructions to prove the existence of connected $r$-regular $(A\times\mathbb{Z}_n)$-distance magic graphs with magic constant $0$, where $A$ is any finite Abelian group of odd order, $n$ is odd, and $r\in\{4,6,8,10,12,14\}$, under explicit sufficient conditions on $n$. Here $\mathbb{Z}_n$ is the cyclic group of order $n$. It suffices to take $n\ge13$ for $r=6$, $n\ge19$ for $r=14$, and $n\ge15$ for $r\in\{4,8,10,12\}$.

papers.title: Your Hypergradient is Skewed: Antithetic Neumann Estimation for Bilevel Optimization
papers.abstract: Bilevel optimization is a core tool in practical machine learning workflows, including hyperparameter tuning, data reweighting, robust learning, reinforcement learning, and imbalanced classification. Hypergradient computation requires the inverse of the inner Hessian, typically estimated via a truncated Neumann series. While existing analyses focus on bias and variance, we show that the product structure of the Neumann series introduces a third source of error: skewness. We identify that, unlike ordinary gradients, whose asymmetry is suppressed by mini-batch averaging, the Neumann estimator amplifies skewness across factors, with the third-moment error growing, under weak contraction, with truncation depth, inner condition number, and per-factor noise asymmetry. This arises in many practical settings such as corrupted labels, outliers, heterogeneous or class-imbalanced datasets. To address this, we introduce the Antithetic Neumann Estimator (ANE), which pairs each Hessian sample with a mirrored counterpart around a reference Hessian and averages the resulting inverse-Hessian estimates. With an exact reference, the antithetic product retains only even-order noise, eliminating all odd-order perturbation terms; with an approximate reference, the residual odd-order contribution is bounded linearly in the reference error. ANE requires only a modification of the Hessian vector step and combines with existing stochastic or variance-reduced bilevel methods. We instantiate ANE-SGD and ANE-VR, the latter adding recursive variance reduction. Across robust regression, data cleaning, offline reinforcement learning, and imbalanced classification, ANE-based methods improve on stochastic and variance-reduced baselines on every task (20 seeds each), lowering loss by 4 to 25% relative to the best baseline; the largest gains, on robust regression, are a 25% lower test loss and a 54% higher test r-squared.

authors.name: Pawel Polak
authors.institution: Pontifical University of John Paul II in Kraków

papers.title: Machine Learning for Scalable Multi-AP Coordination in IEEE 802.11bn Networks
papers.abstract: As Wi-Fi deployments become denser, fully distributed random channel access no longer guarantees the required quality of service. The multi-access point coordination (MAPC) framework introduced in IEEE~802.11bn lets neighboring access points (APs) cooperate, but choosing which APs transmit together and how to configure them remains an open, computationally hard problem. We develop and validate a stack of machine learning (ML) coordination methods, progressing from lightweight hierarchical multi-armed bandits (H-MABs) to a generative pipeline built on graph neural networks (GNNs) and flow matching (FM). The methods are evaluated in simulation and on a hardware testbed, improving throughput over legacy access and scaling coordination to dozens of APs where analytical and search-based methods become intractable.

papers.title: Polynomial Swap Coboundary Expansion with Applications to LTCs and PCPs
papers.abstract:
Swap coboundary expansion, introduced independently by Bafna--Minzer and Dikstein--Dinur, is a local-to-global property that underlies agreement tests in the low-acceptance regime and recent constructions of succinct PCPs. Previous works obtained bounds of $\exp(-O(\sqrt{r}))$ for the $r$-swap coboundary expansion of Chapman--Lubotzky complexes. We establish the first inverse-polynomial bounds for bounded-degree complexes: suitable skeleta of Kac--Moody--Steinberg (KMS) complexes have $r$-swap coboundary expansion at least $r^{-O(1)}$.
  Our theorem supplies a key ingredient in forthcoming work of Ben Yaacov--Dikstein--Liu, which obtains local tests for sparse algebraic codes with guarantees even at arbitrarily small acceptance probability. These tests use $\exp(\operatorname{poly}(1/\varepsilon))$ queries and guarantee that any word accepted with probability at least $\varepsilon$ agrees with a codeword on an $\varepsilon^{O(1)}$ fraction of coordinates. Separately, substituting our bound into the existing analysis of Bafna--Minzer--Vyas--Yun improves the soundness dependence of their two-query PCP construction, giving perfect completeness, soundness $\varepsilon$, and proof length $n(\log n)^{\exp(\operatorname{poly}(1/\varepsilon))}$.
  Our proof exploits the product structure of the groups arising in KMS complexes. The main new ingredient is a decomposition lemma for Dehn functions, which separates the analysis of group relations into independent problems on much smaller factors, with only polynomial overhead.

authors.name: Inga Valentiner-Branth
authors.institution: HOGENT University of Applied Sciences and Arts

papers.title: Foliations, free cores, and Terao's conjecture for seventeen lines
papers.abstract: We prove that freeness is determined by the intersection lattice for arrangements of seventeen lines in the complex projective plane. The proof reduces a possible counterexample to smaller arrangements whose realisation spaces can be computed. A minimal logarithmic derivation defines a foliation; its inflection divisor and a local singularity count imply that the non-free member of a counterexample is nearly free with exponents $(7,10)$. Deleting four lines then produces a thirteen-line arrangement whose second Chern class is controlled by a combinatorial deficit. When the deficit is four, the remaining arrangement is free with exponents $(6,6)$. An exact covering argument places the necessary thirteen-line cores in four finite classes, containing $3{,}829{,}691$ lattices. We compute their realisation spaces and reconstruct all relevant seventeen-line extensions, including specialisations of positive-dimensional families. Among the candidate lattices, exactly sixteen admit a non-free realisation; they are rigid and have no free realisation. Together with the known cases, this establishes Terao's conjecture for central arrangements of at most seventeen planes in $\mathbb{C}^3$.

papers.title: Sharp Covering-Number Bounds for Feedforward ReLU Networks via Parameter Symmetries
papers.abstract: In neural networks, distinct parameter configurations often realize the same input--output mapping, indicating that nominal parameter counts can overstate functional complexity. In this paper, we characterize the parameter-space symmetries of ReLU and Leaky ReLU networks across fully connected, convolutional, and residual architectures. We prove that every quasianalytic parameter map preserving the network function is a composition of positive channel scaling and channel permutation. By quotienting out both symmetries, we derive uniform covering-number upper bounds in which positive scaling reduces the complexity exponent from the total parameter count $S$ to $S-H$ (with $H$ denoting the number of scalable channels) and permutation symmetry divides the bound by the factorial count $G$ of channel permutations. We establish matching lower bounds showing that the exponent $S-H$ is sharp in general and that the divisor $G$ is attained for one-hidden-layer and generically identifiable networks. We further extend these results to general continuous piecewise-linear activated networks. Finally, we apply our covering-number bounds to derive statistical risk guarantees for empirical risk minimization and capacity control beyond i.i.d.\ settings, and show how the underlying symmetries help explain weight rebalancing in function approximation and flat directions in empirical risk optimization.

papers.title: HKT-Einstein metrics on circle bundles
papers.abstract: We consider a construction of hyper-Hermitian structures on total spaces of circle bundles over 3-quasi-Sasakian manifolds. We study the HKT-Einstein equation in this setting, proving that a large family of non-homogeneous hyper-complex manifolds admit compatible HKT-Einstein metrics with positive Einstein factor. We also show that the hyper-Hermitian structures on such circle bundles are quaternionic balanced or quaternionic Gauduchon if and only if they are HKT. Finally, the HKT-Einstein condition is investigated under the twist construction.

papers.title: APG-Planner: Learning Vision-Based High-Speed Trajectory Planning via Analytic Policy Gradient
papers.abstract: Vision-based high-speed navigation requires a trajectory planner that can reactively generate smooth, collision-free trajectories from onboard visual observations. Deep reinforcement learning offers a promising approach to vision-based trajectory planning, as it enables the optimization of sequential decision-making policies in complex environments. However, model-free policy gradient methods rely on sample-based policy gradient estimation, which yields noisy gradient estimates and inefficient training. To this end, we propose a framework for learning trajectory planning policies using the analytic policy gradient (APG) method and use it to train APG-Planner, a vision-based high-speed trajectory planner. The proposed framework leverages differential flatness to analytically reconstruct vehicle states from planned trajectories, thereby enabling differentiable trajectory-level state transitions without requiring an explicit low-level dynamics model. By iteratively performing trajectory planning and differentiable state transitions, we construct a differentiable episode rollout and analytically compute policy gradients from episode-level losses, improving both training efficiency and policy performance. After approximately 30 minutes of training on a single GPU, APG-Planner demonstrates comparable or superior performance to existing baseline methods in simulation and achieves speeds of up to 11\,m/s in real-world flight experiments. We further validate the proposed framework on a skid-steer ground robot, demonstrating its applicability to differentially flat robotic systems beyond quadrotors.

authors.name: Jinwoo Lee
authors.institution: Seoul National University of Science and Technology
