authors.institution: Ulsan National Institute of Science and Technology

authors.name: Hyondong Oh
authors.institution: Korea Advanced Institute of Science and Technology

papers.title: On the Difficulty of Sequence-Level Supervised Learning for Autoregressive Language Models
papers.abstract: During the supervised learning phase, autoregressive language models are typically trained by minimizing the negative log-likelihood of the training data, which decomposes as a sum of token-level cross-entropies via teacher forcing. This objective is simple and efficient but potentially suffers from so-called exposure bias: a mismatch between the way the model is trained and the way it is used at inference time. Can we instead design sequence-level loss functions that incorporate inference-time decoding procedures, such as greedy decoding or autoregressive sampling? We show that two natural attempts lead to loss functions that are fundamentally flawed: unbounded below. We further show that these two flawed loss functions are intimately connected: using autoregressive Gumbel tricks, the sampling based loss is the expected greedy loss under Gumbel perturbations. Since the pathology stems from the dependence of the decoded sequence on the model parameters, we analyze the update direction obtained by applying a stop gradient on the sampling procedure, leading to a moment matching direction. While it is not the gradient of any loss function, we prove that it defines a valid descent direction in function space for the autoregressive negative log-likelihood. Despite these theoretical insights, the moment matching direction suffers from high variance. We conclude that teacher forcing may well be ``all you need'' for supervised learning of autoregressive models.

papers.title: Spectrum of non-Hermitian self-normalized random matrices with heavy tails
papers.abstract: We study non-Hermitian matrices $Y_n$ obtained by normalizing each row of an $n\times n$ matrix with i.i.d. entries to Euclidean norm one. We consider regularly varying radial tails of index $\alpha\in[0,2]$, with $\alpha=0$ denoting slowly varying tails, and the broader normal domain of attraction. For $0<\alpha<2$, assuming angular tail convergence, we prove convergence in probability of the empirical singular value measures of every shift $Y_n-zI$ to deterministic laws characterized by the root resolvent of a column-normalized directed Poisson weighted infinite tree, extending the framework of Bordenave, Caputo and Chafai (arXiv:1006.1713). Under a bounded density assumption, the empirical eigenvalue distribution converges in probability to a deterministic law $\mu_\alpha^{\mathrm{SN}}$ on $\mathbb{C}$. This law is rotationally invariant, is supported in the closed unit disk with outer radius one, and has neither point atoms nor mass on the unit circle. The laws interpolate between $\delta_0$ as $\alpha\downarrow0$ and the circular law as $\alpha\uparrow2$. These also describe the limiting eigenvalue distributions of $Y_n$ for real entries with slowly varying tails and for centered entries with bounded density in the normal domain of attraction, respectively. For real symmetric entries with bounded density, the spectral radius converges to one in probability for $0<\alpha\le2$, using the upper bound of Francois, Heiny and Hu (arXiv:2608.28169). We also give a general criterion identifying the outer support radius of rotationally invariant laws from fractional moments of fresh cavity weights, under explicit trace and radial-recovery assumptions.

papers.title: FLEX-LBP: Learning Local Binary Patterns with Exact Binary Inference for Texture Classification
papers.abstract: Local Binary Patterns (LBP) remain among the most widely used texture descriptors, from industrial inspection to medical imaging. Yet their radius, sampling angles, color transform and thresholds are fixed by hand for each dataset. We present FLEX-LBP, which learns these parameters by backpropagation while every forward pass computes exact binary codes and hard histogram counts. A straight-through estimator acts only in the backward pass, so the deployed descriptor is an interpretable hard-binary LBP with 90 learnable parameters and unchanged inference cost. In a controlled ablation on six color texture benchmarks, the component worth learning is dataset-dependent. One configuration, applied unchanged everywhere, learns the geometry and thresholds with the color transform frozen. It improves the nearest-neighbor accuracy of the identical fixed descriptor by 3.55 points on average over five seeds, significantly on five of six benchmarks and never significantly worse. With a linear discriminant readout, it gains 0.9 points; the fully learned descriptor gains 2.7 and has the highest mean. FLEX-LBP is more accurate than five classical LBP-family descriptors, PCANet and a neural LBP on five of six benchmarks. Its mean nearest-neighbor accuracy exceeds that of frozen ImageNet ResNet-50 features (23.5 million parameters). On the Kather colorectal cancer histology benchmark, the fully learned descriptor reaches 93.8%, significantly above the best classical descriptor (Completed LBP, 92.8%). The learned radii adapt in directions that recur across seeds. Noise drowns single-pixel comparisons and illuminant change flips inter-channel ones; median sampling or gray-world normalization restores 96-97%. The code is available as a drop-in PyTorch layer at https://github.com/medalimoussa/FLEX-LBP.

authors.name: Amal El Kaid
authors.institution: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique

papers.title: Is Jev a Good Multilingual Judge?
papers.abstract: Generative large language models are widely used for multilingual text evaluation, yet whether decision models that directly output judgment probabilities can serve as multilingual judges has received limited attention. We evaluate Jev against generative LLM judges on four multilingual benchmarks with human annotations, covering up to 47 language varieties and three evaluation formats: binary decisions, pairwise comparisons, and graded ratings. At approximately $1/31$ to $1/61$ of GPT-6.1's evaluation cost, Jev is competitive on most multilingual judging tasks, but falls behind GPT-6.1 on knowledge-intensive answer verification. Further analysis shows that Jev is more likely to accept incorrect answers in low-resource languages than in English and that its probability outputs help identify errors across tasks. Based on these findings, we offer recommendations on evaluation instructions, confidence-based selection, and model routing, providing empirical guidance for using Jev as a multilingual judge.

authors.name: Xiyan Fu
authors.institution: Tianjin Medical University Cancer Institute and Hospital

papers.title: Higher-Order Exceptional Point Sensing with Rydberg Micro-Ensemble Arrays
papers.abstract: Higher-order exceptional points arise from the coalescence of multiple eigenvalues and eigenstates, leading to enhanced spectral responses to weak perturbations. However, realizing and controlling such higher-order degeneracies in interacting many-body systems remains challenging due to the complex coupling among multiple interacting eigenstates. Here, we construct spatially structured microensemble arrays in cold Rydberg gas, where long-range interaction and spatial connectivity enlarge the effective non-Hermitian dimensionality, enabling higher-order exceptional points. By varying the spatial arrangement of these sites, we realize different orders of non-Hermitian exceptional points. We further show that interactions between Rydberg excitation sites can enhance the quantum Fisher information, thereby improving sensing sensitivity. The resulting higher-order exceptional points exhibit increasingly nonlinear phase-boundary responses, which can be further tuned by varying the measurement time and atom number. By tracking shifts of these phase boundaries, we achieve a sensitivity of 0.47(10) nV cm-1 Hz-1/2, surpassing the standard quantum limit. Our results establish Rydberg microensemble arrays as a platform connecting higher-order non-Hermitian criticality, many-body dynamics, and microwave sensing.

authors.name: Guang-Can Guo
authors.institution: University of Electronic Science and Technology of China

authors.name: Li-Hua Zhang
authors.institution: Kunming University of Science and Technology

authors.institution: University of Science and Technology of China

papers.title: Hy ASR 3.0 Technical Report
papers.abstract: We present Hy ASR 3.0, a large language model (LLM)-based automatic speech recognition (ASR) system that delivers strong recognition accuracy, supports flexible contextual conditioning, and maintains robust recognition performance across diverse speech conditions. Hy ASR 3.0 supports Mandarin Chinese, English and 13 Chinese dialect groups, including Cantonese. Among the evaluated systems, it achieves the lowest aggregate error rates on public Mandarin Chinese, English, and Cantonese benchmarks and the lowest error rates on the corresponding internal test sets, alongside first-tier dialect recognition performance. Beyond audio-only transcription, Hy ASR 3.0 supports multiple forms of external context, including hotword lists, question--answer dialogues, and summaries, enabling the use of task-relevant information during recognition. The model also leverages intra-utterance context to disambiguate homophonic and phonetically similar keywords using information from other parts of the same utterance, without requiring a separate contextual input. Evaluations demonstrate strong contextual recognition in both external-context and intra-utterance settings, as well as robust recognition of long-form speech, children's and older adults' speech, low-volume speech, and speech in noisy environments. This report describes the model architecture and training methodology and presents evaluations across recognition accuracy, context utilization, and robustness.

authors.institution: State Key Laboratory of Materials Processing and Die & Mould Technology

papers.title: Interpreting Selective-Review Coverage for Head-and-Neck Auto-Contours
papers.abstract: Selective-review systems aim to reduce human review by passing candidates predicted to be low risk. However, coverage (the fraction passed) can be misleading when measurements needed to interpret risk are unavailable. We separate structural evaluability (a nonempty mask with all required measurements available), computational-endpoint status, and pass-or-review decisions using archived Mayo records and controlled OpenKBP analyses. In 3,968 Mayo records, all 1,167 recorded empty predictions (predicted target-organ masks containing zero voxels despite nonempty reference masks) were endpoint-negative and passed both modules, accounting for approximately 76% of each pass set. In a held-out OpenKBP test, a logistic-regression router achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.833 and average precision of 0.449 but passed all 544 non-evaluable candidates, including 542 prespecified empty-mask controls and 2 erosions that became empty. A structural gate removed those passes without changing scores or the threshold, preserved all evaluable passes, and assigned 98.71% of endpoint-positive candidates to review. Under the original preprocessing and in patient-disjoint development evaluation, a router trained only on evaluable candidates and a router modeling an unavailable state likewise passed no non-evaluable candidates, with similar evaluable discrimination and at least 99.0% of endpoint-positive candidates assigned to review in pooled outer-fold predictions. These results show that coverage should be interpreted jointly with candidate eligibility, endpoint scope, missingness handling, and routing rules; they do not establish clinical validity, deployment safety, or natural-failure prevalence.

papers.title: Supervision-Aware Evaluation of MedGemma for Reference-Assisted Radiotherapy Contour Ranking
papers.abstract: Radiotherapy contour ranking can support quality assurance, but vision-language model (VLM) gains may reflect supervision, score construction, available inputs, or representation access. We evaluated frozen MedGemma 1.5 in a single-institution study, a 12-patient held-out HaN-Seg test, five-fold cross-fitting on 30 non-test HaN-Seg patients, and transfer without refitting to 120 SegRap2023 patients. On held-out HaN-Seg, a supervised readout of the final prompt state exceeded a supervised readout of the model's yes/no output probabilities by +0.3047 pooled average precision (AP; 95% patient-bootstrap interval [+0.2822, +0.3269]); the advantage persisted against a parameter-count-matched nonlinear control. A readout of projected visual tokens exceeded the final-state readout in cross-fitting and transfer (+0.0706 AP averaged equally across patients on SegRap; 95% interval [+0.0607, +0.0804]), while a structured panel-feature readout remained competitive with visual tokens. The anatomy-conditioned readout did not demonstrate an advantage over the native-feature comparator. These results motivate visual-token and structured-feature controls in medical-imaging VLM evaluations; outcomes were computational or synthetic, not clinical acceptability.

papers.title: A risk-aware individualized blood pressure target to avoid hypotension in surgery
papers.abstract: We propose an online method for choosing both a blood pressure target and a norepinephrine dose for an individual surgical patient. From a short record of mean arterial pressure (MAP) and norepinephrine delivery, the method fits a reduced pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic model and uses a local Gaussian approximation to propagate uncertainty to future MAP readings. It searches for the lowest target for which a bolus and constant infusion keep the predicted probability of at least one MAP reading below 65 mmHg after the rise phase within a prescribed limit. If no such target is found, the decision returns to the clinician. We assess calibration of the predicted minimum MAP on retrospective surgical records under the doses actually administered. In a cohort of 4,096 virtual patients, the method recommended a dose for 74 % of patients at a nominal risk of 5 %. Among the patients receiving a recommendation, 6.9 % had a reading below 65 mmHg. A fixed target of 70 mmHg yielded a rate of 25 % when applied to the full virtual cohort.

papers.title: Asymptotic Consistency of a Weighted Nadaraya-Watson Estimator Driven by Fractional Brownian Motion at Random Times
papers.abstract: Nonparametric regression conventionally assumes equispaced observations, a premise often violated by empirical data with irregular sampling and long-memory noise. This study establishes the asymptotic mean square ($L^2$) consistency of a weighted Nadaraya-Watson (wN-W) estimator for stochastic processes sampled at random times and perturbed by fractional Brownian motion (fBm). Leveraging the occupation time formula and Fernique's Theorem, we derive exact parametric restrictions on bandwidth and sampling rates ensuring convergence. We validate these theoretical findings via extensive simulations evaluating the mean squared error under varying noise persistence. Crucially, we explicitly benchmark the performance of the estimator under random sampling times against classical deterministic grids, while assessing the relative efficiency of quartic versus Gaussian kernels. Finally, we introduce an interactive Shiny application to dynamically visualize the admissible parameter space, and we empirically validate our theoretical framework by applying the estimator to the Vostok ice core paleoclimatological dataset. This real-world application demonstrates the practical capacity of the methodology to extract macroscopic trends while robustly avoiding severe overfitting under random sampling times.\

papers.title: Melting Ice Activates Mechanical Forcing from Entrapped Air
papers.abstract: Natural ice commonly contains entrapped air, yet its dynamical role during melting remains unresolved. Using numerical simulations and theoretical analysis, we show that melt-front-released bubbles activate entrapped air as a mechanical forcing on the liquid. Bubble buoyancy disrupts density-anomaly-induced thermal structure and injects momentum into the melt-controlling boundary layer, producing melt rates more than twice the bubble-free value at percent-level gas fractions. The evolving interface and background convection regulate this coupling, which weakens again under sufficiently vigorous convection, producing a finite coupling window. A mechanical-power ratio comparing bubble-generated and background-flow power organizes this behavior. Recasting the bubble contribution as an effective near-boundary velocity extends standard ice-ocean melt closures, while reported field conditions can enter the mechanically significant regime. More broadly, a moving phase boundary can activate an embedded dispersed phase as an internal mechanical forcing.

papers.title: The Closest Super-Eccentric Giant Planet: Dynamical History and Orbital Future of Gaia-3b
papers.abstract: With new high-resolution spectra and radial velocities (RVs) from the NEID spectrometer, we reaffirm the planetary designation of the previously identified super-eccentric giant planet Gaia~3b. Our additional 23 RVs span 356 days, including an RV observation obtained within hours of the periastron passage. By modeling all of the available RVs we collapse a previously tri-modal orbital period posterior distribution and report a more precisely measured value of $P=331.52\pm0.02$ days. Our measure of the eccentricity ($e=0.9462\pm0.0017$) is in agreement with previous measurements and thus corroborates the status of Gaia~3b as the third most eccentric planet known to date. We generate synthetic realizations of the Gaia astrometric time series and derived RUWE to show that only the planetary-companion and close to equal-mass binary cases are plausible when compared to the reported RUWE. We then show that the close to equal-mass binary case is unlikely based on the Gaia color-magnitude position and the shape and amplitude of the bisectors measured from the NEID cross-correlation functions. The confirmation of Gaia~3b's planetary status makes it the closest known super-eccentric giant planet ($d \approx 35$ pc) and leads us to anticipate that Gaia DR4 will detect more super-eccentric planets orbiting nearby Sun-like stars. Finally, due to the presence of a distant stellar companion, we demonstrate that a plausible pathway exists for excitation of the planet's eccentricity by von Zeipel-Kozai-Lidov oscillations.

papers.title: A faint thermonuclear X-ray burst from SAX~J1808.4--3658 observed with NICER: possible evidence for burst-driven changes in the inner disk structure
papers.abstract: We present spectral and temporal properties of a faint thermonuclear X-ray burst observed from SAX~J1808.4--3658 by NICER. Unlike the previous analysis of the same burst \citep{2023ApJ...948..117C}, our analysis focuses on the persistent spectral evolution and changes in the accretion environment. Following a peak flux of approximately 5\% of the Eddington limit, the burst emission settled into a stable state characterized by a temperature of 0.46 keV and a flux 14\% greater than the pre-burst value in the tail. Although the observation was truncated, it resumed after 3 hours, revealing that the source flux returned to its pre-burst level. Our spectral fitting results indicate that at the peak of the burst, the neutron star's surface emission was fully exposed, subsequently becoming increasingly obscured while remaining above the pre-burst emission. Fitting the persistent spectra also reveals an increase in the visible fraction of the neutron star's surface from 25\% to 41\% during the period from 100 s to 550 s after the burst, suggesting a change in the disk structure (the height or the inner radius). The spectral evolution suggests a transient reorganization of the inner accretion flow during the burst peak, followed by partial recovery as the burst flux declines.

authors.name: Bo-Yan Chen
authors.institution: National Yang Ming Chiao Tung University

papers.title: Zero-Hopf Networks
papers.abstract: A zero-Hopf bifurcation can occur for dynamical systems that have a singularity where the linear part has a zero eigenvalue and a pair of purely imaginary eigenvalues. We call a zero-Hopf network a regular network whose adjacency matrix has a zero eigenvalue and a pair of complex eigenvalues with zero real part. In this work, we prove that there is an infinite number of zero-Hopf networks for which the zero-Hopf bifurcation can occur as a generic codimension-one phenomenon for the class of the network admissible smooth vector fields. Our results are achieved using the network adjacency matrices and the associated eigenvector structures. General results are presented for four-cell zero-Hopf networks concerning the network set of synchrony spaces. As a case study, we present a classification of all connected zero-Hopf 4-cell regular networks of valency two showing that, up to permutation of the cells, there are 9 distinct such networks. Moreover, the normal forms of these networks are computed using the method of Rink and Sanders (Trans. Amer. Math. Soc. 367 (2015) 3509--3548) for coupled cell networks. It is remarked that these normal forms are less simplified as the input symmetry of the network admissible smooth vector fields restricts the admissible normal form transformations. Nevertheless, the networks share a common coupling function normal form.

authors.name: Ana Dias
authors.institution: Centro de Estudos do Ambiente e do Mar

papers.title: Autonomous Trail Racing with a Bicycle Robot
papers.abstract: Navigating off-road trails on a mountain bike requires diverse locomotion skills, including aerial maneuvers, cornering, and slip recovery, paired with sophisticated perception for scene understanding. Translating these capabilities to autonomous, two-wheeled robots remains a formidable challenge. We show that autonomous, high-speed trail navigation can be achieved through a single idea: encoding the trail as a semantic layer of the terrain. In simulation, this layer embeds the navigation task into the training environment; during deployment, it is reconstructed onboard from camera and LiDAR data. First, we introduce a unified learning framework that treats local navigation and locomotion as a joint optimization problem, bypassing the twist or pose command interface of classical control hierarchies. With fixed reward weights, the same framework produces both trail racing and agile parkour, shaped only through terrain semantics and episode length. Second, our perception pipeline combines a frozen vision foundation model with a lightweight dual-head decoder that predicts per-pixel terrain semantics and confidence scores, which are fused with LiDAR range measurements into an egocentric semantic elevation map at 30 Hz onboard an NVIDIA AGX Orin. We validate our framework on the Ultra Mobility Vehicle (UMV), a bicycle robot that autonomously raced across all sections of a kilometer-long, unstructured mountain bike trail at speeds exceeding 5 m/s and averaging 3.26 m/s. In simulation, our policy fails up to an order of magnitude less often than hierarchical baselines while driving faster.

papers.title: On the statistical reliability of chaotic simulations at reduced precision
papers.abstract: Reduced-precision arithmetic is increasingly used to accelerate scientific simulation, while AI workloads are driving its growing prominence in hardware design. Yet small arithmetic errors do not necessarily imply accurate statistics. Finite representation limits spatial resolution, while rounding can merge trajectories that should separate in chaotic systems, progressively concentrating probability on a shrinking collection of computer states. This redistribution can distort statistical averages well before periodicity becomes apparent; furthermore, disjoint computational basins can induce an initialisation bias, even when the intended equilibrium statistics are independent of the initial ensemble. We use functional graphs and their transfer operators to connect these pathologies to bounds on statistical bias, the duration of accurate averaging, and the effect of reducing precision. Exhaustive numerical experiments on four chaotic maps, with 1-24 significand bits and the 24-bit endpoint matching IEEE FP32, show how initially accurate ensembles drift towards incorrect statistics, with lower precision often bringing this deterioration forward. Stochastic rounding substantially extends some useful averaging windows but leaves others severely biased. Longer computed trajectories can therefore worsen inferred statistics, and a finite average can outperform the "infinite-time" computer average by orders of magnitude. This exposes a risk of statistically biased inference at reduced precision and provides a further motivation for collecting statistics from ensembles of shorter trajectories.

papers.title: Packing sets by rigid motions and similarities
papers.abstract: For nonempty Borel sets $E\subset\mathbb R^d$ and $\Theta\subset O(d)\times\mathbb R^d$, where $d\ge2$, let $\Theta(E)$ be the union of the rigid copies $gE+z$, where $(g,z)\in\Theta$. We prove that $\Theta(E)$ has positive Lebesgue measure whenever $\dim_{\mathrm{SF}} E+\dim_H\Theta>\frac{d(d+1)}2$, where $\dim_{\mathrm{SF}} E$ is the spherical Fourier dimension of $E$. This resolves a conjecture on packing by arbitrary Borel families of rigid motions. Our proof develops a discrete-to-continuous framework by adapting a finite-field averaging argument to $\mathbb R^d$ using Sobolev estimates on the group of rigid motions. We also obtain analogous packing results for similarities. The same framework can be used to show that if $\tau$ is a compactly supported probability measure on the similarity group with finite $\bigl(\frac{d(d-1)}{2}+1\bigr)$-energy, then every compactly supported $\tau$-stationary probability measure on $\mathbb R^d$ has a smooth density. We deduce that a nonempty compact set has nonempty interior if its family of similarity self-embeddings has Hausdorff dimension greater than $\frac{d(d-1)}{2}+1$.

papers.title: Folding of multishape metamaterials guided by plasticity
papers.abstract: Multishape metamaterials can morph into several different shapes and offer exciting prospects in areas as diverse as tunable optics, wearable electronics, soft robotics, and aerospace. Yet, multishape metamaterials are typically actuated with complex multiaxial or multiphysics loading. Here, we introduce a uniaxial folding strategy that turns kirigami, 2D sheets patterned with cuts, into multishape metamaterials with tunable rigidity. Our folding approach leverages plasticity and loading history to guide multiple and tunable distinct shape changes upon cycles of stretching and compression. The deployed shapes exhibit a wide range of mechanical properties spanning three orders of magnitude. Self-guided plastic folding provides a uniquely scalable route to deploy load-bearing metamaterials from the micrometer up to the industrial scale.

papers.title: Direct imaging of plasmonic coupling between gold nanoparticles and one-dimensional van der Waals materials
papers.abstract: Hybrids of plasmonic metals and van der Waals (vdW) materials combine electromagnetic field enhancement with the electronic properties of the vdW component, but the studies reported so far concern two-dimensional layers, and the near field at the metal/vdW interface is generally inferred from far-field measurements. Here we report the plasmonic coupling between Au nanoparticles and a one-dimensional (1D) vdW material, NbS3, and measure the near field at the Au-NbS3 contact directly. NbS3 nanowires and nanoribbons were grown by salt-assisted vapor-liquid-solid growth on graphene-covered TEM grids, and atomic-resolution electron microscopy shows atomically sharp Au/NbS3 interfaces. Photon-induced near-field electron microscopy at 1030 nm shows that an Au particle in contact with NbS3 produces a near field of higher intensity and larger extent than an isolated particle of similar size, and that the hot spot at a contact is excited only when the incident polarization is parallel to the particle-NbS3 axis. Finite-difference time-domain simulations reproduce these observations and quantify the dependence of the coupling on the particle-NbS3 gap, the NbS3 thickness, and the dimension ratio of the NbS3 structure. Size-specific Au nanoparticles on NbS3 nanowires enhance the Raman scattering of rhodamine 6G by a factor of 1.8-4.2 relative to Au nanoparticles alone, with a detection limit of 10^-7 M. These results extend plasmonic metal/vdW hybrids to 1D vdW crystals and establish a multimodal approach that correlates the atomic structure of a metal/vdW interface with its nanoscale plasmonic response.

authors.name: Huy Hoang
authors.institution: Vietnam National University Ho Chi Minh City

papers.title: Contiguity of unions of perfect matchings and random regular uniform hypergraphs
papers.abstract: For fixed integers $s\ge3$ and $r$ satisfying $\log(r!)>\frac{r(s-1)}s\log r$, the union of $r$ independent uniform perfect matchings of the complete $s$-uniform hypergraph is mutually contiguous to the uniform simple $r$-regular $s$-uniform hypergraph, as $n\to\infty$ through multiples of $s$. In particular, $r=\lceil e^s\rceil$ suffices. The main input is the sharp entropy inequality for random permutations of Bristiel and Caputo. It proves the global maximization needed for the second moment of the number of complete factorizations. The remaining calculation, including its lattice factor, matches the short-cycle contribution required by small-subgraph conditioning.\\ This is an expanded version of a proof provided by ChatGPT-Astra.

papers.title: Propositional Dynamic Logic without tests does not have Craig Interpolation
papers.abstract:
It was shown recently by Borzechowski et al. (2026) that Propositional Dynamic Logic (PDL) has Craig Interpolation. Whether test-free PDL, i.e. PDL without the `?' operator, has interpolation remained open. Here we answer this question in the negative with a counterexample: a test-free PDL validity for which no test-free interpolant exists. The validity only uses one atomic program and the Kleene star, so it implies that the basic modal logic K extended with the reflexive transitive closure does not have interpolation, as previously shown by Studer (2009).
  The example was originally obtained using LLMs and Lean. We describe our methodology and provide links to all prompts, LLM output summaries as well as the Lean proof.

papers.title: Two Unconventional Hall Effects in the Kagome Magnet TmMn4Cr$_2$Sn$_6$
papers.abstract: We identify two Hall anomalies in the kagome magnet TmMn$_4$Cr$_2$Sn$_6$. We propose that the high-field anomaly reflects a discontinuous spin reorientation and differing sublattice contributions to Hall transport and magnetization. At low fields, Hall hysteresis persists despite negligible magnetic hysteresis, suggesting a chirality-related contribution, although its microscopic origin remains unresolved. These contrasting regimes show how magnetic transitions can mimic unconventional Hall signals and highlight the limits of magnetization-based Hall decomposition.

papers.title: Irreversible dynamics for ideal fluids on Riemannian manifolds: metriplectic energy-conserving alternatives to Navier-Stokes
papers.abstract: For modelling dissipative phenomena such as friction, diffusion and viscosity, the Hamiltonian framework has a key limitation: once the Casimir invariants are fixed, Hamiltonian flows preserve phase-space volume, which rules out relaxation to equilibrium. Thus modelling dissipation requires modifying the Hamiltonian structure. Following the metriplectic (equivalently, GENERIC) approach, we add to the Hamiltonian vector field a dissipative term generated by a symmetric bracket, here constructed from a Riemannian metric. The resulting flow conserves the energy, and optionally further invariants, while driving a chosen generalised entropy monotonically, which makes the dynamics irreversible; when the entropy is bounded on energy level sets in the direction in which it is driven, it acts as a Lyapunov functional. We apply this construction to ideal fluids on compact Riemannian manifolds, choosing Casimirs of the Lie-Poisson bracket as entropies. In two dimensions, dissipating enstrophy yields the already-known energy-constrained Navier-Stokes equations, which include a nonlocal term restoring energy balance. In three dimensions, where enstrophy is no longer a Casimir, we derive new irreversible models. For incompressible and compressible fluids carrying an advected scalar, dissipating potential enstrophy or higher potential-vorticity moments gives a nonlinear, anisotropic diffusion that acts to align the gradients of the scalar and of the potential vorticity. For a purely incompressible fluid, taking helicity as the entropy gives a first-order, non-smoothing dissipative term whose stationary states are Beltrami fields.

authors.name: Cristina Stoica
authors.institution: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique

papers.title: Asymmetric Frequency Conversion and Violation of Kirchhoff's Law of Thermal Radiation in Phased Floquet Metasurfaces
papers.abstract: We study a system of three closely spaced conducting sheets, whose thermal emission largely violates Kirchhoff's law through nonreciprocal frequency conversion enabled by Floquet phenomena. We leverage surface mode transitions controlled by temporal modulation of one of the metasurfaces, resulting in largely asymmetric frequency conversion. Our findings broaden the capabilities of Floquet metasurfaces for wave conversion and energy manipulation, paving the way towards magnet-free nonreciprocal photonic devices with opportunities for thermal management and efficient photonic refrigeration.

papers.title: SALT: State-Aligned Low-Rank Transfer for Single-Temporal Cross-Dataset Structural Localization in Remote Sensing
papers.abstract: Change detection in remote sensing conventionally relies on spatially aligned bi-temporal imagery, which may be unavailable or unreliable in practical scenarios. Recent single-temporal approaches address this limitation by learning structural evidence, such as building regions, from a labeled source dataset and transferring it to unseen target imagery using only the current image. However, adaptation to the source dataset can over-specialize pretrained features and reduce their cross-dataset generalization, a risk that this paper argues is higher when the feature adaptation is parameterized independently of the states used for prediction. To address this issue, the current study introduces SALT, a State-Aligned Low-Rank Transfer framework. SALT keeps a DINOv3 backbone frozen and learns negative and positive structural states that both score each patch and, through State-Aligned Low-Rank Adaptation (SALA), span the rank-2 subspace in which patch features are corrected. Directional State Alignment supervises these corrections to raise the evidence of positive patches and lower that of negative ones, while Geometry Preservation limits changes to the pairwise relations among pretrained patch features. Experiments on LEVIR-CD and the WHU aerial building dataset show that, at the pixel level and in both transfer directions, SALT outperforms four baselines reproduced under a common source-only protocol, improving over the strongest reproduced baselines by 9.45 and 5.79 points in pixel-level AP and by 27.69 and 14.25 points in IoU (LEVIR-CD to WHU and WHU to LEVIR-CD, respectively), with only 0.068M trainable parameters and 40.2 ms per image. In order to facilitate reproducibility and further research, the source code of SALT is available at https://github.com/gthpapadopoulos/SALT

authors.name: Georgios Th. Papadopoulos
authors.institution: Athena Research and Innovation Center In Information Communication & Knowledge Technologies

papers.title: Designing Institutions for Autonomous AI
papers.abstract: As autonomous AI agents increasingly interact in persistent populations, their collective capabilities and alignment depend not only on individual models, but also on the institutions governing their interactions. Yet AI research has largely focused on individual agents. In this Perspective, we argue that institutional design must become a distinct focus of AI research. Drawing on institutional political economy, social epistemology and organizational theory, we develop seven principles for designing AI institutions that sustain cooperation, enable reliable collective judgments and remain accountable to legitimate human purposes. These address reciprocal contributions, accountable authority, functional differentiation, epistemic pluralism, criticism and correction, human direction, and institutional adaptation. We illustrate their application through machine science, where autonomous research challenges institutions developed around human capabilities and constraints. We then propose an experimental research programme in which matched populations of AI agents operate under alternative institutional arrangements, and describe MoltJournal, an API-first journal for autonomous research agents, as an illustration of how such institutions can be made programmable and observable. Together, these contributions establish institutional design as a research agenda concerned not only with aligning autonomous agents, but with understanding how institutions can transform them into capable, reliable and accountable collectives.

papers.title: Internalizing Investment Mandates: A Neurosymbolic RL Approach to Portfolio Allocation
papers.abstract: Institutional portfolios operate under investment policy statements that specify asset allocation constraints, often conditioned on market regime information. Deep reinforcement learning has been shown to optimize financial performance but typically does not enforce rule compliance, making it unsuitable for real-world deployment. Existing neurosymbolic methods such as Probabilistic Logic Policy Gradient (PLPG) offer constraint-satisfying reinforcement learning (RL) via differentiable symbolic supervision but assume a finite, discrete action space. We present a PLPG-inspired continuous allocation method that estimates the probability that the policy's own executed action satisfies the investment mandate, using reparameterized Monte Carlo sampling, and adds it to the training objective. No post-hoc enforcement mechanism intercepts actions at inference time and compliance is learned by the agent. Audited directly on deterministic mean actions with no correction, the policy reduces violations of a six-rule regime-conditional mandate from 96-98% for unconstrained RL and 33.4% for a reward-penalty baseline to 4.8%, showing that a continuous-action neurosymbolic policy can substantially internalize a symbolic mandate.

authors.name: Zeynep Yildiz
authors.institution: Dr Lütfi Kırdar Kartal Eğitim ve Araştırma Hastanesi

papers.title: Towards Unified File Management for Data Lakehouse Systems
papers.abstract: Data lakehouse systems have garnered widespread adoption, yet their metadata management systems face a fundamental architectural dilemma. File-based OTFs (Open Table Formats) scale well, but suffer from metadata bloat, high commit latencies, the absence of multi-table transactions, and unsafe garbage collection. On the other hand, catalogs relying entirely on a transactional database incur severe scalability bottlenecks due to analytic file-level metadata. To reconcile this tension, we present Raven, an operational catalog that stores transactional metadata within a database while offloading analytical metadata to underlying OTF structures. Based on this hybrid architecture, Raven introduces an extended Merge-on-Read (MoR) mechanism to reduce commit latency and mitigate metadata bloat, alongside multi-table transactions under snapshot isolation. Furthermore, Raven unifies core data lakehouse semantics including versioning and reference tracking under an extensible ER (Entity-Relationship) metadata model, enabling safe global garbage collection across diverse types of assets. Empirical evaluations demonstrate that Raven substantially reduces commit latency and metadata bloat when integrated with Apache Iceberg and Delta Lake, maintains a catalog storage footprint orders of magnitude smaller than database-only systems like DuckLake, and achieves scalable garbage collection with minimal disruption.

papers.title: Coarse-to-Fine 3D MRI Reconstruction via Resolution-Agnostic Neural Operators
papers.abstract: Deep-learning-based 3D MRI reconstruction is limited in practice by the GPU memory and compute cost of full-volume training; 3D acquisitions are thus most often reconstructed by 2D models applied slice-by-slice and then stacked, which ignores through-plane (stacking-axis) structure. We reconstruct in full 3D and ask whether a model can be trained at low resolution (fast and memory-feasible) yet deployed at higher resolution. This coarse-to-fine strategy needs reliable cross-resolution performance, but standard networks are resolution-specific and degrade substantially when evaluated outside the training setting. We therefore use resolution-agnostic neural operators (NOs) and propose KIR-NO (k-space-to-Image Reconstruction Neural Operator), a discretization-agnostic framework for accelerated 3D MRI reconstruction. KIR-NO is trained with full backpropagation on low-resolution volumes and applied zero-shot to higher-resolution volumes at inference. Its core building block is a 3D neural operator based on discrete-continuous convolutions: convolutional filters are parameterized in a continuous basis and sampled at arbitrary voxel resolutions while preserving the local inductive bias of convolution. KIR-NO integrates these learned operators with physics-based consistency: a k-space neural-operator head first refines the undersampled Fourier measurements, and image-space neural-operator cascades then refine the reconstruction through interleaved data-consistency updates. Across 3D knee and brain MRI benchmarks, KIR-NO improves over classical and CNN baselines: it improves over a state-of-the-art 3D CNN by 2.2 dB PSNR at half resolution under 4x acceleration on SKM-TEA, with gains persisting at 8x and 16x. These results show that resolution-agnostic operators make coarse-to-fine 3D MRI reconstruction - cheap low-resolution training with high-resolution deployment - practical across anatomies.

authors.name: Jiayun Wang
authors.institution: University of Shanghai for Science and Technology

papers.title: Duality and hidden symmetries for time-inhomogeneous Markov processes
papers.abstract: We study the notion of duality in the setting of time-inhomogeneous Markov processes. We define duality with time-dependent duality functions. We establish the connection between duality and time-dependent symmetries and intertwinings. We illustrate the abstract results with examples from interacting particle systems and diffusion processes.

papers.title: Robust Safe Control Under Uncertainty: Estimation, Contraction, and Regret Bounds
papers.abstract: Disturbance uncertainty requires safety filters based on control barrier functions (CBFs) to leave a robustness margin, which can alter the nominal control input and degrade closed-loop performance. This paper studies safety and the resulting performance loss for discrete-time nonlinear systems with additive disturbances and polytopic input constraints. We develop a causal disturbance observer and construct two robust barrier conditions. The first uses a time-dependent bound on the estimation error. The second uses a constant margin when the disturbance increments are uniformly bounded and moves the requirement on the initial error from the online filter to an explicit initialization condition. For affine barriers, both filters are quadratic programs. We bound their input deviations from an oracle filter with access to the current disturbance and derive sufficient conditions for uniform contraction of the oracle closed loop. The contraction analysis accounts for state-dependent actuation, unmatched disturbances, and active physical input limits. Combining the sensitivity and contraction estimates gives finite-time dynamic regret bounds that quantify the effects of observer convergence, disturbance variation, and robustness margins. With sublinear cumulative certified disturbance variation and observer innovation error, the bounds yield sublinear regret.

papers.title: Control-Gibbs Distribution: Sampling for Optimal Control and Diverse Actions
papers.abstract: While conventional optimal control selects an optimal input sequence, probabilistic control assigns probability mass over all possible inputs and exploits a distribution of control sequences. Control distributions help enable exploration, capture diverse solutions, and solve deterministic optimal control problems. This work reviews an important probabilistic model for control distributions, the control-Gibbs distribution, i.e., the Gibbs distribution with an optimal control objective as the energy function. We point out its fundamental role in various probabilistic control frameworks, e.g., maximum entropy control, control-as-inference framework, model predictive path integral control, and energy-based models for control. This provides a model-central perspective to unify these probabilistic control frameworks. We also review the associated extensions of dynamic programming for computing closed-loop control distributions. To sample the control-Gibbs distribution, we consider projected Langevin sampling and develop non-asymptotic guarantees. The guarantees show the dual benefits of sampling the control-Gibbs distribution: obtaining diverse control solutions and solving the deterministic optimal control problem. We provide a numerical example where diverse arm trajectories are sampled from a control-Gibbs distribution.

papers.title: Acoustically driven motion of single molecules at hBN surfaces
papers.abstract: Developments in single-molecule imaging and sensing techniques have enabled direct observation of biomolecular dynamics at interfaces, which has important implications for the fields of membrane biophysics, nanofluidic sensing and transport. However, integrating active surface transport, localization and control over molecule motion remains challenging, limiting further progress in the realization of single-molecule devices. Here, we introduce an integrated surface acoustic wave (SAW)-hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) platform as a contactless actuation platform for directional transport of biomolecules over hBN surfaces. hBN provides an atomically flat surface on which DNA can be confined and still retain in-plane mobility, whereas SAW actuation enables active and guided transport without requiring specific electrical, dielectric or magnetic properties of the biomolecules. Trajectory- and jump-based analyses show that increasing the SAW power leads to higher displacement bias in the streaming direction, resulting in transport velocities along increasingly more linearized trajectories. We thus demonstrate that SAWs can induce tunable directional transport of DNA molecules confined on hBN surfaces, providing a new approach for the on-chip manipulation of biomolecules in nanofluidic systems. Our findings have important implications for the development of advanced single-molecule sequencing platforms and other technologies for biomolecular manipulation and analysis.

papers.title: Subsurface schematisation from sparse CPT data using the tabular foundation model TabPFN
papers.abstract: Subsurface schematisation supports geotechnical decisions but remains challenging because sparse site-investigation data leave substantial gaps in information about ground conditions. This study explores TabPFN, a foundation model pretrained on general synthetic tabular data, for this task. Using only grid coordinates and soil behaviour type index observations from sparse cone penetration tests (CPTs), we first reconstruct two-dimensional sections without geotechnical fine-tuning or predefined layer boundaries. We evaluate the approach on synthetic sections and at two field sites in the Netherlands, comparing it with SchemaGAN, a conditional generative adversarial network trained on synthetic geotechnical sections, and with reference interpolation methods. In the baseline comparisons, TabPFN achieved mean errors close to SchemaGAN's on synthetic sections and lower mean errors at both field sites. On synthetic sections, TabPFN's mean absolute error decreased at each tested increase in CPT count, and, under the baseline input setting, its pointwise prediction intervals had mean coverage close to nominal levels. Subsequent fine-tuning on the synthetic sections used to train SchemaGAN improved synthetic test accuracy but increased mean errors at both field sites. These findings indicate that general-purpose tabular foundation models offer a promising route for updating subsurface predictions from sparse and evolving site-investigation data without retraining.

papers.title: Measuring, Revealing and Mitigating Harmful Content Propagation in Recommender Systems
papers.abstract: Recommender systems help users navigate vast amounts of information by filtering content according to their historical behaviors. As these systems increasingly shape everyday information access, they largely determine the content users are exposed to. However, current research typically prioritizes catering to user interest, while overlooking the existence and propagation of harmful content, such as violence, hate speech, and pornography. In this work, we take a systematic step toward investigating harmful content in recommender systems from three aspects: measuring, revealing, and mitigating. First, we construct datasets with harmfulness-related annotations and present new evaluation metrics to quantitatively measure the harmfulness of recommendation results. Second, our empirical analysis reveals that users tend to engage with harmful content and prevailing recommendation methods often contribute to the proliferation of such content. Third, to address this issue, we introduce a generic framework, MitiHarm, which integrates harmfulness-related signals into both item and user representation learning. Experiments show that MitiHarm can significantly mitigate the propagation of harmful content while preserving user satisfaction. Resources of this work are available at https://github.com/Zhang-xiaokun/MitiHarm.

papers.title: The impact of DNA replication on the timing of cellular events
papers.abstract: Cellular timing often relies on the accumulation of a regulatory protein to a threshold. For a stable protein produced at a constant rate, the threshold alone sets timing precision: the squared coefficient of variation of the first-passage time is the inverse of the threshold number of molecules. This counting limit appears to be a fundamental constraint. However, production rates vary across the cell cycle. By solving exactly a stochastic model coupling DNA replication and protein accumulation, we show that when a gene replicates at an optimal time, precision exceeds the counting limit.

papers.title: Flow-CAD: Flow Matching for Contextual Anomaly Detection and Explanation in Tabular Data
papers.abstract: Contextual anomaly detection in tabular data aims to identify objects whose behavior is unexpected under their contextual conditions. In data-engineering pipelines, this task screens table rows whose measurements violate context-dependent integrity relationships. Most existing approaches rely on either shallow conditional models with limited distributional expressiveness or localized estimators that require per-context modeling, making it difficult to capture complex conditional relationships and scale to high-dimensional settings. We propose Flow-CAD, a new framework for contextual anomaly detection based on Flow Matching. Flow-CAD learns a single global and amortized conditional generative model that flexibly represents behavioral distributions conditioned on context, without assuming simple parametric forms or retraining local models. To enable robust and interpretable anomaly scoring, we introduce a scale-normalized and truncated residual energy derived from the learned conditional flow, which stabilizes anomaly scores, mitigates domination by extreme deviations, and supports feature-wise attribution. We further provide theoretical insights showing that the proposed residual-based anomaly score is stable under velocity estimation error, and that its Monte Carlo estimator satisfies concentration bounds. Experiments on 20 benchmark datasets with 13 competitors demonstrate that Flow-CAD has the best average rank for PR AUC, ROC AUC, and P@n, highlighting its effectiveness and practicality for contextual anomaly detection in tabular data. We provide the source code at https://github.com/ZhongLIFR/FlowCAD.

authors.name: Qi Huang
authors.institution: Southwest University of Science and Technology

authors.name: Yang Cao
authors.institution: Hunan University of Traditional Chinese Medicine

papers.title: Cluster-roots of $n$-representation-finite algebras
papers.abstract: We study cluster-roots of $n$-representation-finite algebras, namely the dimension vectors of cluster-indecomposable modules. We give a direct proof of Mizuno's higher analogue of Gabriel's theorem, and show that cluster-roots are precisely the non-negative integer vectors whose Coxeter orbits contain the dimension vector of an indecomposable projective module. Moreover, we give an explicit description of all cluster-roots of the $(n-1)$-Auslander algebras of type $A$. For $n=2$, we use periodic integer sequences to give a method for constructing counterexamples to Mizuno's positivity conjecture within this family, which reduces to determining whether finitely many quadratic equations admit non-negative integer solutions.

papers.title: Continuum space hierarchical Cannings process: II. Genealogies and ancestral web
papers.abstract:
The present paper is the second in a series of three papers in which we consider a \emph{spatial multi-type population model} arising as the many-individuals-per-site limit of individual-based models. The evolution mechanisms in this model are: migration, Fleming-Viot resampling, $\Lambda_0$-Cannings resampling, and $(\Lambda_k)_{k \in \N}$-Cannings block-resampling. This evolution leads to a collection of \emph{measure-valued} processes indexed by a continuum geographic space $\Omega_N^\infty$, called the \emph{continuum hierarchical group}, obtained as the limit of a discrete hierarchical group $\Omega_N^L$ as $L\to\infty$, where $\Omega_N^L = \oplus_{k \geq -L} Z_N$ with $Z_N$ the cyclical group of order $N$. On this geographic space, each component is a probability measure on a type space $\K$.
  In the first paper \cite{gh1}, we \emph{constructed} the measure-valued process on $\Omega_N^\infty$ describing the type frequencies in the population and identified its main properties. We found a \emph{dichotomy} between this process being \emph{stochastic} (= locally monotype) or \emph{deterministic} (= locally multitype). In the present paper we turn to the \emph{genealogies} of the population on $\Omega_N^\infty$.

papers.title: Luenberger observers for two-gene regulatory networks with sigmoidal regulation: explicit observability conditioning, polytopic convergence certificates, and a logistic--Hill comparison
papers.abstract: Only a few species of a gene regulatory network can be measured, so the others must be reconstructed by a state observer, and how well this works depends on the function chosen to describe regulation. We examine this for the two-gene negative feedback loop with one measured protein, for monotone regulation functions including the logistic function and the Hill function with its leaky and shifted variants. Using standard tools, we show that the answer is set by the smallest and the largest slope of the regulation function on the concentrations visited. For every function considered, the unmeasured concentration can be recovered from the measured signal and its rate of change, with an error sensitivity set by the smallest slope. A Luenberger observer with explicit gains converges exponentially from any initial guess and tolerates bounded measurement noise whenever a checkable matrix condition involving only the largest slope holds, as it does for every model examined with bounded slopes. The guaranteed rate cannot exceed the degradation rate of the unmeasured protein unless the smallest slope is positive, and faster rates then hold only for small initial errors. All reported rates are certified from above and below. At matched threshold and steepness, no family is uniformly better: the logistic function is better conditioned when the threshold lies mid-range, leaky or shifted Hill functions when it lies low. Hill functions with exponent below one have an unbounded slope at zero concentration and lose the global guarantee, which logistic and shifted Hill functions keep.

papers.title: LHAASO's Peanut source is a laboratory for studying magnetic fields in the Milky Way
papers.abstract: Recently, the LHAASO Collaboration reported gamma-ray emission from the Peanut-shaped source (Peanut), which extends over $4.5^\circ$ parallel to the Galactic plane at $b=-17.5^\circ$. The source is associated with the millisecond pulsar PSR J0218+4232, located at the eastern edge of the Peanut, at a distance of 3 kpc from the Earth and 0.9 kpc from the Galactic plane. Its location and bright gamma-ray emission above 25 TeV make it a natural laboratory for studying the Galactic magnetic field (GMF) in the transition region between the Galactic plane and halo. We interpret the observed emission as inverse-Compton scattering of CMB photons by electrons propagating along the large-scale GMF, accounting for turbulence through two models: Kolmogorov and Goldreich-Sridhar (GS). These models correspond to diffusive and ballistic particle propagation, respectively. While the GS case naturally provides conditions for one-sided gamma-ray emission, in the Kolmogorov case assumptions of one-sided particle injection and magnetic mirror at the source are necessary. We find that, in the Kolmogorov scenario, the Peanut's hotspots are likely associated with magnetic bottling, whereas in the GS scenario, they are related to magnetic field line geometry. Both models yield constraints on the GMF at the location of the Peanut.

authors.name: Maksim Kleimenov
authors.institution: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique

authors.name: Gwenael Giacinti
authors.institution: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique

papers.title: A discrete realization of the boundary sine-Gordon model and the Schmid transition
papers.abstract: The phase diagram of the boundary sine-Gordon model (bsG), or equivalently of the resistively shunted Josephson junction, has been the subject of recent debate. We introduce a discrete model that reproduces exactly the properties of the bsG model and can be simulated extremely efficiently using cluster Monte Carlo algorithms. This enables us to explore a broad range of parameters and compute the complete universal crossover between the weak- and strong-tunneling regimes. We establish the self-duality of the model and unambiguously identify the vertical line of critical fixed points characteristic of the Schmid transition, recovering the conformal field theory predictions along this line with high accuracy. We further clarify the essential distinctions between the Schmid and Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless transitions. Our results definitively establish the existence and nature of the Schmid transition and demonstrate the validity of the Schmid-Bulgadaev scenario.

authors.name: Nicolas Paris
authors.institution: Centre de Recherche en Informatique de Lens

authors.name: Oscar Bouverot-Dupuis
authors.institution: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique

authors.name: Christophe Mora
authors.institution: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique

papers.title: From $3\times2$pt to $4\times3$pt: calibrating galaxy bias and intrinsic alignments with galaxy clustering and weak lensing bispectra
papers.abstract: Combining galaxy clustering and weak gravitational lensing beyond two-point statistics offers a way to extract additional cosmological information while calibrating astrophysical nuisance parameters. We investigate this approach by combining 1-loop power spectra with tree-level bispectra, including all auto- and cross-bispectra of galaxy clustering and weak lensing, a combination that we refer to as $4\times3$pt by analogy with the well-known $3\times2$pt analysis. Modelling two- and three-point statistics consistently, with galaxy bias and intrinsic alignments described by the TATT model, we perform Fisher forecasts of dark energy constraints for a Euclid-like survey, with conservative scale cuts. When combined with CMB data, adding $4\times3$pt bispectra to the $3\times2$pt improves the dark energy figure of merit by about $30\%$, a gain that remains stable when using the three, four or five lowest redshift bins of our ten. To extend the analysis to ten tomographic bins, we compress the bispectra into skew-spectra, which improve the figure of merit by $20\%$ with the CMB and by $37\%$ without. We show that most of this improvement comes from the calibration of second-order galaxy bias parameters by three-point statistics, mainly by the galaxy-auto and the GGL bispectra. We also find that baryonic feedback is correlated with second-order intrinsic alignment parameters once the amplitude of the matter power spectrum is constrained by the CMB, and that bispectra reduce this correlation by calibrating intrinsic alignments, almost entirely through the GGL bispectra, a mechanism that could become more valuable with more flexible baryonic feedback models. These results demonstrate the potential of combined galaxy clustering and weak lensing bispectra to improve cosmological constraints from stage-IV galaxy surveys through the calibration of galaxy bias and intrinsic alignments.

papers.title: Disentangled Embedding Optimization for Diffusion-Based Dataset Distillation
papers.abstract: Dataset distillation aims to compress large-scale datasets into compact synthetic subsets that enable efficient model training with comparable performance to the original data. Recent advances show that diffusion models are highly effective for this task due to their strong generative capability. Existing diffusion-based approaches typically perform class-wise clustering and use the obtained cluster prototypes as diffusion inputs to generate distilled samples. However, the uniformly distributed original samples in a category inevitably lead to entanglement near cluster boundaries, pulling the cluster prototypes closer and reducing the inter-cluster separation. Consequently, the diffusion model receives overly similar latent inputs, resulting in synthetic data with limited diversity. To address this issue, we propose Disentangled Embedding Optimization (DEO), a simple yet effective framework that replaces static clustering with trainable embeddings. These embeddings are optimized to match the Gaussian statistics (i.e., mean and covariance) of the original data distribution, while a diversity regularizer is designed to encourage separation among these embeddings to improve the intra-class variability. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our proposed DEO can generate more diversified and representative distilled data than existing cluster-based diffusion methods, achieving state-of-the-art performance and superior generalization across multiple datasets.

authors.name: Hongcheng Li
authors.institution: The Affiliated Yongchuan Hospital of Chongqing Medical University

authors.name: Xiaoyan Gu
authors.institution: State Key Laboratory of Organic-Inorganic Composite Materials

papers.title: Beyond Compressing Everything: Contrastive Memory Learning for Selective Context Compression
papers.abstract: As large language models (LLMs) advance toward increasingly long inputs, soft context compression offers a promising approach to efficient inference by converting long inputs into compact memory slots. Under limited memory budgets, effective context compression remains challenging because task-relevant evidence varies substantially across queries, ranging from localized evidence to multiple distant spans or information dispersed throughout the full document. Instead of compressing everything indiscriminately, we propose CoMem, a query-guided selective context compression framework that learns memory representations conditioned on both the document and the query. CoMem develops Contrastive Compressor Learning to achieve query-sensitive yet context-preserving memory representations. To inject a strong prior over query-dependent evidence distributions, we devise a same-context hard negative mining strategy by pairing a single document with multiple queries, requiring the compressor to selectively retain information according to each query's distinct evidence needs. To address the restricted information flow imposed by causal masking, we further enable bidirectional attention among memory slots. Experiments demonstrate that CoMem consistently outperforms existing context compression methods across compression ratios on question answering and RULER-NIAH benchmarks. Our code is available at https://github.com/scar-on/CoMem.

authors.name: Sikui Zhang
authors.institution: University of Chinese Academy of Sciences

papers.title: ACE-CaP-0: Real-World Code-as-Policies in the Era of Experience
papers.abstract: Recent advances in frontier models have pushed the boundaries of agentic robot control, enabling agents to perform complex robotic tasks through reasoning and interaction. However, repeated calls to these models during execution can substantially increase task completion time. Code as Policies (CaP) offers a route for coding agents to acquire physical skills through experience and retain them in executable programs, allowing the reasoning invested in development to be reused across runs. Developing reliable code policies while limiting the cost of physical experimentation remains a central challenge. We investigate human guidance as a source of priors for feasible actions and simulation as an auxiliary environment for exploring and testing candidate policies. Our findings favor robot demonstrations available on request and simulation used selectively during real-world policy refinement. These findings inform ACE-CaP-0, an agentic recipe that couples policy revision with experience acquisition through Demonstrations on Request and Simulation on Demand. Across eight real-world manipulation tasks spanning alignment, multi-object handling, and bimanual coordination, the resulting frozen programs achieve 92.1\% success (221/240 trials). Mean execution times across tasks range from 0.97 to 2.27 minutes. The programs execute with runtime perception and control, without a human or coding agent in the loop. These results highlight CaP's potential to turn experience into reliable, reusable physical skills.
