papers.title: SoK: Design Choices in Tendermint BFT Consensus
papers.abstract: Tendermint is a consensus protocol that tolerates Byzantine faults, implemented first by the Tendermint Core engine and now by CometBFT. Realizing the protocol's separation of agreement from execution, the Application Blockchain Interface (ABCI) of these engines keeps consensus apart from the replicated application, so one engine can serve many independent proof-of-stake chains. A sustained body of research proposes changes that span the protocol's mechanisms, from vote dissemination to block proposal and reward distribution, yet to our knowledge no survey studies the protocol and these works as one family, and broader surveys do not take Tendermint as their subject. We describe the baseline, the protocol as consolidated from its original descriptions, by its design choices. Each is a decision, such as how votes spread or how proposers rotate, through which the baseline provides safety and liveness or another property under its fault and timing model. We classify each work by the design choice it renegotiates, that is, modifies or replaces, by the properties it strengthens or weakens, and by whether its result needs a stronger model. Taking a broader perspective on that classification, we group the surveyed works' solutions into a few threads of concern in the baseline, namely its performance, the accountability of its validators, and the protection of exploitable information. For each thread, we identify the recurring strategies that their approaches follow. Together, these threads and strategies describe the current state of research on the Tendermint family. Where the strategies leave gaps, we pose future directions, each as an open question under an explicit fault and timing model.

papers.title: SBA: A Practical Memory Performance Denial-of-Service Attack
papers.abstract:
Modern cloud platforms use memory bandwidth regulation to isolate co-located workloads, implicitly assuming that high aggregate bandwidth consumption implies high interference. We show that this assumption is fundamentally flawed.
  We present the Single-Bank Attack (SBA), a practical memory denial-of-service attack that induces extreme cross-core slowdowns---over three orders of magnitude on memory-intensive victims (e.g., LLM decode)---while consuming less than 1 GB/s of memory bandwidth. SBA exploits the gap between peak and worst-case DRAM throughput by concentrating memory write operations on a single bank, forcing persistent row conflicts and frequent write draining, thereby collapsing the memory service rate. Across Intel and AMD systems, including DDR5- and HBM2E-based platforms, SBA consistently causes orders-of-magnitude slowdowns under realistic multi-tenant settings, revealing a fundamental limitation of bandwidth-centric memory isolation.
  We further show that this localized contention propagates system-wide: single-bank congestion saturates memory controller queues and induces back-pressure into shared cache and coherence structures, ultimately throttling memory request injection across cores. Consequently, severe interference can arise even at low aggregate bandwidth, evading existing bandwidth-based QoS mechanisms such as Intel RDT MBA.
  To address this limitation, we propose IQ-MemGuard, a lightweight, software-based memory bandwidth regulator that detects sustained contention using microarchitectural signals and selectively throttles pathological request injection. Our implementation on an Intel platform effectively mitigates SBA, whereas Intel's hardware QoS mechanism fails completely.

papers.title: Snoopie: A Multi-GPU Communication Profiler and Visualizer
papers.abstract: With data movement becoming one of the most expensive bottlenecks in computing, the need for profiling tools to analyze communication becomes crucial for effectively scaling multi-GPU applications. While existing profiling tools including first-party software by GPU vendors are robust and excel at capturing compute operations within a single GPU, support for monitoring GPU-GPU data transfers and calls issued by communication libraries is currently inadequate. To fill these gaps, we introduce Snoopie, an instrumentation-based multi-GPU communication profiling tool built on NVBit, capable of tracking peer-to-peer transfers and GPU-centric communication library calls. To increase programmer productivity, Snoopie can attribute data movement to the source code line and the data objects involved. It comes with multiple visualization modes at varying granularities, from a coarse view of the data movement in the system as a whole to specific instructions and addresses. Our case studies demonstrate Snoopie's effectiveness in monitoring data movement, locating performance bugs in applications, and understanding concrete data transfers abstracted beneath communication libraries. The tool is publicly available at https://github.com/ParCoreLab/snoopie.

papers.title: Analogs of crystalline measures in tube sets
papers.abstract: Let $\mu$ be a pure point complex measure on a tube set $R^d+i F$, where $F$ is a compact convex subset in $R^d$, such that this tube set is the minimal closed convex tube set containing support of $\mu$. Furthermore, assume that the Fourier transform $\hat\mu$ (in the sense of distributions) is a measure. We determine conditions on the measure $\mu$ under which the variation of the measure $\hat\mu$ grows at least as $\exp\{2\pi H_F(t)\}$, as well as conditions under which this variation grows at most as $\exp\{2\pi H_F(t)\}$; here $H_F(t)$ is the support function of $F$.

authors.name: Sergii Favorov
authors.institution: V. N. Karazin Kharkiv National University

papers.title: Objects as Addresses: Instance Binding in Vision Transformer Attention
papers.abstract: Humans naturally parse visual scenes into coherent individual objects rather than scattered features, a capability cognitive science calls object binding. While recent work shows that pretrained Vision Transformers (ViTs) intrinsically acquire this ability, how native self-attention computations mechanistically keep object instances separate remains unresolved. By studying this across eight pretrained ViTs, we found that instance separation is expressed more strongly in attention routing than in token content: selected query-key relations distinguish individual objects more reliably than value similarity or residual representations. Inside heads, patches belonging to one individual tend to read from a common image region, which we term their attention address. Visually distinct parts of one person share an address, whereas identical duplicated instances receive separate, movable addresses. These shared destinations arise in part because query interactions with the spatial structure of keys direct attention toward consistent regions for one object and elsewhere for another. In DINOv2 and most other backbones we tested, editing this query component at the selected head redirects its attention address toward another individual. Grouping patches by this query component separates same-category instances, reaching .615 FG-ARI versus .289 for the same clustering of final-layer features, which tend to merge them.

papers.title: Performance Analysis of Quantization-Aware Neural Channel Estimation with Low-Precision Inference
papers.abstract: Neural channel estimators can improve radio performance of 5G receivers, but real-time deployment in the radio access network (RAN) imposes strict latency and power budgets. Prior studies of quantized neural channel estimators assess this cost through mean-squared error or analytic operation counts. In this paper, we train a 1D convolutional neural network (CNN) channel estimator for the 5G NR physical uplink shared channel (PUSCH) with INT8 and FP8 quantization-aware training (QAT), and we evaluate its radio performance together with its latency, power, and energy on an NVIDIA H100 GPU. On TDL-A and TDL-C channels at user equipment (UE) speeds up to 35 m/s, both 8-bit models stay within 0.025 dB of FP32 at 10% block error rate (BLER). At batch size 128, INT8 reduces the latency by 16%, the incremental GPU power by 33%, and the energy per query by 26%, compared with 6%, 26%, and 21% for FP8. INT8 is therefore the preferred format.

papers.title: Sparse Matrix Multiplication Exponent 1.5 in the Low-bandwidth Model
papers.abstract:
We study sparse matrix multiplication in the low-bandwidth model: $n$ computers multiply two $n\times n$ matrices, and each computer can send and receive one $O(\log n)$-bit message per round. The input matrices are uniformly sparse, meaning that there are at most $d$ nonzero entries in each row and column, and the task is to compute a uniformly sparse part of their product.
  In prior work, Gupta et al.~(SPAA 2022) presented an $O(d^{1.907})$-round algorithm over fields for this problem when the sparsity structure is globally known in advance (this is referred to as the supported setting). The upper bound was later improved to $O(d^{1.832})$ rounds.
  In this work, we give a deterministic algorithm that solves this problem in $O(d^{3/2})$ rounds in the supported setting, improving the previous bounds over fields and semirings.

papers.title: DPA: Decentralized Primal Averaging with Quasi-Global Momentum for Highly Heterogeneous Data
papers.abstract: Decentralized training of deep learning models keeps training data local and supports on-device learning over networks. In realistic scenarios, heterogeneity across agents' local data poses an optimization challenge and can severely degrade test accuracy, especially on sparse communication graphs. Building on recent advances in centralized primal averaging, we propose Decentralized Primal Averaging (DPA), a decentralized learning algorithm that combines primal averaging with a local quasi-global momentum buffer. DPA maintains three coupled sequences for optimization, gradient evaluation, and output averaging, while using consecutive mixed iterates to construct a network-aware momentum direction without transmitting an auxiliary tracking variable. For smooth nonconvex objectives, we establish a convergence bound for DPA and identify conditions for linear speedup in the number of agents for sufficiently many iterations. We also introduce DPA-1G, a variant that uses one communication round per iteration and matches the per-iteration communication cost of DSGD-style baselines. Experiments following the GUT decentralized image-classification benchmark show that DPA compares favorably with DSGD, gradient tracking, QG-DSGDm, momentum tracking, and QG-GUTm across datasets, architectures, topologies, and heterogeneity levels, with the largest gains under high heterogeneity on sparse rings. At the same total communication cost, both DPA variants achieve higher mean test accuracy than the best baseline on CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 with ResNet-20. Our code is publicly available.

authors.name: Stefan Werner
authors.institution: Norwegian University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Optimal approximation results for non-standard growth functionals in the super-dimensional case
papers.abstract: In the super-dimensional case $p>n$ we show that $W^{1,p}$-functions can be uniformly approximated by H\"older continuous functions with improved exponent $\frac {p-n}{p-1}$. We use this to show density of smooth functions and absence of Lavrentiev's phenomenon for $(p, q)$-growth with optimal conditions. The special cases of double phase and Musielak--Orlicz growth are also included. Finally, we improve the conditions for maximal regularity of the double phase minimizers. In each case the optimality of our range of exponents is shown by known examples.

papers.title: Robots That Talk Too Much and Don't Listen Enough
papers.abstract: Until recently, the biggest obstacles to natural spoken interaction with social robots were speech recognition errors and turn-taking failures. Advances in speech recognition have enabled much better spoken interaction, but turn-taking failures and other misunderstandings continue to be far too prevalent. This short paper looks back at earlier methods for improving speech recognition and turn-taking in interaction with social robots, and then looks at what can be done today, arguing that multimodal bidirectional streaming is needed to reduce the frequency of turn-taking failures.

authors.name: Kristiina Jokinen
authors.institution: National Institute of Advanced Industrial Science and Technology

papers.title: Nevanlinna theory for generalized tropical meromorphic functions and applications to ultra-discrete equations
papers.abstract:
The main purpose of this paper is to establish the tropical Nevanlinna theory to piecewise linear real functions with arbitrary first-kind discontinuities (called generalized tropical meromorphic functions). The key point is that we introduce the directional jump counting functions $J^+(r,f)$ and $J^-(r,f)$ for the case of arbitrary first-kind discontinuities to refine the single function $J(r,f)$ in the previous theory. We first obtain the new tropical version of the Poisson-Jensen formula, the first main theorem. Under the assumption that $f$ is slope-admissible, we show that $T(r,f)$ is nondecreasing and establish a logarithmic derivative lemma. These results unify the classical continuous case due to Halburd and Southall and the one-sided continuous case due to Halonen, Korhonen and Filipuk.
  As applications, we study several first-order and second-order ultra-discrete equations, showing that certain equations admit infinitely many generalized tropical meromorphic solutions, and that under suitable conditions infinite-order solutions also exist. Finally, using the logarithmic derivative lemma obtained above, we establish a tropical Clunie lemma.

papers.title: Geometry-Aware Smoothing Selection for Noisy Scattered Surface Reconstruction: Evidence from Synthetic Benchmarks and Water Quality Data
papers.abstract: Sampling geometry may influence both reconstruction stability and the smoothing needed to control noise. This study distinguishes geometry-dependent failure of exact multiquadric radial basis function (RBF) interpolation from variation in validation-selected smoothing. A synthetic benchmark crossed four response families, four 16-point geometries, three slice levels, five observation regimes, and 24 repeated holdouts, yielding 17,280 method-level evaluations. Clough--Tocher cubic interpolation, exact RBF, and smoothed RBF were compared, followed by a Water Quality Portal pilot with 1,950 complete activities. On the synthetic shared-valid domain, exact RBF achieved the lowest noise-free mean RMSE (0.0206), whereas smoothed RBF performed best under noise (0.1807 versus 0.2414 for cubic and 0.6106 for exact RBF). Clustered-gap support produced the largest noisy exact-RBF RMSE (1.2706). Geometry added little explanatory power for log-transformed smoothing: the combined model had $R^2=0.4259$, compared with 0.4096 for noise alone. Reported failure-regression results suggest a stronger geometry signal, but remain unverified without their original model specification. In the environmental pilot, smoothed RBF achieved mean RMSE 0.9877 with no negative-$R^2$ failures. Conflicting responses at identical predictor coordinates made exact interpolation unsuitable. All environmental smoothed-RBF fits selected the largest candidate, preventing geometry--smoothing correlation analysis. The findings motivate geometry-aware failure screening but do not establish a transferable rule for smoothing magnitude. Independent multisite validation, appropriate coordinate scaling, joint scale--smoothing tuning, and conditioning diagnostics are needed before an adaptive policy can be claimed.

papers.title: RESYNC: Residual Latent-State Synchronization for Deadline-Bound Streaming Inference
papers.abstract: Predicting every observation in a high-rate stream requires a model to finish before the next arrival. A large model may offer better predictions but miss that deadline. We propose RESYNC: the large model runs asynchronously, while a fast path updates its latest exact but stale latent state using the observations received since that state was computed and applies its unchanged prediction head. The updater learns from the frozen model's representations without task labels. Across one real and two synthetic streams and five architecture families, RESYNC beats the best compact or distilled alternative with a paired 95% interval above zero in all twelve dataset--architecture pairs with a material teacher advantage at anchor ages of 4--12 observations, and in eleven pairs at older tested ages up to 32. The share of the teacher's gain preserved remains complete on the real stream but is lower and generally declines with anchor age on the synthetic streams. In live replay with 1 ms arrivals, the synchronous large models cannot deliver any predictions on time while RESYNC serves at least 99.4% of arrivals within the interval, with 0.35--0.62 ms median latency on one CPU thread: around the same speed as or faster than the compact model, and 7.9--17.7$\times$ faster than synchronous large-model inference. RESYNC targets settings with background compute available but a strict per-observation response deadline.

papers.title: The solutions of the Diophantine equation $(2^{k}-1)(3^{l}-1)=7^{m}-1$
papers.abstract: In this paper, we will show that the positive integer triple $(k,l,m)$ satisfying the equation in the title is $(2,1,1).$

papers.title: Fast Computation of the Kippenhahn Hypersurface of a Joint Numerical Range
papers.abstract: We present a fast modular interpolation method for computing the hypersurface components of algebraic Kippenhahn varieties over number fields. Starting from Hermitian matrices, we factor their determinantal polynomial and use Katz's test to identify the factors whose duals are hypersurfaces. For each such factor, we sample smooth points over finite fields and compute their tangent hyperplanes. These give points on the dual hypersurface, from which we interpolate its defining equation. For number-field coefficients, we use primes at which the defining polynomial of the field factors completely into distinct linear factors. Interpolation across all its roots recovers the residues of the coefficients in a fixed number-field basis. Chinese remaindering and rational reconstruction then recover an equation over the original number field from the computations at different primes. An exact polynomial divisibility test and an irreducibility check certify each reconstructed equation. Four determinantal quartics arising from matrix examples in the literature yield certified dual surfaces of degrees $12$, $18$, $24$ and $34$. We give implementations in Magma and Singular and compare their running times with Gr\"obner basis elimination.

authors.name: Carlos Rito
authors.institution: University of Trás-os-Montes and Alto Douro

papers.title: CosmoSim: Lens-parameter estimation of the Einstein Cross NGC 6505 using machine learning
papers.abstract: CosmoSim is an open-source tool for simulating gravitational lenses and reconstructing lens mass distributions, either by ray tracing a parametric lens model or through a Roulette expansion of the lens potential. It is also used to generate the large, labelled synthetic image sets needed to train machine-learning (ML) parameter estimators. We present the first application of CosmoSim to real data. A convolutional neural network trained only on CosmoSim images estimates Singular Isothermal Ellipsoid lens and source parameters directly from observed images. We test the pipeline on 21 images of 19 strong lenses from Euclid and the AGEL survey, after removing the foreground lens light with a custom decontamination tool built on AstroPy. As a case study we reconstruct the Einstein Cross NGC 6505 both from the lens model published by the discovery team and from parameters predicted by our ML model. Both reconstructions recover the observed four-image structure, and the ML-based reconstruction performs at least as well as the literature-based one: it scores better on masked structural similarity, intersection-over-union and Chamfer distance, with an essentially equal Hausdorff distance. Across the ensemble, the predicted Einstein radii are consistent with catalogued values within the quoted uncertainties (mean relative difference 0.08 for Euclid and 0.19 for AGEL lenses), and the enclosed masses agree to within a median of 0.12 dex. The predicted ellipticities differ systematically from the catalogued values, while the comparison of orientations is inconclusive. These results establish CosmoSim as a tool that can be applied directly to observational data.

authors.name: Ben David Normann
authors.institution: Norwegian University of Science and Technology

authors.name: Hans Georg Schaathun
authors.institution: Norwegian University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Certifying Majorana persistence through Hamiltonian learning from boundary measurements
papers.abstract: Finite measurements at a chain end can certify local quantum dynamics without determining bulk topology. We combine Hamiltonian learning with commutator bounds to certify the persistence of localized Majorana operators in Kitaev chains. Time-resolved single-shot boundary measurements and local bond calibrations define joint confidence sets for local Hamiltonian coefficients. Under explicit device assumptions, these sets yield state-independent lower bounds on symmetrized autocorrelations with a prescribed failure probability, valid for all compatible continuations. With equal hopping and pairing on the first bond and no additional boundary terms, an exact identity enables inference from the end qubit alone, even with arbitrary time-independent interactions elsewhere. Synthetic benchmarks near a boundary sweet spot certify persistence for up to about 60 times the measurement window. Three- and six-qubit IBM records strengthen conditional guarantees for the programmed coherent Hamiltonian. Applications to quantum-dot models relate tuning precision to persistence times and detuning-induced splitting.

authors.name: Tohid Farajollahpour
authors.institution: Norwegian University of Science and Technology

authors.name: Alireza Qaiumzadeh
authors.institution: Norwegian University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Baxter $\mathbb{Q}$-operator and Separation of Variables for BC-type open $SL(2,\mathbb{C})$ spin chain
papers.abstract:
We construct two-parameter Baxter $\mathbb{Q}$-operators for the transfer matrices of noncompact open $SL(2,\mathbb{C})$ BC-type spin chains with general boundary interactions, treating both one-boundary and two-boundary models. The $\mathbb{Q}$-operators are defined as traces of general monodromy matrices over infinite-dimensional auxiliary spaces carrying principal series representations of $SL(2,\mathbb{C})$.
  At specific values of parameters the two-parameter $\mathbb{Q}$-operators degenerate into simpler one-parameter Baxter operators. We prove that the general transfer matrices factorize into products of these one-parameter $Q$-operators. We provide both an algebraic derivation based on local operator identities and a diagrammatic proof using Feynman diagrammatic techniques.
  Finally, we apply the quantum Separation of Variables (SoV) method to the spectral problem of the one-boundary transfer matrix. We derive the system of separated difference equations for the transfer matrix eigenfunctions and show that, under the assumption of kernel factorization, it reduces to a one-dimensional difference equation coinciding precisely with the Baxter equation for eigenvalues of appropriately normalized one-parameter Baxter $Q$-operator.

authors.name: P. Antonenko
authors.institution: Dnipro State Agrarian and Economic University

papers.title: Super Learner: A Practical Tutorial
papers.abstract: The selection of an optimal predictive model is a pervasive challenge in biostatistics and epidemiology. Relying on a single a priori algorithm risks overfitting and reduced generalizability when applied to new settings. Super Learner is a flexible ensemble machine-learning method that mitigates these risks by combining multiple candidate algorithms into a single prediction model. Using cross-validation, it defines a weighted combination of learners that minimizes a specified loss function, ensuring performance asymptotically equal to or better than the best candidate algorithm. This tutorial provides a comprehensive, practical guide to implementing Super Learner in R for applied researchers. Using a simulated epidemiological dataset with a binary outcome, we demonstrate the step-by-step construction of the ensemble. We cover the foundational statistical concepts, basic implementation, evaluation through cross-validation, hyperparameter tuning, feature screening, and performance optimization for metrics such as the Area Under the ROC Curve (AUC). Additionally, we detail advanced usage, including computational parallelization and the integration of custom algorithms and screening procedures. The guide also includes a consolidated section on best practices for specifying SL, covering loss function selection, effective sample size determination, CV scheme definition, library curation, and discrete vs. ensemble SL decisions, plus a practical reference to the caret package for model preprocessing and comparison. This guide equips epidemiologists and clinical researchers with the tools to confidently incorporate robust machine learning techniques into their predictive modeling workflows.

papers.title: Maximum Principles and Principal Eigenvalue for Coupled Local/Nonlocal Models
papers.abstract: In this paper, we analyze the validity of the maximum principle and the existence of a principal eigenvalue for a problem involving two regions, in one of them the main operator is the classical Laplacian (a local operator) while in the other region the operator is a nonlocal one (these regions are coupled via a transmission term that is also nonlocal). The main difficulty here comes from the lack of compactness of the nonlocal part that occurs since we are considering non-singular kernels.

papers.title: Exact power spectra and effective dimensionality in critical block-GOE networks
papers.abstract: Criticality in neural networks is crucial for optimal information processing. Recent studies have shifted focus from static criticality to frequency-dependent behavior, particularly in oscillatory systems modeled by block-Gaussian orthogonal ensemble (block-GOE) matrices. However, analytical tools to predict spectral properties such as power spectrum and effective dimensionality remain scarce. In this work, we derive exact solutions for the network-averaged power spectrum $\operatorname{Tr}_{N}[\mathbf{S}(\omega)]$, the network autocovariance $\operatorname{Tr}_{N}[\mathbf{C}(\tau)]$, and the normalized effective dimensionality $D_N(\omega)$ in block-GOE ensembles. These results provide a comprehensive framework for understanding how oscillatory networks operate near criticality, offering insights into the dynamic balance between stability and flexibility in large-scale neural systems.

papers.title: Kitaev Exchange and Altermagnetism in the Double Perovskite Sr$_2$CoTeO$_6$: An Ab Initio Study
papers.abstract: The Co$^{2+}$-based double perovskite Sr$_2$CoTeO$_6$ attracts attention due to its nontrivial magnetic properties. \textit{Ab initio} density functional theory calculations reveal a substantial ferromagnetic Kitaev exchange $|K|\sim J/3$ between nearest neighbors that, combined with the face-centered cubic lattice, leads to pronounced exchange frustration and places Sr$_2$CoTeO$_6$ among Kitaev materials with moderate Kitaev interaction strength. In addition, Sr$_2$CoTeO$_6$ is found to be altermagnetic with a sizable non-relativistic spin splitting, which can give rise to a transverse piezomagnetic effect and a nontrivial magneto-optical response.

papers.title: Designing Collaborative Virtual Environments for Software Engineering Education
papers.abstract: Collaborative virtual environments offer opportunities to make software models available for shared inspection, but educational design and usability need to be examined separately from claims of learning effectiveness. This article presents MetaSEE, an approach connecting requirements guidance, a Web XR feature model, a reusable UML component, and a browser-based multiuser platform. We synthesize documented formative evaluations of the framework (16 participations), feature model (15), UML component (9), and platform (14). These counts represent evaluation participations; the same 12 developers took part in the first two evaluations. The principal platform study involved six teachers working individually and eight students working in four pairs through desktop or notebook computers, keyboard, and mouse. The documentary synthesis traces educational intentions to implemented features and reported difficulties. Participants identified potential value in shared modeling and simulation, alongside navigation, interaction, visualization, and distraction concerns. A numerical audit reconstructs a student System Usability Scale mean of 67.50 from published item frequencies, conflicting with the reported 79.38; an incomplete teacher item distribution prevents recovery of that group's overall mean. The contribution is a traceable account of educational design and formative limitations, with practical implications for onboarding, model readability, collaboration, and evaluation reporting. The evidence supports bounded feasibility and perceived usefulness, without establishing learning gains, sustained engagement, or adoption.

authors.name: Filipe Fernandes
authors.institution: Centro de Investigação e Desenvolvimento em Engenharia Mecânica

authors.name: Claudia Werner
authors.institution: Universidade Federal do Rio de Janeiro

papers.title: DafnyCert: Certifying Specification Strength in Dafny
papers.abstract: Formally verifying a method with Dafny guarantees correctness relative to its specification. However, a specification may be too permissive, allowing multiple outputs for the same input, even when the implementation produces only one. In this paper, we propose checkable certificates that provide independently verifiable evidence of whether a specification is weak or strong. A certificate of weakness contains an alternative implementation that verifies against the original specification, together with a witness input on which the original and alternative implementations produce different results. A certificate of strength is produced by constructing a harness around the original method such that successfully verifying the harness guarantees that the specification allows at most one possible output for any given input. We present DafnyCert, a tool that automatically produces these certificates. Strength is established by constructing and verifying the harness. Weakness is demonstrated by using the MutDafny mutation tool to find mutants that verify against the original specification, and by using the Hypothesis property-based testing framework to generate inputs that produce different outputs for the original program and the mutant. The resulting mutant and witness form a recheckable certificate of weakness. On a dataset of 3,910 verified Dafny methods from Dafny-Synthesis and VeriEquivBench, DafnyCert automatically certifies 3,570 methods (91.3%). We also provide certificates for the remaining 340 methods. To our knowledge, this is the first dataset in which every specification is backed by a checkable certificate of strength or weakness. These labels disagree with the benchmarks' original labels for 16.3% of the methods. These findings highlight the importance of supporting specification strength labels with independently checkable evidence.

authors.name: Isabel Amaral
authors.institution: i3S - Instituto de Investigação e Inovação em Saúde, Universidade do Porto

papers.title: AIDA: Analysis of Interval Data in R
papers.abstract: AIDA is an R package that provides tools for the analysis of interval-valued data, including construction, visualization, robust estimation, and explainable outlier detection. The package is built around the intData class and is designed to support methodological research and applied workflows involving interval-valued data. AIDA implements methods for symbolic covariance estimation based on the Mallows distance, robust estimation via the Interval Minimum Covariance Determinant estimator, and explainable outlier detection using Shapley values. The package also includes visualization tools to support interpretation of the results and several interval-valued datasets.

authors.name: Catarina P. Loureiro
authors.institution: Centro de Matemática Computacional e Estocástica

authors.name: M. Rosario Oliveira
authors.institution: Centro de Matemática Computacional e Estocástica

papers.title: Patterns for Designing CI/CD Workflows
papers.abstract: CI/CD pipelines are difficult to build and maintain, and information about them is scattered across empirical studies, practitioner books, and catalogues of 'smells'. We collected candidate practices and anti-practices converted them into patterns, and then consolidated these into patterns. These patterns address issues such as security, pipeline scheduling, workflow structure, performance and failure and release management. Each pattern is contextualised and describes the problem it solves, the forces at play, the solution and the consequences.

papers.title: AgriSense: Vision-Language Decision Support and Robotic Intervention in a Virtual Greenhouse Copy title
papers.abstract: Autonomous greenhouse management increasingly requires robotic systems that integrate perception, navigation, environmental regulation, and plant-level intervention. This paper presents AgriSense, a framework combining an Isaac Sim virtual greenhouse, a quadruped mobile manipulator, RGB and LiDAR-inertial sensing, environmental control, and supervised vision-language decision support. Frozen DINOv2 and BERT encoders, together with structured environmental inputs, support joint prediction of twelve environmental references, a target zone, and an intervention flag. Checkpoint replay reproduces 41/43 zone decisions. Across five seeds on a source-grouped test set, the full, image-removed, and language-removed configurations each achieve 43/44 correct zone decisions, providing no evidence of incremental multimodal zone-accuracy improvement. The full model achieves mean absolute errors of 0.249 degrees C for temperature, 2.030 percentage points for humidity, and 0.997 percentage points for soil moisture. Sensor-only inputs match full-model zone accuracy, while language-only inputs achieve 68.64%. External real-image benchmarks reveal distribution-shift limitations. Five offline Point-LIO routes yield rigidly aligned trajectory errors of 5.22-17.32 mm. Of 40 virtual-arm targets, 32 satisfy geometric acceptance criteria and eight are rejected at boundaries. Six long-horizon climate cases and fault protocols characterize integration limits. Navigation and integrated treatment rely on simulator-state inputs; physical greenhouse performance and agronomic treatment efficacy remain unvalidated. The contribution is an evaluated decision-support and robotic-intervention framework for a virtual greenhouse.

authors.name: Lyes Saad Saoud
authors.institution: Khalifa University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Minimal Finite Non-Commutative Centrally Essential Rings
papers.abstract: A ring $R$ with nonzero unity is called centrally essential if for every nonzero element $a$ of $R$ there exist nonzero central elements $x$ and $y$ such that $ax = y$. In this paper we obtain a complete classification, up to isomorphism, of non-commutative centrally essential rings of minimal order $64$.

papers.title: Frames and representing systems in Hardy spaces
papers.abstract: We study representing systems of Cauchy kernels or dilations of a given function in Hardy spaces. We give a complete geometric description of countable sets $\Lambda \subset \mathbb{D}$ such that the system $\{\hat{k}_{\lambda}\}_{\lambda \in \Lambda}$ of normalized Cauchy kernels forms a generalized frame in the Hardy space $H^p(\mathbb{D})$ with $p \in (1, \infty)$ with respect to a particular coefficient space. For a wide class of functions we construct representing systems of their dilations in $H^2$. We also obtain a linear method for expanding functions in series of Cauchy kernels in $H^2$.

papers.title: Volume asymptotics for a family of hyperbolic 3-manifolds with totally geodesic boundary
papers.abstract: For the family $\{\mathcal{M}_{g,k}\}_{g\geqslant k\geqslant 0}$ of orientable hyperbolic 3-manifolds with totally geodesic boundary and cusps introduced by R.~Frigerio, B.~Martelli, and C.~Petronio, the volume of the manifolds depends only on the non-negative integer parameters $g$ and $k$; thus the volume function $Vol(g,k)$ is well defined. The main result of the paper is an asymptotic description of this function: it is approximated by a linear function of $g$ and $k$ whose coefficients are explicitly expressed in terms of the volumes of the regular ideal tetrahedron and the regular ideal octahedron; moreover, the volume does not exceed the linear approximation by a difference of order $O(1/g)$. As consequences, three theorems comparing volumes are obtained: monotonicity under coordinatewise increase of the parameters, estimates for the passage from parameter $g$ to $g+1$, and monotonicity along lines of constant complexity $g+k$. For small values of the parameters, approximate values of the volumes are computed and collected in a table used in verifying the cases $g<8$.

papers.title: CARE-Drive: Coupled Alternating Refinement for Ego-trajectories
papers.abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models bring multimodal understanding and world knowledge to end-to-end autonomous driving. To further improve the quality of predicted trajectories, existing studies introduce candidate refinement, residual denoising, and token correction. However, these methods typically focus on unified refinement of the entire trajectory, paying limited attention to the distinct physical quantities and their interactions. We further investigate physical specialization and coordination in trajectory refinement, centering on position and heading for simpler and more intuitive correction modeling. To this end, we propose CARE-Drive (Coupled Alternating Refinement for Ego-trajectories), which decomposes trajectory refinement into waypoint residual correction and position-conditioned heading generation. Through imitation learning and a future-token auxiliary task, the backbone provides predictive representations and a base trajectory. The position expert predicts bounded metric waypoint residuals, while the heading expert reconstructs vehicle orientation from adjacent angular increments conditioned on the corrected path. With the backbone frozen, the two experts are optimized alternately through supervised initialization and reinforcement fine-tuning. This design simplifies refinement through clear physical specialization while preserving conditional coupling during prediction and optimization. On NAVSIM v1, CARE-Drive achieves 88.8 PDMS, improving by 2.4 points over the unrefined base trajectories generated by the same backbone. Ablation studies further support the effectiveness of specialized experts and staged training.

authors.name: Zhiquan Hu
authors.institution: Huazhong University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Escaping the Curse of Dimensionality in One-Step Flow-Based Generative Models
papers.abstract: Flow and diffusion-based generative models achieve state-of-the-art quality, but require multiple forward passes at inference time, making them computationally costly. Consistency models overcome this by learning a flow map directly, enabling few-step generation and dramatically reducing the computation needed at test time. However, formal statistical guarantees for such one-step generators are scarce. Existing results either suffer from the curse of dimensionality or rely on impractical loss functions. We investigate whether one-step flow-based models can escape the curse of dimensionality under the assumption that the data distribution is generated by a low-dimensional surface perturbed with Gaussian noise. In this setup, we derive approximation and generalization error bounds for the flow map estimate that circumvent the curse of dimensionality. Our findings provide the first principled explanation for practical success of one-step flow-based generative models.

papers.title: An exact certificate-based enumeration of Rolle words of degree six
papers.abstract: For a real polynomial of degree $n$ with $n$ distinct real roots, assume that no two different nonconstant derivatives, including the polynomial itself, share a root. Recording the derivative orders of all roots from left to right gives a Rolle word. We present an exact, computer-assisted classification in degree six: $2706$ words are realizable, with a word and its reversal counted separately. Starting from $33592$ formal interlacing words, published necessary restrictions leave $13404$ candidates. Integer realization certificates and $53$ exact exclusion stages classify every candidate. The surviving set agrees exactly with the set of certified realizations. All verification uses integer and rational arithmetic. The accompanying code, certificates, proof notes, and per-word exclusion ledger make the computation reproducible. The result concerns degree six; it does not resolve the classification problem in arbitrary degree or count connected components of coefficient space. Most of the mathematical development, code, certificates, and initial manuscript were generated using ChatGPT under the author's direction. No independent human audit of the complete proof chain has yet been completed.

papers.title: What stands behind luminosity peak of type IIP supernovae?
papers.abstract: We explore the origin of an initial broad luminosity peak that precedes the light curve plateau in type IIP supernovae. It is well known that the explosion of an evolutionary red supergiant model in the frame of radiation hydrodynamics fails to reproduce the initial luminosity peak. A common practice to compensate this drawback is to introduce massive (> 0.3 Msun) circumstellar shell attached to the evolutionary model. This remedy, however, has a negative side effect - a strong deceleration of the outer ejecta, which is inconsistent with early spectral data. An alternative way out suggests modification of a hydrogen envelope of the evolutionary red supergiant model - the outer layers should have steeper density gradient. We perform the search for the optimal multi-parameter hydrodynamic model of type IIP SN 1999em based on the Markov Chain Monte Carlo sampling. The major result is that the initial luminous peak is well reproduced by the explosion of the red supergiant with the logarithmic density gradient smaller than -3 in the outer layers of about 0.9 Msun. We suggest that the mechanism for the density steepening in the hydrogen envelope is closely related to the unknown mechanism responsible for the creation of the ubiquitous low-mass (< 0.01 Msun) dense confined shell detected in type IIP supernovae.

papers.title: Direct estimation of the lunar-solar precession with geodetic very long baseline interferometry
papers.abstract: Geodetic very long baseline interferometry (VLBI) is capable of measuring the Earth's instantaneous rotation pole (IRP) components (hereafter, $X_{IRP}$ and $Y_{IRP}$) with sufficient accuracy using the VLBI delay rate. The least-squares fit of the $X_{IRP}$ and $Y_{IRP}$ polynomial expansion coefficients produces the precession model parameters independently of planetary motion theories. Our aim was to estimate the precession parameters using VLBI delay rate observations as well as the nutation coefficients in order to produce a full transformation matrix from the IRP to the Geocentric Celestial Reference System (GCRS). Then, the goal was to incorporate the free core nutation (FCN) effect from the VLBI group delay to form a complete and simple analytical model. We obtained an empirical model of the transformation from International Terrestrial Reference System (ITRS) to Geocentric Celestial Reference System (GCRS) based on observational results. Similar to the IAU2006 theory, the new model produces time series of $X_{IRP}$ and $Y_{IRP}$ angles, but these two angles now point out the direction of the IRP rather than the celestial intermediate pole (CIP). A simple analytical model defines the IRP location for any epoch during the interval of observations. Therefore, the non-rotation origin concept is not required for the transformation matrix construction. The estimate of the lunar-solar precessional parameter based on analysis of VLBI delay rate is $\psi_{A}= 5038.500\pm 0.019"$/cy (referred to the observational epoch 2000.0), which is close to the adopted IAU2006 precessional parameter value $\psi_{A}= 5038.4815"$/cy.

papers.title: Multimodal Semantic Communication using Shared and Unique Representation Decomposition
papers.abstract: Semantic communication (SemCom) has emerged as a promising paradigm for bandwidth-constrained mobile and vehicular networks. This paper proposes a unified representation learning framework for multimodal SemCom (MSC), which encodes heterogeneous data into a compact semantic space for efficient transmission and source recovery. The framework addresses the multimodal semantic representation gap, which arises when at least one modality contains semantic information that cannot be fully inferred from the other. To preserve this information for reconstruction, the framework decomposes each representation into shared and modality-specific components. We formulate a mutual information objective for source reconstruction, cross-modal alignment of the shared components, and decoupling of the shared and modality-specific components. To enhance transmission efficiency, we introduce a shared knowledge base implemented as a compact codebook of semantic vectors learned during training. The shared components are transmitted digitally as codebook indices, while the modality-specific components are sent in analog form. We apply knowledge distillation during training, using a pretrained vision foundation model to guide the learning of quantized shared features. On image--text pairs over additive white Gaussian noise (AWGN) and Extended Vehicular A (EVA) channels, the proposed framework improves image reconstruction over conventional separate source-channel coding (SSCC) and representative multimodal and unimodal SemCom systems. Further evaluations show gradual degradation under channel-estimation mismatch, complementary effects of alignment, decoupling, and knowledge distillation on the shared representation, and alignment of shared features across modalities with separation of the modality-specific features.

papers.title: Novel upper bounds for Borsuk numbers from contact points and spherical partitions
papers.abstract:
Let $b(n)$ be the least $m$ such that every bounded set in $\mathbb{R}^n$ of positive diameter can be partitioned into $m$ sets of smaller diameter. We prove that \[
  b(4)\le6,\qquad b(5)\le12,\qquad b(6)\le31,\qquad b(7)\le45,\qquad b(8)\le89, \] and that \[
  b(n)\le1+2^{n-1}\left(\tfrac{39}{64}\right)^{\lfloor(n-1)/8\rfloor}
  \qquad\text{for every } n\ge9 ; \] for instance, $b(9)\le157$ and $b(17)\le24337$. Further constructions give, for example, $b(10)\le289$ and $b(13)\le2313$. These bounds improve Lassak's bound $b(n)\le2^{n-1}+1$ of 1982 in every dimension $n\ge4$. In dimension four they also improve the recent bounds $b(4)\le8$ (Tolmachev and Voronov, May 2026) and $b(4)\le7$ (Arman, Bondarenko, Prymak and Radchenko, October 2026); the bound $b(4)\le6$ was announced independently by Chalmers in November 2026.
  The bounds for $n\ge7$ have analytic proofs: a quantitative form of Lassak's reduction to coverings of the sphere is combined with normal partitions of weighted vector configurations, for which the smallest inner product within a region is estimated explicitly. The bound for $n=6$ uses a covering of $S^4$ by thirty sets, checked in rational arithmetic. For $n=4,5$ three contact points of the circumscribed ball reduce the problem to a four-parameter family of bodies, which is split by finitely many power diagrams; that all parts have diameter less than one is verified by a computer program with rigorous error control.

authors.name: Alexander Tolmachev
authors.institution: State Scientific Institution “Institute for Single Crystals” of National Academy of Sciences of Ukraine

papers.title: ATune: Unsupervised Photo Retouching Through Image-Editor Controls
papers.abstract: Photo retouching models are trained on pairs of original and retouched photographs, usually edited by experts. Expert edits are costly, so the two main public sets, FiveK and PPR10K, hold only 16,161 originals. Good photographs on their own are far easier to find: commercial stock collections and free ones such as Pixabay and Unsplash hold millions. We learn retouching from them alone: we damage each photograph the way a camera or a careless edit would, which gives a worse and a better version of the same photograph. From these pairs, our model, ATune, learns how 13 measured attributes, such as brightness, contrast and sharpness, should change to raise a photograph's quality. The edit is declarative: ATune sets target values for the attributes, and a simple search adjusts the sliders of an out-of-the-box photo editor until the photograph reaches them. Every edit is a list of slider values a person can read and adjust. The same model can drive any editor that makes those changes; we test RawTherapee and darktable. We train on 10M photographs from a commercial stock collection and test on FiveK, PPR10K and SPAQ. Nine quality judges score every edit, and in a user study 157 human raters made 9,253 choices between our edit and another method's edit of the same photograph. When Claude Opus 5 and GPT-6 Astra edit the same photographs in the same editor, raters prefer our edits to GPT-6 Astra's (54.3%) and rate them even with Claude's (50.5%). We also compare with supervised retouchers on their home ground: NeurOP on FiveK and AdaInt on PPR10K, each trained on that set's own expert edits. Raters chose our edits in 46.3% of those comparisons. ATune, a 54M-parameter model trained without a single expert edit, now matches frontier models at setting an editor's sliders.

papers.title: Polynomial eigenfunctions and recurrences of fixed length
papers.abstract: This paper solves the fixed-length recurrence problem posed by Horozov, Shapiro and Tater. For the rational Darboux transformations specified here, it also resolves the order and classification questions raised by their two conjectures. It classifies monic polynomial sequences whose members are eigenpolynomials of one fixed nonscalar differential operator of arbitrary finite order with polynomial coefficients and for which multiplication by the variable involves a fixed number of consecutive polynomials. Orthogonality is not assumed, and only sufficiently large degrees need be prescribed. If the lowest recurrence index is $n-m+1$, with $m\ge3$, the differential order equals $m$ times the degree of the eigenvalue as a polynomial in $n$. After translating the variable, every such sequence is a finite rational Darboux transform of an explicit family with differential order $m$ and eigenvalue $n$. Necessary and sufficient conditions on the factors determine all polynomial differential eigenoperators of the resulting family. For families that cannot be obtained by these transformations from families of smaller minimum differential order, the minimum differential and recurrence orders coincide. All such families are classified in minimum differential orders at least three, including additional families in composite orders.

papers.title: Paired Geometric Supervision for Generalizable Deepfake Detection
papers.abstract: We present OrthoPairGTL, a geometric training framework for cross-domain deepfake detection, built on a partially frozen DINOv3 backbone ($\sim$300M parameters), and make three contributions: (1) We re-evaluate six recent transfer-learning detectors (Forensics Adapter, Effort, three GenD variants and FakeSTormer) using the authors' released checkpoints under a single preprocessing pipeline across 17 cross-domain datasets (2018-2025), so that the reported gaps reflect method rather than per-method pipeline tuning. (2) We model the transformation between paired real and fake samples, training Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning (PEFT) adapters with an orthogonal pair decomposition, hyperspherical regularisation, and (in the GSD-LoRA variant) a set-level coherence objective. (3) Under LoRA, this regularisation gives a more stable optimisation profile: GSD-LoRA's post-peak validation degradation is $4.2\times$ shallower than plain LoRA at the same parameter footprint, and the time-averaged validation AUC across training is 1.82 pp higher. On the 17 datasets, GSD-LoRA matches or exceeds every re-evaluated baseline (92.82% vs. 91.58% for the strongest; paired Wilcoxon signed-rank $p=0.015$, 13/17 per-dataset wins), with the largest gains on modern reenactment-heavy benchmarks (DSv1.1, DSv2). Under strict parameter budgets, LayerNorm-only tuning ($\approx$0.03% of the backbone) is the most stable configuration and matches the strongest baseline with a mean of 91.97%.

papers.title: Non-concordant knots with the same trace
papers.abstract: Miller and Piccirillo demonstrated the existence of non-concordant knots that share the same 0-trace. In this short note, we generalize their result by showing that every smooth concordance class contains a knot K such that, for every nonzero integer n, there exists a knot $K_n$ whose n-trace is orientation-preservingly diffeomorphic to that of K, but for which $p[K_n] \ne p[K]$ in the topological concordance group for every positive integer p. Furthermore, $p[K_n]$ is distinct from $p[K']$ for any knot K' obtained from K by mirroring and/or reversing its orientation.

papers.title: EvenVLM: A Text and Multimodal Dataset for the Even Language with Vision-Language Fine-Tuning
papers.abstract: We present EvenVLM, the first text and multimodal (VQA) dataset for Even (Lamut), an endangered Northern Tungusic language spoken by approximately 6,800 people in Siberia. Our dataset comprises 50,521 structured Even-Russian entries extracted from dictionary and phrasebook sources via GPT-4o Mini-based parsing, from which we synthetically generate 107,543 training examples spanning translation, grammar, reading comprehension, and semantic classification. To address tokenization inefficiency on Even's agglutinative morphology, we propose a three-step tokenizer expansion algorithm that adds Even-specific graphemes (eng, oe, o-umlaut), whitelisted vocabulary, and BPE merges, reducing average tokens per word by 27% (4.99 to 3.64). Using LoRA fine-tuning of Qwen3-VL-4B, we adapt the model for text tasks (0.53% trainable parameters, rank 32) and separately for visual question answering (rank 64, frozen vision encoder). Our best configuration achieves 11.4% exact match and a 13.6 weighted score on text benchmarks, 0.1283 chrF for sentence translation, and 65% accuracy on VQA (up from 0% for the base model and text-only fine-tuning). We release our datasets, evaluation benchmarks, and training pipeline to support further research on Even and other low-resource languages.

authors.name: Ivan Bondarenko
authors.institution: Institute for Physics and Power Engineering

papers.title: Delta-Iterations: A General-Purpose Linear Regression Solver for Huber's Penalty, $\epsilon$-Insensitive Loss, and Other Moreau Envelope-Based Loss Functions
papers.abstract: A general-purpose linear regression solver for a class of smooth loss functions is presented. The method applies to loss functions of the Moreau envelope type, which are continuously differentiable and have Lipschitz-continuous first derivatives. This class includes piecewise-defined cost functions consisting of constant, linear and quadratic segments, such as Huber's loss, insensitive least squares, one-sided least squares. The convergence guarantee provided by the associated proximal operator, the simplicity of the method and its versatility in handling various cost functions within a unified framework are its main advantages. MATLAB code for reproducing the numerical results presented in this article is provided.

papers.title: NonSense: On the (In)security of FPGA Anti-tamper Sensors
papers.abstract: FPGAs are widely used in mission-critical systems, where a successful physical attack can have serious consequences. This makes resilience to such attacks a critical security requirement. To defend against active physical attacks, such as glitching attacks, modern FPGAs rely on on-chip sensors that detect these disturbances and trigger responses, such as key zeroization, before a device is compromised. These sensors are deployed as both hard-IP blocks and soft-IP cores, and their trustworthiness is often taken for granted. In this work, we challenge that assumption and argue that the sensors themselves are a fragile and underexplored attack surface. Drawing on recent results, we show that both the detection and response mechanisms of state-of-the-art sensors can be bypassed without invasive tampering. We further argue that sensor reliability is reduced by factors rarely captured in threat models, including the spatial and frequency-dependent behavior of the system's power delivery network, which can steer a fault to a target while sparing nearby sensors; environmental conditions such as temperature, which shift detection thresholds; and long-term aging, which drifts sensor calibration and may open silent detection gaps. Finally, we propose a set of countermeasures that harden detection and response mechanisms against these effects.

authors.name: Maryam Saadat Safa
authors.institution: Iran University of Science and Technology

papers.title: ADAPT: Agentic Diff-Aware Patch Testing for Pull Requests
papers.abstract:
Modern software development relies on pull requests (PRs) that introduce small, targeted code changes. Once merged, these changes should be protected by focused tests that exercise the behavior the PR introduces, yet developers often submit PRs without such tests, leaving the new behavior unguarded against future regressions. Most test generation techniques target entire software units and optimize objectives such as code coverage rather than the behavior a change introduces, and prior diff-aware approaches have had limited success in capturing it.
  We propose ADAPT (Agentic Diff-Aware Patch Testing), a regression test generation approach that uses an autonomous coding agent to produce change-focused tests for PRs. Given a PR, the agent analyzes the diff between the base and head versions to identify the modified functions and their context, then plans and generates candidate unit tests. A dedicated fail-to-pass (F2P) verification tool runs each candidate on both versions and, after F2P success, reports which executable changed lines remain uncovered; guided by this feedback, the agent iteratively refines its tests.
  We evaluate ADAPT on the same 426 real-world PRs used by the prior state-of-the-art baseline, with GPT-4o and GPT-5-mini. ADAPT+GPT-4o reaches an F2P rate of 62.0% (264/426), compared with BLAST's reported 35.4% (151/426), while ADAPT+GPT-5-mini reaches 89.9% (383/426). On 137 PRs shared with Change And Cover (ChaCo), ADAPT achieves full patch coverage on 83.9% of PRs, compared with 79.6% for ChaCo, at considerably lower time and cost. A manual evaluation confirms that the F2P-valid tests target each PR's intended change, with mean scores of up to 4.54/5 for importance, 4.35/5 for assertion strength, and 4.49/5 for readability, often covering behavior beyond the developer-written tests.

papers.title: Structure-Preserving Leaky Integrate-and-Fire Dynamics on Arbitrary Time Scales
papers.abstract: The leaky integrate-and-fire (LIF) neuron combines a passive membrane law with threshold-triggered firing and reset. We formulate this hybrid neuron model, under constant input, on an arbitrary Hilger time scale $\mathbb{T}$. Our central result is that, after the first spike, the firing times satisfy $t_{n+1}=\Pi_{\mathbb{T}}^{+}(t_n+T_c)$, where $T_c$ is the classical reset-to-threshold travel time. This recursion requires no periodicity, homogeneity, or translation invariance of $\mathbb{T}$; it holds for every time scale that is unbounded above. To preserve the passive membrane physics, we use the inverse cylinder transformation to construct a positively regressive coefficient $p_m$. The resulting delta-dynamic equation is exactly the restriction to $\mathbb{T}$ of the classical continuous-time LIF trajectory. By contrast, the direct transcription $V^\Delta=-(V-V_\infty)/\tau_m$ exhibits graininess-dependent sign reversal and amplification at coarse right-scattered points. The first firing time is the forward projection of the classical continuous threshold-crossing time onto $\mathbb{T}$, and, when the graininess is bounded by $\mu^\ast$, the per-event forward-projection delay -- from each reset to the next realized firing time, relative to the continuous crossing time computed from that same reset -- is bounded above by $\mu^\ast$. On $\mathbb{T}=h\mathbb{Z}$ we obtain the explicit lattice-quantized law $T_{\mathrm{ISI}}^{(h)}=h\lceil T_c/h\rceil$, which converges to the classical continuous-time inter-spike interval as $h\to0^+$. The framework therefore separates preserved membrane physics from the temporal opportunity structure imposed by the time domain. To our knowledge, this is the first systematic Hilger-calculus treatment of a threshold-and-reset LIF spiking neuron on an arbitrary time scale.

papers.title: Multi-View 3D Reconstruction Using V-JEPA Features
papers.abstract: Predictive video encoders provide dense visual representations, but adapting them to 3D reconstruction requires accurate depth, camera poses, and cross-view geometry. We study supervised RGB-only multi-view reconstruction using an architecture that combines video-pretrained features, camera estimation, scene aggregation, epipolar transport, and residual pointmaps. Experiments compare global and spatial camera regression with joint relative objectives on CO3D, alongside an independently trained TUM RGB-D model. On 168 CO3D five-view windows, the spatial-camera configuration achieves 29.3% lower absolute trajectory error than the global-camera configuration, but performs worse than identity poses in trajectory error and worse than the global configuration in depth error. The joint relative-objective configuration improves normalized intrinsics error and similarity-aligned Chamfer distance from 0.6447 to 0.5573, but increases raw Chamfer distance from 3.5535 to 4.4374. On 163 indoor windows, camera error is 0.3063 m versus 0.3694 m for identity poses, while depth error is 0.4279 versus 0.2516 for constant median depth. Refinement worsens indoor camera error, and additional experiments show competing depth and pose effects. Overall, the results distinguish representation adaptation, aligned shape, and raw reconstruction, highlighting the need for isolated component and encoder comparisons before attributing reconstruction gains to predictive video pretraining.

authors.name: Anwar Shamim
authors.institution: Instituto de Química de São Carlos

authors.name: Jeffrin Sam
authors.institution: Skolkovo Institute of Science and Technology

papers.title: DroneDiffusion: Uncertainty-Guided Diffusion Path Planner for UAV Navigation
papers.abstract: We present DroneDiffusion, a perception-aware diffusion planner for local 3-D UAV trajectory generation that explicitly models and avoids failure zones caused by lens flare, overexposure, and reflective surfaces. A vision-language perceptual safety estimator produces a pixel-aligned reliability map that highlights regions of degraded sensing. A denoising diffusion probabilistic model (DDPM) is conditioned on this map together with the onboard RGB image, goal point, and initial velocity to generate egocentric 3-D trajectories. To enforce obstacle avoidance at inference time without retraining, we apply training-free CHOMP guidance over a 3-D Euclidean signed distance field. The model is trained entirely in simulation and deployed zero-shot on a real drone. Reliability conditioning raises the mean perceptual reliability along generated trajectories to 0.71, compared with 0.63 for a geometric baseline, while guidance halves the collision rate of the learned prior from 14.7% to 7.8%. Perceptual safety conditioning and geometric guidance are therefore complementary: treating sensor reliability as a first-class signal reduces incursions into unreliable regions while maintaining competitive navigation performance.

papers.title: A simple proof of the Bourgade-Sodin-Zeitouni theorem on the excess of the sine-$\beta$ process for non-integer $\sqrt{2/\beta}>1$
papers.abstract: We give an alternative proof of the Bourgade-Sodin-Zeitouni theorem on the excess of the sine-$\beta$ process for the Paley-Wiener space when $\sqrt{2/\beta}\in (1,+\infty)$ is not an integer. Let $k(\beta)=\lfloor\sqrt{2/\beta}\rfloor$. For almost every configuration, removing any $k(\beta)$ points leaves a minimal uniqueness set for the Paley-Wiener space. The same conclusion holds for each Bernstein space $\mathcal{B}^p$ of $L^p(\mathbb{R})$-integrable functions with $m(\beta)<p<\infty$, where $m(\beta)=\beta(k(\beta)+1)-\sqrt{\beta^2(k(\beta)+1)^2-2\beta}$.

authors.name: Sergei M. Gorbunov
authors.institution: Moscow Institute of Physics and Technology

papers.title: A polynomial-time approximation scheme for the weighted Euclidean Minimum Latency Problem in fixed dimension
papers.abstract:
In the Traveling Salesman Problem, a route must visit all customers and return to its starting point while minimizing its total length. The Minimum Latency Problem, also known as the Traveling Repairman Problem, instead minimizes the sum of the times at which customers are first visited. We give a deterministic polynomial-time approximation scheme for the weighted Euclidean Minimum Latency Problem in every fixed dimension, with arbitrary nonnegative customer weights.
  Our proof restricts the form of a solution in three steps, each with a controlled increase in cost. First, a decomposition based on Sitters' method assigns customers to phases that start and end at the root. Second, within each phase, we divide the route into a constant number of blocks and charge each customer at the end of its assigned block. The resulting objective is a nonnegative linear combination of block lengths. Third, we add an auxiliary dimension and use a fixed Minkowski norm to close each block path into a tour. Arora's closed-tour estimate then gives paths that cross the boundaries of a common dissection only at designated portals and a bounded number of times per face. A dynamic program optimizes the restricted objective, and projecting its paths back to the original space gives the final route. Rounding weights and coordinates keeps the state space polynomial.

authors.name: Daniel Skachkov
authors.institution: Moscow Institute of Physics and Technology

papers.title: Enabling Mie Resonances for Optomagnetism in Epitaxially Grown Garnet Nanodisks via Photonic Crystals
papers.abstract: An all-garnet photonic-crystal substrate compatible with epitaxial growth on gadolinium gallium garnet is proposed for controlling the optomagnetic response of a single bismuth iron garnet nanodisk. The photonic environment modifies the spectral positions and relative strengths of the electric- and magnetic-dipole contributions and redistributes the optical field inside the disk. Compared with a reference nanodisk on a homogeneous substrate evaluated near the broad maximum of its summed multipolar response, the peak axial optical contribution to the inverse Faraday effect in the examined cross-sections is enhanced by factors of approximately 7.3 and 6.3 in the magnetic- and electric-dipole-dominated regimes, respectively. The enhancement reaches approximately 7.9 at the maximum of the summed multipolar scattering contributions. These results demonstrate spectral control of the magnitude and spatial distribution of the local optomagnetic response through the photonic environment, without changing the nanodisk geometry.

authors.name: P. V. Zorina
authors.institution: Moscow Institute of Physics and Technology

papers.title: An upper bound on the number of edges of a Gomory corner polyhedron
papers.abstract: We establish the first nontrivial upper bound on the number of edges of a Gomory corner polyhedron, resolving a long-standing open question. For an $n$-dimensional corner polyhedron associated with an integer lattice of determinant $\delta$, the number of edges is at most $$ O\left(n6^n \cdot \bigl(1+\log_2(2\delta)\bigr)^{2n-3}\right). $$ This improves the standard bound obtained by counting pairs of vertices, reducing the logarithmic exponent from $(2n-2)$ to $(2n-3)$.

authors.institution: N. I. Lobachevsky State University of Nizhny Novgorod

papers.title: Secular Dynamics and the LFL for $\beta$ Corner Process
papers.abstract: In this paper, we consider the Gaussian $\beta$ corner process, whose edge particles are known to converge to the Tracy-Widom $\beta$ law. We study the almost sure behaviour of the extrema of the whole trajectory of the edge particles and establish a law of fractional logarithm (LFL) for the corner process for every fixed $\beta>0$, extending the previous known results in the case $\beta=1,2$. Our proof relies on the upward Gamma and downward Dirichlet secular equations, which can be regarded as two discrete dynamics to form the corner processes. The secular dynamics are used in both the correlation estimate and the decorrelation estimate, which are known as two key steps of proving LFL in \cite{BCEHK-LFL} for the Wigner minor process. Especially, in the decorrelation part, they are used as discrete analogues of the continuous Dyson Brownian motion.

papers.title: Overcoming Spurious Correlations in Conditional Diffusion Models via Doubly Robust Target Correction
papers.abstract: While conditional diffusion models have achieved remarkable success in generation tasks, they memorize spurious correlations within training data. This causes them to deviate from ideal target distributions. Minimizing a covariate shift-adjusted target risk can address this issue. However, retraining models from scratch for different distributions is computationally prohibitive. To overcome this limitation, we propose DR-Diff, a framework that efficiently fine-tunes pre-trained conditional diffusion models. Specifically, DR-Diff leverages a functional gradient approach to derive a pseudo-target. This pseudo-target captures the residual between the base model's noise prediction and the ground-truth noise under the target distribution. Training the model to fit this pseudo-target enables efficient target adaptation. Theoretically, we prove that DR-Diff guarantees target risk reduction at the population level. It also achieves a pseudo-doubly robust property, providing resilience against density ratio estimation errors and base model misspecifications. Empirically, DR-Diff matches the noise prediction accuracy of models trained from scratch on synthetic datasets. Furthermore, it mitigates inter-group disparities in downstream classification tasks.

papers.title: Gradient stability for the Sobolev inequality with optimal dimensional dependence
papers.abstract: Figalli and Zhang [29] established gradient stability for the sharp Sobolev inequality with the optimal exponent $r_p=\max\{2,p\}$. We prove that, for every fixed $p>1$, the corresponding optimal stability constant $\mathsf C_{n,p}$ admits effective upper and lower bounds of order $n^{-1}$ for all integers $n>p$. In particular, the dimensional dependence $n^{-1}$ is optimal. Our result extends the optimal dimensional dependence established for $p=2$ by Dolbeault, Esteban, Figalli, Frank, and Loss [18] to every $p>1$.

papers.title: Effect of Gas Pressure and Molecular Structure in the Spatial-Mode Conversion of Terahertz Radiation from a Plasma Filament
papers.abstract: In this work, the generation of terahertz (THz) radiation under single color filamentation of a femtosecond laser pulse in an optical cell with compressed gases (argon, nitrogen, CO2) in broad pressure range from 0.001 to 25 atm is experimentally studied for the first time. A nonmonotonic dependence of the integral energy of the THz signal on the gas pressure is revealed, which can be attributed to the competition between an increase in the plasma density and the development of plasma selfabsorption processes, multiple filamentation of the femtosecond pump, and collision induced absorption in the neutral medium. We show that the molecular structure of the gas critically determines the pressure optimum of generation, shifting the maximum of the THz energy yield to the region of elevated pressures (from 10 to 15 atm) for monatomic argon and to the region of subatmospheric pressures (approx. 0.1 atm) for molecular carbon dioxide due to strong vibrational rotational dissipation. On the basis of numerical 3D modeling, it is shown that the cylindrical metal waveguide insert used for signal collection operates in a strongly multimode regime and substantially transforms the angular spectrum of the THz source. We demonstrate that the conical structure of the THz radiation recorded in the experiment is a consequence of intermode interference and diffraction at the output end face of the waveguide, which transforms the true parameters of THz generation in the plasma channel.
