papers.title: Asymptotic SINR Analysis of Linear Detectors in Uplink Massive NTN MIMO Transmissions
papers.abstract: This paper examines the performance degradation of receivers caused by imperfect channel state information (CSI), arising from training-based and semi-blind channel estimation techniques. We focus on the uplink of massive multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) systems operating in time-division duplexing (TDD) mode, considering the asymptotic regime where the number of base station (BS) antennas grows large while the number of users remains fixed. Leveraging random matrix theory (RMT), we analyze the asymptotic behavior of the signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR) under linear MRC and MMSE detection schemes. We derive closed-form approximations of the achievable rates, prove their asymptotic tightness, and validate their accuracy through simulations for systems of finite dimensions. Numerical results under realistic non-terrestrial network (NTN) conditions further demonstrate that semi-blind channel estimation enables MRC and MMSE receivers to outperform their training-based counterparts, while also quantifying the number of pilot symbols required to achieve a desired SINR level.

authors.name: Abla Kammoun
authors.institution: King Abdullah University of Science and Technology

authors.name: Mohamed-Slim Alouini
authors.institution: King Abdullah University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Families of (Pluri)subharmonic Functions and Separate Subharmonicity
papers.abstract: We study the singular sets of pointwise bounded-above envelopes of families of functions. For families of subharmonic functions on open subsets of $\mathbb C$, of plurisubharmonic functions on open subsets of $\mathbb C^N$, and, more generally, of functions subharmonic in each complex variable separately, we prove that the singular set of a pointwise bounded-above envelope is relatively closed and nowhere dense. In contrast, for $N\ge3$ we construct a sequence of subharmonic functions on $\mathbb R^N$ whose upper envelope is finite everywhere but nowhere locally bounded above. We also characterize the singular sets that arise for admissible classes of functions, both with and without a continuity assumption, and give applications to separately subharmonic functions.

papers.title: Removability Criteria for Separately Harmonic and Subharmonic Functions
papers.abstract: Cegrell and Sadullaev showed that a separately harmonic and subharmonic function is subharmonic outside the product of two closed nowhere dense sets. We obtain sufficient conditions, expressed in terms of the second set, under which the function is subharmonic on the whole domain. In particular, we prove that this holds whenever the second set is polar.

papers.title: WaveFlow-UIE: A Single-Pipeline Wavelet-Domain Flow Model for Efficient Underwater Image Restoration
papers.abstract: Underwater image restoration remains challenging because color distortion, scattering, and detail loss affect low- and high-frequency image components differently. Recent diffusion-based methods have shown strong restoration quality, but often rely on multi-stage pipelines and costly iterative refinement. We present WaveFlow-UIE, a single-pipeline wavelet-domain flow model that directly learns to transform degraded underwater wavelet representations into clean ones. Our method applies a discrete wavelet transform, estimates lightweight physics-inspired degradation cues including transmission and ambient light, and conditions a velocity network trained with flow matching in wavelet space. The training objective combines flow-matching, frequency-weighted reconstruction, perceptual, color-consistency, and physics-consistency losses. Across UIEB, LSUI, UFO-120, and EUVP, WaveFlow-UIE achieves a strong quality-efficiency tradeoff, with especially competitive results on perceptual metrics. Relative to a strong wavelet-based diffusion baseline, the proposed model substantially reduces inference cost while maintaining or improving restoration quality on several paired benchmarks. We show that reducing the inference process from five flow steps to a single step preserves nearly all of the restoration quality while providing an additional speedup of about $4\times$ on UIEB at $256\times256$ resolution. This single-step result suggests that a single-pass wavelet-domain model is an effective alternative to heavier diffusion-style refinement.

authors.name: Muzammil Behzad
authors.institution: King Fahd University of Petroleum and Minerals

papers.title: A Reliability Study of Explainable AI for Freight Mode Classification
papers.abstract: Machine learning models are increasingly used to support freight transportation decisions, but their predictions are rarely accompanied by evidence that the associated explanations can be trusted. In this study we investigate explainable machine learning for classifying shipments as Air/Air Charter or Truck/Ocean using the PEPFAR Supply Chain Management System Delivery History dataset, with 5,964 shipment records and 47 input features after cleaning, where freight cost and pack price are excluded as near-proxies of the transportation mode. We compare three Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP) architectures, Logistic Regression, Random Forest, and gradient boosting with imbalance-aware metrics and paired significance tests across one hundred random replications. We then evaluate the explanations themselves, namely the stability of SHAP feature rankings across retraining and across models, the faithfulness of SHAP and LIME attributions under a feature-deletion test, and the geographic structure of the destination effects, which we map for all 38 destination countries. The results suggest that the tree ensembles significantly outperform the neural and linear models (86.8% against 83.3-85.0% mean testing accuracy) while their leading features remain the most stable across retraining. Removing the five features ranked most important by SHAP or LIME changes the predicted probabilities roughly four times as much as removing randomly chosen features. The destination effects form a coherent geographic pattern that simple port access does not explain. However, models with similar accuracy disagree substantially on which features matter most, and thus explanation stability and faithfulness should be assessed before such explanations are used to support freight transport decisions.

authors.name: Mansur M. Arief
authors.institution: King Fahd University of Petroleum and Minerals

papers.title: Optimal One Health control of antimicrobial resistance: a household mean-field model with community feedback and parameters from Burkina Faso
papers.abstract: We study how to combine three One Health interventions against antimicrobial resistance: prescription-only dispensing of antibiotics to people, access to veterinary care for animals, and treatment of household sludge and manure. Each household is a Markov chain on the carriage states of its people, animals and soil, and households are linked through the community, whose prevalence feeds the acquisition rates. We prove that, as the number of households grows, the distribution of household states converges to the solution of a nonlinear mean-field equation. This system is monotone for the stochastic order, so that no intervention increases carriage anywhere, and for every constant intervention it has exactly one equilibrium, which attracts all solutions and is given by a scalar equation. For the optimal control problem we prove existence, necessary conditions, positivity of all controls under a quadratic cost, uniqueness for short horizons, and a turnpike property under an explicit dissipativity condition, which we verify for our parameters by a computer-assisted numerical certification. With parameters from Tenkodogo, Burkina Faso, the optimal combined strategy averts about 17% of human carriage over three years in the baseline scenario, and 11% to 28% over the plausible scenarios for the parameters that the survey cannot identify; these figures are projections conditional on the model. The strategy itself is robust: the value of perfect information on the unmeasured parameters is about 2% of the achievable benefit. A compartmental model with the same transmission rates but without households underestimates the benefit, and targeting the interventions by zone of the town increases it.

authors.name: Pingawinde Sawadogo
authors.institution: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique et Technologique

papers.title: AraCrypto-ML: A Multi-Label Corpus of Communicative Functions in Arabic Facebook Cryptocurrency Discourse
papers.abstract: Arabic cryptocurrency discourse on social media is communicatively heterogeneous: a single post may report prices, explain protocols, promote investment, warn of scams, or invoke Islamic jurisprudence. Yet no annotated resource captures this functional diversity. We introduce AraCrypto-ML, a 10,000-post multi-label corpus of Arabic Facebook cryptocurrency discourse (2014-2024) from 2,898 public pages using a set of related keywords. Collected posts are annotated into six categories: Market Commentary, Educational, Promotional, Skeptical-Warning, Religious Framing, and Other/Unclear, using Fanar-2-27B under a prompt-only multi-label protocol. We validate 1,000 posts against adjudicated gold labels (macro kappa = 0.74) and apply Rogan-Gladen calibration to correct labelling bias. The two annotators agree with each other at macro kappa = 0.62 before adjudication, below the model's agreement with either of them (0.70 and 0.69). Reaction profiles differ strongly by function: Love is about 70% of reactions per post on Educational and Promotional posts but about 33% on Skeptical-Warning, which draws the largest Haha share (about 39%).

papers.title: Buffer-Gas-Assisted Fluorescence Spectroscopy of Molecular Ions
papers.abstract: Sustained fluorescence detection of generic molecules has been challenging due to the lack of cycling transitions and limited photon budgets. We demonstrate a nondestructive method for continuous fluorescence of strongly rovibronically open molecular ions, $^{232}$ThF$^+$. Effective quasi-cycling transitions are established by room-temperature buffer-gas collisions, which replenish the population back to the laser-addressed states. In situ images and rotationally resolved spectra are obtained without optical repumping or auxiliary atomic readout ions. Combined with low-background spectroscopic detection, this approach achieves a signal-to-noise ratio of approximately 6 in a 1 s exposure on the P(1) line of $^{232}$ThF$^+$, despite a thermal population of only approximately 0.17% in the addressed state at room temperature. The ability to repeatedly interrogate trapped ions is particularly promising for scarce molecular samples, broadband spectroscopic searches, and in situ monitoring of molecular reactions.

authors.name: Kenji Shu
authors.institution: RIKEN Center for Emergent Matter Science

authors.name: Xing Fan
authors.institution: Samarkand State University named after Sharof Rashidov

papers.title: Improved Single-Input Space Vector for DC-Biased Sinusoidal Current Control in Battery Cyclers
papers.abstract: This paper presents improvements to the single-input space vector (SISV) concept for current control in a battery cycler based on a two-phase interleaved buck converter. The cycler is controlled to output a dc-biased sinusoidal current, enabling investigation of second-harmonic ripple effects on lithium-ion cell aging. A modified SISV generation scheme is introduced to track current references containing both dc and sinusoidal components, and an impedance-angle compensation method is proposed to decouple the d and q control axes without disturbing dc tracking. A dq phase-portrait visualization method is also introduced to evaluate transient performance for both SISV and proportional-integral-resonant (PIR) control methods. Simulation and experimental results validate dc-biased sinusoidal current tracking using PIR control and SISV control with different decoupling schemes. The phase-portrait framework allows for straightforward evaluation of transient performance for both SISV and PIR control methods and supports controller tuning to obtain desired trajectories. The results demonstrate the feasibility of SISV-based current control as an alternative to PIR control for battery-cycler applications. The proposed improvements support the development of battery cyclers capable of controlling both dc and sinusoidal current components.

papers.title: A Master Identity for Forsyth-Glaisher-Type Series for $1/\pi$
papers.abstract: We derive a novel three-parameter master identity for Forsyth-Glaisher-type series for $1/\pi$. By unifying disparate results from the literature into a single overarching framework, we demonstrate that Glaisher's original series and numerous known variations emerge naturally as special cases through systematic choices of the parameters. This master identity simplifies the derivation of existing formulas, provides a mechanism for generating an infinite number of new series for $1/\pi$, and is further utilized to derive associated series involving harmonic and odd harmonic numbers.

papers.title: Multicontinuum Poroelasticity Model. Analysis and Computation
papers.abstract: In this work, we develop and analyze a macroscopic multicontinuum model for Biot poroelasticity. The full macroscopic multicontinuum system is derived by projecting the microscopic weak formulation onto continuum-dependent Galerkin spaces enriched with first-order multiscale corrections. This construction retains generalized pressure storage and coupling terms, with effective coefficients inherited from the microscopic bilinear forms. Under suitable coefficient assumptions, we establish well-posedness and energy stability of the macroscopic multicontinuum model. A fully discrete scheme combining the Galerkin finite element method in space with the backward Euler method in time is then developed. Its well-posedness and stability are proved, and a priori error estimates are derived using appropriate projection operators and energy arguments. Finally, numerical experiments for periodic and non-periodic high-contrast media demonstrate the accuracy of the multicontinuum model with respect to the averaged fine-scale solution.

authors.institution: Khalifa University of Science and Technology

authors.name: Dmitry Ammosov

authors.name: Jian Huang
authors.institution: Sichuan Academy of Medical Sciences & Sichuan Provincial People's Hospital

papers.title: Asymptotic stability of self-similar blow-up for the two-dimensional Zakharov system
papers.abstract: We prove asymptotic stability of the small-parameter Glangetas-Merle self-similar blow-up solutions of the two-dimensional Zakharov system under nonradial perturbations in the energy space. The proof establishes dissipation on the wave time scale by canceling the fast density coupling. We impose nonlinear orthogonality to the ground state of the density-dependent Schr\"odinger operator for modulation and use successive energy corrections after subtracting the instantaneous density response from the Schr\"odinger error. The resulting dissipation yields power-law decay of the rescaled errors in the Schr\"odinger gradient, weighted local mass, and wave energy norms.

authors.name: Jie Liu
authors.institution: Xi'an University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Estimates of short exponential sums with primes in major arcs
papers.abstract:
When solving a number of additive problems with almost equal summands, along with estimating short trigonometric sums with primes of the form $$ S_k(\alpha;x,y)=\sum_{x-y<n\le x}\Lambda(n)e(\alpha n^k), $$ on the minor arcs, estimates of these sums on the major arcs are also needed, except in a small neighborhood of their centers, as well as an asymptotic formula in a small neighborhood of the center of the major arcs.
  In this paper, using the second moment of Dirichlet $L$-functions on the critical line, for $S_k(\alpha;x,y)$ on the major arcs $\mathfrak{M}(\mathscr{L}^b)$, $\tau=y^5x^{-2}\mathscr{L}^{-b_1}$, $\mathscr{L} =\ln xq$, except in a small neighborhood of their centers $|\alpha-\frac{a}{q}|>\left(2\pi k^2x^{k-2}y^2\right)^{-1}$, for $y\ge x^{1-\frac{1}{2k-1+\eta_k}}\mathscr{L}^{c_k}$, $$ \eta_k=\frac{2}{4k-5+2\sqrt{(2k-2)(2k-3)}}, \qquad c_k=
  \frac{2A+22+\left(\frac{2\sqrt{2k-3}}{\sqrt{2k-2}}-1\right)b_1}{2\sqrt{(2k-2)(2k-3)}-(2k-3)}, $$ a nontrivial estimate of the form $$ S_k(\alpha;x,y)\ll y\mathscr{L}^{-A}, $$ is obtained, where $A$, $b_1$, $b$ are arbitrary fixed positive numbers, and an asymptotic formula is proved in a small neighborhood of the centers of the major arcs.

papers.title: Accelerating Distributed Variational Quantum Computing over Wireless Networks with Incentive Mechanism Design
papers.abstract: Distributed variational quantum computing (DVQC) appears as the emerging paradigm to address the limitations of near-term quantum devices by decomposing large parameterized quantum circuits (PQCs) into smaller subcircuits executed across multiple quantum processors. In this context, how to incentivize quantum processors to participate actively is crucial for accelerating DVQC, yet remains largely unexplored in the literature. To address this significant gap, we propose a novel two-stage incentive framework for wireless DVQC. In the first stage, we minimize processor-side energy cost via a joint optimization of subcircuit parameters, number of noise measurements, and transmit power, efficiently solved using block coordinate descent (BCD) and successive convex approximation (SCA). In the second stage, we maximize aggregator-side system utility by selecting an optimal subset of processors based on their optimized energy costs derived from the first stage, formulating a non-convex combinatorial selection problem addressed using the alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM). Extensive numerical experiments on the MNIST and CIFAR-10 datasets demonstrate that our DVQC framework achieves training and testing performance comparable to centralized quantum computing in terms of accuracy and loss, with similar convergence behavior on MNIST and slightly slower initial convergence on CIFAR-10. Moreover, our optimization approach consistently outperforms baseline schemes in energy efficiency and system utility, revealing a strong synergy between processor-level energy minimization and incentive-driven processor selection, where reduced energy costs directly enhances a processor's likelihood of selection and contributes to higher overall system utility.

papers.title: Quasi-Static Fault-Tolerant Feedback Control of a Quadrotor Carrying a Slung Payload under Rotor Failure
papers.abstract: This paper presents a nonlinear control law for a slung payload system (SPS) consisting of a quadrotor unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) carrying a slung payload. We propose a fault-tolerant control (FTC) design for the case of a complete single-rotor failure, i.e., only three functioning propellers. The failure is not modeled as a disturbance to be handled by estimation. Rather, we model the faulty SPS in control-affine form and design a quasi-static feedback law directly for the faulty dynamics. The controller achieves local exponential convergence of the payload position to a geometric path in space, rather than tracking a timed reference trajectory. Moreover, the transverse dynamics are exponentially stable, and the path-following manifold is rendered controlled invariant by feedback. Controlled invariance allows motion along the path to be prescribed independently through a tangential command while the state stays on the path-following manifold. The UAV body angular velocity remains bounded under bounded applied torque despite the failure. To validate the control design, numerical simulations apply the controller derived from the faulty SPS model in coordinates to the coordinate-free SPS model. Code and animations are available at https://gradslab.github.io/qs-sl/.

papers.title: Covering the Square Lattice and the Honeycomb with Non-Overlapping Unit Disks
papers.abstract: For $d>0$, let $\mathcal{S}_d$ be the square lattice and $\mathcal{H}_d$ the honeycomb point set with minimum distance $d$. We study for which $d$ these sets can be covered by closed unit disks with pairwise disjoint interiors; the periodic constructions of Phetmak, Nuntasombat and Fakcharoenphol cover them only from $d=1/2$ and $d=2/\sqrt{37}$ on, with gaps. Writing $\mathcal{N}(d)$ for the largest number of points in a closed unit disk and $\rho$ for the number of points per unit area, we show that neither set can be covered when $\mathcal{N}(d)<2\sqrt3\,\rho$, and we determine these spacings exactly, thirteen intervals for $\mathcal{S}_d$ and twelve for $\mathcal{H}_d$. At their right endpoints the bound is attained; there $\mathcal{S}_d$ is never coverable, and $\mathcal{H}_d$ is not coverable at nine of the twelve endpoints. We also give new periodic coverings, of $\mathcal{S}_d$ at $d=2/\sqrt{34}$ and of $\mathcal{H}_d$ for $2/9\le d\le1/\sqrt{19}$. Consequently, the smallest coverable spacing lies in $(0.2581,\,2/\sqrt{34}]$ for the square lattice and in $(0.1781,\,2/9]$ for the honeycomb point set, and coverability is not monotone in $d$ for either set.

papers.title: Sky Monitor AI: classifying night-sky conditions from an observatory all-sky camera with a CNN ensemble, label-free sky types and exact evidence maps
papers.abstract: Small and remotely operated observatories must decide every night whether the sky is clear enough to observe. We classify frames of the auxiliary all-sky camera of the Higashi-Hiroshima Observatory as clear or cloudy, using 8806 frames from 32 nights. A circular sky mask removes a printed date stamp that would act as a shortcut, and all evaluations use whole held-out nights. On six test nights, hand-crafted sky statistics reach 77.1% accuracy, a small CNN trained from scratch 84.3%, and a validation-selected ensemble of the small CNN and two ImageNet-pretrained ResNet-18 variants 86.7% (AUC 0.924) with the smallest night-to-night scatter. Moonlight is the dominant difficulty: across Moon altitude the ensemble's accuracy varies by 5 percentage points, the hand-crafted model's by 20. Fine-tuning deeper ResNet layers overfits with about 24 training nights, underlining the need to match model capacity to the number of independent nights. The labels were assigned in blocks of 1-2 h, and many remaining errors are mislabelled or partly cloudy frames. Without labels, clustering of pretrained CNN embeddings recovers the clear/cloudy split with 87% purity and isolates frames with water droplets on the camera dome. Gradient-based maps and a rim test indicate that the networks rely on sky regions. For networks ending in global average pooling, the decision decomposes exactly into local logits, giving gradient-free evidence maps and a cloud-cover estimate. We release Sky Monitor AI, an open-source application for single frames, whole nights and live cameras.

papers.title: Uniform Hyperbolicity of Automorphism Orbit Graphs in Rank Two
papers.abstract: We study automorphism orbit graphs of oriented conjugacy classes in the  free group of rank two, with every elementary Whitehead move assigned unit cost. Collapsing signed permutations of the basis turns each orbit component into a tree of edges and triangles. We obtain this description by combining the known rank-two conjugacy-class stabilizer structure with the Bass-Serre tree of the rank-two outer automorphism group. The simplified graph and all its vertex-induced subgraphs have optimal thin-triangle constant zero for tree components and 3/4 otherwise. Every whole orbit component of the original graph has thin-triangle constant at most 2, while every component of every vertex-induced subgraph has constant at most 5/2. Both bounds are sharp in the primitive orbit and apply to the full geometric realization, including edge-interior triangle corners. The hereditary upper estimate also follows from known chordality theory; the whole-component improvement uses the geometry of adjacent permutation fibres. These results complement earlier fixed-length and minimum-length orbit classifications.

authors.name: Bilal Khan
authors.institution: Kohat University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Parameter-Efficient Conciseness Adaptation: Differentiable Length Control for Concise Clinical Reasoning in Smaller Language Models
papers.abstract: Smaller language models (SLMs) make it feasible to deploy clinical natural language processing where large proprietary models are too costly, and parameter-efficient fine-tuning allows them to be specialised on commodity hardware. One obstacle persists after training: on medical tasks these models answer at far greater length than the clinical question requires. In clinical decision support and point-of-care use, where time is short, such verbosity is hard to act on even when the underlying reasoning is sound. Existing length-control methods depend on preference optimisation, reward models, or proprietary teachers that undercut the accessibility making SLMs attractive. We introduce Parameter-Efficient Conciseness Adaptation (PECA), which adds a single differentiable conciseness term to the QLoRA supervised fine-tuning objective. Because the token count is discrete and non-differentiable, PECA instead raises the end-of-sequence probability once generation exceeds a token budget, a smooth signal optimised during ordinary training, with no preference data, no auxiliary model, and a single commodity GPU. On a 1.7-billion-parameter model fine-tuned on the medical-o1-reasoning-SFT corpus, PECA reduces mean response length by 72.8% while improving multiple-choice diagnostic accuracy from 40.8% to 44.0%. A sweep over the conciseness strength traces an interpretable accuracy-to-length frontier for balancing brevity and diagnostic completeness.

authors.name: Sana Liaqat
authors.institution: Pakistan Institute of Engineering and Applied Sciences

papers.title: Beyond Word Error Rate: A Failure Taxonomy of Streaming Dictation ASR
papers.abstract: Speech recognition (ASR) systems are usually compared by word error rate (WER) on recorded files, after punctuation, capital letters and number format are removed. In dictation, the audio is streamed live and the text goes into the user's message as written, so what matters is which mistakes the user has to fix. The test set, streamed to eleven ASR systems, comprises 106 scripted English dictations from one speaker (read in a quiet room, with a fan on, and whispered), 20 clips in each of eleven other language and dialect sets, and 400 recordings that join clips in two languages. Every error was sorted by a fixed rule into four levels: recognition, output formatting, language handling and, for the self-hosted models, audio dropped before the model. Systems with similar WER failed in different ways. Zoom Scribe and OpenAI's GPT-Live-Transcribe have almost the same WER on quiet English (7.4% and 7.3%), but 34.7% and 8.8% on whispered English. Zoom and both AssemblyAI models left out 26-28% of whispered words, and still 21-26% with their end-of-turn detection relaxed or off; seven other systems left out at most 3%. Qwen3-ASR's 32% came from the speech detection in our own deployment (6% when relaxed). Across 107 EARS speakers, the same four systems lost 7-31% of whispered words, while six others lost under 2%. With only English selected, Gemini, Deepgram and our self-hosted Whisper lost the non-English part of a two-language recording in 86-99% of recordings, against 33-46% with both languages selected, while GPT-Live-Transcribe, OpenAI's realtime Whisper and Meta lost it in at most 20%. Running Whisper behind a Silero voice activity detector that drops audio judged to be silence raised whispered WER from 10.1% to 51.4%. Most English results come from one read speaker. The code, the recordings, both references and every transcript are released.

authors.name: Harras Mansoor
authors.institution: National University of Computer and Emerging Sciences

papers.title: Who (or what) are they prompting? How CS students conceptualize and use LLMs
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used by students in computing courses. Yet computing education research has not fully examined how teaching and inclusion of LLMs shape students' conceptualization and understanding of LLMs, and how these factors relate to their subsequent use. Although prior work has examined prompting strategies and AI literacy, the relationships among students' conceptualizations of LLMs, their understanding of LLM mechanisms, and their prompting behavior remain underexplored. We studied these relationships in a post CS1 course that introduces students to the various CS subfields. We adapted the course to teach and allow the usage of LLMs. We administered an end-of-course survey, using open-ended items to elicit students' representations of LLMs and their explanations of how LLMs work, alongside closed-response measures of prompting style and prompt count (N=283 students consented and provided codable responses). Using qualitative coding, we categorized students' understanding of how LLMs work into four ordinal knowledge levels based on the Structure of Observed Learning Outcomes (SOLO) taxonomy and coded their metaphoric conceptualizations along two dimensions: persona type and relational role. Our results show that students most often conceptualized LLMs as human assistants, and context-rich prompting was the preferred style. The study contributes a two-dimensional characterization of students' LLM metaphoric representation and exploratory analyses also identified associations among these constructs showing how understanding these systems relates to their usage.

authors.name: Sehrish Basir Nizamani
authors.institution: Mirpur University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Learning Nonlinear Transient Dynamics in Fluid Flow Networks with the Neural Basis Method
papers.abstract: Fluid flow networks, from pipeline infrastructure to biological vasculature, are governed by nonlinear edgewise hyperbolic laws coupled through continuity and conservation at junctions. Many-query tasks require rapid evaluation across unseen parametric settings, but conventional methods re-solve the system for each query at prohibitive cost. Existing physics-informed neural approaches impose the governing equations through penalty losses over generic neural approximators; these losses act only as optimization surrogates, with no guarantee that their reduction reduces solution error, and the resulting optimization is prone to ill-conditioning, particularly for hyperbolic systems. Building on the "representation-then-projection" principle of the neural basis method, we introduce a new approach for modeling fluid flow networks. Fixed neural bases define the representation space on each edge, while projection of the discretized equations determines the expansion coefficients, embedding edgewise laws into a conservative formulation. Edge subdomains are coupled through non-overlapping domain decomposition, and a neural operator learns, directly in this reduced space, the parametric map to the expansion coefficients. On looped and branching network topologies, we reproduce references with relative $L^2$ errors below 0.02%, whereas the physics-informed neural network baseline fails. Across unseen boundary conditions in both interpolation and extrapolation, we maintain mean pressure errors below 1% and mean flux errors below 3.3%, while the physics-informed DeepONet baseline reaches 8-18% pressure errors and 85-95% flux errors. These results highlight the framework's potential for real-time monitoring, design exploration, and uncertainty quantification of fluid flow networks.

authors.name: Aijaz Nazir
authors.institution: Sher-e-Kashmir University of Agricultural Sciences and Technology of Kashmir

authors.name: Yuhe Wang
authors.institution: China Academy of Chinese Medical Sciences

papers.title: Calibration and Conformal Prediction for Medical Question Answering in Arabic and English: Evidence from Two Non-Parallel Benchmarks
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly tested on medical exam questions, but accuracy alone does not show when an answer can be trusted. I study the calibration and uncertainty of two open-weight models, Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct and Jais-adapted-7B-chat (both run in 4-bit precision), on 2,816 English multiple-choice questions from MedMCQA and 4,927 Arabic multiple-choice questions from MedAraBench. Accuracy was 0.561 (English) and 0.430 (Arabic) for Qwen, and 0.369 and 0.308 for Jais. Raw option probabilities were overconfident in all four settings (expected calibration error 0.242 to 0.486), and a single temperature parameter removed 82% to 93% of that error. Split conformal prediction reached its nominal coverage in all 24 settings I tested (within 0.006), but the sets were large when accuracy was low: at 90% coverage, temperature-scaled sets contained on average 63% (Qwen, English), 78% (Qwen, Arabic), 86% (Jais, English) and 89% (Jais, Arabic) of the options. The margin between the top two option probabilities separated correct from incorrect answers best for Qwen on English (AUROC 0.734) and worst for Jais on Arabic (0.579). Answering only the 20% most confident questions lowered Qwen's English error from 0.439 to 0.098. Jais showed a strong prior for option C (49% of English and 60% of Arabic predictions). Scoring Latin letters only cut the Arabic share to 29% but left accuracy, raw ECE and AUROC nearly unchanged. Because the two benchmarks differ in subject, level and number of options, I do not attribute differences between languages to language itself. Code is available at https://github.com/Mariyaaleem/arabic-english-medqa-uncertainty.

authors.name: Mariya
authors.institution: Sher-e-Kashmir University of Agricultural Sciences and Technology of Kashmir

papers.title: Actor, Judge, or Teacher? Understanding Decision Models in Long-Horizon Agents
papers.abstract: Decision models answer a question with a typed output, such as a choice among options with a probability for each, so one model can choose an agent's actions, evaluate actions already taken, or score every action to teach a policy with reinforcement learning. Prior work has studied them mainly as actors, judging their usefulness by how well they act. We ask whether a decision model that acts poorly can still teach well. We compare three decision models and three general LLMs as actors and judges on ALFWorld, and use JEV as a teacher on ALFWorld and WebShop. As actors, all six models are pulled away from a subgoal that must come first by an easier one. As judges that see the whole trajectory, the same models credit the steps toward that subgoal, and asking whether each action helped, rather than whether the task will succeed, separates useful from useless actions. As a teacher, JEV raises a Qwen2.5-1.5B policy over GRPO from 72.8% to 82.9% success on ALFWorld and from 56.8% to 71.4% on WebShop. These results suggest that a poor actor can still teach well, because judging an action after the episode ends reveals the consequences that acting must anticipate. Code is available at https://github.com/ZJU-REAL/decision-agents.

authors.name: Haochen Liu
authors.institution: Nanjing University of Science and Technology

authors.name: Qianhao Zhu
authors.institution: Commonwealth Scientific and Industrial Research Organisation

authors.name: Weiming Lu
authors.institution: Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications

papers.title: ChJGBench: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Chinese Legal Judgment Generation with Diagnostic Evaluation
papers.abstract: With the rapid development of LLMs, increasing attention has been paid to whether they can reliably generate complete and legally valid judicial documents. This calls for a benchmark capable of evaluating whether models can accurately apply statutes and resolve outcome-critical issues, including claims, charges, penalties, and monetary obligations. However, existing benchmarks typically focus on isolated legal tasks or coarse-grained evaluation. We introduce ChJGBench, a benchmark for generating the reasoning and dispositive sections of Chinese judgments across civil, criminal, and administrative cases. Built from 3,462 real-world judgments, ChJGBench provides a case-type-aware diagnostic evaluation framework comprising 13 metric types and adopts a hybrid paradigm. Experiments reveal no uniform advantage for legal-domain models over general-purpose models, with model strengths varying across diagnostic dimensions. Performance is generally stronger on criminal cases, while civil and administrative cases continue to present substantial challenges.

papers.title: Tracing dependency networks explains how origins shape downstream vulnerability
papers.abstract: Many systems sustain outcomes through chains of prerequisites, yet these dependencies are often partially observed. We trace backward from sampled outcomes to recover dependency structure and measure edge importance by the fraction of outcomes lost after an edge fails. Across 1,620 synthetic networks, revealing 90% of origins required tracing 7.24% of outcomes on average. We define pair thickness as the number of origin and outcome pairs connected through an edge. Under strict dependency, where every input is necessary, thickness counts each affected outcome once per upstream origin, whereas loss counts it once. Edges therefore form origin groups with distinct thickness and loss relations, also seen in software, citation and river topologies. Within a network, greater origin diversity corresponds to lower strict loss at equal complete thickness. We develop a growth model that predicts how edges populate these groups and how losses are distributed under partial observation, tested on 2,560 independent networks. Separating origin counts from downstream reach improves identification of edges causing the greatest losses among unsampled outcomes in strict synthetic tests. Substitutable inputs reduce losses and change which importance scores perform best. Edge importance thus measures a dependency's contribution to sustaining later outcomes, guiding the protection of critical connections.

papers.title: GHAgentCI: A Dataset of Coding-Agent Invocations in CI Workflow Histories
papers.abstract: Coding agents are increasingly integrated into GitHub Actions to review pull requests, triage issues and modify code. Identifying these integrations is challenging because agentic workflows often resemble ordinary CI files, with evidence appearing in action references, shell commands and workflow conventions. We present GHAgentCI, a dataset of 15K+ workflow histories from 6K+ of 196K+ mined GitHub repositories, comprising 159K+ revisions and 205K+ agent-evidence records linked to workflow triggers and declared execution constraints. Our open-source extractor, cai-miner, detects agent-related evidence using an extensible catalogue. Manual validation of 576 stratified records confirmed 96.1% of dedicated-action matches and 98.8% of GitHub Agentic Workflow matches, with lower rates for other evidence kinds. Exploratory analyses reveal a shift toward command-line and GitHub Agentic Workflow integrations, differences in declared safeguards, and frequent removal of detected agentic workflows. GHAgentCI supports longitudinal studies of coding-agent integration into CI.

authors.name: John Businge
authors.institution: Mbarara University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Magellan PFS Discovery of a Cold Gas Giant Exoplanet Likely Formed by a Gas Disk Gravitational Instability
papers.abstract: Using the Planet Finder Spectrograph (PFS) on the 6.5-m Magellan Clay Telescope at the Las Campanas Observatory we have discovered a cold gas giant exoplanet orbiting the K7V dwarf star HIP88962. 16 yrs of PFS observations imply an exoplanet with an orbital period of $\approx$ 19.3 yrs and a radial velocity semiamplitude (K) of 94.9 m s$^{-1}$. With a host star mass of 0.62 $M_\odot$, this implies a planet mass $M_p sin(i) \sim 5 M_{Jup}$. While stable M dwarfs have a PFS RMS of $\approx$ 3 m s$^{-1}$, the single Keplerian fit for HIP88962 has an RMS of $\approx$ 6 m s$^{-1}$, hinting at a second exoplanet. The best double planet Keplerian fit, with a 4.113 d period, still results in a RMS of $\approx$ 5 m s$^{-1}$. HIP88962 has Ca II H lines with twice the emission of four stable stars, implying that stellar activity may contribute to the RMS jitter error for the single Keplerian fit. When combined with Hipparcos and Gaia astrometry, HIP88962 b has a nearly edge-on orbit with inclination 91 $\pm$ 22 deg, true planet mass $4.83$ M$_{Jup}$, semimajor axis 6.15 $\pm$ 0.5 au, and eccentricity 0.718 $\pm$ 0.02. Including a PFS jitter of $\approx$ 7 m s$^{-1}$ yields $\chi^2 = 0.995$ for the combined solution. A massive gas giant orbiting at $\approx$ 6 au around a 0.62 $M_\odot$ star is incompatible with published core accretion population synthesis models, but consistent with formation by gas disk gravitational instability.

authors.name: Jiayin Li
authors.institution: Shaanxi University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Dynamic Block-Online Streaming ASR for Low-Resource Agglutinative Code-Switching Speech with Morphology-Aware Evaluation
papers.abstract: Low-resource, agglutinative languages challenge low-latency ASR, as fixed lookahead windows fail when grapheme order diverges, suffixes cross code-switch boundaries, or code-switching data is imbalanced. We present the first comprehensive study of streaming ASR for intra-sentential Bangla-English code-switching, identifying a mismatch between strict causal streaming and long-range morphological dependencies. We introduce a Dynamic Block-Online framework with VAD-aligned inference that balances semantics, latency, and context, enabling global bidirectional attention to preserve morphological integrity. To mitigate data scarcity, we propose Script-Anchored Loanword Injection, augmenting training text with English loanwords to model phonotactic transitions. We introduce CS-WER to diagnose switch, root, and suffix errors, and show that flexible latency budgets enhance recognition of agglutinative and mixed-language speech, with successful transfer to menstrual-medical domains.

authors.name: Md. Romzan Ali
authors.institution: Jashore University of Science and Technology

papers.title: AVA: Agentic Variant Adjudication for Automated, Auditable Read-Level Review in Cancer Diagnostic Sequencing
papers.abstract: Identifying a tumor's DNA mutations is central to cancer diagnosis and treatment, but distinguishing genuine mutations from sequencing artifacts is error-prone. In practice, genuine mutations are identified using fixed variant-allele-frequency (VAF) and depth thresholds which cannot separate artifacts from genuine mutations in the borderline low-VAF zone where they overlap. A laboratory specialist must manually inspect the read-level sequencing data, a slow step that has high inter-rater variability and causes diagnosis delays. We present AVA: Agentic Variant Adjudication; an agentic framework that automates this read-level inspection with subagents that reason over evidence, generate investigative code, and return a real-or-artifact adjudications with an auditable reasoning trace all without training on existing data. On both the SEQC2 DNA-seq benchmark and patient RNA-seq data, restricted to a subsample of borderline variants where thresholds fail, both closed-source (Claude Sonnet 5) and open-weight (GLM 5.3 Flash and Gemma 4 31b) agents outperform the best achievable VAF/depth thresholds. Ultimately, AVA is suited for privacy-constrained clinical deployment, since the framework can run on locally deployed open-weight models with descriptive reasoning traces to keep specialists in the loop.

authors.name: Siddharth Arya
authors.institution: Pandit Bhagwat Dayal Sharma University of Health Sciences

papers.title: An $O(L^3)$ Spherical Harmonic Transform on $L^2$ Samples
papers.abstract: For the representation of signals on the sphere band-limited at $L$ using the optimal number of samples, $L^2$, equal to the number of degrees of freedom in harmonic space and placed on $L$ iso-latitude rings, we develop a spherical harmonic transform (SHT) that is theoretically exact, requires no solution of linear systems and no precomputation beyond the placement of the rings, and has complexity $O(L^3)$. The transform rests on the observation that, for each order $m$, the samples on the rings that resolve order $m$ are a complete set of samples for the order-$m$ profile of the signal, so that its values on the remaining rings follow from a closed-form Lagrange basis, the sampling functions of order $m$. We prove that the proposed optimal-dimensionality SHT (OSHT) recovers every band-limited signal exactly in exact arithmetic, so that the $L^2$ samples admit a sampling theorem in the collocation sense. For the final harmonic analysis we give two exact back-ends: Gauss-Legendre quadrature of the interpolated profiles and the algorithm of the equiangular sampling theorem, which applies without change because the rings coincide with its grid. We identify the amplification constant that governs numerical error, show that it replaces the condition number used previously for the placement of rings, propose a placement that minimizes it, and give an error propagation model that explains the growth of error with the band-limit. A multi-pass refinement converges in two passes to the rounding floor of the samples. We also describe a stable log-domain evaluation of the sampling functions, a rescaled Legendre recurrence, and a forbidden-region skipping rule that halves the cost of the elimination. Numerical experiments up to $L=2048$ characterize the accuracy, measured by the maximum and mean coefficient errors and the signal-to-noise ratio, the stability and the computation time.

papers.title: Mind the Accuracy-Approval Gap: How Users Evaluate Sycophantic AI in Everyday Tasks
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) often exhibit sycophancy, a tendency to agree with users, flatter or affirm them, and preserve their face, even when independent judgment or critical feedback would be more useful. Prior work has largely evaluated sycophancy through benchmark evaluations, but less is known about how users perceive and respond to sycophantic AI in everyday tasks. We combine benchmark evaluations with two large-scale user studies. We study four personas defined through system prompts: objective (instructed to prioritize accuracy over agreement), soft-sycophantic, hard-sycophantic, and baseline (no persona-specific system prompt). Benchmarks show that even baseline exhibits substantial sycophancy, agreeing with users' stated views 71.7% of the time on NLP Survey, compared with 54.8% for objective and 89.5% for hard-sycophantic. Under conversational pressure on TruthfulQA, accuracy ranged from 81.9% for objective to 59.6% for baseline and 8.7% for hard-sycophantic. Participants were assigned to one of the four personas, and either discussed contested policy topics or collaborated with AI on email writing. Despite its higher accuracy under pressure, objective AI was rated significantly less respectful and satisfying than the other personas, and less trustworthy than baseline. Baseline and sycophantic personas did not differ significantly. Persona did not significantly affect how often participants changed their opinions, although participants who discussed with objective AI had greater odds of reduced confidence. Objective AI prompted greater writing expansion than soft-sycophantic AI, but final writing quality did not differ significantly across personas. These findings highlight a tension between accuracy and user approval: personas with substantially lower accuracy under conversational pressure received more favorable ratings for respect and satisfaction than objective AI.

papers.title: Stability of Hilbert--Samuel functions with linear bounds in homological degree
papers.abstract: Let $(R,\mathfrak{m})$ be a Noetherian local ring and let $I$ be generated by a filter regular sequence. Set $A=R/I$, $s=\dim A>0$, and $D= \operatorname{hdeg}(A)$. If $A$ is equicharacteristic, we prove that perturbations of order $(2s+1)D$ preserve the Hilbert--Samuel function in every dimension. In arbitrary characteristic, we obtain the order $[s+(s+1)(k!)^{k-1}]D^k$, where $k$ is the maximum of $1$ and the dimensions of the lower deficiency modules of $\widehat A$. Both bounds depend only on the final quotient. The proof constructs monic annihilating equations for the deficiency modules and uses them to choose a parameter $d$-sequence with an explicit relation to a reduction of the maximal ideal. In the equicharacteristic case, a dimension filtration and characteristic polynomials over regular subrings give equations of degree at most the arithmetic degree, with coefficients in the required powers of the reduction.
