authors.institution: Harbin University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Certified Dynamic Subspace Optimization for Bayesian ISAC Design
papers.abstract: Full-space covariance optimization is costly in large-array Bayesian integrated sensing and communication (ISAC). A fixed transmit subspace can reduce this cost, but the resulting optimality loss depends on the posterior distribution. In this paper, a certified dynamic subspace method is developed for angle Bayesian Cram\'er-Rao bound (BCRB) minimization under joint angle and complex-gain uncertainty. For uniform linear arrays, exact response preservation over a nondegenerate posterior angular interval requires the full antenna space. Subspace sufficiency is therefore assessed through full-space objective-gap bounds. A communication-feasible basis is initialized from the user-channel span and local BCRB sensitivity. Restricted semidefinite programs are then solved. Primal restoration and dual repair yield gap bounds that remain valid after lossless user-beam recovery. When an accurate restricted solve does not certify the requested tolerance, the basis is expanded using a direction identified from the covariance dual slacks. Under a strict communication-power margin, joint uniqueness of the restricted optimal dual multipliers is established. With exact restricted solves, this uniqueness guarantees strict BCRB improvement after certificate-driven expansion. Numerical results validate the bounds against full-space references for the sampled problems. Compared with a fixed Fisher ordering, the proposed method can reach the same certificate target with fewer dimensions. On large arrays, total runtime is reduced relative to the full-space and factorized baselines at matched certificate targets.

authors.name: Qingjiang Shi
authors.institution: Henan University of Science and Technology

papers.title: XBot-Omni: An Omni-Modal Model for Embodied Understanding and Interaction
papers.abstract: Embodied interaction requires an agent to integrate multimodal perception with verbal and nonverbal behaviors to effectively communicate its intentions, including speech, body motion, and facial expressions. We present XBot-Omni, a Thinker--Talker--Actor architecture that extends the Omni paradigm to robotic modalities, including body motion and facial expressions, with ``X'' representing the extensibility to robotic-specific modalities. The Thinker processes text, images, audio, and video to formulate contextually appropriate responses, which are then realized by the Talker and Actor through speech and coordinated bodily expressions, respectively. In this report, we innovatively introduce the concept of ``Actor'' as a dedicated component for embodied agents: a coordinated, streaming module that leverages the native representations of the Thinker and Talker within an end-to-end pipeline, introducing only modest latency overhead. This unified architecture enables multimodal generation conditioned on omni-modal inputs directly to prevent information loss in staged designs. We comprehensively evaluate XBot-Omni across seven benchmarks, demonstrating strong multimodal understanding capabilities on both general-domain and robot-centric videos, as well as high-quality, natural, and well-coordinated motion generation. Furthermore, our results validate its capability to generate embodied multimodal responses directly from omni inputs, meeting the diverse requirements of embodied interaction. XBot-Omni enables robots not only to perceive the omni world but also to express themselves through speech and bodily behaviors, extending Omni models from conversational interaction to embodied communication in physical environments.

authors.name: Jiaxin Huang
authors.institution: Chongqing University of Posts and Telecommunications

papers.title: Understanding the Asymptotic Transience of Q-Learning via Distributional Expansion
papers.abstract: Q-learning has been empirically observed to exhibit substantial transient error. This transient remains uncaptured by the leading Gaussian limit because the central-limit normalization removes the smaller-scale displacement generated by the initial nonlinear evolution. On the other hand, worst-case finite-sample guarantees, while accounting for transient effects, can obscure the mechanisms responsible for the error on a particular problem instance. We develop a finer asymptotic analysis that gives an asymptotically exact characterization of this transient for a fixed instance. Specifically, for synchronous Q-learning in finite discounted Markov decision processes, we separate the last-iterate error into an optimal-policy temporal-difference (TD) component and a nonnegative displacement caused by maximization. The centered TD component has Gaussian fluctuations at scale $n^{-1/2}$, whereas the maximization transient is of order $n^{-1}$ and converges almost surely, after rescaling by $n$, to a random limit. This limit represents the propagated effect of maximization errors generated before the greedy policy stabilizes. We combine this characterization with an Edgeworth expansion of the TD component to identify the corrections to its Gaussian approximation, separating the effects of initialization, non-Gaussian TD fluctuations, and maximization. The results reveal how transient errors arise for individual Q-learning instances and how their effects persist below the central-limit scale.

papers.title: Fast Inference-Time Policy Refinement via Action-Affine World Models
papers.abstract: Imitation policies can perform complex manipulation, yet small execution errors can accumulate and cause failure. Refinement can correct these errors, but existing approaches often require additional on-policy learning or costly online planning. Our key insight is that a pretrained policy already supplies a useful nominal behavior: refinement can focus on predicting how small action corrections change its outcome. We therefore learn this local response in a form that is cheap to optimize. Our \textit{action-affine world model} (A\textsuperscript{2}WM) learns local action sensitivities offline from action-perturbed policy rollouts. Given interaction history and a policy proposal, it predicts task-relevant geometry as a nominal trajectory plus a linear response to corrections. It predicts the full planning horizon directly, avoiding the propagation of intermediate errors through recursive model evaluations. Quadratic penalties on predicted task errors and linear correction constraints then yield a cheap convex quadratic program (QP). Online refinement requires one model evaluation and one QP solve, while both policy and model weights remain frozen. Across four simulated manipulation tasks, our framework achieves the highest success rate among evaluated baselines, adding only 3.8 ms of mean refinement overhead per control step, excluding base-policy sampling.

papers.title: Non-normal Limits and Joint Calibration of Cross-fitted Heterogeneity Tests
papers.abstract: Cross-fitting is used to test whether a ranking learned in a randomized experiment separates units that benefit from treatment from those that do not: each fold is ranked by a model fitted to the other folds, and the standardized difference in estimated effects between units ranked high and low is compared with a normal distribution. Under the null hypothesis of no heterogeneity the ranking is determined by noise, and because each fold helps to rank the others the fold estimates are dependent. We show that this dependence changes the shape of the null distribution, not just its variance. For least squares on one covariate the limit is bimodal for two folds and skewed for many, no variance correction restores the level, and the model is a counterexample to a published central limit theorem. With many covariates the limit approaches normality, but its variance stays inflated. Removing the non-normal component of the statistic removes its power, so we keep the statistic and change its reference distribution: joint calibration simulates together the moments that choose the rankings and those that evaluate them and applies the same selection to the draws; it has asymptotically exact level and requires no refitting. Applications to clinical and marketing trials, together with random treatment reassignments on their covariates, demonstrate that the standard test substantially inflates Type I error and can produce spurious rejections that joint calibration avoids.

papers.title: eDMD: Endpoint Distribution Matching for Few-Step Diffusion Distillation
papers.abstract: Distribution matching distillation (DMD) has emerged as a leading paradigm for distilling diffusion models into few-step students, where an auxiliary fake score model tracks the student's distribution and the discrepancy between the teacher and fake predictions drives the student toward the teacher. In multi-step distillation, although only the student's final output is delivered, existing methods train the fake model on intermediate states or across all denoising steps. Consequently, the student's update signal becomes entangled with intermediate distributions, which can distort the matching direction and remain nonzero even after the student's final outputs already match the teacher distribution. To resolve this mismatch, we propose Endpoint Distribution Matching Distillation (eDMD), which trains a single shared fake model exclusively on the student's final outputs and uses it to correct every denoising step. Our theoretical analysis proves that this endpoint reference guarantees that the distribution matching term vanishes if and only if the student's final output distribution matches the teacher's, regardless of intermediate distributions. Beyond the fake reference, we further strengthen teacher supervision through a precise teacher (PT) that replaces single-step guided predictions with short multi-step trajectories on the final noise interval, paired with a calibrated query density for intermediate steps. Experiments on SD3-Medium, FLUX.2-klein (4B and 9B), and Qwen-Image-2.1 demonstrate that eDMD consistently outperforms existing distribution matching methods for 4-step generation.

papers.title: Three-ends Furstenberg estimates and approximate rectangles
papers.abstract: We prove a three-ends incidence estimate whose multiplicity exponent is sharp for one-dimensional Katz-Tao point sets.} At the heart of the argument lies rectangular non-concentration and its incidence theory introduced earlier by the authors. As an application, we obtain a strong quantitative bound on the number of approximate rectangles with the vertices belonging to four separated camps, each retaining a non-concentration condition.

papers.title: Improving Airflow Network Models of Natural Ventilation: Geometry-Specific Pressures and Fluctuation Corrections
papers.abstract: Building energy models typically predict natural ventilation rates using airflow networks, which solve a system of orifice equations with exterior pressures as boundary conditions. This study investigates two improvements to these models: (i) geometry-specific exterior pressures obtained from large eddy simulations (LESs) and (ii) analytical corrections accounting for the nonlinear effects of pressure fluctuations on mean ventilation rates. We evaluate these improvements against coupled interior-exterior LESs of flows through 5824 windows, 2688 skylights, and 2752 interiors across idealized urban canopies. Replacing standard ASHRAE pressure coefficients with pressures from exterior-only LESs reduces the RMSE of predicted ventilation rates by approximately 50%, largely by capturing urban canopy flow effects that are poorly represented by standard shelter factors. Independently of the pressure source, mean-pressure airflow network predictions exhibit a nonlinear relationship with the LES ventilation rates. To address this discrepancy, we derive fluctuation corrections for mean-dominated and fluctuation-dominated flow regimes. These corrections eliminate the systematic nonlinearity and further reduce RMSE by 10-40% for most opening types and ventilation configurations. For windows, the combined improvements from geometry-specific surface pressures and fluctuation corrections increase the coefficient of determination $R^2$ from approximately 0.4 to 0.9. The results demonstrate the potential to accurately predict natural ventilation rates across different interior layouts while accounting for urban canopy effects and pressure fluctuations, using exterior-only LES pressure information.

papers.title: A Three-Stage Unsupervised Online Physics-Informed Neural Network for Microgrid Optimal Power Flow
papers.abstract: Optimal allocation of generators is a key challenge in power systems to achieve economical dispatch while satisfying operational constraints. Conventional optimization techniques can be computationally expensive, limiting their applicability in real-time environments, and neural networks often require offline retraining under new operating conditions. This paper proposes a three-stage unsupervised online physics-informed neural network (PINN) framework for optimal power flow (OPF). Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed framework satisfies load demand and system constraints while achieving a $43,665 lower operating cost than fmincon-based optimization under the same operating conditions. The training process analysis further demonstrate the framework's ability to adapt its parameters online to variations in load demand and renewable generation in real time.

papers.title: Symplectic capacities of 4-dimensional monotone toric domains
papers.abstract: We compute the cylindrical contact homology chain complex associated with a monotone toric domain in $\mathbb{R}^4$. The chain complexes allow us to compute the cylindrical contact homology capacities associated with monotone toric domains with one or two inflection points. These capacities are conjecturally equal to the Gutt-Hutchings capacities defined using $S^1$-equivariant symplectic homology. Using our results, we find embedding obstructions between toric domains.

papers.title: KernelMutate: Mutation-Guided Validation of Generated GPU Kernels
papers.abstract: Generated GPU implementations are commonly accepted after a few differential tests, although replacement obligations may remain unchecked. We present KernelMutate, an empirical study of validation reliability using controlled faults, released implementations, and replacement tests. A five-draw anchor accepts 548 of 838 CUDA candidates. The full suite finds native FP32 witnesses for 136 accepted candidates and dtype-only findings for another 362, mostly low-precision execution limitations without established publisher guarantees. Source-guided testing identifies the full suite's 692 candidates at 26.1% lower charged cost, but yields only dtype evidence for 16 accepted candidates with native witnesses in the full suite. Independently observed context and boundary findings cover the same candidate set. Task-held-out template matching reveals differences in ranking and observation coverage: global top-eight recommendations match more probes than class-conditioned lists (51 versus 48 of 75), while conditional analyses restrict the apparent advantage at smaller limits. These template-matching results are offline measurements, not deployed-suite gains. Independent controls and replacement cases expose numerical-policy, binding, and custom-execution boundaries. Validation therefore needs to report witness domains and observation coverage alongside candidate yield and cost.

papers.title: KernelAudit: Contract-Aware Auditing of Validators for LLM-Generated GPU Kernels
papers.abstract:
The effectiveness of generating GPU kernels driven by a large language model (LLM) is highly dependent on the quality of the used validator (used to accept or reject a generated kernel candidate against the contracts of the given kernel-generation task), whose results inform reward assignment, candidate selection, and speedup claims during kernel generation. However, an existing validator suffers from various limitations, e.g., wrongly accepting a candidate due to missing its forbidden library use or wrongly rejecting a candidate due to determining its permitted library use as forbidden (constraints on library uses are stated in the task contracts).
  To assess the quality of a validator against the given task contracts, we propose an independent-audit approach for the validator by (1) construction of audit oracle: labeling a candidate as PASS or FAIL based on three separate dimensions in our proposed contract model (i.e., semantic correctness, implementation integrity, and measurement integrity) and (2) auditing of the validator against the audit oracle: comparing the labels of the candidate against the validation results produced by the validator. For semantic correctness, reference-calibrated stress tests check output correctness on valid inputs for a candidate. For implementation integrity, reference and candidate execution traces are used to determine specific library uses. For measurement integrity, timing checks assess whether the reported runtime reflects the full time needed to complete the candidate's computation. We apply our approach to assess the quality of six validators and 716 candidates from seven corpora, including constructed controls. The evaluation results show that our approach helps assess the existing six validators to have nontrivial false-reject rates. There is high-degree agreement between the candidate labels produced by our audit oracle and human judgments.

papers.title: AIFR: Adaptive Identity Feature Recovery for Diffusion-Based Makeup and Anime Portraits
papers.abstract: Diffusion-based makeup and anime portraits are increasingly popular in online content creation (e.g., virtual makeup editing and anime avatar generation), but their altered appearances can hinder face recognition (FR) in identity-based content screening. Existing methods mainly adapt FR encoders or restore input images. The former require costly gallery re-encoding, while the latter may be incomplete or distort identity-related facial details. To address these limitations, we aim to correct identity features within a frozen FR model to recover its output embeddings in its original space. Appearance changes vary in strength and affect facial regions differently. To this end, we propose Adaptive Identity Feature Recovery (AIFR), a framework that inserts a lightweight recovery module at a single intermediate layer to predict sample-level correction strength and spatially adaptive residual updates. Module training uses fused identity targets to guide embedding recovery in the original FR space and an identity-shift score to regulate correction strength and limit unnecessary changes. At inference, AIFR processes a single portrait in one forward pass without reference images, producing recovered embeddings that can be directly matched with existing gallery templates without re-encoding. With only 1.22M trainable parameters, AIFR improves the average TAR at FAR=$10^{-4}$ from 66.1\% to 90.2\% over the original ArcFace, and further experiments show improvements across unseen makeup styles, stylization strengths, and generators. Beyond recognition, the recovered embeddings can directly condition a pretrained Arc2Face model to generate faces with improved identity preservation, showing compatibility with embedding-conditioned downstream generation.

papers.title: SwarmSafe-Delta: Isolating Message Effects on LLM Agent Safety
papers.abstract:
When a tool-using LLM agent team violates policy, aggregate outcomes do not reveal whether an upstream message changed the executor's action. We introduce SwarmSafe-Delta, a paired executable protocol that freezes upstream computation, varies real, hidden, and format-matched placebo delivery, and scores a single committed action against deterministic benign and risky policy states under preassigned budgets.
  Across four models and constructed optional tasks, real delivery at $N=4$ produces 21.4% risky-world violations, versus 5.0% with placebo and 1.0% with hidden delivery (paired differences +16.4 and +20.3 percentage points). Real delivery also improves benign task success, illustrating that suppressing communication sacrifices utility. In a second regime constructed to require an upstream lookup route, real delivery improves safe completion by 74.2 points relative to hidden delivery. These effects quantify message-delivery contrasts under specified information dependencies, not naturally occurring failure rates.
  Exploratory action-level analyses show that the effect depends strongly on whether the upstream message recommends a prerequisite check or direct execution; model differences also largely track these message compositions. The contribution is a controlled, execution-grounded measurement protocol rather than a general claim that agent communication is harmful or protective.

papers.title: Autonomous Mobile Robots on a Computing Field
papers.abstract: We introduce CABOT, a computational model for autonomous mobile robots in which the discrete plane the robots operate on is not a passive stage but an active computing medium. In the classical Look-Compute-Move (LCM) model every increase in computational capability is obtained by strengthening the robots themselves, with lights, memory or wider visibility, at a cost paid once per robot. CABOT strengthens the environment instead: each cell of the grid holds a state from a finite set Q, the states evolve synchronously under a uniform local rule that also senses whether a robot stands on the cell, that is, the floor is a cellular automaton, and the Look operation returns the states of the visible cells in addition to the positions of the visible robots. The robots are as weak as we can make them: oblivious, silent, lightless, myopic with visibility range 1, without multiplicity detection and unable to write to the floor. The number of field states |Q|, rather than any robot capability, becomes the measure of the resources required. On an inert floor (|Q| = 1) such robots can neither form a line, nor gather from scattered positions, nor explore a grid. We show that a handful of states changes this. Line Formation from connected configurations is solvable with four states, and field-silently, so that the floor also reaches a fixed point, with five. Gathering from arbitrary, possibly disconnected, configurations is solvable with three states and Line Formation from arbitrary configurations with six; we prove that neither can be solved field-silently with any number of states. A single robot explores every finite grid forever with four states and every torus with two, which is optimal. Further rule sets, validated by simulation only, equalize the spacing of robots on a row, fill a pattern painted on the floor and guide robots through a maze, and indicate the range of the model.

papers.title: Ramsey numbers of loose triangles versus cliques
papers.abstract:
An $r$-uniform loose triangle $C_3$ consists of three edges that intersect pairwise in exactly one vertex and have no vertex common to all three. For graphs, this is the usual triangle, and the Ramsey number $R(C_3,K_t)$ has order of magnitude $t^2/\log t$ by celebrated results of Ajtai, Koml\'os, and Szemer\'edi and of Kim.
  Kostochka, Mubayi, and Verstra\"ete proved that $R(C_3,K_t^{(r)})=O_r(t^{3/2})$ for every fixed $r\ge3$ and showed that this bound is sharp up to a logarithmic factor. Motivated by the logarithmic saving in the graph case, they conjectured in 2013 that the upper bound could be improved to $o(t^{3/2})$.This conjecture has since received significant attention and has been reiterated in several papers. We prove the conjecture by showing that, for every fixed $r\ge3$, \[
  R(C_3,K_t^{(r)})
  =O_r\left(\frac{t^{3/2}}{\sqrt{\log\log t}}\right). \]

papers.title: Partition of Unity Data-driven Finite Element Method for Anisotropic Diffusion in Magnetized Plasmas
papers.abstract: Numerical simulation of transport processes in magnetized plasmas is characterized by extreme anisotropy, where diffusion along magnetic field lines can be many orders of magnitude larger than in the perpendicular direction. This anisotropy leads to thin, steep boundary layers and numerical pollution that standard finite element methods struggle to resolve without prohibitive mesh refinement. In this paper, we introduce the Partition of Unity Data-Driven Finite Element Method (PU-DDFEM), a data-driven local model reduction approach, for anisotropic diffusion. The method utilizes a bottom-up construction to enable a complete offline-online splitting. We parametrize the local magnetic field and boundary conditions to generate a snapshot space that captures the essential physics of plasma confinement. Dominant modes are extracted via a local spectral problem to identify representative features. These modes are then mapped to the global domain using a partition of unity to form a conforming approximation space. This ensures that the basis functions are fully reusable across different global magnetic configurations, significantly reducing the online computational overhead for large-scale plasma simulations.

papers.title: Scalable Conversational Assessment: Chat-Based Exams with a Two-Agent LLM Pipeline
papers.abstract: Oral exams are compelling because (1) students can be asked to provide their reasoning for an answer and (2) their interactive nature permits follow-up questions to resolve ambiguous answers. But oral exams scale poorly. In this paper, we present scalable conversational assessment, an LLM-based system that conducts interactive text-based conversations with students to assess their ability to make and support an argument. We use a two-agent architecture to separate concerns and reduce the likelihood that answers are leaked to the student: the interviewer interacts directly with the student, but only receives guidance about the next question to ask the student; the hidden evaluator knows the goals of the whole activity, tracks the student's progress using a rubric, and guides the interviewer on when to follow-up on the current question or proceed to the next question. The system was first tested using a collection of simulated students with LLM personas of a particular ability level or adversarial tactic (e.g., answer-extractors, prompt-injectors, confident fabricators). A novel element of this evaluation was that it required the use of a fictional assessment topic to prevent personas that shouldn't have information from using knowledge present in the LLM's pre-training. The system was also deployed in a small, elective AI literacy course in both formative and summative contexts. Through manual and post-facto AI review of the transcripts we identified opportunities to improve the follow-up question generation and ensure that grading only credited ideas that the student (and not the interviewer) contributed.

papers.title: Mean-field Fluctuations for First-Passage Percolation with Symmetric Kernels
papers.abstract: We study first-passage percolation on finite weighted graphs whose normalized Weibull edge hazards form a symmetric Markov kernel on $N$ vertices. We prove that a uniform absolute spectral gap and an $O(N^{-1})$ bound on a fixed even-step return probability imply the stochastic mean-field passage-time limit and an independent Gaussian hopcount limit. Jointly with these quantities, the entire geodesic from an arbitrary source to an independent uniform target is approximated in total variation by an independent Markov chain stopped at the hopcount. This comparison yields laws of large numbers for fixed-length path segments and joint central limit theorems for bounded additive observables. The results extend to edge laws with a uniform relative hazard error $o(1/\log N)$, including common noise distributions with a power-law hazard and a positive-power error near zero. Applications include integrable singular torus kernels, macroscopic spread-out graphs, non-transitive regular graphs, finite groups, and discretizations of symmetric continuum kernels.

papers.title: Golod thresholds of ideals and products of ideals in dimension 3
papers.abstract: Let $I$ be a proper ideal in a standard graded polynomial ring $P$ with homogeneous maximal ideal $\m$. We show that there exists $k_0\in \mathbb{N}$ such that $\m^kI$ is Golod for all $k\geq k_0$. The smallest such $k_0$ is denoted $\mathrm{gt}_{\m}(I)$. We give an explicit formula for $\mathrm{gt}_{\m}(I)$ in the case when $I$ is a monomial complete intersection and bounds for $\mathrm{gt}_{\m}(I)$ for other classes of ideals. We show that under a certain degree condition, the product of a Golod ideal with a maximal homogeneous ideal is Golod. In the last section, we show that in a regular local ring of dimension 3, the product of any two proper ideals is Golod; this solves a question posed by Dao-Stefani \cite[Question 4.5]{dao2022monomial} and VandeBogert \cite[Question 4.11]{vandebogert2022products}.

papers.title: CF-UAMG: A Coarse/Fine Splitting-Based Parallel Unsmoothed Aggregation Algebraic Multigrid Method
papers.abstract: In this paper, we propose a coarse/fine splitting-based parallel unsmoothed aggregation algebraic multigrid (AMG) method, referred to as CF-UAMG. The proposed method utilizes the strong-connection structure identified by classical AMG (C-AMG) coarse/fine splitting to guide the selection of aggregate roots and the formation of aggregates, aiming to improve the quality of the aggregation-based coarse space and thus the convergence of unsmoothed aggregation AMG (UA-AMG). We also prove uniform two-grid convergence of CF-UAMG with a convergence bound independent of the matrix size for symmetric positive definite M-matrices with nonnegative row sums. Numerical experiments on three classes of three-dimensional problems, including Poisson-type equations, radiation diffusion equations, and incompressible Navier-Stokes equations, demonstrate the robustness both in convergence and parallelism of CF-UAMG. Compared with UA-AMG methods employing four commonly used aggregation algorithms, CF-UAMG achieves average speedups of 1.29x, 2.04x, and 1.94x for the three classes of problems, respectively.

papers.title: Your Vision Foundation Model Is Secretly an EEG Foundation Model
papers.abstract: Electroencephalography (EEG) foundation models are pretrained on thousands of hours of recordings, yet their frozen features transfer poorly to downstream tasks, and this transfer does not consistently improve with larger models or more pretraining data. We show that a vision foundation model that has never seen EEG is a stronger frozen EEG encoder than these specialized models, once the signals are rendered as images that a vision transformer can read. Our method, SeeEEG, keeps the vision backbone frozen and learns only how EEG is displayed to it. Each channel occupies a dedicated row of patches and is drawn either as a waveform at a fixed gain or as a scalogram whose frequency range spans the patch height, so that task-relevant patterns fall within individual tokens. The montage, filtering, and contrast parameters of this display are initialized from a standard clinical montage and optimized with the task loss through the frozen backbone, which amounts to at most 1,113 trainable parameters per view. We compare SeeEEG with seven EEG foundation models on eight clinical, sleep, affective, and brain-computer interface datasets, with every encoder frozen and paired with identical readout heads. With a frozen DINOv3 ViT-B, SeeEEG outperforms every EEG foundation model in balanced accuracy on all eight datasets and reaches a mean rank of 1.3 in Cohen kappa or AUROC, compared with 2.9 for the strongest baseline, REVE. The learned displays transfer without further optimization to the video encoder V-JEPA 2.1, which outperforms every EEG foundation model on both metrics on six of the eight datasets. Replacing DINOv3 with a randomly initialized ViT-B lowers the score by 15.2 points on average, so the ability to read rendered EEG comes from visual pretraining.

papers.title: Stochastic Dominance in Discrete Parking Processes on Graphs
papers.abstract: In a recent study on the one-dimensional discrete parking process, it was conjectured that the number of occupied sites in the sequential model first-order stochastically dominates its static counterpart on any path graph. In this paper, we first prove this conjecture for all path graphs and then explore whether stochastic dominance holds for general graph topologies. We show that the property extends naturally to all cycle graphs, and an exhaustive computational analysis confirms that it holds for all 31 connected simple graphs with fewer than 6 vertices. For graphs with 6 or more vertices, we demonstrate that this dominance does not hold universally by constructing explicit counterexamples in which the static model dominates the sequential one; moreover, while one model always dominates the other for all connected graphs with up to 7 vertices, we show that stochastic comparability fails starting at 8 vertices. We also prove that stochastic dominance is inherited by disjoint unions when all connected components share the same dominance direction, and we exhibit mixed unions in which stochastic comparability is either preserved or lost. Finally, supported by algorithmic computations, we formulate a conjecture proposing that the dominance of the sequential model over the static one holds for all graphs with maximum degree at most 3.

papers.title: IsharaBART: An efficient BART-Based Framework for Low-Resource Bangla Sign Language Translation
papers.abstract: Millions of Bangla Sign Language (BdSL) users lack reliable automatic translation tools. Existing systems are limited by data scarcity, unidirectional design, and computationally expensive architectures that are not suitable for low-resource deployment. We introduce IsharaBART, a bidirectional generative framework for gloss-sentence translation in BdSL. IsharaBART uses Bidirectional and Auto-Regressive Transformers (BART)-based conditional language modeling with denoising learning objectives. We developed a parallel dataset of 1,000 professionally annotated gloss-sentence pairs, balanced across tenses and structures. We expanded the dataset to 4,831 pairs through four augmentation techniques: rule-based tense transformations, masked token substitutions, back-translation, and one-shot prompting. A compact denoising sequence-to-sequence model was pre-trained from scratch on monolingual Bangla text from six different corpora, then fine-tuned on the annotated and augmented datasets. We compare IsharaBART against four larger baseline models under identical conditions, where it achieves comparable or superior bidirectional performance. On the gloss-to-sentence (G2S) task, it attains Bilingual Evaluation Understudy (BLEU-4) score up to 51.7, and on the sentence-to-gloss (S2G) task, it achieves 61.40, outperforming multilingual models despite having fewer than 10% of the parameters. Ablation studies demonstrate that pre-training provides 62.5-90.4% faster convergence and 11.5-118% higher BLEU-4 than scratch. Low-rank adaptation (LoRA) reduces trainable parameters by 99.3%, but with 28.0-52.2% loss of BLEU-4 compared to full-parameter fine-tuning.

papers.title: Non-Functional Requirements to Hyperparameter Translation for Quantum Software via LLMs
papers.abstract: Quantum software engineering (QSE) lacks validated approaches for translating natural-language non-functional requirements (NFRs) into execution parameters such as shots and transpiler optimization levels. Existing methods emphasize semantic similarity rather than execution outcomes. We evaluate seven large language models (LLMs) against a deterministic heuristic baseline using 540 synthetic and 18 real-world user stories. We assess semantic accuracy and execution outcomes, including time, cost, top-state probability, and two-qubit gate exposure, through Qiskit/Aer simulations. All LLMs significantly outperformed the heuristic in semantic accuracy, achieving 55.6 to 83.3 percent on real-world stories compared to 16.7 percent for the heuristic. However, no LLM demonstrated statistically significant superiority over others on the real-world dataset. Speed- and cost-oriented configurations reduced execution time and cost, but fidelity improvements were not supported. Some failures resulted from provider safety refusals rather than translation errors. Our findings demonstrate the potential of LLMs as middleware for NFR-to-configuration translation in QSE, while emphasizing execution-based validation, human oversight, and careful interpretation of model differences.

papers.title: Studying temperature-induced decrease of spontaneous polarization in PbTiO$_3$ from vibrational amplitude
papers.abstract: PbTiO$_3$ is a typical ferroelectric polarization induced negative thermal expansion (NTE) material at a wide range of temperature. The elegant TiO$_6$ octahedron is used to study the polarization and NTE, whereas lacking its quantitative characterization. In this work, we propose a concise projection of vibrational amplitude to describe anisotropic distortion of atoms with temperature based on $ab$ $initio$ molecular dynamics simulations. We find that the huge negative mode Gr\"uneisen coefficient is mainly from the different vibrational modes of the TiO$_6$ octahedral rotation at two boundary symmetry points in tetragonal phase along $c$ direction. The potential energy surface as a function of amplitude suggests the $c$-axis compression facilitates the TiO$_6$ octahedral rotation. We show that the vibrational mode of TiO$_6$ octahedral rotation around negative-expansion axis can promote spontaneous polarization reduction with increasing temperature, making transformation of PbTiO$_3$ from tetragonal to cubic phase occur, via the projected amplitude, potential energy surface, and forces of individual atoms.

authors.name: Fuyang Tian
authors.institution: University of Science and Technology Beijing

papers.title: Janus: One Agent, Two Roles for Digital Twin Construction and Network Orchestration
papers.abstract: Next-generation wireless networks are increasingly large-scale, heterogeneous, and dynamic, posing significant challenges to network modeling and control. Digital twins offer a promising solution, but existing approaches typically rely on static models and decouple twin construction from network orchestration, limiting adaptability. Meanwhile, large language models (LLMs) provide strong reasoning capabilities but struggle with graph-structured data and are highly sensitive to prompt design, making inference unreliable. In this paper, we propose Janus, an agentic LLM-based framework that unifies digital twin construction and network orchestration within a closed-loop system. At the core of Janus is a novel NetTwin agent, which introduces a new one-agent, two-role paradigm, enabling a single agent to simultaneously construct the digital twin from partial observations while performing task-driven network decision-making. To realize this, we design a modular architecture with three functional roles, including planner, modeler, and coder, along with a newly designed unified prompt module that further enhances graph reasoning robustness. Extensive evaluations on wireless networks with up to 200 nodes and two representative tasks, including user association and SAGIN routing, show that Janus achieves over 90% digital twin accuracy and near-optimal performance with gaps within 10.53%, while maintaining moderate computational overhead. These results demonstrate the effectiveness, scalability, and generalizability of Janus, paving the way for AI-native autonomous wireless network orchestration.

authors.name: Yi Wei
authors.institution: University of Electronic Science and Technology of China

papers.title: Agreement Is Not Assurance: Evidence-Independent Safety Gates for Agentic AI in DER-Rich Distribution Grids
papers.abstract: Physics-based safety gates for large language model (LLM) agents can approve unsafe actions when the agent and gate rely on the same corrupted measurements or network records. We formulate this shared-evidence failure for voltage-constrained distributed energy resource (DER) export decisions and analyze how nearly critical DER telemetry can bias state estimation while evading residual-based bad-data detection. We propose evidence-independent verification (EIV), which combines advanced metering infrastructure (AMI) voltage readings, measurement selection based on predicted voltage rise, and bounded physical probes. An IEEE 123-bus hidden-truth testbed evaluates 1,654 near-limit requests under telemetry attacks and record errors. For telemetry attacks targeting the nominal gate, an AC-twin gate with bad-data detection approved 95% of unsafe requests, compared with 3.1% for EIV; EIV rejected 22% of safe clean requests. At matched false-rejection settings, direct AMI checks outperformed incorporating the same readings into state estimation. Gate-targeted attacks exposed a vulnerability in telemetry-based response prediction. Command-based prediction removed that route, but targeted attacks on fresh validation cases still produced a 20% unsafe-approval rate under the tested attack pool. LLM agents frequently sought independent evidence voluntarily, but injected instructions and phase-label errors caused unsafe decisions. When offered the EIV checker as a tool, they used it in 93-100% of episodes; mandatory use did not reduce observed violations, which primarily reflected checker errors. These results distinguish enforcement of verification from reliability of the verifier itself.

papers.title: daVinci-Prover: Agent-Native Mid-Training for Formal Theorem Proving
papers.abstract: Advances in large language models (LLMs) are rapidly transforming formal theorem proving. Yet further progress remains constrained by the lack of a transparent and effective data recipe for systematically improving theorem-proving models. In this work, we argue that effective agentic provers require strong mathematical skill priors to ground theorem proving and agentic trajectories to enable long-horizon, interactive proof construction. To this end, we synthesize an agent-native 33.7B-token mid-training corpus covering decomposition, search, self-verification, and revision, together with verifier-grounded agentic trajectories. We further introduce the daVinci-Prover harness, which enables models to construct proofs and interact with a Lean verifier in an isolated workspace, and use it to collect approximately 36K high-quality agent trajectories for supervised fine-tuning. Our mid-training recipe yields an average improvement of 13.7 points over the matched Qwen3-8B SFT-only baseline across MiniF2F, FATE-M, and ProofNet. When applied to the Qwen3.5 series, our approach also yields strong performance across theorem-proving benchmarks and achieves near-saturating MiniF2F performance with memory compaction. The results highlight agent-native mid-training as an effective foundation for developing stronger interactive theorem-proving agents.

papers.title: Report of the 8th LSVOS Challenge: Mobile Unified Multimodal Understanding
papers.abstract: This report summarizes the Mobile Unified Multimodal Understanding (MUMU) track of the 8th Large-scale Video Object Segmentation (LSVOS) Challenge, held in conjunction with ECCV 2026. MUMU asks for a single unified model that jointly performs multi-concept image tagging over quality, scene, and event vocabularies, open-vocabulary object detection, and concise image captioning, within a budget of 0.5B parameters and 8 GB of peak inference memory. Submissions are ranked by a weighted task score scaled by an efficiency factor. We describe the tasks, rules, and evaluation protocol, report the final results, and review the methods of the top three teams. All three leading solutions build on the compact Florence-2-base model, but extend it in different ways: lightweight tagging heads with cross-task inference refinement, a shared low-rank adapter trained on coverage-aware multi-source data with task-dependent decoding, and a training-free pipeline that maps captions to tags and applies detection test-time augmentation. The results show that a compact prompt-based vision-language model can serve all three outputs when supervision, decoding, and cross-task cues are designed for each task, while open-vocabulary detection on novel categories remains the main bottleneck.

authors.name: Ronghao Zheng
authors.institution: State Key Laboratory of Industrial Control Technology

authors.name: Ruohan Shi
authors.institution: First Affiliated Hospital of Bengbu Medical College

authors.name: Chengfeng Qiu
authors.institution: Southern University of Science and Technology

papers.title: HEIR: Harness Egocentric Intent for Human-Robot Interactions
papers.abstract: For robots to assist, serve, and collaborate with humans, they must not only interpret human requests conveyed through language and multimodal intentional cues, but also execute long-horizon tasks that interleave navigation and manipulation. In this paper, we introduce HEIR, a resource for studying how to Harness Egocentric Intent for Human-Robot Interaction. HEIR pairs human speech, measured gaze, and egocentric video with robot observations and teleoperated navigation-manipulation trajectories, while each session preserves successive episodes, with each request fulfilled through multiple execution subtasks. The captured data, together with human-authored annotations, support the study of intent grounding, execution planning, and task completion within a unified interaction setting. To demonstrate the value of HEIR, we conduct extensive offline experiments to evaluate how models benefit from additional human-centric context across these tasks, together with real-robot experiments that assess execution task completion. HEIR thus provides a valuable resource for studying user-centric robot interaction in naturalistic household environments. Our demo and dataset are available online.

authors.name: Sen Cui
authors.institution: State Key Laboratory of Power System Operation and Control

papers.title: Sidorenko inequalities and symmetry-forcing for graph orientations
papers.abstract: We study directed graphs whose homomorphism densities never increase or never decrease when the host edge directions are randomized. We call these properties oriented Sidorenko (OS) and oriented anti-Sidorenko (OAS), respectively. A directed graph is symmetry-forcing if equality between its original and randomized densities forces quasi-random edge directions. We characterize connected OS directed graphs in terms of weakly norming graphs and show that they are symmetry-forcing exactly when their underlying graphs contain a cycle. We also prove that a connected graph is step forcing exactly when it is step Sidorenko and contains a cycle, giving a negative answer to a question of Dole\v{z}al et al. Both forcing results follow from a characterization of strict convexity: the homomorphism density functional of a graph is strictly convex on nonnegative kernels exactly when the graph is weakly norming and contains a cycle. On the OAS side, we construct an infinite symmetry-forcing family and a nonbipartite example. We also classify OS and OAS orientations of stars, paths, and cycles.

papers.title: Measuring the growth index in the $w_0w_a$CDM background
papers.abstract: We produce a measurement of the growth index, $\gamma$, which is used to parametrize the scale-independent growth of linear matter perturbations on sub-horizon scales, for the $w_0w_a$CDM background model. In 2023, assuming the $\Lambda$CDM background, the value $\gamma =0.633^{+0.025}_{-0.024}$ was obtained, excluding the General Relativity value of $\gamma=0.55$ at $3.7\sigma$ statistical significance. In 2025, an analysis of baryon acoustic oscillation data from the Dark Energy Spectroscopy Instrument (DESI) demonstrated a preference for a dynamical dark energy over the cosmological constant model, $\Lambda$, ranging from $2.8-4.2\sigma$, depending on the external datasets used. Therefore it is important to determine how the $\gamma$ measurement is modified in the context of dynamical dark energy and verify whether the tension with the expected theoretical value persists. Considering data from Planck cosmic microwave background anisotropies, $f\sigma_{8}$, baryon acoustic oscillation from DESI and supernova Ia luminosity distances from Phanteon+, we find $\gamma_{w_0w_a}=0.633\pm0.024$, essentially the same value found for the $\Lambda$CDM background. This result excludes the General Relativity value for the $w_0w_a$CDM background evolution at $3.4\sigma$ level. We also show that the $\gamma$ posteriors across many datasets combinations are consistent with each other and that main driver of the "$\gamma$ tension" is the $f\sigma_{8}$ dataset.

authors.name: Icaro. B. S. Cortes
authors.institution: Universidade Federal do Rio Grande do Norte

authors.name: Leo G. Medeiros
authors.institution: Universidade Federal do Rio Grande do Norte

authors.name: Ronaldo C. Batista
authors.institution: Universidade Federal do Rio Grande do Norte

papers.title: A Geometric Perspective for Marginal R2: Estimation and Inference in Generalized Linear Mixed Models
papers.abstract: Generalized linear mixed models (GLMMs) are widely used across scientific disciplines, yet quantifying response variation explained by auxiliary information remains challenging for non-Gaussian outcomes and hierarchical dependence. Existing $R^2$ measures provide useful summaries, but their variance-based constructions are not generally linked to a common geometric interpretation, a fixed-design marginal estimand, and corresponding statistical inference. We propose marginal quasi-$R^2$ through two distinct operations. First, marginalization integrates over latent random effects, retaining their uncertainty in the marginal response moments and specifying the model for explanatory assessment. Second, a Quasi-GLM formulation supplies a local working information metric under which orthogonal projection yields an Pythagorean decomposition of explained and unexplained variation. We define a fixed-design population estimand, establish consistency and asymptotic normality of its estimator, and derive cluster-robust sandwich standard errors and confidence intervals under stated regularity conditions. Simulations assess estimation accuracy and interval coverage across response families and random-effects structures. Two ecological applications illustrate the importance of reporting estimation uncertainty alongside marginal quasi-$R^2$. The method is implemented in the R package quasiR2.

authors.name: Hao Qin
authors.institution: Tianjin Medical University Cancer Institute and Hospital

authors.name: Allison K. White
authors.institution: The University of Texas Rio Grande Valley

papers.title: What Do Tokenizer Comparisons Measure? Disentangling Granularity, Root Assignment, and Word-Level Readout across Amharic and Hausa
papers.abstract: Morphology-aware tokenizers are expected to help morphologically rich languages, and their reported gains over byte-pair encoding (BPE) are usually credited to their linguistic units. A comparison with BPE cannot support this attribution, since such a tokenizer also segments text more finely (granularity) and, on token-level tasks, changes how much the sub-token readout matters. We separate both factors from the effect of grouping words by their roots (root assignment) in Amharic, a Semitic language whose Ge'ez abugida hides consonantal roots inside syllabic glyphs, with Latin-script Hausa as an orthographic contrast. Our design combines a lossless root-and-pattern tokenizer with controls that change one factor at a time, in two independent implementations. In both, real root assignment improves Amharic named-entity recognition over scrambled roots (+4.9 and +4.7 F1), and root-frequency structure explains little of this gain. In small from-scratch models, the readout choice moves F1 by up to 13.4 points and reverses the sign of every comparison of the root-and-pattern arms with BPE, whereas in two pretrained encoders it moves F1 by less than one point. The granularity effect changes sign across languages and implementations. We recommend decomposing tokenizer effects, and reporting the readout, before a gain is attributed to linguistic structure.

papers.title: Novel Esscher concepts for informational risks and valuation in market models under random horizon
papers.abstract: This paper considers the setting constituted by the triplet $(S,\mathbb{F},\tau)$. The pair $(S,\mathbb{F})$ is the initial model where $S$ is the discounted price process of risky assets (Stocks) and $\mathbb{F}$ is the ``public" flow of information that is available to all agents over time. $\tau$ is an arbitrary random time, which might not be seen through the flow $\mathbb{F}$, and it represents a default time in credit risk and a death time of an insured in life insurance where mortality and/or longevity risks present serious challenges. For simplicity, we suppose $S$ follows a geometric jump-diffusion model with stochastic volatiles and $\mathbb{F}$ is generated by a Brownian motion and Poisson process. In this setting, we address how the Esscher densities and/or measures notions can evolves with the informational risk induced by $\tau$. In fact, we introduce the notion of Esscher with degrees-of-freedom associated to the informational risks generated by $\tau$. On the one hand, we give various and complete characterizations of these Esscher notions in our informational setting. On the other hand, we fully characterize the Escher-prices bounds, for vulnerable claims (claims built on the occurrence of $\tau$), using constrained backward stochastic differential equations (CBSDEs for short hereafter) that appear to be novel as well.

papers.title: Quantum Cost of Emptiness in a One-Dimensional Bose Gas
papers.abstract: The probability $P_0(R)$ of an empty interval of radius $R$ probes the far tail of density fluctuations in the thermodynamic ground state of the repulsive Lieb--Liniger gas. Here $\rho$ is the bulk density and $c$ the repulsion. As $\ell = \rho R \to \infty$ at fixed $\gamma = c/\rho > 0$, we find $-\log P_0 = f(\gamma)\ell^2 + B(\gamma)\sqrt{\ell} - \frac{1}{4}\log\ell + O_\gamma(1)$, with no linear term and $B = 2\zeta(3/2)\sqrt{f/(\pi\gamma)}$. Exact Gaussian completion of the auxiliary-field determinant reduces the leading collective response to an electrostatic slit problem, yielding $f(\gamma)$ in elliptic integrals. Its dipole polarization tail drives auxiliary scattering returns whose local density saturates while the active rapidity range expands as $\sqrt{R}$, producing the square-root boundary cost. The full return spectrum and the occupied-rapidity endpoints together fix the $-1/4$ logarithmic coefficient. Through the contact identity, widening the void probes a dense healing scale at the boundary whose growing characteristic occupation supports an emergent classical-field description even in a strongly interacting bulk.

papers.title: GC-MoE on SM120: Overlapping Expert-Parallel Token Dispatch with Warp-Level FP8xFP4 Block-Scaled MMA on Consumer Blackwell
papers.abstract: Expert-parallel Mixture-of-Experts decoding is latency bound: each layer serializes a token exchange, a grouped GEMM over routed experts, and a combine, while only a few tokens per rank are in flight. Prior GC-MoE fused these phases into one persistent, Green-Context-partitioned CUDA Graph on Hopper (SM90) and datacenter Blackwell (SM100). This paper rebuilds the operator for SM120 (compute capability 12.0, e.g. RTX PRO 5000) over PCIe. SM120 exposes block-scaled tensor cores only through warp-level mma.sync.aligned.kind::mxf8f6f4: no tensor memory, no two-CTA MMA, no cluster multicast. We rebuild the kernel around a swap-AB warp-level block-scaled MMA with FP4 weights in the register A operand and FP8 activations in B, plus SM120-specific mechanisms: scale-byte selection through MMA immediates, a compact-weights path, an adaptive token-tile geometry, an expert-granular streaming dispatch with a batched bulk-pull engine and a 64-bit deduplicating pull cache, full-width BF16 returns drained by resident relay copiers over a position-major arena, and shared experts folded into the compute role. On 8xRTX PRO 5000 over PCIe the operator is 1.522x and 1.387x faster than the FlashInfer CuTe DSL W4A8 MegaMoE and the Cake MegaMoE across 18 decode points (18/18 wins each), and 1.388x faster than Cake with shared experts fused; all 94 numerical cases and 752 per-rank checks pass, at cross-operator cosine similarity of at least 0.9999997.

authors.name: Haoyu Wang
authors.institution: Changchun University of Science and Technology

authors.name: Tao Lan
authors.institution: University of Science and Technology of China

papers.title: On Ignorability Beyond Missing at Random: Completion-Invariant Missingness for Nonmonotone Missing Data
papers.abstract: The missing-at-random assumption underlies most analyses of incomplete data. Under nonmonotone missingness, it is especially stringent, imposing pattern-specific restrictions with different conditioning sets. A strictly weaker normalization condition is known to justify maximizing the observed-data likelihood. We show that every law satisfying this condition has a unique missing-at-random counterpart sharing its observed-data and complete-data distributions. Observed-data procedures developed under missing at random for identified functionals, including doubly robust estimators, therefore remain valid, with the same semiparametric efficiency bound. We then prove that the condition holds if and only if filling in the missing values from their conditional distribution under the true full model preserves the complete-data distribution, hence the name completion-invariant missingness. We use a characteristic kernel to compare the completed distribution with the fitted model and assess the joint compatibility of the specified full model and completion-invariant missingness. We derive the asymptotic null distribution with estimated parameters and establish bootstrap and multiplier calibration. Since a parametric full model alone need not identify completion-invariant missingness, we give identification conditions for Gaussian, Student $t$ and finite mixture families. Simulations assess sensitivity to departures from each assumption, and applications to clinical laboratory measurements and childhood growth illustrate the diagnostic.

papers.title: Constraining Dark Matter Gravitational Production with the 21cm Signal at the Cosmic Dawn
papers.abstract: The origin of dark matter is one of the major problems in modern cosmology. We can infer its existence from the gravitational potential wells around astrophysical objects, but there is no convincing explanation for what its nature and origin are. Moreover, experiments for direct detection, indirect detection, or particle production in accelerators have not shown, until now, any conclusive interaction between dark matter and particles in the standard model. This may imply that dark matter does not interact with ordinary matter and originates from pure gravitational interaction. In this manuscript, we investigate the possibility to constrain the gravitational production of dark matter from the 21cm brightness temperature at the cosmic dawn. Considering only the time when the absorption profile occurs, we can impose upper limits on the dark matter's mass. Future measurements have potential to extend current constraints and help understanding the nature of dark matter.

authors.name: Andre A. Costa
authors.institution: Universidade Federal do Rio de Janeiro

papers.title: Unraveling the Magnetic Fields of Starspots with Transit Mapping
papers.abstract: Stellar magnetic activity is known to decrease as stars age, but the underlying physical mechanism for this decline remains a key question. Does this evolution occur because individual starspots become magnetically weaker (a change in quality), or because the total area covered by spots diminishes (a change in quantity)? We address this question by synthesizing results from two recent studies that leverage starspot transit mapping of Kepler and CoRoT targets. First, we show that the magnetic field strength of starspots remains consistently high, on a saturation plateau of approximately 3500 G, regardless of stellar age or rotation period. This suggests that the intrinsic quality of spots does not significantly evolve. Second, we demonstrate a strong anticorrelation between starspot area coverage and stellar age, with young stars exhibiting large filling factors (up to 29%) that decrease sharply over time. Our combined results provide compelling evidence that the evolution of stellar magnetic activity is primarily driven by a change in the quantity of magnetic flux emerging on the surface, not by a change in the intrinsic strength of the spots themselves. These findings have direct implications for refining stellar dynamo models and improving age-dating techniques.

papers.title: Exploring 3-CNF Formulas Generated From Partial Steiner Triple Systems
papers.abstract: Steiner triple systems (STS) and subsets of these known as partial STS (PSTS) are combinatorial objects that have received substantial interest from mathematicians since their introduction in 1847. Over the last three decades, (P)STS have found applications in diverse fields ranging from digital circuit testing to wireless transmission. Perhaps unsurprisingly, the triple in (P)STS allows for a mapping to 3-conjunctive normal form (3-CNF) formulas, the Boolean formula used as input to 3-SAT. Prompted by this ready conversion of (P)STS to 3-CNF formulas and numerous real-world applications of (P)STS, we explore the intersection of (P)STS with 3-SAT and its counting version \#3-SAT. We explain the properties of (P)STS-generated 3-CNF formulas in terms familiar to the SAT community and experimentally compare them against randomly-generated 3-CNF formulas. We find that PSTS-3-CNF formulas are statistically distinct from randomly generated 3-CNF formulas, in both probability of satisfiability and expected solution count.

papers.title: Bipartite Matchings, Matrix Permanents, and Zeon Power Series
papers.abstract: Perfect matchings of a bipartite graph are counted by the permanent of the graph's biadjacency matrix, and permanents of sequences of structured biadjacency matrices lead to integer sequences. We consider a number of such sequences and illustrate how zeon-algebraic representations of bipartite graphs lead to recursively defined zeon sequences. Then, using formal power series methods, we show that the ``$\Omega$-exponentials'' of these zeon sequences reveal numbers of perfect matchings in the graphs.

authors.name: Muhammad Waqar Ul Hassan
authors.institution: University of Electronic Science and Technology of China

papers.title: When and How SignSGD Outperforms SGD: A Functional Scaling Law Perspective
papers.abstract: We study how the sign operator interacts with gradient noise to shape the learning dynamics and scaling behavior of sign-based optimizers. In power-law kernel regression with diagonal features, we establish a functional scaling law (FSL) for SignSGD under general learning rate schedules. The FSL describes the learning dynamics through two processes: signal learning and noise forgetting. The key mechanism is noise-induced preconditioning: gradient noise smooths the sign operator, inducing an effective preconditioned SGD. Noise-curvature alignment enables this preconditioning to transform the effective Hessian from $\mathbf{H}$ to $\mathbf{H}^{1/2}$. The resulting dynamics exhibit faster signal learning but slower noise forgetting than SGD. This tradeoff yields a regime-dependent comparison with SGD: (i) SignSGD achieves improved data efficiency in the hard-task regime; (ii) both optimizers achieve the same data efficiency in the easy-task regime, but SignSGD maintains this efficiency at larger batch sizes, requiring fewer optimization steps for a fixed data budget. Power-law kernel regression experiments support the proposed mechanism and predicted scaling behavior. LLM pre-training experiments further suggest that the SignSGD FSL better captures the batch-size dependence of loss dynamics for sign-based optimizers than the original SGD FSL.

authors.name: Jinbo Wang
authors.institution: Frontier Science Center for Quantum Information of the Ministry of Education of China

papers.title: Categorical orbifold theory
papers.abstract: We investigate the orbifold theory for condensable algebras in fusion categories $\mathcal{C}$. We prove that the algebra automorphism group of a condensable algebra $A$ is finite and explicitly characterize its elements in terms of the fusion action and indecomposable $\mathcal{C}_{A}^0$-bimodule decomposition of $\mathcal{C}_{A}$. We further show that a finite group action on $A$ gives rise to a group extension of the category $\mathcal{C}_{A}^0$ in $\mathcal{C}_{A}$. Conversely, every such group extension arises from a finite group of algebra automorphisms of $A$. Finally, we also construct a canonical maximal group extension of $\mathcal{C}_{A}^0$, thereby providing a categorical framework for the classical correspondence among finite group actions, fixed-point algebras, and twisted modules.

authors.name: Siu-Hung Ng
authors.institution: Hong Kong University of Science and Technology

authors.name: Li Ren
authors.institution: Southwest University of Science and Technology

papers.title: STVLA: Spatial-aware and Temporal-memory forVision-Language-Action Models
papers.abstract: Robotic manipulation often requires both spatial scene understanding and task history. However, many vision-language-action (VLA) policies rely primarily on current observations, without explicitly integrating spatial structure and task history. Appearance-based memories can be sensitive to occlusion and viewpoint changes, while spatial representations of the current scene alone do not preserve how the scene has changed during task execution. We introduce STVLA, a framework that incorporates features from a pretrained visual geometry foundation model into temporal memory alongside visual representations. This allows the policy to recall past scene structure as context for current action decisions. To select informative history, STVLA uses a mathematically grounded scoring rule that balances relevance to the current observation with complementary evidence from memory. Across evaluations on LIBERO, LIBERO-Mem, MIKASA-Robo, and SimplerEnv Bridge, STVLA achieves the highest average success rate among the compared methods on each benchmark. On real-world block stacking, object organization, and phone packaging, it improves success over $\pi_{0.5}$ by $58.33$, $30.00$, and $35.00$ percentage points, respectively. These results support integrating scene geometry into temporal memory to improve manipulation requiring both spatial precision and task history. Project website: \href{https://stvla.github.io/}{https://stvla.github.io/}

authors.name: Hongwei Han
authors.institution: Southwest University of Science and Technology

authors.name: Yongcheng Liu
authors.institution: State Key Laboratory of Advanced Special Steel

papers.title: Markov Population Potential Game: An Alternative Framework for Markovian Traffic Assignment
papers.abstract: Understanding the equilibrium behavior of large populations of interacting agents in transportation systems is challenging due to the high-dimensional state space and the coupled decision-making among agents. This study proposes the Markov population potential game (MPPG) that integrates Markov games, potential games, and population games as a unified framework for analyzing such interactions. The framework extends the classical Markov potential game to the population level and establishes theoretical conditions on stage rewards and state transitions under which the Markov population game admits a Beckmann-type potential function. Accordingly, every KKT point of the associated optimization problem yields an MPPG equilibrium. We further demonstrate that if only the reward condition holds, each KKT point of the optimization problem corresponds to a support-restricted $\varepsilon$-equilibrium, meaning the Q-values of any two active actions differ by at most $\varepsilon$, thereby significantly extending the applicability of MPPG. We further establish both priori and posteriori upper bounds of $\varepsilon$ to efficiently evaluate the approximation error. Inspired by the equivalent optimization problem, a projected-gradient (PG) policy iteration algorithm is developed. The theoretical bounds and PG algorithm are demonstrated through numerical experiments on a parametric Markov population game.

papers.title: SUMNO: Spatially Unrolled Multigrid Neural Operator for Fluid Flow Surrogates
papers.abstract: Data-driven surrogate modeling has emerged as a powerful paradigm for accelerating computational fluid dynamics, and hierarchical U-shaped networks, which resemble the structure of classical Geometric Multigrid (GMG) methods, have become prevalent designs. Modern surrogates built on these designs achieve competitive accuracy at a fraction of the cost of numerical solvers; however, accurate prediction of complex flows remains challenging, and no existing architecture leads across them. In such networks, the multigrid analogy mainly concerns the multi-resolution topology, while their components largely follow common vision practice. To address this, this study introduces SUMNO, a multigrid neural operator for fluid flow fields on regular grids that spatially unrolls a V-cycle into a feed-forward U-shaped network. Parameter-free down- and upsampling stand in for restriction and prolongation, and additive skip connections for coarse-grid correction, with normalization-free transfer and skip pathways. Within this macro-architecture, convolutions are used at the fine and intermediate resolutions and shifted-window attention at the coarsest, whose window partitioning is generalized to handle periodicity independently per axis. Evaluated on unseen test configurations across four unsteady and steady flow benchmarks against five representative baselines, SUMNO is best in 5 of 7 settings and ranks second in the remaining two. It reduces the 10-step rollout MSE by about 30% relative to the strongest baseline, and outperforms three baselines with over 130 million parameters using 9.4 million parameters.

papers.title: MuEdit: An efficient multi-task editing method towards inter-domain knowledge conflicts
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) require frequent knowledge updates across heterogeneous domains, but existing editing methods fail when applied sequentially to multi-task settings. We trace this collapse to inter-domain null-space misalignment: heterogeneous tasks induce distinct Jacobian geometries, causing their common null space to shrink dramatically and leaving insufficient admissible directions for conflict-free updates. We propose the Conflict Index to quantify this geometric interference, and introduce Mu-Edit, which mitigates multi-task conflicts via (1) conflict-aware ordering to minimize cumulative interference, and (2) dynamic low-rank approximation to expand the null space when ordering alone is insufficient. Experiments across five functional domains and three backbones show that Mu-Edit significantly outperforms existing baselines in multi-task editing performance while preserving general capabilities, and remains effective under incremental task arrival.

papers.title: DaYu-TC: a global-regional nested AI system for tropical cyclone forecasting
papers.abstract: Accurate tropical cyclone intensity forecasts are essential for disaster preparedness, yet persistent intensity underestimation limits the value of artificial intelligence (AI) weather models for predicting these destructive storms. Here we present DaYu-TC, a global-regional nested system that links the preservation of strong-wind and low-pressure signals with high-resolution regional prediction. Its global and regional models share an architecture and extreme-aware training objectives. The regional model combines evolving local states with global forecasts valid at each target time, connecting large-scale environmental information with finer-scale cyclone evolution. In an independent evaluation of 16 western North Pacific tropical cyclones in 2023, the global model retains competitive conventional forecast skill while reducing five-day maximum-wind root-mean-square error (RMSE) by 6-22% relative to other evaluated global AI models. Relative to the global model, regional nesting reduces maximum-wind RMSE by 22.0-33.1% and minimum-pressure RMSE by 28.6-39.8% across 12-120 h. The complete system outperforms concurrent operational high-resolution forecasts from the European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts for minimum pressure at 12-120 h and maximum wind speed at 48-96 h, with respective RMSE reductions of 26% and 12% at 72 h. Without retraining, the same regional model enhances three other global AI models, reducing overall maximum-wind RMSE by 22.6-28.6%. Five-day forecasts take under one minute on a single GPU. These results establish a transferable multiscale approach to reducing cyclone intensity underestimation, extending advances in AI weather forecasting towards more accurate prediction of high-impact weather events.

papers.title: AcrossPlace: Do Vision--Language Models Recognize Places Beyond Their Source Views? A Comprehensive Benchmark
papers.abstract: Language-guided place recognition requires recovering geographic identity across visual observations beyond the image from which a description originates. However, aggregate retrieval scores often entangle observation transfer, gallery competition, and linguistic evidence, obscuring the underlying recognition capability. We introduce AcrossPlace, a provenance-aware benchmark establishing a systematic evaluation standard for bidirectional language--vision place recognition. Built upon GSV-Cities, AcrossPlace comprises 56,726 places across 23 cities, 156,800 automatically generated, rule-filtered descriptions, and 113,404 target images. Each description retains its source-image provenance, while retrieval operates on disjoint target observations. Text-to-image (T2I) and image-to-text (I2T) retrieval share a unified place-identity relevance criterion supporting multiple valid matches. Two geographic protocols evaluate unseen places within represented cities (P0) and generalization to held-out cities (P1). Paired observation comparisons, gallery-controlled evaluations, fixed-query scaling, and blinded annotation auditing systematically characterize retrieval performance. Across three training seeds, place-supervised SigLIP2 T2I Recall@1 decreases from 19.69% on source images to 12.31% on independent targets under P0. For fixed P1 queries, expanding the gallery from 500 to 8,425 places reduces Recall@1 from 14.67% to 2.87%. A 240-description audit further reveals discrepancies between automated acceptance and factual evidence. These findings establish AcrossPlace as a reproducible evaluation standard for assessing transferable place identity across visual observations and geographic environments.

papers.title: EasyFoam: Skill-Oriented OpenFOAM Agents with Evidence-Driven Evolution
papers.abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents are increasingly capable of automating end-to-end OpenFOAM workflows for computational fluid dynamics (CFD). However, current progress is bottlenecked by two critical limitations. First, existing evaluations are dominated by tutorial-level cases and execution-oriented metrics, masking a substantial executability--acceptability gap: successfully executed simulations often fail to satisfy prescribed numerical or quantity-of-interest (QoI) criteria. Second, domain expertise in existing systems is tightly coupled with bespoke agent architectures, limiting its reuse and continual refinement across agent implementations. To address these challenges, we introduce ExtFoamBench, a challenging benchmark for OpenFOAM agents that spans five axes of workflow variation, and separately assesses execution completion, numerical soundness, and QoI satisfaction. Complementing this, we propose EasyFoam, an agent framework that decouples CFD expertise into modular, externalized skills driven by a dual-loop mechanism. An execution loop constructs workflows from explicit task requirements and uses structured simulation evidence to diagnose failures and guide targeted repairs. Meanwhile, an evolution loop distills task experience into reusable skill updates selected through paired evaluation. Empirical evaluations demonstrate that EasyFoam achieves substantially higher task acceptance rates than baseline agents, establishing this work as a starting point for future research toward self-improving CFD agents.
