Coordinated observations from the Goode Solar Telescope and the Solar Dynamics Observatory, together with nonlinear force-free field extrapolations, allow us to trace the event from the merging of two low-lying filamentary structures to the failed eruption of the resulting elongated filament. Before the rapid rise, the modeled flux rope had entered a regime susceptible to kink instability, while low-atmospheric internal reconnection had already occurred; both may have contributed to the initial acceleration. The rising flux rope remained below the torus instability threshold and was confined by a strong, asymmetric overlying field that compressed it against the overlying loops. An elongated interface brightening, bidirectional plasmoid-like motions, newly brightened loop systems, and progressive weakening of the filament are consistent with external reconnection that changed the magnetic connectivity, removed magnetic flux from the rope, and disrupted its coherent structure. Differential emission measure analysis indicates that the external reconnection heated the active region loop system. A transient, localized structure with high-temperature emission was observed at the interaction interface, consistent with the expected location of a current sheet associated with external reconnection. These results suggest that the strong confining field halted the filament eruption and sustained the interface compression required for current sheet formation, enabling external reconnection to disrupt the flux rope and heat the active region loop system.

authors.name: Dongxu Liu
authors.institution: Public Health Clinical Center of Chengdu

papers.title: Thin Edges in Braces
papers.abstract: A connected graph with at least two vertices is matching covered if each of its edges is contained in a perfect matching. A bipartite matching covered graph is a brace if no nontrivial cut meets every perfect matching in exactly one edge.An edge $e$ of a brace $G$ is thin if $G-e$ is matching covered and its retract is a brace. Every brace can be reduced to $K_2$ or $C_4$ by successively deleting thin edges and taking retracts. Indeed, Carvalho, Lucchesi and Murty proved that every brace of order at least six has at least two thin edges. They conjectured that there exists a positive constant $c$ such that every brace of order $n\ge6$ has at least $cn$ thin edges. In this paper, we prove that every simple brace of order $n\ge6$ has at least $\left\lceil\frac{n+2}{6}\right\rceil$ thin edges and that every brace of order $n$, withparallel edges allowed, has at least $\frac{n}{13}$ thin edges. This proves the conjecture. Moreover, we prove that every cubic brace of order $n$ has at least $\left\lceil\frac{n+1}{5}\right\rceil$ thin edges for $n\ge6$ and that the coefficient $\frac15$ is best possible.

papers.title: Multi-Step Underwater Acoustic Channel Prediction via Dual-Domain Structure Preservation and Pretrained Transformer
papers.abstract: Accurate future channel state information (CSI) is essential for underwater acoustic (UWA) communication because delays associated with signal propagation, feedback, scheduling, and transceiver reconfiguration can render currently available CSI outdated. However, most existing predictors estimate only the next channel state and obtain multi-step forecasts through recursive rollout, which causes prediction errors to accumulate as the multipath structure evolves. The scarcity of sea-trial measurements further limits reliable model training. To address these challenges, we propose LLM4UACP, a dual-domain, structure-preserving framework that adapts a pretrained Transformer for few-shot multi-step UWA channel prediction. LLM4UACP extracts complementary features from the channel impulse response (CIR) and channel frequency response (CFR), aligns them through Fourier-consistent fusion, and encodes the fused representation as delay-time tokens. A pretrained Transformer with a frozen backbone is adapted through Butterfly Orthogonal Fine-tuning to jointly predict multiple future CIRs in a single forward pass, thereby avoiding the error accumulation associated with recursive prediction. Experiments on the measured SO-06 and SO-07 channels show that LLM4UACP achieves normalized mean squared error (NMSE) values of 0.0411 and 0.0399, corresponding to reductions of 88.53% and 85.15%, respectively, relative to the most recent baseline. With only 0.11M trainable parameters, LLM4UACP maintains robust performance across varying prediction horizons and observation-window lengths, limited-data settings, and cross-dataset transfer scenarios.

authors.name: Deqing Wang
authors.institution: Central Party School of the Communist Party of China

authors.name: Liqun Fu
authors.institution: Nanjing University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Collision-Resilient All-to-All Broadcast Scheduling in Underwater Acoustic Networks
papers.abstract: This paper studies all-to-all broadcast scheduling for underwater swarms with collision-resilient physical layers that can decode asynchronously overlapping packets. Propagation-aware collision-free schedulers coordinate packet arrivals but do not account for this reception capability. We first design a data-driven neural reception model that captures per-interferer power and timing effects. The model improves prediction accuracy over SINR baselines while admitting an exact mixed-integer linear programming (MILP) formulation. The resulting neural-network-embedded MILP (NN-MILP) optimizes transmission times while explicitly encoding schedule-dependent overlaps and the predictor's inference, enabling globally optimal scheduling for small-scale instances. For larger networks, a two-stage ant colony optimization (ACO) heuristic combines low-cost transmission-order search with neural-aware timing refinement. Simulation results show that ACO shortens broadcast rounds compared with existing schedulers. It approaches the NN-MILP optimum on small-scale instances while supporting larger networks at substantially lower computational cost.

authors.name: Enqi Zhang
authors.institution: Nanjing University of Information Science and Technology

authors.name: Deqing Wang
authors.institution: Central Party School of the Communist Party of China

authors.name: Liqun Fu
authors.institution: Nanjing University of Science and Technology

papers.title: A symmetry on Young tableaux with walls and holes
papers.abstract: The Pons--Batle conjecture on tree-child networks was regarded as a specific and challenging problem in the phylogenetics community. We found an unexpected weighted symmetry for a class of three-row Young tableaux with walls and holes. This weighted symmetry implies the Fuchs--Yu identity, which together with the bijection of Chang, Fuchs, Liu, Wallner, and Yu leads to a simple proof of the Pons--Batle conjecture. We construct an involutive proof of this symmetry via introducing decorated binary networks as an intermediate structure. We also provide an elementary proof of this weighted symmetry using recurrence relations.

authors.name: Jing Liu
authors.institution: Ministry of Education of the People's Republic of China

papers.title: Cleanness and real rank zero in $C^*$-algebras
papers.abstract: A unital $C^*$-algebra is called clean if every element is the sum of an idempotent and an invertible element. We prove that cleanness is equivalent to real rank zero. More precisely, the invertible summand can be chosen with inverse norm at most $2+\varepsilon$ for every $\varepsilon>0$, and the constant $2$ is optimal. In particular, every von Neumann algebra is clean, answering a question of Lam. Clean decompositions with uniformly bounded idempotent summands characterize real rank zero and stable rank one. Moreover, $*$-cleanness, defined by requiring the idempotent summands to be projections, is equivalent to real rank zero, stable rank one, and triviality of the $K_1$-group. Finally, sharp cleanness, defined by requiring clean decompositions with inverse norm at most $2$, is equivalent to real rank zero and the $SAW^*$ property.

authors.name: Wei Yuan
authors.institution: Shaanxi University of Science and Technology

papers.title: SurvEval: Listwise Re-Ranking Evaluator via Survival-Based Exposure and Multi-Objective Value Modeling
papers.abstract: Re-ranking is a crucial stage in recommender systems, yet existing evaluators oversimplify user browsing assumptions and collapse multi-objective signals into a single scalar, limiting their ability to reflect true listwise utility. We propose \textbf{SurvEval}, a listwise evaluator that jointly models user exposure and item value for re-ranking evaluation. We formalize the sequential browsing process as a discrete-time survival model, deriving monotonically decreasing reaching probabilities that capture the cascading structure of user browsing. We further introduce a multi-objective value estimation module with dedicated per-objective prediction heads and uncertainty-based loss weighting to adaptively balance objectives of varying scales and noise levels. Both components are jointly optimized via a unified transformer backbone, and the listwise utility is obtained by summing the position-wise products of reaching probabilities and conditional item value estimates. Extensive experiments on KuaiRand and Avito demonstrate that SurvEval achieves superior performance over state-of-the-art baselines.

papers.title: ReAlign: Reward-Guided Preference Alignment for Generative Re-Ranking
papers.abstract: Re-ranking refines the upstream ranked list to maximize listwise user utility. Existing two-stage generator-evaluator methods decouple list generation from list evaluation, leaving the generator without direct access to the listwise utility signal, while scoring-based one-stage methods score items under a fixed upstream permutation context without explicitly searching the permutation space. We propose \textbf{ReAlign}, a reward-guided preference alignment framework that couples a listwise reward model with a candidate-aware autoregressive generator. The reward model decomposes the listwise reward into position-wise contributions, modeling user exposure through a survival-based exposure module and item value through per-objective heads for heterogeneous engagement signals. The generator is trained in two stages: supervised pre-training on logged exposure lists to establish a relevance prior, followed by reward-guided post-training that aligns the generator with the reward model through complementary distribution and ranking alignment over within-pool standardized rewards. Extensive offline experiments show that ReAlign consistently outperforms existing state-of-the-art baselines.

papers.title: On JT boundary algebras
papers.abstract: We construct the canonical boundary algebras of Jackiw--Teitelboim gravity coupled to free bosonic matter. For a nonempty finite or countable family of species with lowest weights greater than one half, the two boundary algebras are mutual commutants and nonhyperfinite type $\mathrm{II}_\infty$ factors. Their nonzero finite corners are nonhyperfinite type $\mathrm{II}_1$ factors. The construction uses bounded heat-regularized fields and a Hilbert algebra, which gives a faithful normal semifinite trace without a path-integral argument. The weight restriction is sharp: elementary point fields remain unbounded after positive heat regularization when $0<d\leq1/2$. For one massless scalar, specified bounded observables and normal states have a high energy limit described by a hyperfinite continuous core. We explain why this limit does not preserve the nonhyperfiniteness of the exact algebra.

papers.title: Asymptotic behaviors of solutions to the critical fractional $p$-Laplace equations with Hardy potential
papers.abstract: In this paper we consider positive weak solutions $u\in\mathcal{D}^{s,p}(\mathbb{R}^{N})$ to the critical fractional $p$-Laplace equation with Hardy potential $(-\Delta_p)^s u-\mu\frac{u^{p-1}}{|x|^{ps}}=u^{p_s^{*}-1}$ in $\mathbb{R}^{N}$, where $N\geqslant 2$, $s\in(0,1)$, $p\in(1,\infty)$ satisfying $ps<N$, $p_s^{*}=\frac{Np}{N-ps}$ and $\mu\in(0,\mathcal{C}_{N,s,p})$, $\mathcal{C}_{N,s,p}$ denotes the sharp constant of the fractional Hardy inequality. By means of a suitable comparison principle for weak subsolutions and supersolutions of the equations $(-\Delta_p)^sf=\big(\frac{\mu}{|x|^{ps}}+a(x)\big)f^{p-1}$ on general open set $\Omega$, with nonzero exterior data and $a\in L^{\frac{N}{ps}}(\mathbb{R}^{N})$, combined with careful constructions of the weak subsolutions and supersolutions, we prove that every positive weak solution $u$ of the above problem satisfies $C^{-1}\leqslant|x|^{\mu_1}(1+|x|)^{\mu_2-\mu_1}u(x)\leqslant C$ for a.e. $x\in\mathbb{R}^{N}$, where $\mu_1<\mu_2$ are the two roots of the indicial equation associated with the Hardy operator and $C\in[1,\infty)$ depends on $u$. Also, we show that the constant $C$ cannot be chosen to depend only on $N$, $s$, $p$ and $\mu$.

authors.name: Zeming Wang
authors.institution: Xi'an University of Architecture and Technology

papers.title: Causals: An Open Knowledge Graph for Research on Causal Reasoning
papers.abstract: Applying causal knowledge to a new event requires connecting the event to relevant entities and the relationships through which its consequences may unfold. We present Causals, an open knowledge graph for research on this form of reasoning. Its initial release, constructed from news reports, contains 369,184 nodes and 1,272,418 edges linking reported events, organizations, commodities, financial instruments, and other entities. Structural relationships, observations, and attributed causal claims retain distinct semantics and links to source records. We describe the construction and representation of the resource and characterize its connectivity and multi-hop retrieval properties. Causals provides shared relational knowledge for studying how language models retrieve relevant context and apply mechanisms to particular events. The dataset is available under CC BY 4.0 at https://causals.org/, and we invite contributions to its ontology, records, and evidence.

papers.title: Unequal Rewards and the Direction of Scientific Work: Evidence from U.S. Public Universities
papers.abstract: Research on pay dispersion has long asked whether unequal rewards increase or depress performance. Tournament theory expects stronger effort, while social comparison accounts expect withdrawal. Both perspectives, however, treat performance as a single scale on which workers can be ranked. Scientific work often resists such ordering. Some contributions extend recognized lines of inquiry and can be evaluated against prevailing standards; others revise the frames through which value is judged and become legible only later. We argue that intellectual tournaments more readily reward the first kind of contribution than the second. Pay dispersion may therefore be associated not only with how much scholars produce but also with what kinds of intellectual exploration are encouraged. We test this argument with administrative payroll records for 105,050 tenure-line faculty in 4,839 departments at 93 U.S. public universities from 2004 to 2026, linked to publication histories in OpenAlex. For each department, we estimate a separate pay equation using rank, contract basis, and seniority, then measure the Gini of the salary variation this local ladder cannot explain. Scholars in departments with greater unexplained pay dispersion publish more papers and receive more citations, but their work is less disruptive, less novel, and more conventional. Additional analyses show that compensation premiums above the ladder go disproportionately to scholars with broad collaborations and topical breadth. Although the design cannot fully separate treatment from selection, the evidence shows that inequality is not only a distributional outcome but also an evaluative structure, shaping which forms of knowledge are recognized, rewarded, and reproduced within organizations and communities.

papers.title: Large Pockels Effect in Multiaxial Ferroelectrics Induced by Polarization Reorientation
papers.abstract: Materials with large linear electro-optic (Pockels) effect have significant potential for fabricating energy-efficient photonic devices. Previous strategies have mostly relied on structural softness---associated with phase boundary, domain wall, or strain induced phase transition---to create large Pockels effect in ferroelectrics. In this Letter, we show that polarization reorientation in multiaxial ferroelectrics may create structural softness and thus induce large Pockels effect. By developing a phenomenological theory, we find that multiaxial ferroelectrics exhibit a hysteretic relationship between the azimuth angles of the polarization and the electric field, and a possible divergence of the linear electro-optic coefficient may occur at an appropriate polarization azimuth angle. This suggests a brand-new strategy for engineering large Pockels effect in multiaxial ferroelectrics. We perform first-principles simulations on several multiaxial ferroelectrics and predict that polarization reorientation can significantly enhance the electro-optic coefficients in monolayer SnSe and bulk KNbO$_3$. This validates the soundness of our strategy and emphasizes multiaxial ferroelectrics as promising platforms toward large Pockels effect.

papers.title: Strong Approximation of Stochastic Burgers Equations with Space-Time White Noise
papers.abstract: In this paper, we establish algebraic strong convergence rates for spectral Galerkin and fully discrete approximations of the stochastic Burgers equation driven by additive space--time white noise. For deterministic initial data in $H^1$, the spectral approximation is shown to be convergent in the spatial supremum norm, uniformly in time and in every finite probability moment, with order arbitrarily close to $1/2$. Furthermore, we prove that an accelerated fully tamed exponential method possesses spatial and temporal strong convergence orders arbitrarily close to $1/2$ and $1/4$ under a CFL condition. The key to our analysis is a polynomial stability estimate for the conservative Burgers flux, which allows us to control the nonlinear error using polynomial moment bounds for the exact and numerical solutions. To the best of our knowledge, these are the first algebraic strong convergence rates on the whole probability space for this equation with additive space--time white noise.

papers.title: DIVAL: Diffeomorphic Vector-Field Alignment for Nonholonomic Motion Planning
papers.abstract: Conventional vector-field-based motion planners for nonholonomic robots consist of two steps: first designing a nominal vector field and then controlling the robot to follow it to approach the target. However, a nonholonomic robot cannot follow the vector field instantaneously and may collide with obstacles, due to the inevitable mismatch between the robot's initial heading and the vector field's direction. This paper proposes a diffeomorphic vector-field alignment (DIVAL) method, which aligns the vector field's direction with the robot's initial heading so the robot can follow the vector field from the start. Specifically, the nominal vector field is locally reshaped by applying a diffeomorphic deformation to the workspace, such that the reshaped vector field has the same direction as the robot's heading at the initial position and coincides with the nominal vector field outside the deformed region. Since DIVAL eliminates the initial heading mismatch, the nonholonomic robot can maintain heading alignment with the reshaped vector field throughout the motion. This heading alignment further ensures that the robot preserves the nominal vector field's properties, including obstacle avoidance, convergence to the target, and smooth control signals. Numerical simulations provide vector-field-tracking baselines where the nominal vector fields are reshaped with DIVAL. Compared to the original baselines, the proposed method achieves collision-free convergence in all trials and avoids control discontinuities. Hardware experiments on a ground vehicle further demonstrate collision-free convergence across different targets and initial conditions under real-world disturbances.

papers.title: Regret Bounds for Quantum Linear Bandits
papers.abstract: We study $d$-dimensional quantum linear bandits with bounded rewards, where the learner selects an action and queries its quantum reward oracle or its inverse in each round. For general action sets, existing algorithms achieve regret $O(d^{3/2}\operatorname{polylog}(T))$ over $T$ rounds. Prior work established a lower bound of $\Omega(d\log(1+T/d))$, leaving open whether the $d^{3/2}$ dependence in the upper bound is necessary. We resolve this question by proving a minimax lower bound of $\Omega(d^{3/2}\log(1+T/d^{3/2}))$. To prove this result, we construct a family of hard instances in which the reward gap of each action is proportional to its squared distance from the optimal action. We establish a posterior Fisher information bound for adaptive quantum queries with quantum memory, relating the information acquired about the optimal direction to the regret incurred. Viewing each selected action as an estimate of the optimal direction, we use a matrix Cram\'er--Rao argument to derive a lower bound on expected regret. When the action set is fixed and has size $K$, we propose two phased elimination algorithms, Soft-G-Elim and QG-Elim. We adapt quantum phase estimation to construct SoftQME, a mean estimator with small bias and controlled tails. Soft-G-Elim estimates the mean reward of every surviving action from independent SoftQME outputs on the support of an experimental design. Controlling the bias and fluctuations of these estimates yields regret $O(d\log T\log(dT)\sqrt{\log(KT)})$, reducing the $\log(KT)\log\log(dT)$ factor in the previous regret bound to $\sqrt{\log(KT)}$. QG-Elim further reduces this factor to $\min\{\sqrt{\log(KT)},\sqrt d\}$.

authors.name: John C. S. Lui
authors.institution: Chinese University of Hong Kong, Shenzhen

papers.title: MetaCom: Meta Codebook Learning for Robust V2X Semantic Communications
papers.abstract: Collaborative perception in Vehicle-to-Everything (V2X) networks faces dual challenges: strictly limited bandwidth and channel impairments. Existing static quantization schemes often suffer from feature manifold drift caused by highly non-stationary traffic environments. To address this, we propose MetaCom, a robust digital semantic communication framework featuring a Meta-Codebook Learning paradigm. First, we introduce a Differentiable Quantized Semantic Communications (DQSemCom) module trained with perturbations induced by the simulated digital modulation and channel via Gumbel-Softmax relaxation. Building on this, we design a Bi-Level Meta-Evolution Mechanism (Bi-MEM) that treats manifold drift as a sequence of rapid adaptation tasks, aligning the codebook via data-level smoothing and parameter-level meta-updates. Furthermore, we validate MetaCom under AWGN, Rayleigh, and Rician fading channels. Experimental results demonstrate that MetaCom achieves superior trade-offs between perception precision and communication overhead, outperforming state-of-the-art methods by a significant margin under low-SNR conditions.
