papers.title: Finite bases for matrix semirings: transfer theorems and nilpotent counterexamples
papers.abstract: We first show that the nonfinitely based six-element ai-semiring $SR_6$ has finitely based full matrix semirings for every $n\ge2$, with a four-identity basis relative to the ai-semiring axioms. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first known example of this phenomenon. We then construct a countably infinite flat ai-semiring $P$ whose scalar and two-by-two matrix varieties are nonfinitely based, whereas its matrix varieties in sizes $n\ge3$ admit a five-identity relative basis. For both examples, the intervals from the scalar variety to each matrix variety of size at least two have cardinality $2^{\aleph_0}$. Finally, we establish transfer results for stronger forms of nonfinite basability and a finite-basis dichotomy for matrix semirings of size at least two over scalars with a genuine zero generating a locally finite variety: finite basability in the multiplicatively nilpotent case, and inherent nonfinite basability otherwise.

authors.name: Jun Jiao
authors.institution: Nanjing University of Aeronautics and Astronautics

papers.title: Rational layers in the low temperature expansion of the three-dimensional Ising model
papers.abstract: A low-temperature expansion orders Ising droplets by wall area, but droplets with different transverse spans can occur at the same order. We instead organize the zero-field simple-cubic model by the excess above the minimum wall area compatible with two prescribed spans. We prove that every fixed excess layer, including all logarithmic cover corrections and Euler inversion, has a rational bivariate generating function with denominator factors restricted to 1 - x, 1 - y and 1 - x - y. The proof compresses repeated coordinate cuts into bounded decorations and assigns each unbounded interval to one monotone chain. A finite controller then enforces induced contacts and arbitrary cover-color reuse. We explicitly assemble the complete layers of excess zero through three over all widths, attributing their known geometric constituents to earlier polyomino enumeration. Exact lattice checks corroborate the formulas. A certified low-temperature comparison shows a modest hybrid accuracy gain at one sampling point and higher evaluation cost. The result establishes an exact layer structure; summation over unbounded excess remains a separate problem.

papers.title: Enhancing Resolution and Reliability with Attention Mechanisms in Nuclear Accident Surrogate Modeling
papers.abstract: Severe accident (SA) analysis of nuclear power plants relies on system codes such as MAAP, whose computational cost limits large-scale applications including dynamic probabilistic safety assessment and reinforcement learning. This study proposes the Accident Binary-Continuous Transformer (ABC-Transformer), a decoder-only surrogate combining causal self-attention with temporal attention pooling. It jointly embeds continuous thermal-hydraulic variables with binary safety-system and severe accident management guideline (SAMG) states, enabling 5-minute-resolution forecasting over 72-hour transients. Trained on 11,000 MAAP simulations of a total loss of component cooling water scenario for the OPR1000, it achieved lower one-step teacher-forcing error than CNN and recurrent baselines at fine resolutions. Autoregressive reliability was characterized as a full per-scenario distribution over 1100 held-out scenarios. For scheduled-sampling (SS) training, the median $R^2$ is $0.947 \pm 0.006$ and $3.8 \pm 1.0$% of scenarios fail ($R^2<0$; mean $\pm$ SD over four training seeds), while errors accumulate with rollout length. A Mahalanobis self-distance computed from each surrogate rollout, before comparison with the MAAP reference, ranks these failures (ROC-AUC 0.895, reference seed). A threshold at the 40th percentile of calibration scores accepts $36.8 \pm 0.5$% of 550 evaluation scenarios, with no accepted rollout below $R^2 = 0$ for any seed, and routes the rest to MAAP.

authors.name: Jeongik Lee
authors.institution: Korea Advanced Institute of Science and Technology

authors.name: Joongoo Jeon
authors.institution: Pohang University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Reframing Video Inverse Tone Mapping as Blind Posterior Inference via Latent Luminance Supervision
papers.abstract: High-dynamic-range (HDR) displays are now common, but most video content, such as archival footage, broadcast material, and the output of generative video models, exists only in standard dynamic range (SDR). The need is sharpest for generated video, which has no HDR master at all and is graded alongside live-action and visual-effects material finished in HDR. Converting SDR to HDR means undoing a tone-mapping operation that was never recorded, and clipping destroys the radiance wherever it acts, so HDR recovery is a blind inverse problem. Methods built on generative video priors fill clipped regions with plausible structure, but their reconstructions are systematically biased: in every public method we test, saturated content leans too bright or too dark, and the direction of the lean moves with the tone operator behind the input. We call this failure the luminance error, measure both its magnitude and its sign, and make it the focus of this work. Reframing ITM as posterior inference under an unknown operator locates the failure in two places and yields two corrections. A fixed affine functional of the video-diffusion latent reads log-luminance without decoding; on that coordinate an asymmetric loss selects an expectile of the posterior, applied only where clipping leaves luminance unconstrained. We also synthesize training SDR through an explicit family of tone operators, so the model marginalizes over what the observation cannot show. Trained this way, our luminance error stays flatter across operators and smaller on average than any public method, and the full system achieves the best perceptual quality on all three benchmarks.

authors.name: Chang-Hoon Jeong
authors.institution: The Catholic University of Korea Bucheon St. Mary's Hospital

papers.title: When Evaluators of AI Agents Disagree: An Empirical Study of Native Scoring, LLM Judges, and Commit-Boundary Checks on tau2-bench
papers.abstract:
Agentic workflows, in which a large language model (LLM) calls tools to read and write data, are evaluated in two ways. Benchmarks compare the final state against a gold answer. Deployed services have none; an LLM judge reads the transcript and decides. Practice treats the two as interchangeable. This paper measures whether they are.
  We ran 2,160 episodes in tau2-bench's airline and retail domains and recorded every database write. We scored each episode four ways: native scoring against gold state, an LLM judge, that judge given the policy document, and the boundary evaluator, a minimal rule-based check of whether a write was expected against whether one occurred in the trace. Two annotators independently labeled 120 episodes for task correctness, policy compliance, and commitment correctness.
  The judge repeated its verdict 98.2% of the time but agreed with native scoring on 56.2%. In 11 episodes the agent executed a forbidden write. The judge passed 10 to 11, with or without the policy or transcript. A stronger judge still passed 6. The boundary evaluator, with no model call, caught all 11; no judge significantly exceeded it on human labels. Forbidden writes occurred in 11.1% of episodes without gates. Verification, correction, and safe-termination gates did not reduce them significantly. The traces show a candidate cause: the gates' evidence digest dropped the order status and customer authentication, so valid requests were rejected. The choice of evaluator decides the conclusion; the minimal check exposes failures the judges miss. Traces, code, prompts, and labels are released.

papers.title: A Cardiorespiratory Foundation Model Pretrained on Ten Physiological Signals for Perioperative and Critical Care
papers.abstract: Arterial, venous, pulmonary artery and intracranial pressures and ventilator waveforms guide decisions in operating rooms and intensive care units, yet foundation models for physiological waveforms have been built almost entirely on the electrocardiogram and photoplethysmogram. We present CARMEN, a single encoder pretrained without labels on ten cardiorespiratory waveforms (2.27 million modality-hours). CARMEN accepts any combination of co-recorded signals from 10 s to 5 min, and a conditioning mechanism, LSCNorm, restores the absolute signal level that normalization removes; without it, the AUROC for intraoperative hypotension fell from 0.894 to 0.780. Across 19 tasks from Korean and US cohorts, the frozen encoder outperformed supervised models on 12 of 15 and three foundation models, one general-purpose and two for biosignals, on 14 to 17 of 19, with none exceeding it on any task. Given the electrocardiogram or photoplethysmogram alone, it matched or exceeded signal-specific foundation models in most comparisons, and it retained its performance when channels were missing.

papers.title: Federated Class Incremental Learning: A Pseudo Feature Based Approach Without Exemplars
papers.abstract: Federated learning often assumes that data is fixed in advance, which is unrealistic in many real-world scenarios where new data continuously arrives, causing catastrophic forgetting. To address this challenge, we propose FCLPF (Federated Class Incremental Learning with Pseudo Features), a method that uses pseudo features generated from prototypes to mitigate catastrophic forgetting. Our approach reduces communication costs and improves efficiency by eliminating the need for past data and avoiding computationally heavy models like GANs. Experimental results on CIFAR-100 show that FCLPF achieves an average accuracy of 51.87% and an average forgetting of 9.62%, significantly outperforming existing baselines with an average accuracy of 47.72% and forgetting of 20.46%. On TinyImageNet, FCLPF achieves 37.56% accuracy and 3.14% forgetting, compared to the baselines' 27.69% accuracy and 24.46% forgetting, demonstrating the superior performance of FCLPF.

papers.title: Reduced-Complexity WMMSE Approach for Cell-Free Massive MIMO Systems With Finite-Capacity Fronthaul Links
papers.abstract: We propose a reduced-complexity weighted minimum mean squared error (R-WMMSE) framework for cell-free massive MIMO (CF-mMIMO) systems with finite-capacity fronthaul links. To maximize the system capacity, we need to jointly design beamforming vectors at distributed access points (APs) and fronthaul quantization noise covariances. Such a task would be addressed using conventional WMMSE algorithms and their variants. However, existing WMMSE-based methods either assume ideal infinite-capacity fronthaul links or incur high computational complexity when jointly optimizing the network-wide beamforming and fronthaul compression variables. To this end, the proposed method jointly optimizes beamforming and fronthaul compression by leveraging a sequential per-AP optimization strategy. Since each subproblem is efficiently solved via Lagrangian duality with closed-form updates, the overall computational complexity can be significantly reduced compared to the conventional WMMSE method. To further reduce hardware cost, we extend the R-WMMSE framework to hybrid analog-digital beamforming systems, tackling the joint design of digital beamforming, fronthaul compression, and analog beamforming. Numerical results show that the proposed scheme achieves performance nearly identical to that of the conventional WMMSE while reducing the runtime by over 99%.

authors.name: Hoon Lee
authors.institution: Ulsan National Institute of Science and Technology

papers.title: MiniPose: Miniature-Based Real Data Collection for 6D Pose Estimation of Large Industrial Pipe Segments
papers.abstract: 6-DOF pose estimation of large and heavy industrial objects, such as large piping systems in shipyards and structural components in petrochemical plants, remains relatively underexplored in robotic perception. Repeatedly repositioning large objects is physically and spatially demanding, making it difficult to acquire real training data with sufficient pose diversity. Synthetic data offer a scalable alternative, but faithfully reproducing real RGB-D observations, particularly the structured measurement errors of real depth sensors, remains difficult. We propose MiniPose, a practical pipeline for miniature-based real RGB-D data collection that addresses both the data-acquisition burden and the sim-to-real gap. We fabricate a scaled-down replica and capture RGB-D data of it in diverse poses using a real RGB-D camera. RGB images are used directly, while depth maps are converted to a geometrically consistent representation of the full-scale object via a simple inverse scaling transformation. This allows training to incorporate real appearance and sensor measurement characteristics that are difficult to reproduce using synthetic data alone. To examine whether the benefit depends on a particular network, we evaluate two RGB-D pose estimators with different formulations, PVN3D and RDPN6D. Mixing at most 1,000 miniature images per pipe type, less than 10\% of the training data, with 10,000 synthetic images improves the mean ADD-S AUC across pipe types over synthetic-only training for both estimators. A comparison with training on full-scale real data further suggests that miniature data can serve as a proxy where full-scale collection is difficult, reducing the data-collection burden for large industrial objects.

papers.title: Scaffolding Self-Transduction with Alignment Attention Mask for Aligner-Encoder ASR
papers.abstract: End-to-end ASR systems must jointly solve speech- text alignment and token prediction from sequence-level super- vision. We study this problem in Aligner-Encoder ASR, where alignment is performed inside encoder self-attention and can thus be directly intervened on with an attention mask. We use forced alignment to build an attention mask that confines selected encoder self-attention heads to a narrow window around the alignment path. The mask is faded out over training, leaving a deployable model with an unmodified inference architecture; alternatively, kept active at training and inference, it serves as an oracle that measures recognition performance once alignment is externally resolved. On LibriSpeech, the faded alignment mask improves test-clean/test-other WER from 3.9/6.4 to 3.5/5.9 over an Aligner baseline. The oracle masks are far stronger, reaching 1.2/2.9 WER, which can be thought of as an upper- bound accuracy in the 100M-class Conformer regime without an external language model. This indicates that alignment inference is a major bottleneck in Aligner-Encoder ASR, and suggests that improved alignment mechanisms might yield substantial accuracy gains for end-to-end ASR.

papers.title: Recompute or Restore? Host-Tier KV for Multi-Model Agent Workflows on a Static-Graph NPU Serving Stack
papers.abstract: Agent workflows issue dependent model calls that share long context prefixes, so serving them efficiently depends on reusing the key-value (KV) cache of those prefixes. On accelerators that compile model graphs ahead of time, however, the device KV budget is fixed, and prefixes evicted under load must be recomputed. Restoring them from host memory avoids this recomputation, but the transfer occupies the same engine thread as prefill and decode, so its benefit is not guaranteed. In this paper, we study when restoring beats recomputing on a commercial static-graph neural processing unit (NPU) stack (Rebellions ATOM+, vllm-rbln 0.10.2) that serves a Qwen3-8B planner on two cards and a Qwen3-0.6B executor on one. We first show that repeated prefill dominates planner work when default serving collapses: 89.5% of the executed planner prompt tokens had been materialized before. We then build a synchronous host-DRAM tier on the runtime's public KV copy calls, together with a scheduler-aware event model whose predictions are frozen before each test cohort. Experimental results show that the host tier raises workflow service-level objective (SLO) attainment from 22.8% to 100% and from 9.4% to 99.8% in the two tested overload conditions, and endpoint confirmation on two new seeds supports conservative load gains of 11.8% (chain) and 18.2% (fork), while mixed and bursty workloads remain seed-sensitive. The frozen model predicts median and 99th-percentile (P99) latency within its 15% tolerance in all 24 common-load conditions, including the 16-18% P99 increase that the tier causes for fork workflows, but it misorders three policy contrasts and overestimates the benefit of a cheaper store path (11% predicted against 3.1% measured). The trade-off therefore depends on runtime scheduling and transfer cost as well as cache capacity.

papers.title: Hybrid Precoding and Combining for O-RAN Massive MIMO Systems
papers.abstract: Recently, the radio access network (RAN) has been reimagined through open RAN (O-RAN) architecture to overcome the limitations of the traditional monolithic, black-box design philosophy and to leverage emerging technologies such as cloud computing, machine learning, and artificial intelligence. Although O-RAN disaggregates the base station (BS) into independent components to enable modular deployment, this paradigm introduces new challenges in signal processing and beamforming. In particular, beamforming in O-RAN must account for fronthaul link (FHL) capacity constraints, coordinated operation of multiple radio units (possibly from different vendors), and resource management, including transmit power allocation. To address these challenges, this work proposes novel beamforming techniques for a downlink multiuser hybrid massive multiple-input multiple-output system, in which hybrid architectures are deployed at both the users and at each BS radio unit. We formulate a sum-rate maximization problem incorporating transmit-power, unit-modulus, and FHL capacity constraints. The proposed algorithm integrates gradient descent and the Lagrange multiplier method to design analog beamformers and digital precoders, respectively, whereas digital combiners are designed to render the received streams parallel to each other. By avoiding computationally intensive operations such as eigenvalue and singular value decompositions, the proposed approach, as evidenced by simulation results, achieves superior performance with moderate computational complexity compared to existing benchmark schemes.

authors.name: Seraphin F. Kimaryo
authors.institution: Seoul National University of Science and Technology

authors.name: Kyungchun Lee
authors.institution: Seoul National University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Helping Hand: A Continuum Robotic Grasper for Traction in Single-Channel Endoscopic Submucosal Dissection
papers.abstract: Endoscopic submucosal dissection (ESD) is a minimally invasive approach for removing large polyps from the colon and offers many benefits compared to other surgical approaches. However, ESD is technically very challenging to perform, leading to limited adoption by physicians. We propose the Helping Hand, a two-segment continuum robotic grasper that, together with an electrosurgical knife, enables tissue traction and cutting within a single 3.7 mm working channel. We achieve this functionality by creating a slot at the base of the Helping Hand that lets the electrosurgical knife extend out, enabling countertraction and cutting through one instrument lumen. We evaluate the Helping Hand's workspace and its ability to provide traction forces from different starting configurations. Finally, we demonstrate the full workflow by isolating and removing tissue in an ex vivo chicken thigh, illustrating the potential for the Helping Hand to help improve ESD procedures.

papers.title: Human Capital in Context: What Employment Survival Reveals About Worker-Firm Match
papers.abstract: There is no best worker in general, only a best worker for a particular firm. We develop a measure of worker-firm match quality that treats fit as a property of the pair, learned from the survival of employment relationships. A two-tower neural network embeds workers, from their career histories and current positions, and firms, from their characteristics and business descriptions, into a common space, and match quality is the cosine similarity of the two vectors. The measure takes its functional form from the skill-weights model of firm-specific human capital, and its only estimated objective, a separation hazard, from the view of the job match as an experience good. Estimated on more than a billion person-periods covering 101 million workers and 8.4 million firms, a 0.1 increase in match quality lowers the odds of separation by 48%. About a quarter of the variance of match quality is specific to the worker-firm pair, which worker-, firm-, and occupation-level measures set to zero by construction. Workers earn more when better matched, especially early in a relationship, and firms whose workforces score higher grow faster, become more profitable, and are issued more, and more valuable, patents over the next five years than their industry peers. Because it scores pairs that never formed, the measure also predicts where movers go, and acquirers record a larger share of the price as goodwill when the target's workers would fit the acquirer better than they fit the target.

papers.title: Learning memory forces and bounding frequency errors in fractional Kuramoto grids
papers.abstract: Missing history creates two different demands on a forecaster for a fractional grid: predicting frequency accurately and reconstructing memory well enough to bound the prediction error. We connect these demands through the hereditary force that remains after an integral observation correction. A compact decoder retains the directions most relevant to that force, and an exact decomposition separates omitted directions from coefficient error. A response-trained linear predictor and neural refinement learn the coefficients for frequency prediction. A separate force reconstruction supplies the reference for a nonlinear energy bound for the specified finite relaxation model, accounting for numerical propagation defects and the difference between the reference and point forecasts. For the outage transients studied here, refinement improves on the linear predictor across the time steps and memory parameters tested. Replacing the noisy origin states reveals why this gain can coexist with greater memory reconstruction error: the learned correction partly compensates for observation error. Separating prediction from reconstruction enables frequency bounds in cases where the point predictor alone cannot support them. A critical radius compares calibrated uncertainty with the angle margin available along the reference trajectory, explaining both issuance and abstention. Under jointly exchangeable calibration and test events, the calibrated guarantee bounds the marginal probability of issuing an invalid envelope. Together, these results connect uncertainty about history outside the observation window to frequency forecasts and explicit conditions for bounding their errors.

authors.name: Hyunju Kim
authors.institution: Korea Advanced Institute of Science and Technology

papers.title: Optimal feature selection for firewall log analysis using Machine learning and Hybrid Metaheuristic algorithms
papers.abstract: Firewall log classification is important to monitor network traffic. Machine learning classifiers using network-related features have shown good results for this task, but high-dimensional features slow down classification. In this paper, we apply feature selection using bee swarm optimization with Q-learning-based local search (QBSO-FS) to the UCI Internet Firewall Data Set, together with random forest (RF), k-nearest neighbor (KNN), and Bernoulli na\"{\i}ve Bayes (Bernoulli NB) classifiers. The first version of this preprint selected and evaluated feature subsets on the same 5-fold cross-validation of the full data set, which contains 12.8\% exact duplicates; the reported scores are therefore optimistically biased. In this extended version, we re-evaluate the method with a leakage-free protocol: the data are split into training, validation, and test sets, features are selected using the validation set only, and accuracy and macro-averaged scores are measured once on the untouched test set, for both the raw data and a deduplicated, preprocessed version. On a single stratified split, QBSO-FS selects 5--7 features. The selected subsets clearly improve Macro-F1 over all features for KNN on both data sets and for RF on the deduplicated data (by 8--19 percentage points). For RF on the raw data and for Bernoulli NB, the differences (0.2--1.5 percentage points) may not hold for a different split. RF with 7 selected features reaches 99.90\% accuracy and 94.88\% Macro-F1 on the deduplicated data. On the same split, this exceeds our re-implementations of the deep neural network configurations of previous studies and the feature subset selected by particle swarm optimization in one of them, while the run time saved on this low-dimensional data set is small. These results suggest that the method can support automatic firewall log analysis, while evaluation over multiple splits remains future work.

papers.title: Optimal-Size Strong Connectivity Preservers under Two Edge Failures in Subcubic Time
papers.abstract: A $k$-edge-failure strong connectivity preserver of a directed graph on $N$ vertices is a spanning subgraph that has the same strongly connected components as the input after each set of at most $k$ edge deletions. The lower-bound construction of Baswana, Choudhary, and Roditty [BCR18], adapted to strong connectivity in [CC20], gives the previous best bound of $\Omega(2^kN)$ necessary edges. Hoppenworth, Saranurak, and Wang [HSW25] prove an $O(k4^kN\log N)$ upper bound, leaving a logarithmic gap for fixed $k$. We close this gap by giving an explicit strongly connected graph on $N=2^d$ vertices with $N-1+(N/2)\log_2N$ edges, every one of which is necessary in a two-failure preserver. Together with the upper bound of [HSW25], this proves that the optimal size in the worst case is $\Theta_k(N\log N)$ for every fixed $k\geq2$, whereas it is $\Theta(N)$ for $k=1$ [GIP20]. The same graph has a one-failure preserver with at most $3(N-1)$ edges. We also give a randomized algorithm that either returns a spanning subgraph or reports failure. For every fixed $c,\varepsilon>0$, with probability at least $1-N^{-c}$ it returns a correct preserver for $k=2$ with $O(N\log N)$ edges, in $\widetilde O(N^{(\omega+3)/2+\varepsilon})$ time and $\widetilde O(N^2)$ space. Here $\omega$ is the matrix multiplication exponent over a fixed finite field.

papers.title: Global-in-time dynamics of the pressureless Euler/incompressible non-Newtonian equations
papers.abstract: This paper addresses a two-phase fluid system on the periodic domain $\mathbb{T}^3$, consisting of the pressureless Euler equations and the incompressible non-Newtonian equations coupled through a drag force. We prove the global-in-time existence of strong solutions to this system for a certain class of stress tensors in the non-Newtonian fluid. Our proof combines a priori large-time behavior estimates for classical solutions with a bootstrapping argument on the $L^2$-Sobolev norms, which effectively handles the difficulties caused by the lack of dissipation in the density of the Euler equation.

papers.title: HyBridge: Bridge-Guided Self-Supervised Hyperbolic Hypergraph Representation Learning
papers.abstract: Hypergraphs capture groupwise relationships among multiple nodes and often exhibit tree-like structures. Although hyperbolic space is well suited for modeling such structures, simply extending existing hypergraph representation learning (HRL) methods to hyperbolic space does not consistently improve performance. In this paper, we investigate the relationship between node structural properties and hyperbolic embedding radii and find that bridge nodes tend to lie closer to the center in graphs, whereas this relationship is not consistently observed in hypergraphs. We further find that conventional bridge score estimation may fail to capture the groupwise connectivity of hypergraphs. Motivated by these findings, we propose HyBridge, a self-supervised hyperbolic HRL framework that (1) estimates node bridge scores by considering the external connectivity of individual hyperedges, (2) learns node and hyperedge embeddings through hyperbolic hypergraph encoding, (3) guides node radial positions according to their bridge scores, and (4) employs contrastive learning to preserve node discriminability. Extensive experiments on 10 real-world hypergraphs demonstrate that HyBridge outperforms 22 competing methods, achieving performance improvements of up to 9.82% in node classification. For reproducibility, we provide the code at https://anonymous.4open.science/r/HyBridge/.

papers.title: HeMeR: Heterogeneous Memory Reconciliation for Embodied Agents via Structured KV Reuse
papers.abstract: Embodied agents make decisions by combining information from heterogeneous memory modules, including declarative memory for explicit knowledge, procedural memory for learned routines, and working memory for current observations. During interaction, the memory contents required for decision making change with the agent's state, goal, and task progress, while many contents remain shared across consecutive decisions. However, existing memory modules are typically accessed through separate interfaces, so each updated memory context is often processed as a new input to the foundation model. This prevents selective key-value (KV) cache reuse for unchanged memory contents and forces full KV cache recomputation even when much of the memory context remains valid. We introduce HeMeR, an inference framework that performs KV reconciliation between dynamically updated memory contexts and reusable KV states. HeMeR tracks declarative, procedural, and working memory contents across action decisions, preserves KV states for unchanged contents, and reconciles only the KV states affected by memory-content updates. This enables efficient and stable inference as memory contents evolve during interaction. We evaluate HeMeR on ALFWorld, Habitat, and real-world robotic deployments requiring coordinated use of heterogeneous memory contents. In the real-world setting, HeMeR achieves 83.20% task success and reduces per-step inference time from 2.94 to 1.87 seconds compared with MemRL, while preserving compatible KV states as task progress updates the memory context.

authors.name: Jinwoo Jang
authors.institution: Pohang University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Probing the Dirac Quantum Geometry in Quantum Magnets from Polarized Raman Spectroscopy
papers.abstract: Magnetic Raman spectroscopy is sensitive to quasiparticle quantum geometry, yet microscopic Raman vertices generally prevent a direct geometric interpretation. Here we establish a symmetry-based extraction principle for two-dimensional quantum magnets with two-band quasiparticle excitations. Opposite circular-polarization spectra separate vertex-weighted quantum-metric and Berry-curvature contractions. Near a $C_3$-symmetric massive Dirac valley, symmetry fixes the leading Raman and velocity doublets up to a common scale, allowing the unknown Raman strength and intensity normalization to cancel from their spectral ratio. For an inversion-related pair of massive Dirac cones, the normalized counter-circular Raman asymmetry at frequency threshold $\Omega_{\rm th}$ is fixed by the Chern number and follows a universal near-threshold frequency scaling. This yields a local spectroscopic readout without absolute-intensity calibration or frequency integration. We demonstrate the principle for Majorana fermions in the field-induced honeycomb Kitaev spin liquid and for topological magnons in a honeycomb ferromagnet, and identify the conditions for resolving it experimentally.

authors.name: Doh Young Kim
authors.institution: Hallym University Kangnam Sacred Heart Hospital

papers.title: Recovering Small Perturbations of a Known Inclusion from One Mixed Steklov Eigenpair with Local Boundary Data
papers.abstract: We study the recovery of small normal displacements of a known inclusion from a single mixed Steklov eigenpair. The data consist of the eigenvalue and the eigenfunction trace on any nonempty open subset of the fixed outer boundary, with the eigenfunction normalized using only that subset. For an inner Dirichlet condition, we prove that the linearized measurement map is injective at every simple eigenvalue. A compatible adjoint identity yields a reconstruction method with a conditional stability estimate on any fixed finite-dimensional space of smooth displacements. For the principal Dirichlet eigenpair, the same local data also determine the inclusion uniquely among sufficiently small normal graphs. In a three-dimensional concentric shell, the eigenvalue determines the mean displacement at first order, while spherical harmonics diagonalize the remaining full-boundary trace map. The singular values decay exponentially with harmonic degree, yielding logarithmic conditional stability under a Sobolev prior. Numerical experiments using the perturbed geometry illustrate the quadratic linearization error and the deterioration of conditioning as the observed patch shrinks. For an inner Neumann condition, we prove linearized injectivity at every positive simple eigenvalue.

papers.title: CADET: Construction of PCB Routing Instances with Executable Demonstrations
papers.abstract: Printed circuit board (PCB) routing is the stage of physical layout that finds paths connecting the placed pads of each net. Public datasets in this domain are few, and most contain only the final states of routed boards, not demonstrations of the electronic design automation (EDA) engine actions that produce them. To close this gap, we propose CADET (Constructing executAble Demonstrations for Engine-grounded Training), which jointly generates synthetic boards and demonstrations built from EDA engine actions. The resulting RouteDemos provides 100,000 synthetic boards routed with zero design rule violations (DRVs), together with their demonstrations. Their distributions over 17 statistics resemble those of 142 real reference boards. CADET trains a routing policy on these demonstrations with behavior cloning and fine-tunes it with reinforcement learning (RL). On real test boards, the policy raised the rate of complete DRV-free routing from 38.0% to 67.2% over an RL-only baseline. This rate was comparable to that of the open-source autorouter FreeRouting and exceeded those of the other baselines, including GPT-6 Astra. We release the dataset and its generation code as open source at https://github.com/LGAI-Research/CADET.

authors.name: Junseok Park
authors.institution: Korea Advanced Institute of Science and Technology

papers.title: Dynamic $k$-Median with Worst-Case Update Time and Recourse
papers.abstract: We study fully dynamic metric $k$-median under unit-weight client insertions and deletions. After each update, the algorithm must maintain at most $k$ centers chosen from the current client locations. We give a randomized constant-factor approximation algorithm with $\widetilde O(k)$ worst-case update time and $O((1+\log\Delta)^3)$ worst-case center recourse, where $\Delta$ is the aspect ratio of the underlying metric space. The approximation guarantee holds simultaneously over any prescribed finite adaptive update sequence with high probability, while the update time and recourse bounds hold on every execution. We also obtain the same asymptotic guarantees for metric $k$-means.

papers.title: Learning When Diffusion Language Models Should Regenerate
papers.abstract: Remasking allows diffusion language models to revisit generated text, but effective correction requires knowing when and what to revise. Our diagnosis on Sudoku reveals two gaps. Hidden states contain error information that token confidence does not reliably expose, and remasking an isolated error usually reproduces it when the surrounding context remains fixed. These findings motivate DiVR , a verifier that predicts whether a partially generated sequence will reach a correct answer. Trained on the final correctness of the model's own trajectories, DiVR decides when to regenerate a block and which alternative to retain, while the generator itself stays unchanged. On five reasoning benchmarks with LLaDA-8B-Base, DiVR raises the average accuracy of the fine-tuned generator from 35.3\% to 43.4\% at $1.9$-$3.5\times$ the cost of greedy decoding, above search baselines that use $3.8$-$7.4\times$. It also complements post-training such as supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning, and generalizes to other generators, including Dream.

papers.title: Together Compiler: Continual Compilation for AI Inference
papers.abstract: Today's AI workloads are rapidly changing: new models are released more often, model architectures are increasingly diverse, and traffic distributions change frequently. The challenge we face at Together AI is continual optimization for these changing workloads. Compiling a deployment into an optimized forward pass is a challenge that is well-suited for agent hill-climbing. Existing systems struggle with continual compilation due to a tradeoff between measurement throughput and fidelity. Many systems use agents to optimize individual kernels from the inference forward pass using offline benchmarks, but timings are low-fidelity because of data-dependent behavior in primitives like mixture-of-experts (MoE). On the other hand, systems use agents to directly optimize end-to-end engines but suffer from slow engine launch times. To address these challenges, we build Together Compiler (TKCC), the first truly continual agent loop designed for AI inference optimization. To address the throughput-fidelity tradeoff, we propose: (1) a Tiered Persistent Engine that decouples engine launch overheads from forward pass computation; (2) a cost model to select the parallelism configurations that seed the optimization process. We also conduct extensive ablations on agent context management and present our insights on deploying TKCC in production. TKCC outperforms highly-optimized hand-written Megakernels on the Llama 1B workhorse workload by up to 1.7x and the best open source engines on the latest frontier models (Kimi K3, GLM 5.3, MiniMax M3.1 Flash, DeepSeek v4.1 Flash) across hardware platforms by up to 2.6x higher TPS on the InferenceX benchmark. TKCC also sets the state-of-the-art performance at batch size 1, with 1111 TPS on M3.1 Flash and 1205 TPS on DeepSeek v4.1 Flash. Finally, TKCC generalizes beyond frontier language model inference. TKCC serves trillions of tokens across our production fleet.

authors.name: Venkata Hasith Vattikuti
authors.institution: The University of Texas at Austin

papers.title: Joint Null-Space Projection for Data-Free Model Merging
papers.abstract: Merging independently fine-tuned checkpoints into a single multi-task model requires no data, no labels, and no gradient steps. In practice the task vectors of different tasks interfere, and the standard remedies--averaging, magnitude pruning, sign election--operate entry by entry, ignoring that each delta induces a low-dimensional update on the hidden features it acts upon. We recast merging as a subspace interference problem. For every two-dimensional weight tensor we take the top-r right-singular subspace of each task's delta--the input directions along which that task moves the representation most--and remove from each task vector the component lying in the union of the other tasks' subspaces. The resulting Joint Null-Space Projection (JNSP) is closed-form and order-independent, needs no forward pass, and is defined entirely by the checkpoint set. On eight CLIP image-classification tasks JNSP merges ViT-B/16 experts to 89.45% average accuracy without using a single image, 11.88 points above the strongest parameter-wise training-free baseline (TIES-Merging, 77.57%), 14.22 above Task Arithmetic, and 0.98 above WUDI's data-free consensus merge (88.47%). The gain holds across three backbones on the independently trained TALL release (+10.8, +12.6, +9.1 over TIES for ViT-B/16, ViT-B/32, ViT-L/14) and replicates there at 89.20%; controls confirm the source--a single shared subspace instead of per-task ones loses 2.9 points, and a sequential variant collapses to 69.6%. On RoBERTa-large the same projection underperforms plain task arithmetic, which we report rather than hide. Code is available at https://github.com.

authors.name: Tian Xia
authors.institution: Jiangsu University of Science and Technology

papers.title: VWEN: A Curated Small Language Model for Vietnamese Paraphrasing
papers.abstract: We present VWEN, a 0.8B-parameter model for Vietnamese paraphrasing at a requested level of change and for five related tasks: generating several paraphrases, simplification, gist, register transfer and paraphrase judgement. VWEN is Qwen3.5-0.8B fine-tuned on about 7k samples chosen by a four-stage pipeline: rules and deduplication, a bidirectional entailment filter, a divergence score that assigns low and high paraphrase levels, and selection for coverage and instruction-following difficulty. We compare it with paraphrase-only recipes from the same pipeline and with training on the ViSP corpus under matched and larger step budgets. On high-divergence paraphrasing, VWEN reaches a success rate (requested level reached and meaning preserved) of 0.61 against 0.46 for the ViSP model at matched compute, a difference that holds on inputs resembling ViSP. Given four times more training examples, the ViSP model closes the gap on such inputs but not on questions, which ViSP lacks and which it often turns into statements. Across all comparisons the entailment filter is the most effective stage. Training on paraphrases alone erases abilities of the base model that the multi-task data preserves.

authors.name: Sang Quang Nguyen
authors.institution: Posts and Telecommunications Institute of Technology

papers.title: On the uniform algebras generated by powers of the coordinates and smooth functions on compact subsets of $\Bbb C^N$
papers.abstract: Let $K\subset\Bbb C^N$ be compact and let $f=(f_1,\dots,f_N)$ be a smooth map on a neighbourhood of $K$. We give sufficient conditions for the algebra generated by $z_1^{m_1},\dots,z_N^{m_N}$ and $f_1,\dots,f_N$ (or by all monomials of degree $n$ and $f_1,\dots,f_N$) to be dense in $C(K)$. We appropriately extend the techniques developed in our previous works [3,4,6] and [8] for algebras of functions on the complex plane to tackle the problem in the several-variable setting. More precisely, the argument separates a purely algebraic reduction, in which the rotated graphs are glued one coordinate at a time, from the study of the single graph of $f$. For the latter we give an exact computation of the Levi form of $|w-f|^{2p}$, which yields a Hermitian matrix criterion on the polynomial hull of the graph; a criterion by peak functions that removes the invertibility hypothesis from a theorem of Preskenis; a division theorem for $f_j=\bar k_jh_j$ with degenerate holomorphic factors $h_j$; and a treatment of the singular set $\{\det(\partial f_i/\partial\bar z_j)=0\}$, which in several variables is not finite. The angle $\pi/m_j$ in the reduction is shown to be sharp.

papers.title: Rigidity of time changes of $\mathfrak{sl}_2$-induced unipotent flows on finite volume quotients
papers.abstract: We study the rigidity phenomenon of the time changed unipotent flows on general Lie groups. Under some spectral gap assumptions, we prove that every ergodic nonsplitting $\mathfrak{sl}_2$-induced unipotent flow on a finite volume quotient space $\mathbf{G}/\Gamma$ is time changed rigid. We also prove that for $\mathfrak{sl}_2$-induced unipotent flow, the splitting condition is equivalent to loosely Kroneckerness. Our result in particular applies to $\mathbf{G}=\mathbf{S}\ltimes\mathbf{N}$, where $\mathbf{S}$ is the identity component of a real semisimple linear algebraic group without compact factors and $\mathbf{N}$ is simply connected and connected nilpotent Lie group. These are extensions of [KVW21,LW25].

papers.title: Subgroup distortion in free-by-cyclic groups with linearly growing monodromy
papers.abstract: Let $G=F\rtimes_\phi\mathbb Z$ be the mapping torus of a linearly growing UPG automorphism $\phi$ of a finitely generated free group $F$. We compute the distortion of every finitely generated subgroup $H$ of $G$, and we show that it is linear, quadratic or exponential. In contrast, for each $d\ge2$, Dison and Riley constructed an automorphism of polynomial degree $d$ whose mapping torus contains a free subgroup with distortion equivalent to the Ackermann function $A_{d+1}$, which grows faster than every iterated exponential function. Using the natural splitting of $G$ over $\mathbb Z^2$ subgroups and its topological representative, we associate to $H$ a family of \emph{horizontal components}, together with \emph{dilation homomorphisms} defined from slopes along these components. We prove that $H$ is undistorted in $G$ if and only if every horizontal component of $H$ consists of only one piece. Otherwise, the distortion of $H$ is quadratic if all dilation homomorphisms are trivial, and exponential if one of them is nontrivial. Along the way, we show that the distortion of $H$ is determined, up to superadditive closure, by the distortions of the stabilizers of its horizontal components.

papers.title: Contain, Conform, Compare (Extended Version): A Red-Teamed Evaluation Kit for Small Coding Agents and the Full Record of Its Experiments
papers.abstract: A hosted score in the Gemma 4 Developer Agent competition is one noisy number, so development needs a local evaluator that is fast, safe for agent-written code, and matching the hosted scorer's prompts. drydock-eval evaluates a small coding agent (Gemma 4 E4B) at about 250 runs per hour on one RTX 5090. Contain runs each job in a fresh container without network and passed 200 scripted escape tests; conform provides eight checks that compare a local stack's requests with the scorer's configuration, down to rendered tokens; compare provides paired statistics that respect repository clusters. AI agents built and attacked the kit; a human owner approved machine use and release. This extended version repeats the short paper and adds the full record of the experiments made with and around the kit: 9,660 rows of agent runs, 2,494 grading controls and 72 serving measurements, all released. On four L4 GPUs the 31B model decodes 38.1 tokens per second in one stream and E4B 105.8. Six configurations of a 31B agent solved between 37 and 44 of 70 development tasks, and no pairwise difference was detected. A pre-registered five-arm experiment (231 tasks, 4,620 jobs) measured four prompt divergences: no E4B solve-rate change was detected (largest estimate -2.1 points, 95% interval -4.4 to +0.4). Three changes of the E4B agent led their screens by +1.0 to +6.2 points; each was then tested once on new tasks under a frozen pass rule, and none was confirmed (gains -0.35, -0.39 and +4.10 points). The unchanged baseline, run again on the same 128 tasks, moved by 1.17 points, and 65% of these tasks were solved in none of eight runs. Prompts and agent bundles are withheld; every run-level result is public.

papers.title: Predicting transcriptional interactions with GrnPFN
papers.abstract: Combinatorial therapies offer opportunities to improve treatment efficacy and overcome therapeutic resistance, but their rational design requires understanding how combined interventions interact beyond their individual effects. Combined genetic and chemical perturbations can elicit nonadditive transcriptional responses, yet the vast number of possible combinations limits experimental characterization. Predicting these interactions is particularly challenging when few or no combinations have been measured. Here we present GrnPFN, a prior-data fitted network that predicts nonadditive transcriptional responses to combinations from single-perturbation profiles. Pretrained on simulated screens generated from random gene-regulatory networks, GrnPFN incorporates measured combinations through in-context learning without retraining. We evaluated GrnPFN in single-cell screens spanning CRISPR activation, RNA knockdown and drug combinations, using separate cells to construct model inputs, training targets and test targets. Without measured combinations in the target screen, GrnPFN outperformed gradient boosting trained on other screens. With limited combination measurements, it outperformed kernel ridge regression fitted to the same measured pairs. These advantages extended to an additional screen combining CRISPR interference with a drug. Our results demonstrate that pretraining on simulated regulatory networks enables prediction of nonadditive transcriptional interactions across perturbation modalities when experimental measurements are scarce.

authors.name: Haihui Zhang
authors.institution: Jiangxi University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Can We Ignore Data Dependence in Inference Implementation? A Positive Answer for Regression Discontinuity Designs
papers.abstract: In empirical economics, regression discontinuity design (RDD) inference is commonly based on asymptotic normality under an independence assumption, but the running variables or disturbances may exhibit unknown and complex dependence. We first rigorously identify a fundamental dilemma for this conventional practice. To address it, we propose a validity recovery procedure that redefines the roles of bias and stochastic calibration, thereby decoupling data dependence from stochastic calibration. Taking the independence-assumption-based confidence interval as our inferential anchor, our procedure restores its validity while preserving its asymptotic leading constant, even when the data are dependent. For fixed-design RDD based on local linear regression, our intervals achieve asymptotically exact nominal coverage and, compared with the anchor, exploit higher-order smoothness without enlarging the asymptotic variance constant, attaining the minimax-optimal shrinking rates up to a mild factor, such as $\sqrt{\log T})$. The procedure requires neither specific dependence frameworks (e.g., mixing or physical dependence) nor dependence-modeling techniques (e.g., long-run variance estimation). For random-design RDD, under more specific dependence assumptions, we derive the rate-explicit coverage error at each nominal level and characterize the trade-off between this rate and interval length. Moreover, modeling dependence becomes an optional enhancement that can further enable validity recovery and improve finite-sample coverage, while averaging over repeated calibrations stabilizes the randomized center and protects against undercoverage in finite samples without increasing interval length. In short, under mild dependence and moment conditions, our procedure makes data independence an implementation default rather than a validity requirement. Simulations support the theoretical results.

papers.title: Averaging Principle and Uniform Large Deviations for Time-Dependent Slow-Fast Systems via Young-Rough Integration
papers.abstract: The main aim of this work is to investigate the limiting behavior and asymptotic properties of time-dependent slow-fast stochastic dynamical systems. The slow component is driven by a stochastic process with H\"older-continuous paths of regularity greater than 1/2, while the fast component is driven by a Brownian rough path. We introduce a novel Young-rough integration framework tailored to such systems and establish well-posedness results, providing the analytical foundation for further asymptotic analysis. Building on this framework, we employ Khasminskii's time-discretization method to establish the strong convergence of the slow component to the solution of the corresponding averaged equation in the L^p-sense. Furthermore, when the driving noise in the slow equation is specified as a fractional Brownian motion, we apply the weak convergence approach to establish a uniform large deviation principle for the slow component, uniformly over compact sets of initial conditions, in the H\"older topology.

papers.title: Matching statistics in regular hypergraphs and applications
papers.abstract:
For fixed $k\ge3$, we determine the first sublinear correction to the logarithm of the matching partition function for a class of $n$-vertex $d$-regular $k$-uniform hypergraphs, uniformly for activities in each fixed compact interval of $(0,\infty)$.Our hypotheses include every regular linear hypergraph of polynomial degree and a class of nonlinear hypergraphs described by higher codegrees and intersection patterns, which we introduce here. The weighted counting estimate implies an averaged version of Kahn's conjecture: under the uniform measure, the expected number of uncovered vertices is $(1+o(1))nd^{-1/k}$, with concentration and large deviations on this scale. The proof combines a novel variant of random greedy counting, based on short stages and regular completions, with a new entropy method that uses intersection patterns to control reconstruction after deleting matching edges.
  We highlight the following applications. (i) Partial transversals in Latin squares. Every Latin square of order $n$ has $(n/e^2)^n\exp((3+o(1))n^{2/3})$ partial transversals. Also, almost all partial transversals have $(1+o(1))n^{2/3}$ missing cells.
  (ii) Linear $3$-uniform hypergraphs. There are $(n/e^2)^{n^2/6}\exp((1/2+o(1))n^{5/3})$ linear $3$-uniform hypergraphs on $[n]$, and almost all have $n^2/6-(1/6+o(1))n^{5/3}$ edges.
  (iii) Matroids of fixed rank. For each fixed $r\ge4$, the number $m(n,r)$ of rank-$r$ matroids on $[n]$ satisfies $\log m(n,r)=\frac{n^{r-1}}{r!}(\log n-r+1)+\left(\frac1{(r-1)!}+o(1)\right)n^{r-1-1/r}$, refining the estimates of van der Hofstad, Pendavingh and van der Pol.

papers.title: How to arrange four points in the plane
papers.abstract:
Arranging points in the plane appears to be an elementary geometric problem, yet it is deeply rooted in statistical physics. As a toy model, we consider the configuration of four points. We completely classify the minimal configurations of four points interaction energy in $\R^2$ under the general Lennard-Jones potentials $V(r)=r^{-p}-br^{-q}$, where $p>q>0$ and $b\in\R$. We find that there is a threshold curve \[
  D_{p,q}=2^{-(p-q)/2}\Bigl(1+\frac{p-q}{q+2}\bigl(1+2^{-(q+2)/2}\bigr)\Bigr) \] to determine the minimal shapes. The main results can be stated concisely as follows: consider $\min\sum_{1\le i<j\le4}\bigl(|x_i-x_j|^{-p}-b|x_i-x_j|^{-q}\bigr)$. For $b\le0$, the minimizer does not exist. For $b>0$, the minimizer is unique up to rotation and translation. Furthermore, the minimizer is \[
  \begin{cases}
  \text{a square},&\hbox{if}\;\; D_{p,q}\ge1,
  \text{a rhombus with angle }\theta\in(\pi/3,\pi/2),&\hbox{if}\;\; D_{p,q}<1.
  \end{cases} \]

papers.title: Where Language-Model Vocabulary Rose on Stack Exchange
papers.abstract: Stack Overflow banned answers generated by ChatGPT five days after the model's release, and many other Stack Exchange sites announced similar rules. I measure the vocabulary of the answers posted afterwards, 3.8 million answers on 170 sites from 2019 to 2024. A fixed list of 56 words that language models overuse rose about 14 percent above its pre-2023 trend, while the highest of 1,000 frequency-matched lists of ordinary words rose about 7 percent. In a screen of 15 site traits measured before the release, the strongest predictor of where the rise happened was the share of answers that received a body edit within 30 days of posting. On the least edited third of sites the list rose about 29 percent relative to matched controls, and on the most edited third it did not change. The gradient is also present among answers that were never edited. It follows the share of answers edited by their own authors, and the share edited by others adds little once that share is held fixed. Use of the model is unobserved, so these results cannot separate lower use on sites with a high self-edit share from any effect of editing on what the vocabulary records. Any vocabulary-based estimate for the network as a whole therefore pools sites where the marker vocabulary rose sharply with sites where it did not change.

papers.title: Fast circular convolution with periodic kernels
papers.abstract: We study the periodic circular convolution or PCC, where the convolution kernel depends periodically on the spatial location. We introduce two fast algorithms to compute the PCC that rely on the Discrete Fourier Transform. One of the algorithms reveals that the matrix representation of the PCC is unitarily equivalent to a block diagonal matrix, which facilitates the analysis of PCCs and operations such as their product and inversion. We present two sample applications. One to deconvolve the action of an optical system whose point spread function depends periodically in space. The second is to compute dispersion relations for a periodic chain of masses.

papers.title: Self-similar cusp formation in a large class of nonlocal transport equations
papers.abstract: We prove finite-time gradient blow-up with sharp $C^{(5-b)/(b+3)}$ H\"older regularity for a class of nonlocal transport equations extending the $b$-family, for all real $1<b<5$. This class includes the Camassa--Holm and Degasperis--Procesi equations and, after rescaling, the generalized hyperelastic-rod wave equation. In the blow-up regime, the nonlocal equations reduce at leading order to the generalized Hunter--Saxton (gHS) equation with parameter $\ell=2/(b-1)$, whose self-similar scaling and corresponding profiles depend on $\ell$. Consequently, standard approaches tailored to a fixed self-similar profile cannot be applied directly. To handle this parameter dependence, we develop a general framework for self-similar singularity formation in evolution equations whose leading-order dynamics are governed by the gHS family. The key ingredient is a family of profile inequalities established for all real $\ell>1/2$, which we combine with a generalized maximum principle to close a parameter-dependent bootstrap argument. We identify model-specific hypotheses adapted to this framework, under which this argument yields the required stability estimates. This leads to a general theorem on singularity formation, which we apply to the entire class of nonlocal equations, thereby establishing finite-time gradient blow-up and sharp H\"older regularity. The theorem can also be applied to other evolution equations once the corresponding model-specific hypotheses are verified, without repeating the profile analysis or the common stability argument.

authors.name: Yunjoo Kim
authors.institution: Korea Advanced Institute of Science and Technology
