papers.title: Gamma-positivity of support enumerators of preorders
papers.abstract: The support enumerator of a finite preorder counts lattice points of its polytope by support size. We prove Athanasiadis and Chapoton's conjecture that this polynomial is $\gamma$-positive. On an $n$-element preorder, the $j$th $\gamma$-coefficient counts points of the preorder polytope with entries in $\{0,1,2\}$, coordinate sum $n$, and exactly $j$ entries equal to $2$. Oh's correspondence for transversal matroids and Hall's theorem give a formula that records the support itself. For arbors, a separate proof gives a refinement by coordinate sum.

papers.title: Countable dynamical systems with a dense orbit
papers.abstract:
We study countable dynamical systems with a dense orbit. Given an infinite compact metric countable space $X$, we show that $\mathcal{DO}(X)$, the collection of continuous functions on $X$ to itself admitting a dense orbit, is always nonempty. We then classify the systems in $\mathcal{DO}(X)$ up to topological conjugacy in terms of the second Cantor--Bendixson derivative $X^{(2)}$: if $X^{(2)} = \emptyset$ then all systems in $\mathcal{DO}(X)$ are mutually conjugate, while if $X^{(2)} \neq \emptyset$ then $\mathcal{DO}(X)$ contains $2^{\aleph_0}$ pairwise nonconjugate systems. The proof of the latter relies on a gluing construction for countable dynamical systems with a dense orbit, which is of independent interest. We also show that $\mathcal{DO}(X)$ is nowhere dense in $C(X,X)$ with the compact-open topology.
  We also study the Ellis semigroup $E(X,f)$ of a countable dynamical system. We characterize, under the assumption that $|\omega(x,f)| = 1$ for each $x \in X^{(1)}$, when the nontrivial functions of $E(X,f)$ are continuous. In particular, for the family constructed on spaces with $|X^{(2)}| \geq 2$, every nontrivial function of the Ellis semigroup is discontinuous.

papers.title: Surface evolution under conformal map and linearized energy-stable parametric finite element methods
papers.abstract: In this paper, we aim to develop a linearized, energy-stable, second-order-in-time parametric finite element method without Lagrange multipliers for surface evolution equations on surfaces with or without boundaries, including (volume-preserving) mean curvature flow and surface diffusion. We first reformulate the original equations into a new unified form in which the tangential motion is determined by requiring the flow map to be conformal. Based on this new formulation, we present a family of parametric finite element schemes that employ a linearized Euler or Crank-Nicolson discretization in time. We prove the existence and uniqueness of the resulting linear system, as well as the energy stability of the schemes. Our discrete methods can be applied to general surfaces although the second-order scheme may degenerate to first-order accuracy in certain cases. Numerical results verify the robustness of our method and demonstrate its ability to preserve mesh quality.

papers.title: Macroscopic $L^\infty$ bounds for the homogeneous Landau--Coulomb equation
papers.abstract: We establish an instantaneous global $L^\infty(\R^3)$ bound at positive times for smooth, rapidly decaying solutions to the three-dimensional spatially homogeneous Landau equation with Coulomb potential, where the upper bound depends solely on the initial mass, momentum, energy, and entropy. This resolves an open problem posed by Golding, Gualdani, and Loher \cite{GGL} without requiring any initial higher velocity moments, Fisher information, or Lebesgue integrability. The proof builds on two main analytical ingredients. First, we establish the instantaneous generation of the negatively weighted Fisher information with weight $\la{v}^{-1}$. On the lifted two-particle phase space, we compare the separable weight matrix against a collision-invariant pair weight and control the rotational commutator near the diagonal via the quadratic local mass decay supplied by the conserved energy, closing a Riccati differential inequality at the second-moment threshold. Second, to overcome the $\la{v}^{-3}$ radial degeneracy of the diffusion matrix at large velocities, we prove a truncated anisotropic mixed Nash inequality on upper level sets of the density that recovers longitudinal regularity from two transverse Fisher directions and the nonlinear high-density part of the Coulomb entropy dissipation. Localizing this functional inequality to radially aligned velocity cells with the critical weight $\la{v}^{3/2}$ and coupling it with a weighted truncated entropy identity across nested exterior domains yields a superlinear De Giorgi recurrence that bounds the velocity tail uniformly in $\R^3$.

authors.name: Lingda Xu
authors.institution: Hetao Institute of Mathematics and Interdisciplinary Sciences

papers.title: Modular representations of reductive $p$-adic groups and the kernel of the trace map
papers.abstract:
The trace map of a finite group gives a perfect duality between conjugacy classes and irreducible complex representations. For reductive $p$-adic groups, an analogous duality holds due to the classical work of Bernstein, Deligne and Kazhdan. In this paper, we study this trace map for modular representations of reductive $p$-adic groups in characteristic $\ell\ne p$. The failure of the duality is measured by the kernel of the trace map on the cocenter of the ``big Hecke algebra''.
  Our main theorem expresses this kernel in terms of corresponding kernels for finite-dimensional Hecke algebras associated with normalizers of parahoric subgroups in suitable central quotients of Levi subgroups, reducing a problem on infinite-dimensional algebras to finite-dimensional ones. We also show that projective representations provide a natural complementary subspace on the compact part of the cocenter.
  For affine Hecke algebras, we prove the naive-kernel conjecture over algebraically closed fields of arbitrary characteristic and for arbitrary compatible nonzero parameters, including unequal parameters and roots of unity.

papers.title: Incidence Geometry of Local Maxima: Howe Duality and Branching
papers.abstract: For a finite-dimensional unitary representation of a finite or compact group, consider the mean squared matrix coefficient on the unit sphere. Its local maxima are the vectors generating irreducible cyclic subrepresentations. We show that for compatible group actions this variational picture retains the incidence structure of representation theory. For two commuting actions, intersections of projectivized local-maximal components recover the weighted support graph of the product representation, including its multiplicity spaces; Howe duality is the multiplicity-one matching case. More generally, for pairwise commuting actions, and for subgroup chains, every positive linear combination of the corresponding functionals has exactly their common local maxima, while every other critical point has a positive Hessian direction. On a fixed irreducible module at the top of a subgroup chain, the simultaneous projective local-maximal components are indexed by vertex paths in the weighted Bratteli diagram. Each component is the product of the projective space of the bottom representation and the projectivized branching multiplicity spaces. In the multiplicity-free case with one-dimensional bottom type, these reduce to the Gelfand-Tsetlin lines. Peter-Weyl, Frobenius reciprocity, Young branching and Schur-Weyl duality provide concrete instances of the general picture.

papers.title: Entropy production decomposition and fluctuation theorems under continuous feedback: From prescribed to stochastic protocols
papers.abstract: When a system is driven by a prescribed protocol, the entropy production can be decomposed into the housekeeping and non-autonomous contributions, each satisfying a fluctuation theorem. Under feedback control, however, the feedback parameter depends on measurement outcomes rather than following a prescribed protocol. To study how the decomposition changes, we consider an overdamped Brownian particle at position $x$ with a low-pass-filtered measurement signal $D$ as the feedback parameter. Regarding each realization of $D$ as a stochastic protocol, we derive fluctuation theorems for the entropy production associated with the dynamics of $x$ and of $D$, and interpret them in terms of the information flow. For a solvable harmonic model, we map the dynamics onto an autonomous system in which the measurement and filtering process acts as an effective thermal bath. Feedback cooling thus corresponds to heat conduction from the physical bath through the particle to this colder bath, and the information flow can be interpreted as the entropy associated with the heat conduction between $x$ and $D$. We verify these results by numerical simulations.

authors.name: Long Him Cheung
authors.institution: Hong Kong University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Axial von Mises Framework for Tensor-Dependent Second-Harmonic Generation
papers.abstract: We derive closed-form relations between projected fibril-axis statistics and tensor-dependent second-harmonic generation (SHG) harmonics using a single axial von Mises population. Under coherent emission within domains and detected intensity addition across domains, each angular harmonic factors into a local tensor coefficient and an axial circular moment. Parallel-analyzer detection contains second, fourth and sixth harmonics; ideal equal-weight analyzer-free detection contains second and fourth harmonics. The resulting formulas identify geometry-specific harmonic zeros, sensitivity loss and ambiguous inversion of a secondary fixed-angle ratio. In particular, the analyzer-free fourth-harmonic zero at $\rho=1/3$ does not imply loss of all orientation sensitivity. Prepared-cornea forward/reverse recordings illustrate extraction of empirical analyzer-free harmonics. In the bundle ROI, second harmonics are resolved in both sweeps, while their normalized amplitudes differ and fourth harmonics remain unresolved. An exploratory central ROI from the same recordings yields a different forward/reverse profile. Within the same operator-identified tissue, low-signal space coverage and apparent fibre alignment vary slightly across recordings. These observations support angular-measurement feasibility while leaving quantitative normalized-shape agreement unestablished. The thermal extension illustrates consequences of assumed kinetics rather than calibrated tissue trajectories. The contribution is an analytical interpretation of SHG harmonics with explicit conditions for physical inference; the measurements do not establish absolute susceptibility ratio $\rho$, axial concentration $\kappa$, or experimental separation of thermal disorder from degradation.

papers.title: Controlling the Vacuum: Tunable Magnonic Casimir Effect in Magnetic Moir\'e Systems
papers.abstract: We prove that the quantum fluctuations of the magnetic degrees of freedom of moir\'e structures can be tuned by adjusting the moir\'e lattice. Using the Bistritzer-MacDonald approach, we explore the consequences of this fact for the magnonic vacuum energy and the magnonic Casimir force, which become functions of the moir\'e pattern parameters. This allows a prototypical engine to be run with the vacuum fluctuations as a working agent and, in that way, to furnish a novel type of magneto-mechanical effect. Our calculations focus on the moir\'e Ladder as an example but can be generalized to any moir\'e structure in a straightforward fashion. We anticipate that our results belong to a generic property of moir\'e structures, regardless of the physical nature of the excitations at hand.

papers.title: A geometric characterization of weighted homogeneity for reduced complex analytic germs
papers.abstract: We prove that a reduced complex analytic germ is weighted homogeneous if and only if, in suitable local coordinates, it admits a holomorphic vector field vanishing at the origin and pointing strictly outward along a single sufficiently small link. On a connected link, transversality suffices. The criterion applies in arbitrary codimension, including to non-isolated singularities. The proof uses a compact composition operator to control the spectrum on the Zariski tangent space and obtains a positive grading from the resulting spectral condition.

papers.title: Exact and Approximation Algorithms for Computing Smallest SESs and BMSs
papers.abstract: Compression schemes represent repetitive strings compactly by using repeated substrings. Computing the minimum size of a representation of a given input string is important for compression and for understanding relationships between compression schemes, although this task is NP-hard for several schemes. In this paper, we introduce exact and approximation algorithms for finding smallest substring equation systems (SESs) and bidirectional macro schemes (BMSs). Specifically, for an input string of length $n$, we give deterministic and randomized algorithms for computing a smallest SES using $O^*(4^n)$ and $O^*(2^n)$ time and space, respectively. We also give a deterministic algorithm for computing a smallest BMS using $O^*(2^n)$ time and space. We further give deterministic and randomized $(1+\alpha)$-approximation algorithms for smallest SESs using $O^*(4^{e^{-\alpha}n})$ and $O^*(2^{e^{-\alpha}n})$ time and space, respectively, for every $\alpha \ge 0$. A conversion from SESs to BMSs gives $4(1+\alpha)$-approximation algorithms for smallest BMSs with the same time and space bounds. All time bounds hold in the worst case, and the randomized algorithms return correct answers with high probability. Our algorithms adapt several approaches to exact and approximation algorithms for combinatorial problems, such as dynamic programming over determinant expansions and a greedy algorithm for monotone submodular functions.

papers.title: Small-angle scattering reveals heterogeneous nanoparticle size distributions through Bayesian inference
papers.abstract: Nanoparticles have attracted considerable attention owing to their broad range of applications. Surface functionalization further expands their functionality, making them useful in fields such as biomedicine, catalysis, sensing, and environmental remediation. In such applications, nanoparticles may form clusters through aggregation under high ionic-strength conditions, while biologically derived nanoparticles can be intrinsically heterogeneous in size. In this study, we apply small-angle neutron scattering (SANS) and small-angle X-ray scattering (SAXS) to nanoparticles and use Bayesian inference to analyze their heterogeneous particle-size distributions. Because SAXS and SANS probe the wavevector dependence of the static scattering intensity, they can sensitively resolve two distinct particle sizes even when a small fraction (< 10%) of larger particles is mixed with smaller particles. We construct multimodal particle-size distribution models within a Bayesian framework and demonstrate the importance of model selection for accurately estimating heterogeneous particle-size distributions. This approach should be broadly applicable to nanoparticle characterization across a wide range of applications.

papers.title: Forecasting Sales Delay through Time-aware Analysis of Sales Events in Textual Reports
papers.abstract: Business-to-business (B2B) companies develop and deliver a one-of-a-kind product in response to a client's orders. To prepare resources for development beforehand, companies estimate dates when they will receive orders from clients in their sales process, called scheduled order dates. However, dates when the companies actually receive orders can differ from the scheduled order dates. This difference increases costs in the development. If the difference could be forecasted before receiving orders, companies could optimize their resource preparation. Towards reducing the costs, we introduce sales delay forecasting, a novel task of forecasting delay days from the scheduled order dates during sales process where sales representatives (sales reps) interact with the clients to receive orders. Sales delay forecasting is challenging because the sales process progress inherently involves uncertainty and depends on the client's willingness to order. To address this task, we propose confidence features which represent sales reps' confidence as a proxy measure of the client's willingness to order. To represent it, our method extracts dates of future sales events anticipated by sales reps from textual reports. To consider whether the confidence objectively looks reasonable, we also introduce status features which describe sales process status based on current date and past events. In experiments using real sales data, our method achieved a 16% lower mean absolute error compared with a feature-based baseline similar to a prior work. Moreover, our method outperformed non-feature-based baselines using large language models, indicating that it is crucial to explicitly create our features.

authors.name: Teppei Inoue
authors.institution: St. Marianna University School of Medicine

papers.title: Hessian sectional curvatures of conjugate symmetric statistical manifolds
papers.abstract: Conjugate symmetric statistical manifolds generalize Hessian manifolds. Shima introduced Hessian sectional curvature in 1995 as an invariant for studying Hessian structures. We extend this invariant to conjugate symmetric statistical manifolds and study related curvature conditions and invariants. Our main results are as follows. For connected Hessian manifolds of dimension at least two, we characterize constant Hessian sectional curvature (CHC) by pointwise orthogonal invariance. We call conjugate symmetric statistical manifolds satisfying this invariance condition weakly CHC. We classify connected weakly CHC statistical manifolds of dimension at least two whose cubic forms are parallel with respect to the Levi-Civita connection. This classification characterizes the non-Hessian statistical structures induced on the classical hyperbolic affine spheres $xyz=c>0$ in the positive octant. We also introduce principal Hessian curvatures and show that they form a complete invariant for left-invariant Hessian structures on $\mathbb{R}^n$ up to statistical isomorphism.

papers.title: Residual ellipticity driven by intense magnetic stress in the hot neutron star era
papers.abstract: A neutron star with a nonaxisymmetric mass distribution continuously radiates gravitational waves. The amplitude depends on the magnitude of the deformation, and is crucial for gravitational-wave astronomy. We studied an evolutionary effect on the magnetically induced ellipticity in the neutron star crust. A large deformation at the hot era before solidification is assumed to be produced magneto-hydrodynamically, and the fate at later time follows owing to the decrease in the force associated with the decay and redistribution of the current. Instead of simulating the evolution of deformation with the magnetic field over a long timescale, we estimate the ellipticity that remains after the formation of the solid crust by comparing two equilibrium models before and after solidification. The relic ellipticity is $\sim 10^{-8} (B_0/10^{13}{\rm{G}})^2$ in the magnitude for dipole field strength $B_{0}$ at the surface. This value was primarily determined by the magnetic field at the later time, with a weak dependence on the initial large deformation. The memory of the presolidification state was retained, but was small because the elastic force contributes little to the equilibrium.

papers.title: Polarized transport in a Thomson slab: Stokes recursion, asymptotic eigenmodes, and Comptonization applications
papers.abstract: We develop a scattering-order-resolved Stokes-vector recursion for axisymmetric polarized transport in a finite plane-parallel Thomson slab. The post-scattering radiation field closes exactly within two depth-dependent coefficients, yielding escape probabilities, angular distributions and linear polarization while conserving photon number. At high scattering orders, the principal eigenmode of the weighted self-adjoint transport operator controls the escape statistics, and the normalized angular distribution and polarization become independent of the seed source. The subdominant spectrum quantifies convergence, with the characteristic scattering order scaling as the square of the optical depth in thick slabs. We derive logarithmic corrections to the thin-slab complete-polarization limit away from the slab normal, together with a finite-optical-depth Galerkin approximation. In optically thick slabs, matching bulk diffusion to a polarized Milne surface layer yields finite-thickness corrections to the Chandrasekhar solution. We provide compact formulae for the principal and leading subdominant eigenvalues and the asymptotic angular and polarization distributions across both regimes. Combining the recursion with an angle-averaged thermal-Compton redistribution kernel gives approximate energy-resolved Stokes spectra. Comparisons with full polarized Compton calculations show that this separable reconstruction is most reliable for cool, optically thick media. Applied to the non-dipping observations of neutron-star low-mass X-ray binary system 4U 1624-49, the model provides acceptable joint fits to the broadband intensity and IXPE Stokes spectra, showing that an extended corona overlying the accretion disc can account for the observed X-ray polarization.

papers.title: Integrating Slides, Mathematics, and Simulation in One Page: GenAI-Assisted HTML Learning Objects for Engineering Courses
papers.abstract: Engineering courses spread their materials across slides (PPTX), typeset notes (LaTeX/PDF), and MATLAB, leaving students to connect them. We describe an instructor-in-the-loop workflow in which generative AI (GenAI) converts these assets into single-file HTML learning objects that combine presentation, mathematics, visualization, simulation, and assessment; a page is released only after its simulations pass numerical verification. Six open demonstrators implement 18 tasks from six engineering courses. In the eight tasks with quantitative cross-checks, every quantity met its tolerance at default settings (1\%, or 2\% for the finite-difference time-domain simulation) and agreed with a separate Python re-computation and a value-blinded MATLAB re-computation run by a colleague not involved in development; the checks also flagged under-resolved settings. In a perception survey, students (19 after post-hoc screening of 28 responses) reported that the pages linked equations with simulation, and 74\% preferred them to separate files, but usability was marginal (System Usability Scale 56.8). Twelve lecturers rated the approach as useful (item means 4.25--4.58) but were hesitant to adopt it; their median ratings on a 12-criterion capability rubric agreed moderately with the first author's ($\kappa_w=0.60$; individual median 0.31). The results show technical feasibility and preliminary positive perceptions; learning outcomes were not measured.

authors.name: Ngoc-Bich Le
authors.institution: Vietnam National University Ho Chi Minh City

authors.name: Le-Minh Nguyen
authors.institution: Japan Advanced Institute of Science and Technology

papers.title: Optimal Sample Complexity for Genus-Two Zeta Functions from Noisy Random Euler Products
papers.abstract: We study exact recovery of the Hasse--Weil zeta numerator from repeated noisy observations of a randomized Euler product. For a genus-two curve over $\mathbb{F}_q$, we attach independent symmetric signs to its closed points and observe the logarithm of the resulting product at $t_q=c/\sqrt q$, where $0<c<1/\sqrt{12}$ is fixed. For every fixed, known additive noise density $f$ satisfying $\sqrt{f}\in H^1(\mathbb{R})$, we prove that the minimax number of independent observations required for exact recovery with error probability at most $\delta$ has order $q^4\log(1/\delta)$. No moment condition is imposed on the noise, so the result includes Cauchy readout. The upper bound estimates the phase of an empirical characteristic function and uses the separation of the integral Weil coefficients. The matching lower bound compares the full observation laws for two actual curves with ordinary, absolutely simple Jacobians. It combines a binomial comparison with a uniform bound on the closed-point tail. Thus access to the full observations does not improve the sample order attained by the phase estimator. The result concerns the information in a specified observation channel. It does not assume an efficient implementation of that channel.

authors.name: Ryoichi Suzuki
authors.institution: National Institute of Advanced Industrial Science and Technology

papers.title: Addendum to "Geodesic fields for Pontryagin type $C^0$-Finsler manifolds"
papers.abstract: In the paper ``Geodesic fields for Pontryagin type $C^0$-Finsler manifolds'', the same authors introduced a geometric object called Pontryagin-type $C^0$-Finsler structures, which includes Finsler structures on a smooth manifold $M$. Such a structure is defined locally by a control system of $C^1$ unit vector fields on an open subset $U$ of $M$, such that Pontryagin's maximum principle (PMP) is applicable. As a result of PMP, we obtain the extended geodesic field $\mathcal{E}$, which is a multivalued vector field on the slit cotangent bundle $T^{\ast}U\backslash 0 = \{(x,\alpha): x\in U, \alpha \in T^{\ast}_x U\}$, such that every minimizing path $x(t)$ on $(U,F)$ is an extremal (projection of a Pontryagin extremal $(x(t),\alpha(t))$). Some time after its introduction, its use and external comments, it is useful to provide remarks that clarify the applicability and limitations of this theory. In addition, we point out two errors contained in that work which, although discernible from the context, we believe should be pointed out. Finally, we prove some cases where the property that a minimizing path is the projection of a Pontryagin extremal can be extended beyond a coordinate system, sometimes to $M$. We also work on the problem of determining when $\mathcal{E}$ does not depend on the control system chosen to represent $F$. In particular, $\mathcal{E}$ satisfies these two properties globally for left-invariant $C^0$-Finsler structures on Lie groups, and for $C^1$-Finsler structures (without the condition of strong convexity).

papers.title: $k$-Product Lists for (Generalized) Feedback Vertex Sets: A Tool for Designing FPT Algorithms
papers.abstract: Enumerating all inclusion-minimal solutions is a powerful approach to designing fixed-parameter tractable (FPT) algorithms. However, for the \textsc{Feedback Vertex Set} problem, this approach faces a fundamental obstacle, as the number of minimal feedback vertex sets is not, in general, bounded by any function of the solution size~$k$. To overcome this limitation, we introduce a data structure called a \emph{$k$-product list}, which implicitly encodes all minimal solutions while admitting non-minimal ones to maintain efficiency. We present FPT algorithms for computing such lists not only for the \textsc{Feedback Vertex Set} problem but also for its natural generalizations, the \textsc{$\ell$-Forest Deletion Set} problem and the \textsc{$r$-Pseudoforest Deletion Set} problem. Our framework yields simple FPT algorithms for a wide range of variants, providing the first such results in several cases and demonstrating the broad applicability of our approach.

papers.title: Fast Radio Burst Population Constrained by Source-Count Growth and Burst Clustering
papers.abstract: Whether all fast radio burst (FRB) sources repeat, or whether some produce only a single burst, remains an open question. Using 3,950 bursts from the CHIME/FRB Catalog 2, we measure how the numbers of apparently single and repeating sources change with observing time, correcting for the declination-dependent, beam-weighted exposure and possible variations in the detection rate. Both source counts increase approximately linearly over 300--44,000~hr, as $N_{\rm s}\propto\Delta t^{0.98\pm0.02}$ for single sources and $N_{\rm r}\propto\Delta t^{1.06\pm0.14}$ for repeaters. Consequently, the observed repeater fraction remains nearly constant at $2.6^{+0.4}_{-0.6}\%$. We interpret these results using population models that account for a distribution of detected burst rates and temporal clustering. The source counts are reproduced by a population spanning a range of rates, including sources expected to produce approximately one detectable burst over the observing time. Its detected burst rates follow a distribution close to $r^{-2}$ over 0.01--1.5~hr$^{-1}$. The burst timing and burst multiplicities provide additional constraints. Among 77 repeaters, only 6 have their first two detected bursts within a single CHIME transit, the median interval between them is 101 days, and 31 of the 52 repeaters with at least three bursts have five or more. These observations support this population and favor moderately clustered emission (Weibull shape $k\simeq0.5$) and active phases lasting months to about a year. Our results are consistent with both a single population of repeaters whose rate distribution steepens below the range probed by CHIME and a mixed population that includes genuinely one-off sources. Thus, the current data do not require a one-off population, but cannot exclude one. Longer observing baselines are needed to distinguish these possibilities.

papers.title: $(r,s)$-Designs in the Nonbinary Johnson Scheme: Constructions and Linear Codes
papers.abstract: Using factorizations of complete graphs, we determine the existence conditions for $(2,1)$-designs in the nonbinary Johnson scheme where each $3$-element subset appears exactly once as a support. Furthermore, by utilizing large sets of Steiner triple systems, we construct designs with index $1$ that cannot be obtained from the known construction combining block designs and orthogonal arrays. For linear codes, we express multiplicative character sums over specified nonzero coordinates as sums over the codewords of the dual code. Using this identity along with the rank of a matrix formed by Krawtchouk polynomials, we provide a sufficient condition for the set of all codewords of a given weight to form an $(r,s)$-design. In this matrix, we can utilize not only the rows corresponding to weights absent from the code, but also the rows corresponding to weights for which the set of codewords already forms a design. Moreover, let $q>2$ be a prime power, and let $0 \neq C \subsetneq \mathbb{F}_q^n$ be a linear code with exactly two nonzero weights. For $t \geq 2$, the set of all codewords of weight $w \geq t$ forms a non-empty $(t,t)$-design if and only if the dual minimum distance is at least $t+2$. Consequently, this provides a negative answer to the Wu--Zhou problem concerning two-weight codes with a dual minimum distance of $3$.

papers.title: Physical interpretation of spin-glass models with correlated disorder
papers.abstract: Ising spin-glass models with a specific type of correlated bond disorder have recently been used to relate properties of spin-glass phases, such as temperature chaos and magnetic-field chaos, to ferromagnetic order. This correlated disorder has a simple physical interpretation, which underlies the sampling procedure introduced by Oshima, Arai, and Hukushima for numerical simulations: the bond configuration is obtained from the Edwards-Anderson model with the symmetric $\pm J$ distribution by drawing one of its equilibrium spin configurations and writing the model in the gauge in which this reference configuration becomes the all-up state. The construction is analogous to the Mattis model, with the roles of the ferromagnet and the spin glass reversed: whereas the Mattis model is a ferromagnet in disguise, the ferromagnetic phase of the correlated model is essentially a spin-glass phase in disguise. The frustration statistics of the correlated-disorder model are exactly those of the symmetric $\pm J$ model, and, in a generalization with an additional parameter $\gamma$, the probabilities of the gauge equivalence classes are determined by $\gamma$ alone, whereas the inverse temperature at which the reference configuration is drawn determines only the distribution within each class. The magnetization of this model is the overlap with the reference configuration. Through this correspondence, studies of its ferromagnetic phase have led to unexpected results on temperature chaos and magnetic-field chaos in the spin-glass phase of the Edwards-Anderson model. Models with correlated disorder have thus provided a new perspective on spin glasses and have proved fertile ground for highly nontrivial results on the spin-glass problem.

papers.title: A One-Sided Sublinear-Query Tester for Bounded-Degree 2SAT
papers.abstract:
We give a one-sided tester for satisfiability of 2CNF formulas in the bounded-degree model. For every degree bound $\Delta$, distance parameter $\varepsilon>0$, and $
u\in(0,1/2)$, its query complexity on $n$-variable formulas is $\widetilde O_{\varepsilon,\Delta,
u}(n^{1/2+
u})$.

papers.title: Strong error estimates for finite element approximations of the stochastic Burgers--Huxley equation with multiplicative noise
papers.abstract: This paper is concerned with strong error estimates for fully discrete finite element approximations of the stochastic Burgers--Huxley equation with multiplicative noise. We use the implicit Euler--Maruyama scheme for time discretization and continuous piecewise linear finite elements for spatial discretization. Moment bounds and exponential integrability estimates are established and used with the discrete stochastic Gronwall inequality to derive error estimates in full expectation. Sub-second-moment error estimates are first obtained in the discrete maximum-in-time $L^2$-norm and the discrete $L^2$-in-time $H^1$-norm. Second-moment error estimates in the discrete maximum-in-time $L^2$-norm are then established using a higher-moment argument. The convergence rates are of order $k^{1/2}$ in time and $h$ in space, with the spatial rate being optimal in the $H^1$-norm. Finally, numerical experiments are provided to examine the convergence rates and the influence of multiplicative noise on the solution.

authors.name: Tin Tran
authors.institution: Vietnam National University Ho Chi Minh City

authors.name: Liet Vo
authors.institution: The University of Texas Rio Grande Valley

papers.title: Cosmic Ray Reacceleration and Gamma-Ray Emission via the Cloud-Wind Interaction in the Galactic Halo
papers.abstract: The interaction between cosmic rays (CRs) and multiphase gas in the Galactic halo may play an important role in shaping the hard gamma-ray spectrum of the Fermi bubbles. We investigate the interaction between a hot Galactic wind and a cold, dense gas clump with a relative velocity of $300\ {\rm km\,s^{-1}}$ using two-dimensional hydrodynamic simulations coupled with momentum-dependent CR transport. The system produces a bow shock and wind reacceleration region downstream, where the wind flow is faster than the initial velocity. For a CR pressure comparable to the gas pressure (CR-rich), the wind acceleration and turbulence behind the clump are enhanced. When CR pressure is dynamically weak, strong gas compression leads to significant CR spectral hardening. In contrast, for the CR-rich case, CR pressure gradients weaken the gas compression and suppress further CR reacceleration. We estimate the gamma-ray intensity from CRs, and find that reaccelerated CRs penetrate the dense clump and enhance hadronic gamma-ray emission. The gamma-ray intensity reaches $\sim 10^{-8}\,\mathrm{erg\,cm^{-2}\,s^{-1}\,sr^{-1}}$ in the 1--10 GeV band, and the gamma-ray spectra become significantly harder, consistent with the Fermi bubbles' emission. These results suggest that an ensemble of dense gas clumps interacting with the Galactic wind may contribute to the gamma-ray emission of the Fermi bubbles.

papers.title: OT-BLS: Optimal-Transport-based Backbone Layer Selection for Frozen DINOv3 in Cross-Domain Few-Shot Segmentation
papers.abstract: Cross-domain few-shot segmentation (CD-FSS) aims to segment a target class in images from a previously unseen domain using only a few annotated support examples. Training-free CD-FSS methods, which typically leverage vision foundation models such as DINOv3, achieve competitive performance without parameter updates. However, the optimal DINOv3 layer for mask prediction varies across support--query episodes. Although several layer-selection criteria have been proposed, they do not explicitly evaluate whether the predicted query foreground and background labels agree with the corresponding support labels. To address this limitation, we propose a novel layer-selection criterion, Optimal-Transport-Based Backbone Layer Selection (OT-BLS). Our key insight is that an effective layer-selection criterion can be derived from the optimal-transport correspondence between query and support patch-token features. Based on this insight, we first estimate the transport plan using a well-established optimal transport algorithm and then compute a layer-selection score by aggregating the transported mass according to the foreground--background partition defined by each candidate query mask. The resulting score reflects how well the predicted foreground and background of the query correspond to those of the support. Experiments on eight benchmark datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of OT-BLS. It outperforms the conventional last-layer baseline in 12 of 16 dataset/shot settings. Furthermore, OT-BLS improves the average mIoU from 55.72 to 57.62 and achieves a 2.99-point improvement over the best-performing existing layer-selection criterion while running 3.7--14.6$\times$ faster.

papers.title: Rigidity of compact quasi-Einstein manifolds with boundary and low-dimensional focal sets
papers.abstract: In this article, we investigate nontrivial compact m-quasi-Einstein manifolds with boundary, m > 1 and constant scalar curvature. We first prove that such a manifold is rigid whenever the set of critical points of its potential function is totally geodesic, which extends to quasi-Einstein manifolds a theorem of Li, Li, Ou, Qu, Wu and Zhou for shrinking Ricci solitons. Then, we prove that, in every dimension, this set is totally geodesic whenever it has dimension two or three, so that the manifold is rigid in this case. The proof is based on a Bochner identity for the covariant derivative of the Ricci tensor at the points of this set. In particular, every such manifold of dimension five is rigid. Finally, we obtain rigidity in arbitrary dimension under an integral Weyl pinching condition when the set of critical points has dimension four.

authors.name: Matheus Andrade Ribeiro de Moura Horacio

papers.title: Fog-FWL: A Large-Scale Full-Waveform LiDAR Dataset for Recovering Fog-Hidden Objects
papers.abstract: LiDAR is a core sensor for autonomous driving, yet it is highly vulnerable to fog. Fog scattering produces strong backscatter near the sensor and attenuates reflections from objects behind it, so weak object returns are often discarded by the peak detection that converts received signals into point clouds. Full-waveform LiDAR (FWL), which records the received optical signal before peak detection, retains these weak returns, but the lack of suitable data has prevented research on recovering fog-hidden objects from FWL. We present Fog-FWL, a dataset foundation for this task that consists of a real-world benchmark, Fog-FWL-Real, and a large-scale synthetic training set, Fog-FWL-Sim. Fog-FWL-Real contains 7,527 real foggy FWL frames from 8 scenes and 58 sequences, which is 579x larger than the only existing real foggy FWL data, together with histogram-level Object/Fog/Noise labels, 10,719 3D bounding boxes, and three difficulty levels defined by the attenuation of object reflections. Fog-FWL-Sim contains 12,000 frames generated by our physics-based simulator, Fog-FWL-Simulator, which integrates spatially heterogeneous fog density fields, time-resolved light transport including multiple scattering, and a photon-counting SPAD receiver model. The two subsets share the same sensor format and annotation protocol, enabling a strict sim-to-real evaluation in which no real waveforms are used for training. Our analysis shows that, under the hardest condition, object returns are included in the three strongest peaks for only 34.9% of object rays, underscoring the need for waveform-level recovery. Fog-FWL-Real, Fog-FWL-Sim, and the Fog-FWL-Simulator will be publicly released to facilitate research on fog-robust LiDAR perception.

authors.name: Ryosei Hara
authors.institution: National Institute of Advanced Industrial Science and Technology

authors.name: Mariko Isogawa
authors.institution: National Institute of Advanced Industrial Science and Technology

papers.title: Null designs and switching in polynomial spaces
papers.abstract: Null designs are finite point configurations with real weights whose polynomial moments vanish up to a given degree. In Godsil's framework of polynomial spaces, we give elementary proofs of sharp lower bounds on the number of points in the Euclidean and spherical cases. We characterize the spherical null designs attaining the bound and give explicit formulas for their weights. We then study how null designs can be used to replace part of a weighted design while preserving its polynomial moments. We give conditions ensuring nonnegative weights and apply the minimum-size classification to switching on circles. Examples on spheres and in Hamming and Johnson spaces illustrate these results, including a replacement between noncongruent spherical $5$-designs that preserves equal weights and the number of points.

authors.name: Hiroshi Nozaki
authors.institution: Toyota Central Research and Development Laboratories (Japan)

papers.title: Core nonemptiness for $2/3$-convex games
papers.abstract: We study the core of $2/3$-convex games, a class of transferable-utility (TU) games that generalizes convex games, which requires at least two of any three distinct coalitions satisfy the supermodular inequality. We show that every $2/3$-convex game admits a marginal worth vector in the core, and hence has a nonempty core. Our proof is constructive and yields a linear-time algorithm for finding such a core allocation. We also show that $2/3$-convexity does not imply permutational convexity in general, while the implication holds under an additional superadditivity condition on pairs of singletons. As an application, we introduce a TU model motivated by the OSCE's consensus-minus-two procedure and show that the resulting game is $2/3$-convex but need not be convex.

papers.title: Sharp Bounds for Near-Maximizers of Gaussian Processes
papers.abstract: For a centered Gaussian process $G$ with continuous sample paths on a compact metric space $T$, a continuous drift $f: T \mapsto \mathbb{R}$, a noise level $\sigma>0$, and $\epsilon\ge 0$, let $A_\epsilon$ be the set of points at which $f+\sigma G$ is within $\epsilon$ of its maximum. Writing $\mathbb{E}\sup_TG$ for the expected supremum of $G$, we prove that the expected squared diameter of $A_\epsilon$ in the canonical pseudometric of $G$ is at most $8\epsilon \mathbb{E}\sup_TG/\sigma$ and that the expected maximal squared distance from a point of $A_\epsilon$ to an exact maximizer is at most $4\epsilon \mathbb{E}\sup_TG/\sigma$. The constants cannot be improved uniformly over index sets, processes, and drifts, and no logarithmic factor in $\epsilon$ appears, unlike in bounds integrated from tail estimates. At $\epsilon=0$ the bounds give the almost sure uniqueness of the maximizer in the canonical pseudometric without nondegeneracy assumptions. Given this uniqueness, both bounds follow from a bound with constant $2$ on the mean square of the largest increment of an independent copy of $G$ from an exact maximizer to a point of $A_\epsilon$. The proof rests on an identity for the mean squared support function of the $\epsilon$-subdifferentials of a smooth convex function at a standard Gaussian vector, obtained from two Gaussian integrations by parts.

papers.title: Intrinsic reduction data and the loci related to indeterminacy of iterate maps for rational functions
papers.abstract: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field of not necessarily characteristic $0$, and $d,n$ be integers $\ge 2$. We first formulate the dynamical moduli spaces of rational functions defined over $k$ in terms of the intrinsic reduction data of non-archimedean rational functions. As an application, we show that the locus $C_{d,n}$ of semistable intrinsic reduction data in degree $d$ whose $n$th iteration is defined and unstable is of codimension $d$ in the intrinsic reduction data space of degree $d$, settling a conjecture of Kiwi and Nie, and show that the image of $C_{d,n}$ in the compactified dynamical moduli $\overline{\mathrm{M}}_{d,k}$ is of dimension $\le d-2$ and the equality holds precisely either if $d$ is even or if $d\ge 5$ is odd and $(4/d)^n<1/(d-3)$ and determine the dimensions even for all the five exceptional pairs $(d,n)$, in addition describing the images of $C_{3,n}$ themselves. We also determine the indeterminacy of iterate maps either on the intrinsic reduction data spaces or on the compactified dynamical moduli spaces.

papers.title: Fluctuations of sample eigenvalues in a spiked covariance model with Haar-rotated spikes: a transition at $p^2 \asymp n$
papers.abstract: We study the outlying eigenvalues of a sample covariance matrix whose population covariance is itself random. The population covariance is $\Sigma_p=A_p+O_pB_pO_p^*+\sigma^2I_p$, where $A_p$ and $B_p$ are deterministic positive semidefinite matrices of fixed ranks $r$ and $s$, and where $O_p$ is Haar distributed on the orthogonal group in the real case, and on the unitary group in the complex case. Conditionally on $O_p$, we observe $n$ independent centered Gaussian vectors with covariance $\Sigma_p$, and we build the sample covariance matrix $\widehat\Sigma_p$ from these vectors. The fluctuations of the spike eigenvalues of $\widehat\Sigma_p$ come from two different sources: the Haar matrix $O_p$, which displaces the population spikes at the scale $1/p$, and the sampling, which acts at the scale $n^{-1/2}$. Comparing these two scales amounts to comparing $p^2$ with $n$, so the ratio which governs the fluctuations is $p^2/n$, while in the classical spiked model it is the aspect ratio $p/n$. We give the limiting law of each spike in four regimes where $n,p\to \infty$. When $p/n\to c>0$, and when $p/n\to0$ with $p^2/n\to\infty$, the sampling term dominates, the limit does not depend on $O_p$ and is Gaussian, as in the classical spiked model. When $p^2/n\to0$, the Haar randomness dominates, and the limit is a weighted sum of independent $\chi^2_1$ variables in the real case, and of independent exponential variables in the complex case. When $p^2/n\to\tau\in(0,\infty)$, the two terms are of the same order, and the limit is the convolution of Gaussian and $\chi^2_1$ or Exponential variables. We then apply these results to a linear mixed model with a continuous batch effect, in which the Haar assumption is what makes the separation of the signal and of the batch possible, and we build a test for the value of a single spike.

papers.title: Symmetry-Enabled Ferroelectric Valley Transduction in Rhombohedral Bilayer WSe$_2$
papers.abstract: Ferroelectric polarization couples to the layer degree of freedom in a bilayer, but a valley-selective energy response requires the valleys to carry different interlayer character. Rhombohedral bilayer WSe$_2$ meets that condition by symmetry: three-fold rotation forbids interlayer tunneling at the $K$ valley, while strong hybridization remains at $\Gamma$. The resulting contrast converts the band-effective ferroelectric layer asymmetry into a shift of the $K$ edge, and so displaces the $K$--$\Gamma$ landscape: a finite-field fit that does not impose the rule leaves the $K$ coupling consistent with zero, and the shift reaches \polshiftdft~meV, the most that asymmetry can give a single valley. Reversing the polarization mirrors the valley landscape in displacement field, so the two registries have equal and opposite differential transconductance $g_d$ at zero field. In the ideal symmetric limit a second parity holds about each registry's own compensation field and places a zero of $g_d$ there. The valley-dependent screening calculated here displaces that zero by only \gdnulllow\% at the read point, so device asymmetry limits the accuracy. The result links a known stacking selection rule to ferroelectric valley transduction, with a quantitative valley shift and a directly testable transport signature.

authors.name: Kazuhito Tsukagoshi
authors.institution: National Yang Ming Chiao Tung University

papers.title: On the $h$-polynomials of cyclotomic standard graded Cohen-Macaulay rings
papers.abstract: We say that a standard graded algebra is cyclotomic if all roots of its $h$-polynomial lie on the complex unit circle. We study which products of cyclotomic polynomials can occur as $h$-polynomials of standard graded Cohen--Macaulay algebras without being of complete intersection type. For each fixed positive integer $a$, we reduce the nonexistence problem for multiplicities $ap$ over all sufficiently large primes $p$ to finitely many cases. Combining this reduction with explicit constructions, we completely characterize the positive integers $k$ for which such a polynomial of multiplicity $8k$ exists: precisely those satisfying \[k\notin\{1,2,3,6\}\cup\{p:p\ge7\text{ is prime}\}\cup\{3p:p\ge17\text{ is prime}\}.\]

papers.title: Chromatic polynomials of signed graphs with a balancing vertex
papers.abstract: We study the zero-free chromatic polynomial $Z_\Sigma(q)$ of a signed graph $\Sigma$ and the characteristic polynomial $\chi_\Sigma(q)=Z_\Sigma(q-1)$ of its associated hyperplane arrangement containing all coordinate hyperplanes. For a connected signed graph on $n\ge 2$ vertices with a balancing vertex, we prove the equivalence of the following four conditions: (i) $Z_\Sigma(q)$ is the chromatic polynomial of an ordinary graph; (ii) the numerator of $\sum_{q\ge 1}\chi_\Sigma(q)t^q$, written with denominator $(1-t)^{n+1}$, has nonnegative coefficients; (iii) $\Sigma$ has a balanced block; and (iv) $\chi_\Sigma(2)=0$. We also provide explicit counterexamples showing that neither the balancing-vertex assumption nor connectedness can be omitted.

papers.title: Accurate calibration method of the Back-linked Fabry Perot interferometer using null channel for space-based gravitational wave antenna
papers.abstract: Accurate calibration of the detector response is essential for precision gravitational-wave (GW) observations. In the Back-linked Fabry-Perot Interferometer (BLFPI), which employs Fabry-Perot cavities to achieve high GW sensitivity, accurate calibration of the cavity response is particularly important because residual calibration errors directly limit the suppression of laser frequency noise. However, no practical calibration strategy for the cavity response has yet been established. In this paper, we propose a method for calibrating the cavity response using a null channel constructed from the three interferometer outputs of the triangular laser-link configuration. In null channel, GW signals are canceled and residual laser frequency noise indicates errors in the cavity response estimates. Therefore we can estimate the cavity response by optimizing the response parameters to minimize the integrated power of the null channel. We derive the estimation bias introduced by technical noise analytically and evaluate the performance of the proposed method numerically. The results show that the residual laser frequency noise after calibration is more than an order of magnitude below the designed BLFPI sensitivity throughout the observation band. This demonstrates that the proposed null-channel calibration method achieves the accuracy required for effective subtraction of laser frequency noise.

authors.name: Yutaro Enomoto
authors.institution: Institute of Space and Astronautical Science

papers.title: Well-Posedness for the Cauchy Problem with Free Boundary in Half-Space Arising from Combustion Problem
papers.abstract:
In this paper, we address the local-in-time well-posedness of an obstacle problem arising from a combustion model. The equation under consideration is a linear inhomogeneous heat equation on the moving domain $(s(t),\infty)$, subject to homogeneous Dirichlet and inhomogeneous Neumann boundary conditions. Our main result establishes the existence and uniqueness of a positive classical solution.
  Although several results are known for the homogeneous heat equation, much less is known about the inhomogeneous case. We show that the boundary function $s(t)$ is $\frac{1}{2}$-H\"older continuous in time when the forcing term has a singularity of order $O(1/\sqrt{t})$ as $t \to 0$. We also prove that if both the initial data and the forcing term are smooth, then $s$ has higher regularity than $\frac{1}{2}$-H\"older continuity.

papers.title: Hump around 30 keV in Suzaku spectra of Aquila X-1 -- Possible evidence of strong rapid-proton capture process --
papers.abstract: In a neutron star low-mass X-ray binary, heavy elements (with mass number ~100) are believed to be synthesized through the rapid-proton (rp) capture process, as indirectly indicated by the long tail of X-ray burst light curves. Although direct evidence for the rp-process was lacking so far, we reported in our previous study that an unidentified hump is present at ~30 keV of the Suzaku spectra of Aquila X-1 in its hard state. The feature was tentatively identified with a recombination quasi-continuum from highly ionized ions of cadmium or indium, which are possibly produced by the rp process during X-ray bursts and lifted up into the neutron-star atmosphere. To reinforce this scenario, we quantitatively evaluated the physical conditions of the assumed emitting region in the atmosphere, and confirmed that the scenario is possible when the putative rp-process ashes in the atmosphere has ~10^7 times higher abundances than their solar values. The results are compared with theoretical model calculations for the nucleosynthesis in X-ray bursts. We suggest that the observed spectral hump is a radiative recombination feature from the stable isotope 106Cd, produced in X-ray bursts via the rp-process. Further issues about the detectability are briefly discussed.

authors.name: M. Kubota
authors.institution: National Center For Child Health and Development

authors.name: K. Makishima
authors.institution: Kavli Institute for the Physics and Mathematics of the Universe

papers.title: Postcritically Finite Unicritical Polynomials over CM Fields
papers.abstract: A rational map of degree at least two is postcritically finite (PCF) if every critical point has a finite forward orbit. For the unicritical family $f_{d,c}(z)=z^d+c$ with $d\ge2$, we call $c$ a PCF parameter if $f_{d,c}$ is PCF. As discussed by Baker and DeMarco, these parameters are analogous to $j$-invariants of elliptic curves with complex multiplication. For every $d\ge2$, we determine which PCF parameters lie in a CM field. The same list gives all PCF parameters over the maximal abelian extension of $\mathbb{Q}$. This extends the classifications of Noytaptim and Petsche over the maximal totally real extension of $\mathbb{Q}$ and of Ferraguti and Pagano over quadratic number fields. The proof uses the totally real classification in degree two, orbit bounds, Kronecker's theorem, Goksel's unit theorem, Lam--Leung's short-sum classification, cyclotomic averages, and known irreducibility results.

papers.title: Information Spectrum Methods for Multiple-Access Channels --Part II : $\varepsilon$-Capacity Regions in the Mixed Finite-Alphabet Case
papers.abstract: In a nonergodic channel such as a slowly fading link, the channel law is drawn once and held fixed for the whole codeword, and the relevant performance measure is the $\varepsilon$-capacity. We study the $\varepsilon$-capacity regions of two-user mixed multiple-access channels (MACs) with finite alphabets, additive cost constraints and an arbitrary mixing measure. The direct parts are derived from a single information spectrum formula; the converse parts use, in addition, Fano's inequality and Ahlswede's strong converse applied to each component. Without knowledge of the realized component, we prove a single-letter inner bound for every $0\le\varepsilon<1$, in which one input serves all components; for $\varepsilon=0$ it is tight, and the capacity region is given by the essential infima of the component mutual informations. We prove a single-letter outer bound, the outage region, in which each component may use its own input; it holds with or without channel state information (CSI) at either terminal, and it is the $\varepsilon$-capacity region when the encoders know the component and the parameter space is countable. Both bounds coincide, in all four CSI scenarios, for well-ordered mixed MACs, which include degradedly ordered families and mixtures with a common optimal input, such as mixed additive MACs. Without CSI the outer bound can be strictly loose, and the no-CSI $\varepsilon$-capacity region for $0<\varepsilon<1$ remains open in general. Finally, we extend Ahlswede's strong converse to $K$ users with cost constraints and show that most of these results extend to $K$-user mixed MACs.

papers.title: Information Spectrum Methods for MUltiple-Access Channels--Part III : The Strong Converse in the $K$-User Gaussian Case
papers.abstract: This paper, Part III of a series, treats $K$-user multiple-access channels (MACs). Its starting point is a pair of fundamental lemmas, a random-coding lemma of Feinstein type and a converse lemma of Verd\'u--Han type, which are the $K$-user extensions of the two lemmas underlying Han's information spectrum approach to the general two-user MAC. From them we derive the capacity region of the general $K$-user MAC with cost constraint and show that it contains the polymatroid capacity region of the $K$-user Gaussian MAC. We then prove, by an elementary information spectrum calculation that adapts a diffuse--exceptional subspace decomposition used in recent second-order converses for the Gaussian MAC, that for every subset $\cS$ of users and every independent input satisfying the power constraints, the conditional information spectral-sup rate of the $K$-user Gaussian MAC does not exceed $\frac12\log(1+P_\cS/N)$, where $P_\cS$ is the total power of the users in $\cS$, with a probability bound that does not depend on the input. Consequently, the strong converse for the $K$-user Gaussian MAC, in the sense that the error probability tends to one for every rate tuple outside the capacity region, follows directly from the converse lemma, without the wringing technique and without hypothesis-testing meta-converses. This strong converse was first established by Fong and Tan, whose per-blocklength bounds yield it, through wringing and quantization. It is the key ingredient in the converse parts of the coding theorems for mixed Gaussian MACs in Part I, where the $\varepsilon$-strong converse would not suffice.

papers.title: Quasi-isometry classes of automorphism groups of K3 surfaces via Sierpi\'nski spaces
papers.abstract: We study quasi-isometry classes of automorphism groups of K3 surfaces using Sierpi\'nski spaces. We introduce K3 surfaces of Sierpi\'nski type and prove that their limit sets are round Sierpi\'nski spaces. For such K3 surfaces, the quasi-isometry class of the automorphism group is equivalent to the rational isometry class of the N\'eron--Severi lattice together with its integral roots. As an application of this rigidity, we construct infinitely many quasi-isometry classes of hyperbolic automorphism groups in Picard rank 4. This reveals a new phenomenon in Picard rank 4, sharply contrasting with the finiteness of quasi-isometry classes in Picard ranks at most 3 and at least 6.

papers.title: Do Large Language Models Show Racial and Sex Bias in Pain Management? A Counterfactual Audit of GPT, Claude, Gemini, Llama, DeepSeek and Qwen
papers.abstract: Racial and ethnic minority patients receive less pain treatment than non-Hispanic White patients, and large language models (LLMs) used as medical AI could reproduce that bias. Prior audits tested a few proprietary models, stated race explicitly and rarely measured the models' own response instability. In exploratory, non-preregistered analyses, Study 1 had four open-weight LLMs assess six acute-pain vignettes in every combination of four races and two sexes, with identity stated or cued only by a name (two names per group), comparing each identity with a White male reference on the same case and sampling seed. In Study 2, 24 configurations of 17 models, including OpenAI's GPT-4.1 mini and gpt-oss, Anthropic's Claude Haiku 4.5, Google's Gemini 2.5 Flash, Meta's Llama, DeepSeek and Qwen, with reasoning on and off and at two precisions, answered the same vignettes and the 50 clinician-written Q-Pain cases. In this single-prompt, JSON-constrained task, no difference survived correction in Study 1, none of 1,386 comparisons survived the false discovery rate in Study 2, and every pain-severity difference was equivalent to zero within one point on a 0-10 scale (within a quarter point for 237 of 238 Q-Pain comparisons). Opioid decisions were bounded less precisely (Study 1 could not exclude differences of about 20 percentage points), so they show no detected difference, not proof of none. The few differences surviving correction within a model favoured Black patients. Models differed far more from one another and across their own settings than between patients (the reference patient received the high opioid dose in 6% to 93% of responses), although serving software, provider and prompt format also differed. Fairness audits of clinical AI should use several names per group, pair comparisons on the seed, report the noise floor and test each deployed configuration.

papers.title: Two-Stage Secret Sharing
papers.abstract: We give an information-theoretic formulation of two-stage secret sharing for situations in which secret information becomes available progressively. In the proposed model, shares for an initial part of the secret are distributed before the remaining part becomes available, and additional shares are distributed to new participants after the remaining part becomes available, without updating the shares already distributed and without using any additional information other than shares. To characterize this setting, we propose the notion of a two-stage access structure and provide its characterization. We further quantify the amount of information about the first-stage secret that the dealer must retain between the two distribution stages, derive a universal lower bound, and present a construction that achieves this bound for every two-stage access structure. We also position advance sharing as a special case of the proposed model and give its characterization and a related construction in classical information-theoretic secret sharing.

authors.name: Mamoru Shibata
authors.institution: International University of Health and Welfare

papers.title: Radiative Transfer Modeling of Multi-Shell Molecular Outflows in the Class 0 Protostar IRAS 15398-3359
papers.abstract: Recent high-angular-resolution observations of protostellar outflows have revealed complex spatial and velocity structures that are difficult to describe with a single shell. We have investigated the primary outflow of the Class 0 protostar IRAS 15398$-$3359 in the H$_2$CO and CS emission observed with ALMA and identified four shell-like components, which trace the cavity walls of the more extended CO outflows. Non-LTE radiative-transfer calculations of H$_2$CO and synthetic ALMA observations of the three-dimensional model show that a common ellipsoidal geometrical form and Hubble-law-like velocity field can broadly reproduce the channel-map and position--velocity structures of the identified shells when the geometry, spatial configuration, and kinematics of each shell are allowed to vary independently. The kinematic timescales and inclination angles of the inner and outer shells are $\sim$1000 yr ($19^\circ$ and $15^\circ$) and $\sim$750 yr ($5^\circ$ and $8^\circ$), respectively. The momentum injection rate of the outer bipolar pair is approximately 2.2 times that of the inner pair. The inferred $\dot{M}_{\rm wind}/\dot{M}_{\rm acc}$ ratios are $0.7$--$3\%$ and $2$--$7\%$ for the inner and outer shells. The observed shell-to-shell differences suggest episodicity of the mass ejection events, where the strength and direction of the outflow activity may vary over short timescales of order $10^2$--$10^3$ yr.

papers.title: Nonlocal multipolar spin accumulation in altermagnets beyond d-wave
papers.abstract: In spin-conserving models of $g$- and $i$-wave altermagnets, the uniform longitudinal conductivity has no spin-odd component. A point injector reveals higher moments of the Fermi velocity through the nonlocal spin accumulation. Boltzmann theory predicts that the rank $m=2,4,6$ of the first nonzero spin-odd velocity moment sets the leading angular harmonic, its asymptotic radial dependence $r^{2-m}$, and its amplitude scaling $\tau^{m-3}$ at fixed distance and injected current. For $g$-wave order, the fourth moment produces a fourth angular harmonic with an asymptotic $r^{-2}$ tail. Quantum transport simulations support the radial profiles predicted by finite-geometry Boltzmann theory without an amplitude fit. Across the three symmetries, the quantum amplitudes exceed the Boltzmann predictions based on the Born scattering time by $15-65$\% in the windows analyzed. In a two-contact ribbon, we detect the $g$-wave fourth harmonic at $6.8\,\sigma$ in an independent set of 1800 disorder realizations using a preselected radial window. Its amplitude decreases when the altermagnetic splitting is reduced.

papers.title: Connection-twisted modules and logarithmic twisted modules of vertex algebras
papers.abstract: We formulate the notion of connection-twisted modules for $\mathbb{C}$-graded vertex algebras, as suggested by Feigin and Lentner, and investigate their fundamental properties. Let $G$ be an algebraic group acting on a vertex algebra $V$ by automorphisms. We establish an equivalence between the category of $\nabla$-twisted $V$-modules and the category of $g$-twisted $V$-modules, where $\nabla$ is a regular singular $\mathfrak{g}$-connection and $g\in G$ is its monodromy. For symplectic fermion and affine vertex algebras, we explicitly compute the commutation relations and the action of the Virasoro algebra on connection-twisted modules, recovering the formulas obtained by Feigin and Lentner \cite{FL24,FL25}.

papers.title: Concatenated Codes with One Inner Code: Low-Rate Gilbert-Varshamov Asymptotics from Algebraic-Geometric Codes
papers.abstract: Constructing codes that attain the Gilbert-Varshamov (GV) bound while admitting efficient encoding and decoding is a fundamental problem in coding theory. We study concatenated codes that reuse a single binary inner code across all outer coordinates. To exploit existing encoding and decoding algorithms, we restrict the outer codes to random subcodes of scaled copies of prescribed algebraic codes and investigate their minimum distance. Our first contribution is a general upper bound on the minimum-distance failure probability that separates two terms controlled by the inner code's bias moments and the dual weight distribution of the prescribed code, together with sufficient conditions for exponential decay. Our second contribution is a concrete construction satisfying these conditions using algebraic-geometric codes from the Garcia-Stichtenoth tower. For every sufficiently small $\varepsilon>0$, we construct a family of random binary codes $C_m$ whose rates approach $\varepsilon^2$ and satisfy \[ \Pr\left[\delta(C_m)\geq\frac12-\sqrt{\frac{\ln 2}{2}}\left(\varepsilon+\frac{\varepsilon^3}{2}\right)\right]\geq 1-2^{-c\varepsilon^4N_m}, \] for all sufficiently large $m$, where $N_m$ is the block length and $c>0$ is independent of $\varepsilon$ and $m$. Thus, the distance guarantee matches the leading coefficient of the GV bound at low rates. For each fixed $\varepsilon$, the construction uses a single inner encoding map throughout the family and admits polynomial-time encoding and unique decoding within a guaranteed radius. This answers the question of Doron, Mosheiff, and Wootters for subcodes of scaled algebraic geometry codes at low rates.

papers.title: Sub-100KB On-Device CNN Training via Dynamic Sparse Updates and Hardware--Software Co-Design
papers.abstract: The increasing demand for real-time processing and personalized deep learning has made edge-device training essential but challenging due to high memory and computational costs. To address this, we propose a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) training accelerator with a dynamic sparse update mechanism that selectively updates important parameters using a random channel strategy, avoiding costly evaluations. Combined with activation pruning, our approach reduces activation storage to just 3.4\% of the original. Our hardware features a fused forward dataflow that concurrently processes group normalization and convolution, reducing training time by 45\% through computation reordering and efficient zero-skipping. Implemented in TSMC 28nm at FP8 precision, the design operates at 800 MHz, achieving 8 TOPS peak throughput, 31.13 TOPS/W energy efficiency, and 14.8 TOPS/mm$^2$ area efficiency, with power consumption ranging from 257 to 272 mW. The design enables on-device training within a sub-100KB on-chip SRAM budget (95KB in silicon).
