Subsequent developments include the work of Bessières [5], Connell and Farb [14], Sambusetti [47], and Bessières, Besson, Courtois, and Gallot [6]. Storm [48, 49, 50] adapted the method to singular spaces, including Alexandrov spaces and cone-manifolds, in the setting of homotopy equivalences. The version of the method used here relies on Sturm’s d2d^{2}-barycenter on 𝖢𝖠𝖳⁡(0)\CAT(0) spaces [51].

In joint work with Connell, Dai, Núñez-Zimbrón, Perales, and Wei [15], we extended the barycenter method to non-collapsed 𝖱𝖢𝖣⁡(K,N)\RCD(K,N) spaces without boundary. A degree theory for maps from 𝖱𝖢𝖣\RCD spaces was not available, so the lower bound in our previous work is expressed in terms of a homological index indH⁡(f)\ind_{H}(f) and a fundamental index indπ⁡(f)\ind_{\pi}(f) [15, Theorem 1.1]. These are defined through singular homology and fundamental groups, and when XX is a closed oriented manifold, indH⁡(f)=|deg⁡(f)|\ind_{H}(f)=|\deg(f)| [15, Section 1]. The case of Alexandrov spaces with curvature bounded below was treated after we showed that the analytical and topological degrees coincide [54, Theorem 5.3]. That proof uses the integral current structure of Alexandrov spaces constructed by Jaramillo, Perales, Rajan, Searle, and Siffert [25], and Mitsuishi’s isomorphism between integral current homology and singular homology [38], which applies to Alexandrov spaces by the local Lipschitz contractibility theorem of Mitsuishi and Yamaguchi [39]. These two topological tools are not yet available for general non-collapsed 𝖱𝖢𝖣\RCD spaces.

papers.title: When Safety Becomes an Attack Surface: Manipulating Abstention in Tool-Using AI Agents
papers.abstract: An AI agent's decision not to act can itself become an attack surface. We study warning-induced over-abstention, an availability attack in which adversaries place fabricated risk warnings in low-trust content to prevent legitimate task completion. Our central premise is that safe abstention requires evaluating both the claimed risk and the authority of the evidence supporting it. We develop controlled counterfactual task variants that vary risk content, source provenance, and warning wording, and evaluate a Verify-Before-Abstain protocol that corroborates warnings against authoritative records or the underlying content. Across three model families and 51 injectable AgentAbstain task pairs, caution-first prompting amplifies the attack. For Gemini, induced over-abstention rises from $9.8\%$ to $86.3\%$, despite unchanged clean-task completion. Matched wording comparisons further reveal sensitivity to warning language, with substantial variation across models and environments. Provenance-aware verification improves legitimate completion, while forgery and sensitive-content controls expose its dependence on authoritative evidence and its limitations in preserving confidentiality. These results motivate evaluating agent safety through the justification for restraint, alongside the safety of actions taken.

papers.title: Self-consistent thermal-runaway electron equilibria
papers.abstract: In this work, we develop and solve a self-consistent equilibrium model for plasmas containing thermal and runaway electron (RE) populations, motivated by observations of residual plasma density during alternating-current (AC) transitions in ISTTOK. We adopt an existing monoenergetic, narrow-pitch guiding-center formulation, while retaining a spatially varying toroidal-field function, and show that prescribing the radius-weighted RE density by the orbit label alone conflicts with particle conservation and vector equilibrium wherever the thermal toroidal-field function varies along an occupied drift contour. Both conditions instead require the ratio of RE density to toroidal field to be constant along each drift contour. Taking this ratio as a function of the orbit label gives a compatible closure that relates the equilibrium RE density to a prescribed reference profile. Combined with Grad-Shafranov-Helmholtz thermal free functions, it yields a closed field equation that retains the displacement between drift and magnetic surfaces. At fixed thermal coefficients, we prove existence for every finite reference-profile amplitude under sign and spectral conditions. We also prove local constrained existence and uniqueness near a thermal equilibrium with a nonsingular current-beta response and derive a current-pressure bound. An ISTTOK ramp-down example with a prescribed 20% energetic-current fraction and 2 keV energy gives a magnetic-orbit axis separation of 2.39 mm. The resulting fields and current distributions can serve as initial conditions for studies of electron survival and plasma recovery through AC reversal.

papers.title: Admissibility of unbounded complexes of smooth representations
papers.abstract: Let $G$ be a $p$-adic Lie group and $k$ a field of characteristic $p$. We prove that a complex of smooth $k$-representations of $G$ has admissible cohomology if and only if it is globally admissible, i.e., its hypercohomology with respect to a torsion-free open compact pro-$p$ subgroup is finite dimensional in every degree. This extends the bounded-below and bounded-above comparison of Schneider--Sorensen to arbitrary unbounded complexes.

papers.title: Low Language Transfer Speech-to-Text
papers.abstract: A multilingual speech recogniser has heard much speech in its own languages. We ask how much of that it brings to a language it was never trained on, when it is fine-tuned on the little that language has. We score 28 open multilingual models untouched on Low-Language-TTS, 50 low-resource languages in 11 writing systems, and fine-tune 24 of them on at most 1,000 clips a language, 82 hours in all, with a dev set choosing every epoch. Fine-tuning lowers every model's macro character error rate (CER), by 16.6 to 53.1 points, to 9.5 at best, and a word language model takes three CTC models 1.2 to 1.4 points lower; WER is still 34.4 at best. On the 12 languages that no model lists, every model starts at 46 or worse and the best ends at 11.7. The same architectures from random weights stay 60 points or more behind, so the gain is transfer, and an encoder left untouched already gives a Whisper or Qwen decoder most of what it needs. It is the language, not the corpus: on FLEURS recordings that ours do not share, the median model keeps 79% of its gain. It costs the languages the models knew, 5.7 points of CER on English, Spanish, French and German in the median model. Low-rank adapters on 4% of the weights come within 1.1 points of tuning everything, and on 2 of 3 models forget less. Seq2seq and language-model decoders are done within three to five epochs, while a new CTC head is still improving at twenty or thirty. Data beats epochs: 25 clips a language take Qwen3-ASR 0.6B from 60.9 to 39.3, and at equal clips presented, ten times the data is worth 9.7 points. A model that first learned forty of the languages learns the other ten no faster. On a public Malay benchmark, untouched Whisper large-v3 scores 8.9 when it detects the language and 14.9 when told the clip is Malay, because it then translates the English that speakers mix in; trained on the Scicom telephony dataset it scores 6.0.

papers.title: Involutive Duality of Lie Operators in the Extended Alpha Group
papers.abstract: This work investigates the involutive, adjoint, and spectral structures arising in the extended Alpha Group. Starting from the four-dimensional Alpha Group transformation matrix, whose angular depen- dence is governed by coupled tan {\theta} and cot {\theta} modes, an iterative commutator procedure generates a sixteen-dimensional real Lie algebra. Within this algebra, the operators B5 and B6 are identified as structurally distinguished elements and analyzed through their adjoint actions. The operator B6 is veri- fied to be involutive and induces an 8 + 8 decomposition of the Lie algebra, while the adjoint action of B5 defines an eight-dimensional invariant mixed sector through a polynomial kernel. The restricted adjoint operators preserve this sector, and their coupled action generates an idempotent operator Q, satisfying Q2 = Q, revealing an invariant projective structure. The spectral analysis further identifies characteristic- polynomial factorizations associated with B5 , B6 , and their compositions, including golden-ratio relations among distinct generators of the extended algebra. These results establish structural connections between the original modal representation, Lie-algebraic involution, adjoint dynamics, projective organization, and the spectral structure of the extended Alpha Group.

papers.title: Characterization of the mechanical vibrations of the Schmidt Camera at the Tonantzintla Astronomical Observatory
papers.abstract:
Mechanical vibrations in astronomical telescopes can degrade image quality, making their detection and characterization essential. This work presents the development and validation of a low-cost, portable vibration monitoring system based on MEMS accelerometers interfaced with a microcontroller. The system integrates sensor acquisition and data analysis capabilities and was evaluated through controlled laboratory tests.
  The system was subsequently deployed at the historic Schmidt Camera of the Tonantzintla Astronomical Observatory in Mexico. After more than 80 years of operation, this study represents the first characterization of its mechanical vibrations. Preliminary measurements reveal dominant frequency components and their corresponding amplitudes, providing insight into the telescope's dynamic behavior and potential structural couplings that may affect image quality.
  Understanding the vibrational environment of astronomical telescopes is essential for the successful integration of new instrumentation. Identifying vibration frequencies and amplitudes can support the development of mitigation strategies, data filtering techniques, and numerical simulations to predict image quality degradation. The results demonstrate the feasibility of low-cost inertial sensing for monitoring heritage-class telescopes and provide a foundation for future instrumentation and preservation efforts at the Tonantzintla Observatory.

authors.name: Daniel Ferrusca R
authors.institution: National Institute of Astrophysics, Optics and Electronics

papers.title: Domination in token graphs of graphs with domination number two
papers.abstract: The $k$-token graph $F_k(G)$ of a graph $G$ is the graph whose vertices are the $k$-subsets of $V(G)$, with two $k$-subsets adjacent if and only if their symmetric difference is an edge of $G$. In this paper we study the domination number of $F_k(G)$ for graphs $G$ whose domination number $\gamma(G)$ is at least two, with a primary focus on the case $\gamma(G)=2$. For $k=2$, we give an upper bound for $\gamma(F_2(G))$ in terms of a dominating pair of $G$, and show that this bound is sharp for every double star $S_{a,b}$ with $2\le a\le b$; moreover, we determine the exact value for every double star, namely $\gamma(F_2(S_{a,b}))=2a+b-1$ for $1\le a\le b$. We also prove that $\gamma(F_2(G))\ge\lceil n/2\rceil$ for every graph $G$ on $n$ vertices with $\gamma(G)\geq2$, with equality for the graphs with the maximum number of edges among those with $\gamma(G)\geq2$. Then, we focus on complete bipartite graphs; we give upper bounds for $\gamma(F_2(K_{r,t}))$ that match the exact values independently established in recent work, together with a short proof that $\gamma(F_2(K_{2,n-2}))=n-2$. For $k\ge3$ we show that $\gamma(F_k(K_{2,n-2}))$ equals, up to lower-order terms, the Tur\'an number $T(n-2,k,k-1)$, and we determine $\gamma(F_3(K_{2,n-2}))$ exactly, obtaining $T(n-2,3,2) +n-4=n^2/4+O(n)$; for $k=4$, determining the leading constant is related to the still-open Tur\'an conjecture for 3-uniform hypergraphs. Finally, for $n\geq 12$ even, we prove that $\gamma\left(F_3(K_{n/2,n/2})\right) =\frac{7}{48}n^2+O(n)$.

authors.name: Sergio Gerardo Gomez-Galicia
authors.institution: Centro de Investigación y de Estudios Avanzados del Instituto Politécnico Nacional

papers.title: $uvby-\beta$ photoelectric photometry of FGK-type pulsating star candidates in the Kepler field: observations, stellar parameters and asteroseismic analysis
papers.abstract: We present $uvby-\beta$ photoelectric photometry of 218 FGK-type stars brighter than $Kp = 12$ mag in the Kepler field. Interstellar reddening was estimated using the observed photometric indices, distances from Gaia DR3, and the Bayestar19 three-dimensional dust maps. The sample was classified into dwarf and giant stars, and their metallicities and effective temperatures were determined using empirical photometric calibrations. The resulting parameters were compared with those reported in previous photometric and spectroscopic studies. We also analyzed the Kepler long-cadence light curves of the sample and determined the global asteroseismic parameters, including the frequency of maximum oscillation power ($\nu_{\max}$) and the large frequency separation ($\Delta\nu$), for red giants exhibiting solar-like oscillations. Finally, we performed a Bayesian isochrone-fitting analysis using PARSEC stellar evolutionary models, incorporating the photometric metallicities and effective temperatures, the asteroseismic parameters, and absolute visual magnitudes derived from Gaia DR3 data as observational constraints. This analysis provides estimates of the fundamental stellar parameters, including effective temperatures, metallicities, surface gravities, masses, and radii, together with their associated uncertainties.

papers.title: Finiteness properties of Bestvina-Brady kernels for graph products with torsion
papers.abstract: We study Bestvina-Brady kernels associated to graph products whose vertex groups are either infinite cyclic or finite. Using a $\mathrm{CAT}(0)$ cubical complex constructed by Ruane and Witzel, on which the graph product with defining graph $\Gamma$ acts, together with an equivariant Morse function, we establish sufficient conditions for homological finiteness properties in terms of the topology of the flag complex $\Gamma^\blacktriangle$, the subcomplex $\Gamma^\blacktriangle_\infty$ spanned by the infinite vertices, and the ascending and descending links of certain vertices. We also prove a partial converse, showing that, under additional vanishing hypotheses on homology in the next degree, non-vanishing homology of these complexes obstructs higher finiteness properties of the Bestvina-Brady kernel. The main new features are the presence of finite stabilizers and the resulting additional link conditions, which are expressed in terms of the flag complex of $\Gamma$. When the finite vertex groups are abelian, we characterize when the kernel has finitely many conjugacy classes of finite subgroups, describe the normalizers of its finite subgroups as Bestvina-Brady kernels of smaller graph products, and obtain a criterion for the kernel to be of Bredon type $\underline{\mathrm{FP}}_n$.

authors.name: Eduardo Flores Martinez
authors.institution: Universidad Michoacana de San Nicolás de Hidalgo

papers.title: Shallow water equations on n-dimensional Riemannian manifolds: a kinetic approach
papers.abstract: We develop an intrinsic kinetic moment closure for shallow-water equations on smooth manifolds of arbitrary dimension equipped with prescribed, possibly time-dependent Riemannian metrics. Hamiltonian transport on the cotangent bundle and metric-dependent momentum integration yield balance laws with hydrostatic pressure, bottom topography, a skew-adjoint force, and dissipative bottom friction. An explicit compactly supported Gibbs equilibrium satisfies the required mass, momentum, and tensor second-moment conditions. We derive the quasilinear formulation and characteristic speeds, establish the continuous mechanical-energy balance with geometric work and frictional dissipation, and obtain a weak entropy inequality for vanishing-viscosity limits under stated convergence assumptions. On the rotating sphere with a fixed round metric, the skew-adjoint force represents Coriolis effects. We construct a kinetic finite-volume scheme combining local fluxes, hydrostatic reconstruction, and geometric source terms. A second-order time integrator uses independently restricted steps at its two Euler stages. The scheme conserves discrete water volume, preserves nonnegative depth under a sufficient CFL condition, and is well balanced for lakes at rest, including wet/dry interfaces. Six-hour simulations of a localized surface disturbance over Earth topography with Manning bottom friction maintain positive depths and conserve water volume to near machine precision. Comparison with a spherical central-upwind method shows similar surface-wave propagation and gauge time series, with remaining differences in late-time local extrema.

papers.title: Assessing the Reliability of Longitudinal Bibliometric Rankings under Incomplete Citation Histories
papers.abstract: Longitudinal bibliometric analyses rely on annual citation histories, yet missing annual observations are frequently difficult to distinguish from true zero-citation years. We present a reproducible case-study framework for auditing citation-history gaps, tracing retrieval provenance, and quantifying the sensitivity of longitudinal indicators and rankings to explicit missing-data assumptions. The case study comprises 595 consolidated publications derived from 616 Google Scholar article records, and examines the completed calendar years 2024-2025. Three scenarios are compared: strictly observed annual counts (A), hypothetical zeros for internal gaps only (B), and hypothetical zeros for all missing years within a valid publication interval (C). The number of publications with computable growth and acceleration indicators increases from 196 (A) to 257 (B) and 490 (C); the corresponding counts for a revival indicator are 131, 152, and 177. Although the ordering of publications eligible under both compared scenarios is unchanged (Spearman and Kendall correlations equal to 1.0), complete-ranking positions and Top-K membership may change markedly. In particular, acceleration exhibits a Jaccard overlap of 0.563 at K=50 between A and C, while revival exhibits 0.667 at K=10. These findings demonstrate that unchanged indicator values and perfect correlations on a common subset do not guarantee stable rankings when eligibility changes. The zero assignments are hypothetical sensitivity assumptions, not evidence of provider semantics. The results are descriptive and based on a single researcher profile. A reusable Google Scholar Tracker software workflow supports the audit and sensitivity analysis; version 1.8.5 is publicly available on GitHub and archived on Zenodo (DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.24170285).

papers.title: From Data to Wisdom: Rethinking AI Through an Epistemic Lens
papers.abstract: This paper proposes the Data-to-Wisdom Epistemic Architecture for AI (EAAI), a conceptual framework treating Data, Information, Knowledge, Understanding and Wisdom as five distinct but recursively interacting epistemic functions: observation, contextual interpretation, modeling and prediction, critical evaluation and informed judgment. Two observations motivate it: sequential readings of the Knowledge Pyramid obscure how these functions interact, and a targeted review of ten Bayesian reference books finds that prior distributions are defined mathematically while "prior information" and "prior knowledge" are not consistently distinguished as epistemic categories. A Bayesian interpretation relates the likelihood, prior and posterior distributions, posterior prediction, model checking and decision analysis to the five functions, without limiting EAAI to Bayesian systems. Extending "prior" in an epistemic sense, the paper distinguishes five kinds of prior context that can shape the model, the likelihood, the prior, evaluation and action. Three worked applications -- quantitative financial risk, actuarial modeling in health insurance and agentic AI for medical reimbursement claims -- show how EAAI structures the analysis of model assumptions, evidence interpretation, validation, dependencies and decision consequences, separating the prediction of a risk, the appraisal of its reliability and the justification of action. It draws implications for AI and machine learning, including evaluation by function, treating intermediate model outputs as evidence open to challenge and separating generation from appraisal, and compares EAAI with work on DIKW, Bayesian workflow, AI evaluation and risk governance. Its contributions are an epistemic vocabulary with recursive relationships, a more accessible reading of Bayesian methodology, a typology of prior context and clearer methodological terminology.

papers.title: Self-Supervised Attention-Based Virtual Metrology for CMP MRR Prediction
papers.abstract: Chemical mechanical planarization (CMP) is a critical semiconductor manufacturing process where material removal rate (MRR) is a key metric for process monitoring and advanced process control (APC). Virtual metrology enables MRR estimation from process time series signals, supporting run-to-run(R2R) control and process optimization while reducing reliance on physical metrology. Existing approaches typically rely on simplified linear assumptions or require handcrafted feature engineering. In this paper, we propose Global Regression Pretraining(GREP), a self-supervised, attention-based framework for CMP MRR prediction. GREP learns temporal representations from unlabeled sensor signals through global proxy-target regression, followed by supervised fine-tuning for MRR estimation. The framework is evaluated against a feature-engineered supervised baseline under three conditions: limited labeled data, sensor noise, and temporal process drift. Experiments on the PHM 2016 CMP dataset demonstrate competitive performance under limited labeled-data conditions, with improvements in selected cases and performance largely comparable to the baseline across different labeled-data fractions. Both models exhibit relatively small changes in prediction error with increasing noise, while GREP achieves a 17.0% RMSE reduction in the final temporal interval.

authors.name: Nagarajan Raghavan
authors.institution: Singapore University of Technology and Design

papers.title: MoE Pretraining:Parallelism Layout Changes the Model, Not Quality
papers.abstract: Large Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models are trained across many machines, and the way the work is split, the parallelism layout, often changes between runs: a job resumes on a different GPU count, a cluster is resized, or an ablation runs on a new setup. In exact arithmetic the layout should not matter, but in real arithmetic it changes the order in which numbers are added, and some MoE rules such as load balancing and expert capacity are often computed per machine. We ask whether the layout changes the trained MoE model. We pretrain the same small MoE language models (25M to 117M parameters, 20M FineWeb-Edu tokens) with the same seed, data and hyperparameters under 9 data-parallel and expert-parallel layouts, in fp32 on CPUs and fp16 on a GPU, and compare each run with the effect of a new random seed. Across 80 runs we find: (1) The layout does not change model quality, but it does change the model: final predictions differ about 80% as much as with a new seed, and over 90% of routing decisions differ. Any layout, a one-bit change to one weight, or a different CPU thread count has the same effect. (2) The cause is the router: decisions that flip are almost exactly those where two experts were nearly tied (AUC 0.97 to 1.00 in the first 16 steps). (3) More, smaller experts create more near-ties (2.7% with 8 experts, 23% with 64) and less reproducible routing (68% vs. 100% of decisions differ), but outputs do not drift further. (4) A dense model of the same active size is far more stable (0.12x the seed level in fp32, 0.58x in fp16), while the MoE reaches about 0.8x at both precisions and twice as fast. (5) When pretraining resumes on a new layout, timing matters: switching at 84% of pretraining barely changes the final model, while switching at 10%, just after warm-up, changes it substantially. We release code, run logs and data.

papers.title: Counting doubly labelled trees and one-component networks
papers.abstract: A phylogenetic network is one-component if the child of every reticulation is a leaf. This class of networks has been widely used as building blocks in the combinatorial study of phylogenetic networks. We establish a bijection between one-component networks on $k$ taxa and rooted binary multi-labelled trees in which every label occurs exactly twice. Using this bijection and Burnside's lemma, we derive a closed formula and a two-term recurrence for the number of one-component networks. We further obtain explicit formulas for counting one-component networks with a prescribed number of reticulations.

papers.title: Differential equations for twisted intertwining operators in abelian orbifold conformal field theory
papers.abstract:
Let $ V $ be a vertex operator algebra with two commuting automorphisms $ g_1 $ and $ g_2 $ (possibly of infinite order and non-semisimple). We derive a Jacobi identity for a twisted intertwining operator $ \mathcal{Y} $ of type $ \left( \begin{smallmatrix} W_3\\ W_1 \, W_2 \end{smallmatrix}\right) $ when $ W_1 $ is a $ g_1 $-twisted $ V $-module, $ W_2 $ is a $ g_2 $-twisted $ V $-module, and $ W_3 $ is a $ g_1 g_2 $-twisted $ V $-module.
  For any abelian group $ G $ of automorphisms of a CFT-type vertex operator algebra, under certain Noetherian assumptions, we derive differential equations satisfied by the multi-series $ \langle w_0, \mathcal{Y}_1(w_1,z_1) \cdots \mathcal{Y}_N(w_N,z_N) w_{N+1} \rangle $ when $ \mathcal{Y}_j $ are intertwining operators among $ C_2 $-cofinite and discretely graded $ V $-modules twisted by elements in $ G $. For modules twisted by automorphisms with only real positive eigenvalues, it suffices to assume $ C_1 $-cofiniteness and discrete grading. When all but at most two external modules are twisted by automorphisms having only positive real eigenvalues, it suffices to assume all in-state and internal modules are $ C_1 $-cofinite and discretely graded.
  When $ G $ is a finite abelian group, we use the theory of regular singular points to prove that the multi-series $ \langle w_0, \mathcal{Y}_1(w_1,z_1) \cdots \mathcal{Y}_N(w_N,z_N) w_{N+1} \rangle $ converges absolutely to a multivalued analytic function when $ |z_1| > \cdots > |z_N| > 0 $ and analytically extends to the region $ z_i \neq 0 $, $ z_j - z_k \neq 0 $, for $ 1 \leq i \leq N $ and $ 1 \leq j < k \leq N $. The vertex operator algebra $ V $ is not assumed to be $ C_2 $-cofinite or simple.

authors.name: Daniel Tan
authors.institution: Agency for Science, Technology and Research

papers.title: Hinge comparison and excess estimates via modified Hessian bounds on manifolds with density
papers.abstract: We study geometric consequences of modified Hessian estimates on Riemannian manifolds with density. For general radial functions, we derive tensorial, spectral, and trace identities for the modified Hessian in the original metric. We also establish a comparison identity relating the modified Hessians of two radial functions and characterize when they are proportional. We then prove a hinge comparison theorem under an upper bound on the modified Hessian, yielding a weighted law of cosines and lower bounds for the excess function. Finally, under nonnegative weighted sectional curvature and suitable density control assumptions, we obtain an Abresch-Gromoll-type upper excess estimate.

papers.title: Pseudovortex-assisted generation of first-order vector modes
papers.abstract: A practical method of generating first-order vector modes like radially and azimuthally polarized modes is using the so-called vortex waveplates. Shining these plates with Gaussian beams produces parasitic higher-order modes besides the target vector beam. The reason is that there is a mismatch between the incident Gaussian mode and the doughnut-shaped profile required for the vector beam. This imposes a limit on the fidelity of the generated mode with respect to the target vector beam. In this work we demonstrate theoretically and experimentally that this limit can be overcome if the input Gaussian beam is replaced with a pseudovortex beam, which is a doughnut-shaped mode without topological charge. We use a spatial light modulator to generate this input mode and a geometric-phase-compensated triangular cavity for mode analysis. We demonstrate vector mode fidelity as high as $0.921 \pm 0.013$, which is considerably better than $0.815 \pm 0.003$ obtained with Gaussian input. We also investigate the fidelity as a function of the input beam waist, leading to a theoretical upper bound for the fidelity of $8\pi/27 \approx 0.931$, in close agreement with the experimental results. This approach presents a reliable method of generating high-fidelity vector modes.

papers.title: SEC: One-Share Everywhere-Short Secret Sharing from Lossless Expanders
papers.abstract: We introduce SEC, an expander-code-based ramp secret sharing scheme over $\mathbb{Z}$-modules, particularly suitable for lattice-based distributed cryptography. It is everywhere-short: bounded secret coefficients yield bounded share coefficients, and the integer reconstruction vectors have bounded entries. Moreover, each participant receives exactly one share, regardless of the number of parties and the privacy and reconstruction thresholds. This improves on prior schemes with bounded share coefficients and bounded entries in the integer reconstruction vectors, in which the number of sub-shares or shares per participant grows either with the number of parties and the threshold or with the security parameter. The construction rests on a coding-theoretic observation: in the bi-adjacency matrix of a lossless bipartite expander, unique-neighbor peeling completes every sufficiently small set of columns to a square unimodular submatrix. We prove correctness, everywhere-shortness, and linearity, and give a publicly computable entrywise bound on the reconstruction vector our algorithm returns for each authorized set. For privacy, we introduce hard-core local leakage resilience, which strengthens the leakage-resilience notion of Nielsen and Simkin (EUROCRYPT 2020) to protect a hard-core function of the secret, and we prove that SEC satisfies it against correlated multi-query local leakage under the MatrixHint-MLWE problem, which admits a reduction from the standard MLWE problem. For $n=60$ participants and security parameter $\kappa=128$, SEC achieves privacy threshold 6 against $2^{64}$ leakage queries and empirical reconstruction threshold 46. The ideal entropy-coded secret and share sizes are about 3.5 KiB and 6.4 KiB, respectively.

papers.title: Algebraic coarsening of hierarchical splines with guaranteed error control
papers.abstract: We present a purely algebraic coarsening operator for hierarchical spline spaces, obtained by inverting locally the refinement matrix that relates the coarsened basis to the current one. Only the B-splines that interact with the coarsened region are involved, so that a coarsening step reduces to one small least-squares problem followed by explicit corrections of the surviving coefficients, without mass matrices or numerical quadrature. The operator is a left inverse of the refinement matrix, hence exact whenever the fine spline belongs to the coarse space, and leaves the spline unchanged away from the coarsened region. The residual of the least-squares problem bounds the $L^\infty$-error with no unknown constants and is available before the mesh is modified, which yields an adaptive multi-level algorithm that guarantees a prescribed tolerance. The construction carries over to truncated hierarchical B-splines, where the corrections disappear. In numerical experiments, the bound is sharp within an order of magnitude, the local transfer is nearly as accurate as a global $L^2$-projection, and much of the refinement left behind a moving front is removed without degrading the solution.

papers.title: Fatigue crack growth without plasticity under cyclically reversed shear
papers.abstract: We show that cyclic fatigue can occur in a system whose elements behave elastically up to an irreversible failure threshold, without plasticity, friction, or any time-dependent process. The model represents a weak interface between two elastic bodies loaded in shear. Under sufficiently large cyclic loading below the static failure threshold, a pre-existing flaw advances progressively, by a few lattice spacings per cycle. Two conditions are needed for this behavior: each bond fails more easily under one sense of the shear than the opposite, and the shear must be reversed during the cycle by an amount large enough to break bonds that have not yet failed. The model thus identifies the minimal conditions for an intrinsic, plasticity-free fatigue mechanism. Such conditions may be met at interfaces and weak planes subjected to strongly reversed shear, as in fretting, rolling contact, and reversed torsion, or in cyclic shear of cemented granular materials.

authors.name: E. A. Jagla
authors.institution: Consejo Nacional de Investigaciones Científicas y Técnicas

papers.title: Encoding rational $\Delta$-triples on elliptic curves
papers.abstract: A $\Delta$-triple for a natural number $n$ is a triple $(x,y,z)$ of divisors of $n$ with $1<x<y\leq z<\sqrt n$ and $n/x-x=(n/y-y)+(n/z-z)$. The numbers that admit such a triple are those with the $\Delta$ property, which governs the existence of certain $n$-simple triangles in factor graphs of split graphs. We allow the three components to be rational numbers, and show that, once the quotient $z/y=a/b$ is fixed, the rational $\Delta$-triples for $n$ are exactly the rational points of the elliptic curve $Y^2=n\,ab\,w(w+ab)\bigl(w+(a+b)^2\bigr)$ lying over the interval $-b(a+b)<w<-ab$. Since a rational $\Delta$-triple for $n$ amounts to $\Delta$-triples for infinitely many of the numbers $\kappa^2n$, the chord--tangent construction becomes a way of producing new $\Delta$-triples from old ones. For perfect squares, the curve always carries a rational point coming from a degenerate triple. This point has order $4$ if $a=b$, and infinite order if $a>b$. As a consequence, for every quotient $a/b>1$ there are infinitely many pairwise non-proportional $\Delta$-triples of perfect squares with $z/y=a/b$, in contrast with the fact that perfect squares have no $\Delta$-triple with $y=z$. For arbitrary $n$, there are infinitely many rational $\Delta$-triples for $n$ with a given quotient if and only if the corresponding curve has positive rank.

authors.name: Victor N. Schvollner
authors.institution: Consejo Nacional de Investigaciones Científicas y Técnicas

papers.title: A completely decomposable modular Jacobian of dimension $1777$
papers.abstract: We exhibit a congruence subgroup $\Gamma\subset\operatorname{SL}(2,\mathbb{Z})$ of level $120$ and index $23040$ whose modular curve $X_\Gamma$ has genus $1777$ and whose Jacobian is isogenous over $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}$ to a product of elliptic curves. This surpasses the previous record of a completely decomposable complex Jacobian of dimension $1297$ found by Ekedahl and Serre in $1993$.

papers.title: A pseudostress-based fully mixed finite element method for the stationary Biot--Poisson--Nernst--Planck system
papers.abstract: We develop a pseudostress-based fully mixed finite element method for the stationary Biot-Poisson-Nernst-Planck system describing ionic transport in a charged, saturated, and deformable porous medium. The mechanical equations are reformulated in terms of a non-symmetric pseudostress and the solid displacement, while mixed formulations are retained for the Darcy, electrostatic, and ionic equations. The nonlinear electrostatic and advective couplings are treated in a Banach space setting. The formulation provides direct approximations of the pseudostress, fluxes, and concentration gradients, and permits algebraic reconstruction of the displacement gradient and Cauchy stress. Under block-stability and small-data assumptions, we establish continuous and discrete well-posedness, with poroelastic stability bounds uniform with respect to the first Lame parameter. A conforming Raviart-Thomas discretization, completed by discontinuous polynomials, yields a priori error estimates and convergence rates. For the coupled scheme in two dimensions, we construct a residual-based a posteriori error estimator and establish its reliability under an additional smallness condition on the prescribed data. Local efficiency is proved for polynomial boundary data, with boundary-data oscillation included for general traces. We also describe the estimator modifications for nonhomogeneous displacement and normal-flux data under corresponding stability and solvability hypotheses. Numerical experiments examine convergence of the mixed and reconstructed fields, robustness in the nearly incompressible regime, adaptive refinement, and ionic polarization in a charged porous medium.

papers.title: Clustering trajectories of modelled estimates: an uncertainty-aware framework, with an application to global cardiovascular disease burden, 1990 to 2023
papers.abstract: Modelled health estimates such as those of the Global Burden of Disease (GBD) study are increasingly used in secondary analyses designed for observed data. However, trajectory clustering typically ignores published uncertainty, selects the number of clusters using criteria blind to it, and assigns countries to groups with unwarranted certainty. We propose an uncertainty-aware framework that separates trajectory level from shape, quantifies membership probabilities by perturbing estimates within their uncertainty intervals, selects clusters based on stability under uncertainty, and examines the roles of development, region, and measurement quality. Applied to age-standardised cardiovascular disease DALY rates for 201 countries from 1990-2023 (GBD 2023), the framework identified two stable trajectory types, whereas the gap statistic selected three. The additional cluster was poorly supported (median membership probability 0.70) and disappeared once uncertainty was considered. The retained clusters had similar burdens in 1990 but diverged markedly over time: a stalled-improvement group of 78 countries (median change $-8\%$, 40 of them in sub-Saharan Africa) and a sustained-decline group of 92 countries ($-52\%$). Thirty-one countries remained unclassified because their memberships were uncertain. Results were reproduced using mortality rates, a 2000-2023 analysis window, and bootstrap resampling. Among countries with the narrowest uncertainty intervals, a third well-supported trajectory emerged in former Soviet and Eastern European countries. These findings show that uncertainty affects both the number and composition of trajectory clusters. Ignoring it risks over-interpreting unstable groups and overstating confidence in country classifications. Incorporating published uncertainty and measurement quality should become standard practice when clustering modelled health estimates.

papers.title: Least Expensive Standard Pensions
papers.abstract: The paper proposes generating annuity payment streams at far lower costs than those implied by traditional theories. For a given investment universe, this enables the design of a least expensive standard pension, providing accurate monthly payments of savings account units over a set period. Such a standard pension invests dynamically in the savings account and the equity market's growth-optimal portfolio to replicate riskless payments with high accuracy at the lowest possible cost. Since this mathematically grounded standard pension is reliable and, by orders of magnitude, less expensive than traditional pensions, it provides a unique opportunity to improve the health of pension systems and provide more benefits for retirees.

papers.title: CoordX Types: A Trustless, Swappable Type System for Shared Records
papers.abstract: The CoordX Protocol carries signed and encrypted entries between parties. It proves who wrote each entry and who had permission to write it. It does not say what an entry means. That task belongs above the protocol layer. This paper describes the CoordX type system, the layer that gives entries a meaning. A type is a short document that says how to read one part of a shared record: which entries count, what each position means, what a party may do there, and what a party must do next. The type system has two key properties. It is trustless: a type is an ordinary signed object fixed by its digest, and every party evaluates it for itself over entries that the CoordX Protocol has already verified. No party has to trust a server, a registry or another party's software. It is swappable: a type names the interpreter it is written for, so many interpreters, of different capabilities and designs, can be used side by side in one record. We describe how to write type schemas, and we define the expressive power of the schema language. Payloads form a regular language. Entry structure forms a regular tree language. Every rule and every computed value is a total function in the primitive recursive class, so evaluation always halts. We compare this with KQML, FIPA-ACL and CBCL, and we relate it to language-theoretic security.

papers.title: Depth determination from core-loss 4D-STEM
papers.abstract: Moving beyond specimen-projected micrographs in scanning transmission electron microscopy to determine the three-dimensional distribution of dopants is of vital importance for materials characterization and development. We present an approach for dopant depth determination using momentum-resolved core-loss four-dimensional scanning transmission electron microscopy data. Within the Born approximation, Fourier transformation over probe position reveals fringes whose frequency encodes the dopant's distance from the focal plane. Two principal challenges arise in extending this approach to realistic experimental conditions. First, dynamical scattering degrades fringe contrast which can be partially mitigated by acquiring off major zone axes. Second, because core-loss doses are punishing, we use a Bayesian framework which, in simulation, achieves nanometre to sub-nanometre depth precision from only 100 to 1000 core-loss counts, depending on the signal-to-background.

papers.title: Generalized ladder operators and construction of families of superintegrable systems with Painlev\'e VI
papers.abstract: We study quantum Hamiltonians whose separated angular component is expressed through a generic Painlev\'e VI transcendent. We construct generalized ladder operators for one-dimensional Schr\"odinger operators with a quadratic spectral variable. For the Painlev\'e VI angular Hamiltonian these operators satisfy $[N,J_\pm]=\pm2kJ_\pm$, where $N=\sqrt M$, and close through an eighth-degree norm polynomial. Combining the angular shifts with the radial shift operators of the oscillator, Coulomb and free Bessel systems yields higher-order integrals and deformed Racah-type polynomial algebras for the two-dimensional superintegrable models. This construction provides new families of Tremblay-Turbiner-Winternitz (TTW)- and Post-Winternitz (PW)-like Hamiltonians with integrals of arbitrarily high order and Painlev\'e VI in the potential. This framework also recovers models from the classification of third- and fourth-order integrals as particular cases. For a representative oscillator extension we compute the Casimir explicitly and recover the finite-dimensional energy spectrum from a deformed-oscillator realization. We then analyze the special-solution sector using the explicit families collected by Gromak, Laine and Shimomura. The resulting potentials are organized into a small number of spectral classes, and the distinction between formal zeros of the ladder norm and physical self-adjoint representations is made explicit. The regular nonclassical rational examples are rational Darboux deformations of the trigonometric P\"oschl--Teller system and lead to strictly isospectral exceptional-Jacobi sectors or to state-adding representations with an isolated angular level. A singular branch produces an interior inverse-square barrier and a split-domain problem. For one regular exceptional sector and two state-adding sectors we display the polynomial algebras.

papers.title: Continuous-Time Random Walks with Internal Stochastic Renewal Process
papers.abstract: We introduce a continuous-time random walk process via a structured density by tracking the state of the particle as the system evolves. Whenever the particle makes a jump, its internal state either increases by one or resets to zero, so that the internal state evolves according to a renewal process. A wide range of governing integro-differential equations may be obtained from this formulation, some of which exhibit various types of anomalous behaviour. For certain choices of reset probabilities, waiting times and jump distributions, we explicitly derive the mode-dependent memory kernels and investigate their continuum limits. The framework can recover the time-and-space-fractional Fokker-Planck equation, which traditionally models the interplay between long wait times and large jumps and exhibits anomalous diffusion. Furthermore, we obtain a process which converges toward the equilibrium distribution as time approaches some finite value through a sequence of waiting times which decrease geometrically. Finally, we investigate a process that incorporates self-excitation and self-inhibition into the waiting times for each state to produce a mean square displacement proportional to $t^\nu$ for any $\nu > 0$. Through these examples, we illustrate the link between the microscopic mechanisms in these processes and their non-local macroscopic governing equations.

papers.title: On the Classification of Nilpotent Lie Superalgebras over Fields of Characteristic 2
papers.abstract: The salient result of this paper is the complete classification of all nilpotent Lie superalgebras in dimensions up to four over an algebraically closed field of characteristic 2. Our method adapts the Skjelbred-Sund method to show that every n-dimensional nilpotent Lie superalgebra arises as a one-dimensional central extension of an (n-1)-dimensional one, and determines precisely when two such extensions yield isomorphic superalgebras. Carrying out this construction for dimensions up to 4, we obtain a finite, non-redundant list of pairwise non-isomorphic examples.
papers.intro:
Lie superalgebras arose in the 1970s as ℤ/2​ℤ\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}-graded analogues of Lie algebras, motivated by supersymmetry in physics. In this setting, elements are assigned degrees, which leads to the appearance of signs in the defining relations. Roughly speaking, a Lie superalgebra is a ℤ/2​ℤ\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}-graded vector space LL equipped with a parity-preserving bilinear map [⋅,⋅]:L×L→L[\cdot,\cdot]:L\times L\to L called the Lie bracket, which is super anti-symmetric and satisfies a graded version of the Jacobi identity. Although simple Lie superalgebras have been classified by Kac ([K]), the classification of other classes of Lie superalgebras, such as nilpotent ones is limited to a few particular cases, see Section 1.2.

The first formal instance of this definition, appears in [LeD], however, earlier analogues may be found in [BMY] and [NR] with the name “strongly anti-commutative graded algebras”.

Due to the introduction of the squaring map, characteristic 2 is a novel case that requires novel techniques. In fact, certain Lie superalgebras in characteristic 2 have no equivalents in other characteristics (see [BGL1, BGLLS, BLLSq, LeD]), the standard example being the four mutually non-isomorphic versions of the Hamiltonian Lie superalgebra. Thus, the classification of both simple and nilpotent cases is an open problem. However, a number of breakthroughs have permeated the setting. Lie superalgebras in characteristic 2 that admit a Cartan matrix have been classified in [BGL1], albeit under the assumption that they each accede a Dynkin diagram with exactly one odd node. Furthermore, the classification of simple Lie superalgebras in characteristic 2 has been reduced to the classification of simple Lie algebras in characteristic 2 (by either queerification or “method 2”), as described in [BLLSq, BGLLS]. The latter classification is itself yet open and a difficult problem in its own right (see [S1, S2]).

For characteristic 0, the dimension 6 classification was achieved by Morozov in 1958 ([M]), whereas the result was achieved for any arbitrary field in 2012, see [CGS, DG]. Over any arbitrary field of characteristic p≥3p\geq 3, the restricted pp-nilpotent Lie superalgebras were classified up to dimension 4 by Bouarroudj and Ehret in [BE]. The method they used built on the classical Skjelbred-Sund method [SS] that can be described as follows. Given a Lie superalgebra LL of dimension n−1n-1, they compute all central extensions of LL by a one-dimensional vector space VV. That is, they define the Lie bracket and the pp-map on the direct sum L⊕VL\oplus V in such a way that VV lies in the center of the extended superalgebra. The obstructions for the extended bracket to satisfy the Jacobi identity are controlled by the cohomology of LL with coefficients in the trivial module VV. This process yields all pp-nilpotent Lie superalgebras of dimension nn. As a final step, they detect and remove isomorphic duplicates from the resulting list. Due to certain similarities between the squaring map and the pp-map, we aim to build on their method to classify nilpotent Lie superalgebras in characteristic p=2p=2.

papers.title: Forecasting Daily Household Electricity Demand in a Hot-Arid City: A Comparative Benchmark of Local, Global, Deep and Foundation Models on ESHED-38
papers.abstract: This study benchmarks 24 forecasting configurations on ESHED-38, daily smart-meter consumption for 38 homes in Erbil, Iraq, collected from May 2020 to June 2025 with station weather and a household survey. The configurations span five base families, plus two cross-family ensembles: naive baselines, per-house statistical models, global gradient-boosted trees, global deep networks, and zero-shot time-series foundation models. All are evaluated on the same 54,720 forecasts from 48 weekly origins over a 359-day held-out period, at lead times up to 30 days, using scaled absolute error, the continuous ranked probability score, calibration, and Friedman, Nemenyi and Holm-corrected Wilcoxon tests. The best configurations cut the scaled error of a seasonal-naive forecast by 20 to 25 percent, and the leading models beat it in all 38 houses. Chronos-2, used without training, is significantly the most accurate model one day ahead; at one week it is statistically tied with TimesFM-2.5, Chronos-Bolt and a pre-specified ensemble, and the two ensembles lead at 30 days. Deep networks trained from scratch do not outperform exponential smoothing on average, and the household survey adds negligible skill. Metered demand peaks in winter and falls as temperature rises. Recorded weather did not improve any model run with and without it. A quality screen helps explain why: on 68 percent of dates a temperature value recurs exactly on other dates, in three annual blocks covering almost all of the test period, suggesting that much of the weather record reuses one annual sequence. The value of weather information is therefore treated as unresolved, and the protocol is released as a baseline.
papers.intro:
A forecast of how much electricity one home will use tomorrow, or next week, is useful to more people than might be expected. Utilities need it to plan supply and to target demand-response offers; network operators need it to judge how close local transformers run to their limits; and households themselves can use it to anticipate bills. Yet the single home is the hardest unit to forecast. A city’s demand averages out thousands of independent decisions, so its daily load follows the weather and the calendar closely. One meter, on the other hand, registers every trip away, every visiting relative and every heater left on overnight.

Yet the single home is the hardest unit to forecast. A city’s demand averages out thousands of independent decisions, so its daily load follows the weather and the calendar closely. One meter, on the other hand, registers every trip away, every visiting relative and every heater left on overnight.

The research literature on household forecasting draws mainly on data from Europe, North America and East Asia. Homes in the hot-arid Middle East differ from those settings in almost every relevant respect: building materials, the appliances that people own, the way they heat and cool, and, in several countries, the reliability of the grid itself. The Kurdistan Region of Iraq is a clear case. Summer days regularly pass 45 ∘C, winter nights are cold enough to need space heating, and many families draw part of their power from private neighbourhood generators. Whether modern forecasting methods work well under these conditions is largely unknown, mostly because public data have not been available.

The ESHED-38 dataset, released by Jaf and Hamarash in 2026 [1], fills part of that gap. It records five years of daily smart-meter readings for 38 homes in Erbil, aligned with weather measurements and a survey of building and appliance characteristics. It is used here to address three practical questions. Which family of forecasting methods works best for daily single-home demand in this setting? How much better than a simple rule are the best methods? And can the uncertainty they report be trusted?

Two developments make these questions timely. One is the ongoing comparison between local models, fitted separately to each series, and global models trained once across many series [2]. The other is the arrival of large pre-trained time-series foundation models, such as Chronos [3] and TimesFM [4], which are meant to forecast series they have never seen. Household meters in Iraq are almost certainly absent from the data these models were trained on, which makes ESHED-38 a useful out-of-distribution test.

This paper contributes the following: 1. To the author’s knowledge, the first forecasting benchmark on ESHED-38: 24 configurations from five base model families plus two cross-family ensembles, compared on identical forecasts under a leakage-free rolling-origin protocol with 48 origins and three horizons. 2. An evaluation that covers point accuracy, the quality of the full predictive distribution and calibration, with non-parametric significance tests that treat each house as a paired observation. 3. Practical findings: zero-shot foundation models are among the most accurate options at a negligible computing cost, networks trained from scratch are not, and survey attributes add only negligible signal for this task. 4. A data-quality analysis showing that most of the weather record behaves like a repeated annual sequence rather than a measured daily series, with direct consequences for any study of weather effects on these data.

papers.title: Can a search hold its own bar? In-loop deflation and its exploits in autonomous strategy discovery
papers.abstract: Corrections for backtest overfitting such as the deflated Sharpe ratio are applied after a search ends: the searcher maximises raw performance and a separate procedure deflates the reported winner. Autonomous searches driven by large language models perform many implicit backtests before reporting, so this paper asks what changes when the correction moves inside the loop and the acceptance threshold is indexed to the running count and dispersion of the search's own trials. The threshold then becomes an object the search can optimise against: we show analytically that a naive in-loop bar admits a variance-dilution effect, in which mediocre near-duplicate candidates lower the bar because the ledger's dispersion falls faster than its trial-count factor grows. We propose two defences, a pre-registered variance floor and a monotone high-water-mark bar, and evaluate the construction under a protocol frozen before any run, with every in-loop decision replaying exactly from its recorded trace. Across 53 audited hundred-candidate searches over two frontier models, two universes, and two feature spaces, the gated search reports "no certifiable discovery" on 36 of 37 runs, un-gated controls report a strategy on all 16, and every arm's out-of-sample confidence interval includes zero. Supporting studies find that state-based stopping reaches the same outcome after 8 to 9 trials at about a twelfth of the trial budget while an adaptive budget adds nothing, that a controlled stress test reproduces the dilution effect and both defences, and that a hundred nominal trials collapse to 6 to 8 effectively independent return streams. We scope these results to the analysed system.
papers.intro:
A strategy that is chosen as the best of many candidates owes its measured score to two ingredients. One is genuine edge, which tends to repeat on data the search never touched. The other is selection luck, which does not. When a process auditions NN candidates and reports the best, the reported score is inflated by the luck that helped put that candidate on top. Empirical finance has long supplied instruments to correct for this, including the deflated Sharpe ratio, the probability of backtest overfitting, and multiplicity-adjusted hurdles (Bailey et al., 2017; Bailey and López de Prado, 2014; Harvey et al., 2016).11 1 The Sharpe ratio is a strategy’s mean return divided by the standard deviation of its returns, annualised throughout this paper. A backtest is a historical simulation of a strategy; point-in-time means universe membership as known on each historical date; SPY is an S&P 500 index fund, used here as the passive benchmark. These instruments share a common arrangement. The search runs first, and the correction is applied afterwards, to the reported winner. The searcher itself stays statistically naive: it maximises raw in-sample performance, and honesty is imposed on its output after the fact.

Autonomous search loops built on LLMs make this arrangement uncomfortable. A refinement agent that proposes, backtests, and revises candidate strategies performs its multiplicity inside the loop, quickly, guided by a critic that sees raw performance numbers. In prior work we instrumented such a system and applied the correction after the fact, finding that the apparent edge of every discovered strategy disappeared once its performance was deflated by the search’s recorded trial count (Gençay, 2026). That verdict is honest, but it arrives only after the search budget has been spent. A natural question follows, and to our knowledge no agent-loop system has made this move: what changes if the correction is moved inside the loop, so that the searcher’s own acceptance threshold, stopping rule, and feedback are indexed to the running count and dispersion of its own trials? Optimisation loops for LLM agents are now common, but they do not carry statistical accounting of this kind.

Moving the correction inside the loop is not simply a matter of relocating a computation, and the analytical core of this paper is to explain why. The live threshold, which we call the bar, is Bk=V^k​K​(Nk)B_{k}=\sqrt{\widehat{V}_{k}}\,K(N_{k}): the dispersion of the trial scores seen so far, multiplied by a factor for the luckiest of NkN_{k} draws. Read in words, the bar is an estimate of the best score that selection luck alone would be expected to produce, given how many candidates have been tried and how spread out their scores are. A candidate is accepted only if it clears this bar. Once the bar is part of the searcher’s environment, however, it becomes something the search can act upon. The trial-count factor K⁡(N)K(N) grows only like 2​ln⁡N\sqrt{2\ln N}, whereas a single near-mean trial shrinks the dispersion factor V\sqrt{V} at the faster relative rate 1/(2​N)1/(2N). Adding mediocre, near-duplicate candidates can therefore push the bar down rather than up. We call this variance dilution, state it as a proposition with explicit assumptions, and propose two defences: a pre-registered variance floor that limits how far the bar can be pushed down, and a monotone bar that is not allowed to fall at all.

papers.title: Finite-Cadence Refresh Equilibria for Streaming Prior-Anchored Ridge: A Closed-Form Forgetting Window and Spectral Correction
papers.abstract: Recursive estimators on drifting streams must forget stale data fast enough to track the target, yet slowly enough to average out noise. In prior-anchored ridge regression, this trade-off admits a closed-form spectral decomposition in which each eigen-direction interpolates between the data solution and the prior with pull weight $s_i = \rho / (\mu_i + \rho)$. When the anchor is refreshed every $k$ steps, we show that the moving-frame offset converges to a finite-cadence equilibrium that lags the pure-leaky path by an explicit $\Delta_k(s)$ while reducing estimation variance by a factor $\Psi(s, r_k)$. Minimizing the cycle-averaged risk gives $\omega^* = (4\nu^2 \Sigma / c')^{1/3}$, $c' = \sigma^2 d_{\mathrm{eff}}(\rho)$, and the plug-in strength $\rho^* = \sigma^2 / (n\delta^2)$. A random-matrix deterministic equivalent extends both laws to finite dimension, renormalizing the anchor to $\rho_{\mathrm{eff}} = \rho (e^{\zeta q} - 1) / (\zeta q)$; it matches simulation within 5% at fixed operating points and within 13% at the method's own, and rank-deficient populations reduce exactly to their active subspace. The resulting method, SPAR, calibrates window and strength online from residuals. On a 27-configuration grid the calibrated window opens on drift without divergence, and the grid defaults transfer to an hourly electricity stream and to BCI IV 2b. The core algebra, refresh chain, and regret bounds are formalized in Lean 4.

A streaming estimator that never forgets accumulates lag under drift; one that forgets too fast amplifies noise. Gradient-based test-time adaptation (Sun et al., 2020; Wang et al., 2021) resolves this balance implicitly, at the cost of a gradient channel, per-data set hyperparameter selection, and imprecise guarantees. Prior-anchored ridge regression makes this balance explicit. papers.title: Structural Results on the Unfair 0-1 Polynomial Conjecture
papers.abstract: A $0$-$1$ polynomial is a polynomial whose coefficients are all either $0$ or $1$. The unfair $0$-$1$ polynomial conjecture states that if $f$ is a $0$-$1$ polynomial and $f(x)=g(x)h(x)$ is a factorisation into non-constant polynomials with non-negative real coefficients, then $g$ and $h$ must themselves be $0$-$1$ polynomials. We call $f$ fair if every such factorisation has this property, and unfair otherwise. In this paper, we study structural properties of possible unfair factorisations and obtain conditions which guarantee fairness. In particular, we prove that if $$ f(x)=x^{n-\operatorname{deg} w}w(x)+v(x), $$ where $v$ and $w$ are $0$-$1$ polynomials and $v$ is fair, then $f$ is fair whenever $$ n\geq\max\{\operatorname{deg} w+2\operatorname{deg} v,\,2\operatorname{deg} w\}. $$

We call such a factorisation fair if both gg and hh are 00–11 polynomials, and unfair otherwise. Similarly, we call ff fair if every factorisation of ff into polynomials with non-negative real coefficients is fair, and unfair otherwise.

papers.title: Abstention Is Not Threshold Compliance: Stated Scoring Rules in Open Language Models
papers.abstract: Kalai et al. propose stating the scoring rule in the prompt with an explicit threshold t, so that a model should answer only when its probability of being correct exceeds t. We probe each requirement of compliance on shared items, in 12 checkpoints from three post-training stages of four fully open 3-8B recipes, with exploratory models up to 32B. At t = 0.75, a line limiting the reply to an answer or "I abstain" (the abstention format) raised the mean abstention rate from 20% to 91%. Yet within this format, raising t from 0.5 to 0.9 changed it by only -0.8 percentage points. Without the line, the higher threshold even lowered abstention, and up to 40% of a checkpoint's items received decisions that no compliant policy with threshold-independent beliefs could make. Given the probability that their answer was correct, the checkpoints barely responded to the threshold in a forced-choice probe. Comparisons with self-assessment signals such as P(True) depended on the grader and on answer drift between prompts. An external threshold on recalibrated P(True) made coverage non-increasing in t by construction. Calibrated on the evaluation distribution (post hoc), it beat the abstention format at t = 0.5; calibrated on TriviaQA and applied to PopQA, however, it fell below that format at 0.75. On OLMo 3 7B, decisions trained on threshold-conditioned targets did not follow unseen thresholds consistently. A post-hoc variant trained at four thresholds answered less as t rose but still failed a pre-specified test, mainly on agreement with its training rule. A high abstention rate is not evidence of compliance: evaluations using stated scoring rules should report how often models abstain, whether decisions respond to the stated threshold, and which items they answer.
papers.intro:
Under binary grading, a guess never scores worse than an abstention, so evaluations that reward accuracy alone reward guessing over acknowledging uncertainty (Kalai et al., 2026). Kalai et al. propose stating the scoring rule in the prompt with an explicit threshold tt: an abstention earns tt, a correct answer 1 and a wrong answer 0, so a model should answer only when its probability of being correct exceeds tt. In their case study, four frontier models abstained more as tt rose, yet all scored below always-abstain at 0.75 and 0.9.

When abstention rises under such a rule, it is tempting to read it as compliance. It need not be. Following a stated threshold requires three things: (i) abstention must be an available reply; (ii) the threshold must be applied to a probability of being correct; and (iii) the model must have a usable estimate of that probability and use it. An instruction that names the abstention reply addresses only (i), yet can raise abstention by itself, so an evaluation reporting only abstention rates cannot tell compliance from a response to the wording.

papers.title: The inscribed $4$-polytope of maximal volume with ten vertices
papers.abstract: We prove that a $4$-polytope with ten vertices inscribed in the unit sphere $\mathbb{S}^{3}$ has volume at most $\frac{25}{384}(10 + 2\sqrt{5})$, and that, up to orthogonal transformations, equality holds only for the convex hull of two regular pentagons inscribed in $\mathbb{S}^{3}$ in orthogonal $2$-planes through the origin. papers.title: Cubic fourfolds with a symplectic involution from finite Prym data
papers.abstract: We study how many polarized anti-invariant factors of the intermediate Jacobians of smooth Eckardt hyperplane sections determine a cubic fourfold with a symplectic involution. In rank three, the equation is determined by its fixed cubic surface and a conic in the dual projective space. The Torelli theorem of Casalaina-Martin--Zhang recovers the surface together with one plane section from each factor. When the surface has no automorphisms, these planes can be compared in a common dual space, and reconstruction reduces to classical conic interpolation. Five factors suffice without parameter data, and four suffice with their ordered parameter configuration; both bounds are sharp. In rank two, we construct two-dimensional families of pairwise nonisomorphic equivariant fourfolds with the same entire unparametrized Prym image. For a fixed fourfold, we also show that the closure of the anti-invariant factor family in an associated OG10 compactification is an integral projective Lagrangian subvariety.

The Torelli theorem of Casalaina-Martin–Zhang shows that the polarized anti-invariant factor of the intermediate Jacobian of a smooth Eckardt cubic threefold determines the corresponding cubic surface together with its transverse plane section [4, Theorem 6.1]. Here an Eckardt cubic threefold is a smooth cubic threefold with a point whose tangent hyperplane section is a cone over a smooth plane cubic, with that point as vertex [4, Definition 1.1 and Proposition 1.2]. Such threefolds occur in a distinguished pencil of invariant hyperplane sections of a cubic fourfold with a symplectic involution. It is therefore natural to ask how many of their polarized factors determine the ambient fourfold, and whether this reconstruction also requires knowing the positions of the sections on the parameter line.

papers.title: Orthogonal Splines Associated to Root Systems and Applications to Function Approximation From Generalized Derivative Samples
papers.abstract:
Let $\mathcal{S}(X)$ be the principal shift invariant space generated by a box spline $B_X$ with $d$-dimensional direction set $X$ and associated differential operator $D_X$. Assuming that each direction in $X$ appears with even multiplicity i.e $X = [X_0|X_0]$, we may endow $\mathcal{S}(X)$ with a special inner product $\langle \cdot , \cdot \rangle_X$ which is similar to a homogeneous Sobolev-like inner product of order $|X_0|$. Then, for the special case when the directions in $X$ are selected from a root system, we introduce bi-orthogonal systems for $\mathcal{S}(X)$. Within any fixed bi-orthogonal system, each basis function is compactly supported albeit the diameter of the supports of the basis functions is not uniformly bounded. On the other hand, the image of any bi-orthogonal system under $D_X$ (which is necessarily finite and discrete) is uniformly finite. In other words, the basis elements, while having non-sparse box-spline representation, are uniformly sparse in their truncated-power representation.
  Using the Sobolev-like inner product and an aforementioned biorthogonal system for $\mathcal{S}(X)$, the analysis-synthesis operator from smooth compactly supported continuous functions into $\mathcal{S}(X)$ is well-defined. Using integration by parts and the orthogonality satisfied by the bases under $\langle \cdot , \cdot \rangle_X$, this operator is a local discrete quasi-interpolation operator. When $X$ comes from an irreducible root system, we can slightly modify these quasi-interpolants to ensure they have optimal approximation order. In other words, if $f$ is sufficiently smooth and compactly supported, we can optimally approximate $f$ from a collection of generalized derivative samples induced by one of our bases.

papers.title: Making Poisson {\sigma} again - an \'etude on groupoidal gauging, anomalies, gerbes, and defects
papers.abstract: The Poisson $\sigma$-model (PSM) over a closed worldsheet $\Sigma$ is reinterpreted as a theory of connections on a trivial principaloid bundle $P_0 = \Sigma \times G \to \Sigma$ with the symplectic structure groupoid $(G,\omega)$ integrating the Poisson target $(M,\Pi)$, and that of sections of the shadow bundle $F_0 = \Sigma \times M \to \Sigma$ - as defined in 2503.09886 [math.DG]. The flat directions of the PSM are explained as linearisations of automorphisms of $P_0$, modelled on maps from $\Sigma$ into the group of lagrangean bisections of $G$, which induce Poisson automorphisms of $(M,\Pi)$. The gauge anomaly of the ensuing field theory is derived and demonstrated to vanish for prequantisable $\omega$. A general anomaly-cancellation mechanism is proposed, which couples the bare model - rewritten as the holonomy of a connection-dependent trivial gerbe on $F_0$ - to a background gerbe over $M$ endowed with a $G$-equivariant structure. The coupling takes the form of the tensor product of the two gerbes and the extended PSM is defined as the holonomy of the product gerbe. An essential generalisation of the theory is then proposed - to shadows $F$ of principaloid bundles $P$ of arbitrary topology, in keeping with the interpretation of the gauging as descent to the orbistack $M//G$. The generalisation uses local product gerbes depending on local connections over trivialisations of $F$. The $G$-equivariant structure is proven to ensure a 2-stacky descent of the local gerbes to a global one over $F$. Its holonomy is taken as the definition of the generalised PSM. A cohomological discussion of obstructions against the descent is provided. Finally, a reformulation of the generalised PSM as a field theory with a topological gauge-symmetry defect is given, in which the $G$-equivariant structure is employed - alongside the transition cocycle of $P$ - as the datum of the defect.

The gauge principle underlies much of modern physical modelling—from the Standard Model of fundamental interactions, through the 2dd σ\sigma-models of string theory on homogeneous spaces, all the way to topological field theory, such as the 3dd Chern--Simons theory. It comes with a neat geometric assignment of field-theoretic types: Gauge fields are identified with connections on bundles of frames (aka gauge bundles), and matter fields are represented by global sections of the latter’s quotients with respect to a principal action of the symmetry model11 1 We intentionally abstain from specifying the symmetry model at this stage. The classic one, largely regarded as synonymous with the notion of symmetry, is a group acting smoothly on a manifold, i.e., an action groupoid. In what follows, we stumble upon generalisations of this classic case, given by arbitrary Lie groupoids. on their total spaces, representing a global change of frame. A ‘minimal’ coupling between the two field species is captured by the covariant derivative, and gauge symmetry is implemented by those automorphisms of the gauge bundles—locally presented as families of diffeomorphisms of their typical fibres, indexed smoothly by points in the spacetime—which are equivariant with respect to the global change of frame. The geometric framework naturally accomodates dynamics—typically driven by the curvature of the corresponding connections—of both: gauge fields and probes charged under these fields. The topological couplings arising in the latter setting, also in a categorified (‘higher gauge’) form, employ differential characters [Alv85, Gaw88], which pave the way to prequantisation of the dynamics and a rigorous description of Aharonov–Bohm-type interference phenomena.

This elaborate geometric structure reflects the deeper idea behind the gauging, to wit: an effective descent of dynamics to the space of orbits of the symmetry within the typical fibre of the configuration bundle of the physical system, i.e., within the space of internal degrees of freedom of the theory. The space of orbits need not admit a smooth structure, and so it is not---in general---directly accessible to field-theoretic constructions, but it does admit a homotopy model---the classifying space of the symmetry-action groupoid, given by the geometric realisation of the groupoid’s simplicial nerve. The homotopy model serves as the base of a universal gauge bundle22 2 The bundle is called the universal principal bundle of the symmetry-action groupoid, see, e.g., [AC11]., reproducing its physical avatar upon pullback to the associated configuration bundle, the latter two fibering over the spacetime of the physical theory. Furthermore, as shown by Dupont [Dup76], it has a well-defined model of differential cohomology—the Bott–Shulman-Stasheff cohomology (and its Beilinson–Deligne-type resolutions)—which suggests itself as a natural source of extensions of cohomological structures on the configuration fibre of the theory to be employed in the gauging. This becomes relevant whenever such structures enter the definition of the dynamics, as is the case, e.g., for the Polyakov–Alvarez–Gawȩdzki (PAG) σ\sigma-model of charged loop mechanics in external higher gauge fields. The existence and status of the universal bundles and their relation to their physical counterparts—the gauge bundles—over the spacetime, indicates the necessity to incorporate all isoclasses of the latter in a consistent gauging, and—indeed—violating this rule has been demonstrated to lead to pathologies in the quantum régime, see: [GSW10, Sec. 4] for a discussion and further references to the literature.

Lifting classical gauge symmetries to the quantum theory may encounter obstructions, which go under the name of gauge anomalies. These are both ubiquitous and naturally quantifiable in the presence of (background) cohomological structures over the configuration bundle—de Rham cocycles and their geometrisations (aka nn-gerbes and related higher-geometric objects)—which couple to charges carried by the internal degrees of freedom of the theory [GSW10]. Such structures are themselves associated with an independent (higher) gauge symmetry, and making the two gauge symmetries compatible with each other—typically through equivariantisation of the original cohomological structure relative to the symmetry to be gauged, see: ibidem, and also [GR03, GSW08, GSW11, RS09, GSW13, Sus12, Sus26]—requires the vanishing of certain obstruction classes in (equivariant) cohomology. This, then, becomes a source of superselection criteria for admissible backgrounds of the dynamics of interest, distinguishing those which allow for an effective descent to the space of orbits of the symmetry under gauging, effectively represented by descent to the quotient configuration bundles of arbitrary topology.

Accordingly, it becomes highly desirable to uncover or reconstruct such a realisation whenever a gauge symmetry manifests, e.g., through the emergence of a nontrivial kernel of the presymplectic form of the theory in its lagrangean formulation [Gaw72].

papers.title: Tripod Reordering: A 33-Queue Layout of Planar Graphs
papers.abstract:
A queue layout of a graph consists of a linear order of the vertices and a partition of the edges into queues so that no two edges in a single queue are nested. The minimum number of queues needed in a queue layout of a graph is called its queue number. A planar product structure theorem of Dujmovi\'c, Joret, Micek, Morin, Ueckerdt, and Wood (JACM, 2020) states that every planar graph is a subgraph of the strong product of a graph of simple treewidth at most $3$, a clique $K_3$, and a path. The result has been used to show that the queue number of planar graphs is at most $49$.
  Recently, Bekos, Gronemann, and Raftopoulou (Algorithmica, 2023) investigated how the general approach based on the product structure can be optimized for planar graphs. They claim that an appropriate reordering of the three vertices associated with each bag in the product structure decomposition, called a tripod, reduces the queue number of planar graphs to $42$. We first highlight a gap in their queue layout algorithm: one of the choices required by the algorithm is not guaranteed to exist. Then we show how to address the limitation and provide an alternative tripod reordering mechanism that reduces the upper bound on the queue number of planar graphs to $33$. As a corollary, bipartite planar graphs have queue number at most $22$.
